title: If You Can't Stop Scrolling, Watch This
category: Mental Health Vlogs & Personal Video Diaries
transcription: Have you ever picked up your phone for just one minute and somehow lost an entire hour? You're not alone. The average person spends hours scrolling every day. But what if you used that time for something that actually improved your life? Here are seven things to do instead of scrolling on your phone. Seven: Read ten pages of a book. Just ten pages a day may not sound like much, but that's over 3,000 pages a year. Knowledge compounds, and a few minutes of reading can teach you more than hours of random scrolling. Six: Go for a walk. A short walk can boost your mood, clear your mind, and improve your health. No fancy equipment needed, just step outside and start moving. Five: Learn one new skill. Spend 15 minutes learning a language, practicing an instrument, or watching a tutorial. Small daily improvements can lead to massive results over time. Four: Call someone you care about. Instead of watching strangers online, connect with real people in your life. A simple conversation can strengthen relationships and make someone's day. Three: Write down your thoughts. Grab a notebook and journal for a few minutes. Writing helps organize your mind, reduce stress, and turn ideas into action. Two: Exercise for 10 minutes. Push-ups, stretching, yoga, or a quick workout—anything that gets your body moving. Your future self will thank you. One: Work on a goal—that project, business idea, skill, or dream you've been putting off. Spend just 20 minutes on it today. Progress beats endless scrolling every single time. The next time you reach for your phone, ask yourself, "Do I want entertainment for a moment or progress that lasts?" If you found this helpful, don't forget to like, subscribe, and share it with someone who spends a little too much time scrolling.

title: Just do the right thing. The rest doesn’t matter.#Selflessness#PersonalGrowth#selfimprovement
category: Mental Health Vlogs & Personal Video Diaries
transcription: On action and duty. Great ideas from the book Meditations by Marcus Aurelius. Just do the right thing, the rest doesn't matter. That quote is basically saying focus on what you can control, and let go of what you can't. Here's what that breaks down to. 1. Just do the right thing. This is the part you can control. It's about your own choices, your own actions, and your own character. Is it kind? Is it honest? Is it helpful? Does it align with who you want to be? Your job is to figure out the right, decent, ethical thing to do in a situation and then do it. That's your duty. 2. The rest doesn't matter. This is the part you can't control, so don't let it paralyze you or stop you from doing your duty. What other people think of you for doing it, whether you'll get credit or even be thanked, whether it will be successful or work out perfectly, how hard or scary it feels. The outcome, sometimes, you can only control your effort, not the final result. Think of it like this. You see someone drop their wallet. The right thing is to pick it up and give it back to them. So you do it. The rest, that doesn't matter. Whether they are suspicious of you, whether they say a heartfelt thank you or just grunt, or whether you're late to your next appointment because you stopped. You did your part. The rest was out of your hands. In a nutshell, pour your energy into being a person of good action. Don't waste your energy worrying about the noise, the results, or the opinions that follow. Your peace comes from knowing you did what you should, not from how the world reacts. It's a call for integrity over image, for courage over comfort, and for focusing on your own behavior in a world you can't control.

title: How to Build Habits That Actually Stick
category: Mental Health Vlogs & Personal Video Diaries
transcription: You're not failing when it comes to habits. You're just starting too many at once. Most people don't struggle because they're lazy. They struggle because they try to change their entire life overnight. They want to wake up earlier, start working out, eat healthier, drink more water, meditate, journal, read more, spend less time on their phone, all at the same time. And for a few days, it feels exciting, but then everything falls apart. Not because you're incapable, because your brain can't sustain that much change all at once. If your habits never seem to stick, the problem isn't motivation. It's the way you're trying to build them. Most habits fail because there's no structure behind them. People rely on motivation instead of systems. They tell themselves, "I'll work out after work tomorrow. I'll start eating healthier in a few days. I'll remember to do it." But vague habits don't survive real life because life gets busy, you get tired, your routine changes, your motivation drops, and if there's no repeatable structure, the habit disappears with it. Another mistake people make is setting the barrier too high. They think, "If I'm going to work out, I'm going to do 1 hour. If I'm going to read, I need to read an entire chapter. If I'm going to meal prep, I need to fix my entire diet." Eventually, your brain starts resisting it, not because the goal is bad, because the effort required feels too big to repeat consistently. That's why intensity usually fails. It asks too much before consistency exists. If you want a habit to stick, make it smaller, smaller than you think it should be. Make it so easy your brain has no reason to avoid it. Want to start working out? Don't commit to an hour. Commit to putting your shoes on and doing 5 to 10 minutes. Want to read more? Read one page. Want to meditate? Sit down for 30 seconds. Your goal in the beginning should not be full transformation. It should be repetition because repetition creates familiarity and familiarity lowers resistance. You're not trying to prove how disciplined you are. You should be trying to teach your brain that this is something you do now. Another thing that helps is attaching your habits to something that already exists. Instead of saying, "I'll do it later," anchor it to something specific. After I brush my teeth, I'll stretch. After work, I'll take a walk for 10 minutes. After making my coffee, I'll journal for a few minutes. The less decisions your brain has to make, the easier consistency becomes. That's what systems do. They reduce friction. Here's the part that nobody likes hearing. Consistency is supposed to feel boring sometimes. Social media makes change look exciting and intense, but real progress usually looks repetitive, quiet, simple, unimpressive. A lot of people quit because a habit no longer feels exciting. But habits that last aren't built on excitement. They're built on repeatability. You don't need perfect days. You need enough days repeated over time. Missing one day isn't failure. title: Aurora Innovation: Business Review Highlights Q4 2025 with Co-Founder & CEO Chris Urmson
transcription: 2025 was a really big year for us. We launched our driverless trucks for the first time. We've been operating them day in and day out. Q4 continued to be great progress for us. We are, as of January, to over 250,000 driverless miles, which is nearly triple the mileage we had in October, increasing our revenue 25% quarter-over-quarter. And of course, we did all this while maintaining a perfect safety record and perfect on-time record. Our latest release unlocks our ability to operate driverlessly in the rain, in the fog, and in heavier wind. This unlocks really meaningful utilization gains because in the past, the Aurora Driver had been blocked from operation up to 40% of the time because of weather. This release also unlocks driverless operation between El Paso and Phoenix and complete bidirectional driverless operation between Fort Worth and El Paso. Fort Worth to Phoenix is a big deal because it's a 1,000-mile lane, and that 1,000 miles means that a person can't drive that in a single day within their hours of service limits. It means that the Aurora Driver is now offering a superhuman benefit to our customers. This year, we're really going to see our generalized AI approach unlock some rapid expansion. We expect to be operating across the Sun Belt this year, going to customer endpoints, really serving the need of our customers. That's going to start with one of the leading US carriers and their endpoint in Phoenix. We're also going between a sand mine and a customer site in Midland for Detmar. Detmar is a great example of how endpoints unlock value for customers. The Aurora Driver is going to be operating 20 hours a day for Detmar, hauling frac sand for their oil and gas industry customers on this 60-mile lane that's mostly freeway, effectively doubling the productivity of their assets. On top of that, we're going to be running from Laredo to Dallas, hauling berries for Driscoll's for Hirschbach. And we're going to end the year with over 200 trucks operating driverlessly day in and day out. Our new fleet's going to come online in Q2. It's going to be on the International LT platform, and we're not going to have to have an observer on board. With Volvo, we've really entered the industrialization phase. We're working with the New River Valley factory, where the first VNL with the Aurora Driver installed has come off the line, and that's really setting us up for the future. This is the foundation you need to really deliver product at scale. Looking further ahead to our third-generation system, we continue to make great progress on Novia. This hardware generation is really going to enable scale, allowing us to produce tens of thousands of trucks. We ended 2025 in a really strong position with $1.5 billion on our balance sheet. We anticipate that'll fund operations until we achieve positive free cash flow in 2028. Scaling over 200 trucks means that we're going to be able to generate somewhere between 14 and 16 million dollars of revenue this year. That's a 400% increase year-on-year. We're seizing the opportunity to transform logistics, one of the most important industries on the planet, and we're well on our way to having tens of thousands of Aurora-driven trucks on the road.

title: How Buyers Actually Evaluate a Business (In Under 3 Minutes)

So, you know, Rick, most owners they they see it through the lenses of the time that they have invested in building the business and, you know, it's always the rose-colored glasses sometimes. When, you know, a buyer comes to the table and it's a private equity group or strategic buyers, they often show up with their own teams of attorneys and analysts and accountants and all the players that are involved. That makes that playing field very complex very quickly and without having the right advisor on your side to help you navigate that, it it can get very, very sticky quickly. Um, you know, one of the reasons we wanted to host this webinar today is because we frequently meet owners who have built remarkable companies, but haven't given much thought at all to the exit process until a circumstance, you know, comes to the forefront. By the time they reach out, you know, we want to make sure that the financials are lender ready for the for the most part because most lenders they want to see clean financials. Um, you know, it doesn't mean that that it can't be fixed, but we need to be able to work quickly with the advisors, with the folks that are involved on on the seller's team to make that more attractive to the lenders so we can get it across the finish line. title: Insurers' Shifting Priorities - Pricing Modernization Webinar Clip
transcription: Okay, so this data comes from our annual survey of insurers on the factors that shape their IT investment priorities. So last year, and in most prior years, the number one thing is growth. If it'll help me grow, I will spend money. But this year, the picture changed noticeably. Growth, as you can see, moved down to third place, while data and innovation emerged as the leading priorities. In fact, last year, data wasn't even in the top five, and so here it is, number one, without even being something that we saw last year. Now, that does not mean that growth and efficiency are no longer important, because nearly all insurers, 98%, still said growth was a big area of focus in 2026. But what's changing is how they're thinking about achieving it, right? Increasingly, insurers are seeing data as the foundation for growth, innovation, and operational improvement. And so these priorities, they're no longer really separate initiatives, they're deeply interconnected, they're increasingly dependent upon each other. So, growth, number one thing that carriers are focusing on. But at the same time, the market environment is changing. Now, this comes from a study of policyholders who had a personal auto claim in the last two years. And we picked personal auto because we were looking at the claims experience. And personal auto is kind of homogeneous when it comes to claims, as opposed to something like, you know, general liability. Anyway, we found that 25% of those who had a claim loved their carrier so much after the claim that they would pay more to stay. But half of all policyholders with a claim told us that they were actively looking for lower premium elsewhere, or had already moved. So, policyholders shopping at historically high rates. And in that environment, the goal can't just be how low can you go to keep your customers, right? Or to attract new customers. That approach always creates long-term profitability challenges. So, the real question is, what is the right price for this specific customer based on their individual risk profile? Now, when insurers rely on broad rating bands, they increase the likelihood of adverse selection, right? Because the lower-risk customers are more likely to leave in search of pricing that more adequately reflects their actual risk, while the higher-risk customers are more likely to stay because they're getting a lower price than they should be paying. And this is why pricing precision matters so much right now, like not only for attracting the customers who are actively shopping, but also for retaining the ones already in your portfolio.

However, she explains that growth remains crucial, with 98% of insurers still prioritizing it, but the method has shifted—insurers now view data as the essential foundation for growth, innovation, and operational improvement.

She warns against competing solely on low prices, as this undermines long-term profitability. transcription: Every business says that they have values and the values lead to the culture. One of the tools that we use as part of this process, there's a number of frameworks as well as strategic business tools and methods that you can use, and one of the frameworks is the United the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals. If you're in a supply chain and you're doing a sustainability impact report, and I'll show you a couple of examples of those that you can take away in a little while, if you map that within your sustainability reporting, corporates understand this this stuff. title: Why Are Top Economists Warning of a Rising Recession Risk in 2026?
transcription: Recession risk is rising fast and could hit within weeks. Will geopolitical tensions and inflation push the global economy over the edge right now? Energy prices are not just a headline. When energy costs rise, businesses face higher expenses and often pass those on to consumers. This causes people to cut back on spending, creating a feedback loop that weakens economic growth. This dynamic is a key reason economists are so worried about inflation's lingering impact on the economy in 2026. Top economist Mohamed El-Erian has issued a stark warning. He says the global economy faces a critical eight-week window to prevent a recession. The trigger is the reopening of a crucial oil route currently disrupted by geopolitical tensions. If this route stays closed, energy supplies tighten further, pushing costs higher and escalating recession risks worldwide. Another leading economist, Mark Zandi, agrees recession risks are rising significantly. He estimates about a 40% chance of recession this year. However, Zandi still sees a path to avoid it, especially if geopolitical tensions ease. The key challenge is managing inflation, which remains elevated even if tensions cool. Investors are already feeling the pressure. Zandi warns the S&P 500 could fall by as much as 30% as the market adjusts to the real economic risks behind inflated stock valuations. This signals a painful correction ahead for many portfolios as the economy deals with these pressures. Even if geopolitical tensions ease and energy routes reopen, elevated prices are expected to persist. Zandi estimates this will cost the average household roughly $1,400 a year. This ongoing inflation squeeze means families will feel the impact directly through higher everyday expenses. What this means for you is clear: the next two months are critical. Energy prices and geopolitical events could shape your financial future. You might face higher costs and a volatile stock market. Staying informed and cautious with spending and investments is key. Subscribe now for the latest updates to help you navigate these uncertain times.

title: Introducing Claude Fable 5
transcription: Today we're launching Claude Fable 5. The most capable model we've ever released to the public. Fable 5 is a mythos class model with safeguards that make it ready for general use. We didn't broadly release our previous model with this level of capability because when we finished training and testing it, we saw that the model, Claude Mythos Preview, was finding thousands of cybersecurity vulnerabilities. A model that can find flaws like that can also be used to exploit them. So instead of releasing it, we handed it to the people who protect the world's critical software and put it to work fixing the holes before someone could break through them. It was the right call for the moment, but it was never the goal. We believe powerful AI should be safe and accessible. That's why we went to work on Claude Fable 5. Every Claude model has safeguards to keep it from doing harm. Fable needed more cautious ones than anything we've built before. Our safety systems for Fable 5 automatically review requests that touch on high-risk areas like cybersecurity or biology. Those requests are then redirected to Opus 4.8. We do that intentionally so people can continue to benefit from the capabilities of a powerful model like Fable without the cyber and biology risks that come with it. The safeguards are broad today, but we'll keep refining them so that they're better at allowing safe requests. We built Claude Fable 5 for your most ambitious work. It can stay with a problem far longer than any model before it. It's highly autonomous and can operate for days without intervention. And it's not just coding. It can take on projects in finance, research, economics, law - complicated tasks that used to need constant supervision. So point it at something that matters. What's the problem we'll look back on and wonder why it took so long to solve? We know what Claude Fable 5 can do. The interesting part is what you'll do with it.

डेली एक सॉफ्टजेल आप ले सकते हैं। तो दोस्तों, अगर आप अपनी एनर्जी को वापस पाना चाहते हैं, अपनी हार्मोन को बैलेंस रखना चाहते हैं और अपनी वाइटलिटी को बूस्ट करना चाहते हैं तो फॉरएवर विटोलाइज मैन को अपनी डाइट में जरूर शामिल करें। अगर आपको इसका 100% ओरिजिनल प्रोडक्ट बेस्ट डिस्काउंट पर खरीदना चाहते हैं तो दिए गए मोबाइल नंबर पर डायरेक्ट डीएम कर सकते हैं। वीडियो अच्छी लगी तो लाइक करें, दोस्तों के साथ शेयर करें और चैनल को सब्सक्राइब करना बिल्कुल ना भूले। मिलते हैं अगली वीडियो में, तब तक स्टे हेल्दी, स्टे स्ट्रांग। अगर आप फॉरएवर लिविंग के साथ अपना बिजनेस शुरू करना चाहते हैं और एक बेहतरीन इनकम अपॉर्चुनिटी के बारे में जानना चाहते हैं, तो डिस्क्रिप्शन बॉक्स में दिए गए मेरे फर्स्ट लिंक फ्री मास्टरक्लास वेबीनार को जरूर देखें। थैंक यू।

title: Company Culture | Simon Sinek
transcription: So, I think the concept of leadership is one of the most misunderstood concepts in business, quite frankly. We think about leadership as a rank or position, like "I'm in leadership." The question is, are you a leader? Leadership is the awesome responsibility to see those around us rise. It is a skill set that needs to be learned and practiced. Most of us, the way we have achieved our leadership position or rank is because we were good at the job. The problem is that's not your job anymore. You know, when we're super junior, the organizations we work for give us tons of training how to do our job. Some of us go to college and how to do our job. If you're an architect, you have to go to school to learn how to be an architect. And if you're really good at your job, they'll promote you until you reach a position where you're now responsible for the people who do the job you used to do. But they don't teach us how to do that. And so the reason we get managers and not leaders is because we don't get taught how to do our new job called leadership. When leaders take themselves on, when leaders uh become students of leadership, you'll find that all of the traditional metrics that we try and push and, you know, and drive every day, go up. Productivity goes up. Engagement goes up. Uh uh innovation goes up. Um I think it's very funny, I love uh I love organizations that when they write their values on the wall, you know, it's like, integrity, innovation, you know, honesty. By the way, if you have to write honesty on the wall, you've got bigger problems. Um But those those things are not things you can do. Those are the result of things. You can't walk into someone's office and say, "Lynn, a little more a little more innovation from you today, please." Like, what are you supposed to do? And so, it's not a value. A value is is is a behavior. And the better we understand our values and the better we incentivize to behavior, the stronger your culture. And the stronger your culture, the more innovation you get, the more integrity get, the more productivity you get, the more uh uh engagement you get. My favorite definition of culture is culture equals values plus behavior. So, values, number one, needs to be written as verbs. It's not integrity, it's do the right thing. It's not innovation, it's find a new way to solve a problem. It's not honesty, it's tell the truth. Which are which are behaviors and we can incentivize and reward to those behaviors. And the people who are best at embodying those values, those are the ones that we should promote into leadership positions because those are the ones that set the example of of how we how we work here.
caption: In a clear, engaging tone, a man discusses the concept of leadership, emphasizing that it is a responsibility to help others succeed rather than just a rank. He explains that people are often promoted because they excel at their tasks, but they aren't taught how to lead. This lack of training results in managers instead of leaders. When leaders focus on learning, productivity and engagement improve. He concludes that culture is the sum of values and behaviors, and that values should be expressed as actions (verbs) rather than nouns to encourage better leadership.

transcription: Okay. So we are putting some timelines in the row one. And here the timelines are a higher window timelines. Means, what I'm saying is we are not putting day one, day two, sprint one, sprint two. We are putting Q1, Q2 because it's like a bigger container planning, no? So we are putting Q1, Q2 kind of a timeline and then you are putting some name of the release, or you- you- see, in a real-time situation, we will not put as simple like this 'Rent-a-Car', 'Share-a-Car'. It will be like 'Release One' hyphen that particular business unit hyphen, no, something based on the functionality of the project, something like that, right? And the releases can happen across EMEA, Asia Pacific, no, the global regions, no? Based on that also, that name will change because here, the template says name of the new release. So you're putting the name, and you are writing the goal. This is very very important. Every go- every release comes with a goal. Every PI comes with a goal. And if- if the release goal is not clear, if the PI goal is not clear, definitely, your product backlog and sprint backlog will get compromised, right? So that homework is been done over here, to a very great extent. Then, then you can put some high level features which is the- so see, now till date, name, goal, it is more on vision and strategy. The moment we go to feature level, it is building the product roadmap itself, right? So here, because features can be even a monthly release or a by, no, okay, twice a month release. So you are actually putting the features over here followed up by the metrics. How will I measure the success for the delivery of this particular features? So, in the YouTube, long back, some three and a half years back, I made a video called GQM: Goal, Question, Metrics, okay. Because some people have a problem of jumping to metrics directly. So there is an intermediate level called question, which will connect the goal to the metrics. I will pick up that video and then send it today in the group. Just go through that video, then you will understand this in a better manner. Okay. Now, how do you customize it in your Jira, or Service Now, or ADO, or Rally, or whatever be the tool? So till now we have seen only on discovery

title: UKREiiF 2026: 'Where the smart money is moving' panel discussion
transcription: So, we're here at UKREIIF this year, talking all things living UK real estate. The current environment for living real estate in the UK is one with viability challenges and concerns. We've got rising build cost inflation, increased regulation, economic difficulties. What there also is, is a huge amount of opportunity. There is pent-up demand, there is under supply, there is no shortage of debt available, there is capital being deployed. It is a huge time for opportunity. The smart money is moving primarily into affordable housing, I would say, though how you define that depends on a number of factors, but clearly the biggest risk to any investment strategy is take-up and demand at this moment, and so through various lenses people are trying to make sure that whatever it is that they're investing in or developing is affordable for the end user, so that the project is viable long-term. I think there's quite a lot of opportunity for living product, because there is a fundamental requirement and demand for good quality accommodation across all the living sectors, asset classes. Especially when there is a bit of an affordability gap. So, those that can deliver product that meets that demand are going to be very well placed. 2026, for me, has also been the year of co-living. We're seeing more institutionalisation of co-living, in terms of an accepted asset class for co-investors. So, I think the opportunities at the moment, very much from a housebuilders point of view, are in the land market. Slightly longer-term strategic sites, gray belt, something where you can work with a landowner to really maximize the number of homes on a site, and really go out there and get a planning consent. I believe that the opportunities in the living sector lie in working in partnership, both with local governments, local councils, with developers, with capital, trying to bring everybody together to achieve the ultimate goal of delivering more housing for the country. I think the smart money in living is moving to affordable with a small 'a'. That's how we deal with the viability concerns. That's where some degree of public subsidy can unlock delivery. I also see there's huge opportunities in partnerships becoming platforms, with long-term sustainable partnerships between registered providers, developers and investors to unlock delivery at scale.

title: Designing the Safer Transit Bus | Innovation for Operator Health
transcription: As was mentioned, I'm Jonathan Hack. I've spent my career in the transportation sector, all in the innovation area. And we've got an exciting panel discussion for you here today. You're going to hear from various perspectives. You're going to hear from the TTC, from Dr. Sarah Fox. You're going to hear from the Amalgamated Transit Workers Union, and you're going to hear from the operators themselves. What I want to talk about today is, um, a kind of deceptively simple idea, which is that if we want safer transit systems, we need to design them with the people who actually do the work. At the end of the day, like, we really want to democratize innovation. We want to make sure that it's cascaded across, so it should be coming from the workers, from the front line. With every new technology that finds its way into the bus, we then take a step back and say, well, how does that now combine with all the other things? Participation is not optional. It's a safety requirement. There's often a tendency to frame innovation that's something that happens to workers. Um, but what this research shows is that transit operators are already experts in safety-critical system management. The challenge moving forward is building processes that recognize and incorporate that expertise.

Ideas were shared, innovations were sparked, and a movement was born. And now, we take it to the next level. title: FIFA World Cup 2026 explained: How the new 48-team format works
transcription: For years, FIFA President Gianni Infantino has talked about getting more countries involved at a World Cup. That push finally took shape in January 2017 when football's governing body voted to expand the tournament from 32 to 48 teams. Under the new format, there will be 104 matches at this World Cup. That's 40 more than at Qatar 2022. Those games will be played across 16 host cities in the USA, Mexico, and Canada. That's a huge change from the compact 2022 tournament in Qatar where a fan could realistically attend two or even three matches in a single day. The 48 teams will be split into 12 groups of four. The top two from each group plus the eight best third-placed teams will move into a new 32-team knockout phase. From there, the tournament runs through the round of 32, the round of 16, quarterfinals, semifinals, and then the final. By the time we get to the decider at MetLife Stadium in New York, New Jersey, on July the 19th, the champions will have played eight matches. That's one more than the seven required by Argentina when they won Qatar 2022.

title: The 2026 FIFA World Cup explained in 2 minutes
transcription: The stage is set for this year's FIFA Men's World Cup, with the opening matches kicking off tomorrow. The tournament, held every four years, will be unlike any before it. Here's why. Firstly, it will be the biggest World Cup in history, the most complex one yet. For the first time ever, the tournament will be shared across three countries: the United States, Canada, and Mexico, and matches will be played across 16 cities. The competition is expanding, too. Instead of the traditional eight groups, this year's tournament will feature 12, made up of four teams each. 48 national teams will compete, instead of 32. With more teams in the mix, the road to glory could be tougher to predict. The expansion means a record number of matches. Teams will play 104 matches over 39 days, making it the longest ever World Cup run. With more teams involved, there could be more opportunities for underdogs to make their mark. Among those returning to the World Cup include the Democratic Republic of Congo, Haiti, and Iraq, while four debutants are getting their boots on the pitch for the first time. They are Uzbekistan, Jordan, Curacao, and Cape Verde. But staging the World Cup across three countries brings major logistical challenges. Some teams could end up traveling thousands of kilometers between venues, crossing borders and time zones. FIFA has grouped matches regionally to reduce travel, but long journeys may still be unavoidable for teams that progress deep into the tournament. And depending on where they're playing, the climates could be different, from the high altitude of Mexico City to Miami's heat and humidity. To manage that, FIFA has mandated cooling and hydration breaks during matches. Next, technology will play a bigger role than ever before. Every player will have a digital avatar to remodel on-pitch actions. These changes make it easier for officials to see what would go on during fast or obstructed plays, so they can provide more accurate calls for offsides or potential handballs. And then, of course, there are the stars. This could be the last dance for several legends. Portugal's Cristiano Ronaldo has confirmed this will be his last World Cup. Argentina's Lionel Messi and Croatia's Luka Modrić are also widely expected to be making their final appearances on the game's biggest stage. For football's greats, one final bow. For a new generation, a chance to make history. The road to World Cup glory is about to begin.

Recorded in a clear, high-quality studio setting with no background noise, her voice is articulate and easy to follow. She details how this tournament will be the largest and most complex in history, co-hosted by the United States, Canada, and Mexico across 16 cities. The speaker explains the expanded format featuring 48 teams playing 104 matches over 39 days. She also discusses the logistical hurdles, such as travel across time zones and varying climates, and introduces technological innovations like digital player avatars. Finally, she touches on the emotional aspect of the tournament, noting it will likely be the final World Cup for legends like Cristiano Ronaldo, Lionel Messi, and Luka Modric, setting the stage for a highly anticipated event.

title: How Mohammad Irfan Went From Street Hawker To India's Most Viral Protest Voice
transcription: सिर्फ पेट रोटी खा लेना ही जीवन नहीं है। शहरी सलम में जीवन नरक है। मैं कहता हूँ लोकतंत्र में ना अहंकार नहीं संवाद होना चाहिए और संवाद के दरवाज़े दोनों तरफ़ से खुले होने चाहिए। संविधान की शपथ में ना गरिमा शब्द का, व्यक्ति की गरिमा, राष्ट्र की एकता और अखंडता को सुनिश्चित, तो व्यक्ति की गरिमा, गरिमा, गरिमा नहीं गिरनी चाहिए सर। जय श्री कृष्णा सर, मैं इरफ़ान सर और आज मुझे आपसे बहुत सारी बातें करनी है सर। चार ट्रिलियन की अर्थव्यवस्था में ना पढ़े-लिखों का ही जीवन संवरा है? A voice that rose about the slogans at Jantar Mantar is now being heard in the country's political corridors. Mohammad Irfan, the hawker with little formal education whose speeches went viral during the student protest, met Congress leader Rahul Gandhi on Monday. Rahul Gandhi said Irfan's understanding of the constitution and his desire to learn reflected the strength of India's youth. Hours after the meet, Irfan spoke exclusively to India Today's sister platform, The Lallantop, with a message that cuts across party lines. मैं आज राहुल गांधी से मिला तो मैंने उनसे यही कहा कि अगर सर आप जो हम आपसे अपनी मांगे रख रहे हैं, आप विपक्ष के बड़े नेता हैं और आज नहीं तो कल सत्ता में आएंगे, अगर आपने हमारी बातों के वादाखिलाफी की तो हम अपनी असहमति आपके खिलाफ भी रखेंगे। For Irfan, accountability does not stop with one government or one political party. और हम न्यूट्रल हैं, हम इस देश का भला चाहते हैं। He also spoke about the struggles of migrant workers. 2024 का एनसीआरबी का डाटा कहता है कि 1 लाख 70 हजार 746 मौतें हुई जिसमें 31% दिहाड़ी मजदूर थे और वजह एक थी कि घर में तंगी और मानसिक संतुलन डिस्टर्ब होना, आर्थिक तंगी थी। तो हम कैसे इग्नोर कर सकते हैं उस वर्ग को जो इस देश की बड़ी आबादी है और खून-पसीना लगा रही है इस देश के निर्माण में? हम कैसे इग्नोर कर सकते हैं उसे? From the streets of Jantar Mantar to the national spotlight, his story is not about political power. It's about the power of a citizen's voice to be heard. transcription: हेलो दोस्तों, हमारे रोहित चंदेल सर के केस को लेकर जितने भी फैंस हैं, आज सुबह से ही हर किसी के मन में बस एक ही सवाल घूम रहा है। क्या आज हियरिंग हुई? क्या कोर्ट से बेल मिली? या क्या रोहित सर को लेकर कोई नया अपडेट आया है? हम सभी फैंस बहुत बेसब्री से इंतजार कर रहे हैं और आप सभी के लगातार आ रहे मैसेजेस और कमेंट्स देखकर मैं अच्छी तरह समझ सकती हूँ कि आप सब भी मेरी तरह कितने परेशान हैं। इसीलिए आज का पूरा सच आपके सामने रखना बहुत जरूरी था। तो बिना किसी एक्स्ट्रा बहस के, सीधे और साफ शब्दों में बता दूँ, आज बेल हियरिंग को लेकर ऑफिशियली कोई भी नया अपडेट नहीं आया है। कोर्ट या लीगल टीम की तरफ से अगली हियरिंग की कोई भी फिक्स डेट ऑफिशियली अनाउंस नहीं की गई है, लेकिन मैं पिछले कुछ दिनों से देख रही हूँ कि सोशल मीडिया और यूट्यूब पर काफी लोग खुद से ही हियरिंग की डेट्स तय कर रहे हैं। हर रोज अपने मन से एक नई डेट बनाकर वीडियो डाल देते हैं कि आज हियरिंग होने वाली है, कल फैसला आ जाएगा या आज बेल मिल जाएगी। लेकिन सच ये है कि ऐसा कुछ भी नहीं है। इस केस से रिलेटेड ज्यादातर लीगल इंफॉर्मेशन पब्लिक नहीं है। कोर्ट का काम अपने हिसाब से चलता है, किसी के अंदाजा लगाने से तारीखें तय नहीं होतीं। इसलिए हर किसी फेक न्यूज़ पर आँख बंद करके भरोसा मत कीजिए। यह सब सिर्फ व्यूज पाने के लिए बनाया जा रहा है। हम सब फैंस रोहित सर का बहुत इंतजार कर रहे हैं और उनके लिए लगातार प्रार्थना कर रहे हैं। हम सब चाहते हैं कि उन्हें जल्द से जल्द बेल मिले और सब सही हो जाए, लेकिन इस इंतजार में हमें स्ट्रांग और पॉजिटिव रहना है। झूठी अफवाहों और फेक वीडियोस को देखकर खुद को परेशान मत कीजिए। पॉजिटिव रहिए और उन्हें सपोर्ट करते रहिए। जैसे ही कोर्ट या लीगल टीम की तरफ से कोई भी असली अपडेट आएगा, मैं सबसे पहले आपके साथ शेयर कर दूँगी। तब तक के लिए अफवाहों पर ध्यान मत दीजिए, पॉजिटिव रहें और चैनल को सब्सक्राइब कर लें ताकि आपको हमेशा सही और सच्ची जानकारी ही मिले। धन्यवाद।

title: Hear from Afroman after the verdict in his civil trial
transcription:
Outside this Adams County courthouse, the sound of victory.
After a jury sided with the musician Afroman, whose real name is Joseph Foreman, after a days-long civil defamation trial. Afroman, speaking to WCPO right after the verdict.
I didn't win. America won. America still has freedom of speech. It's still for the people, by the people.
...the jury finds in favor of the defendant.
Seven Adams County Sheriff's deputies sued the musician. They argued Afroman used security video from a 2022 raid of his home and put it in music videos using deputies' likeness without permission.
There's damage to reputation, there's pain and suffering, there's public humiliation. There's everything you saw and heard from these detectives, from the witness stand.
This raid taking place nearly a year ago following search warrants related to possession and trafficking in drugs and kidnapping. The rapper was never charged. Along with using the surveillance video in multiple music videos, including in the song "Lemon Pound Cake", the deputies also say Afroman called them thieves and pedophiles among other things on social media.
I didn't go down here and sue the police department. I fixed up the damages they made, and I sung songs about them to raise money to do it. They were unapologetic.
The deputies wanted Afroman to pay $3.9 million in damages.
We got about a total of 250 pieces given out. This is the last one, and I'd like to give it to you.
Supporters of Afroman coming from near and far, with a message both verbally and symbolically.
For me, this isn't really about Afroman, it's about free speech. So, when someone like Afroman stands up for my free speech by using his talents, his musical talents, to fight the corrupt system, we gotta come out and support him.
I'm glad thing, you know, things went my way. But if they would have took it all from me, I was happy about all the love I was getting from everybody. After them people kicked my kicked my door in.
In Adams County, Jay Warren, WCPO 9 News.
When life give you lemons, you make lemon pound cake.

title: Afroman speaks after winning civil lawsuit
transcription:
A jury has sided with the rapper Afroman in the civil lawsuit filed against him by Adams County deputies. WCPO 9 News reporter Jay Shakoor is live outside the courthouse tonight. This verdict, Jay, was read right about 30 minutes ago, and you spoke to Afroman as he was leaving. What's his reaction?

That's right, Afroman had a very emotional reaction, the jury, as you mentioned, siding with the rapper Afroman, whose real name is Joseph Foreman, in this case. Here's video from inside the courtroom as this case went on. During closing arguments, the attorney representing the deputies in this case claimed Afroman intentionally lied about and defamed the deputies in his songs, but Afroman's attorney maintained throughout this trial, it is his right to say what he wants to say. This goes back to 2022 when Afroman's home was raided following search warrants related to possession and trafficking in drugs and kidnapping. Though he was never charged, the attorneys for the deputies suing say Afroman used security video from the raid on his home and put it in a music video using deputies' likenesses without permission. Again, this jury in Adams County finding he did not defame those deputies. Here is Afroman speaking directly after that verdict.

I didn't win. America won. America still has freedom of speech. It's still for the people, by the people.

Afroman becoming emotional there as he says this fight was bigger than him. It was about free speech and what he describes as corruption in this sheriff's department. I spoke to one supporter who came all the way from Dallas. I have more on that and more reaction from the rapper tonight at 11:00. In Adams County, Jay Shakoor, WCPO 9 News.

पर देख पा रहे होंगे जहां पर रोहित 11 और शार्दुल ठाकुर 11 बनाकर यहां पर प्रैक्टिस मुकाबला खेला था। शार्दुल 11 ने टॉस जीतकर पहले बल्लेबाजी का फैसला किया था। शार्दुल 11 की तरफ से रोबिन मिंज़ इसके साथ ही राज अंगद बावा यहां पर बैटिंग करने आए थे। रोबिन मिंज़ ने यहां पर 32 गेंदों में 66 रन की ताबड़तोड़ पारी खेली थी। राज अंगद ने यहां पर 30 रन केवल 14 गेंदों में बनाए थे बेहतरीन शुरुआत दी थी। इसके साथ ही मयंक रावत ने 45 रन 29 गेंदों में बनाए थे और गेंद के साथ 34 रन देकर एक विकेट भी लिया था। इसके साथ ही शार्दुल ठाकुर ने फिनिशिंग टचेस दी थी, 10 गेंदों में 23 रन बनाए थे, दो विकेट लेकर 45 रन देकर दो विकेट भी इन्होंने लिए थे। मयंक मार्कंडेय ने 30 रन देकर एक विकेट लिया था। दीपक चाहर ने यहां पर 34 रन देकर एक विकेट लिया था। इसके साथ ही यहां पर 198 रन 9 विकेट पर 20 ओवर में यहां पर शार्दुल 11 ने बनाए थे। दरअसल बॉल बाय बॉल इसके साथ ही जो फास्ट हाईलाइट है वो टेलीग्राम पर हम पोस्ट कर चुके हैं, तो फटाफट आप डिस्क्रिप्शन बॉक्स खोलकर टेलीग्राम चैनल को ज्वाइन कर लें। वहां पर सभी टीमों के लाइव प्रैक्टिस गेम भी चलते हैं, इसके साथ ही हर मैच की हाईलाइट सब कुछ वहां पर प्रोवाइड कर रहे टेलीग्राम पर। इंट्रा स्क्वाड मुकाबले भी देखने को मिलेंगे तो डिस्क्रिप्शन बॉक्स खोलकर आप टेलीग्राम चैनल पर पहुंच जाएं। फिर रोहित की टीम टारगेट का पीछा करने आई थी। रोहित की तरफ से यहां पर रोहित शर्मा ने बेहतरीन शुरुआत दी, नमन धीर ने उनके साथ ओपन किया था। नमन धीर ने 27 गेंदों में 51 रन बनाए, जबकि रोहित शर्मा यहां पर 43 गेंदों में 95 रन पर नाबाद थे जहां पर एक छक्का तो 121 मीटर का रोहित ने लगाया था। अपनी स्क्रीन पर देख पा रहे होंगे, इसके साथ ही दानिश मेलवार ने नाबाद 19 गेंदों में 34 रन बनाकर फिनिशिंग टचेस दी थी तो रोहित शर्मा 11 ने 199 रन चार विकेट पर केवल 17.5 ओवर में ही स्कोर कर लिया था। अभी विदेशी खिलाड़ियों ने टीमों को ज्वाइन नहीं किया है, केवल इंडियन प्लेयर इस मुकाबले का भाग हैं। इसके साथ ही रघु शर्मा ने तीन विकेट लिए यहां पर चार ओवर में 31 रन देकर। इसके साथ ही अश्विनी कुमार ने 23 रन देकर दो विकेट लिए और मोहम्मद इजहार ने बेहतरीन गेंदबाजी करी 21 रन देकर तीन विकेट चार ओवर में लिए थे, तो इस प्रकार से ये मुकाबला था। इस मुकाबले की कंप्लीट हाईलाइट हमने टेलीग्राम पर डाल दी है और भी बाकी टीमों के जो प्रैक्टिस चल रही है वो सब कुछ टेलीग्राम पर हम प्रोवाइड कर रहे हैं तो आप फटाफट टेलीग्राम चैनल को ज्वाइन कर लें और आप कमेंट करके बताइए और कौन सी टीमों की आप इंफॉर्मेशन जानना चाहते हो।

transcription: दोस्तों आईपीएल 2026 को लेकर आरसीबी टीम की कड़ी प्रैक्टिस शुरू हो चुकी है। जी हां दोस्तों, इसी बीच आरसीबी के खिलाड़ियों द्वारा दोस्तों 20-20 ओवर का वार्म अप मैच खेला गया। जी हां दोस्तों, इस वार्म अप मैच में एक तरफ थी कुणाल पांड्या की टीम, वहीं दूसरी तरफ थी वेंकटेश अय्यर की टीम और वहीं दोस्तों, इस वार्म अप मैच में दोस्तों वेंकटेश अय्यर की टीम पहले बल्लेबाजी करने के लिए आई और दोस्तों, हमें इस मुकाबले में जितेश शर्मा की काफी ताबड़तोड़ और विस्फोटक बल्लेबाजी देखने को मिली। जी हां दोस्तों, आपको बता दें कि इस मुकाबले में जितेश शर्मा मात्र 37 गेंदों में 81 रनों की शानदार पारी खेले और वहीं दोस्तों, टीम डेविड मात्र 14 गेंदों में 36 रनों की ताबड़तोड़ पारी खेले और वहीं कप्तान वेंकटेश अय्यर के 16 गेंदों में 30 रन और विराट कोहली के 12 गेंदों में 29 रनों की बदौलत वेंकटेश अय्यर की टीम कुणाल पांड्या की टीम के सामने सात विकेट के नुकसान पर 234 रन बनाती है। 235 रनों के लक्ष्य का पीछा करते हुए कुणाल पांड्या की टीम की तरफ से रजत पाटीदार और देवदत्त पडिक्कल की काफी तूफानी और विस्फोटक बल्लेबाजी देखने को मिली। दोस्तों, आपको बता दें कि इस मुकाबले में देवदत्त पडिक्कल और कप्तान कुणाल पांड्या बतौर ओपनर बल्लेबाजी करने के लिए आए और दोस्तों, देवदत्त पडिक्कल ने 33 गेंदों में 63 रन, वहीं कुणाल पांड्या ने 23 गेंदों में 58 रन बनाए और दोस्तों, रजत पाटीदार के 25 गेंदों में 74 रनों के बदौलत कुणाल पांड्या की टीम निर्धारित 20 ओवर में 247 रन बनाई। तो दोस्तों, यहां पर आपको क्या लगता है कि आरसीबी टीम आईपीएल 2026 को लेकर जिस तरह से प्रैक्टिस कर रही है, वह अपने आने वाले वाले मुकाबले में दोस्तों हैदराबाद को हरा पाएगी कि नहीं, अपनी राय कमेंट बॉक्स में जरूर बताएं।

प्रैक्टिस मुकाबला खेला गया था, जहाँ पर MSD 11 ने पहले टॉस जीतकर गेंदबाजी का फैसला किया था, ऋतु 11 को यहाँ पर पहले बल्लेबाजी कराई थी जहाँ पर ऋतुराज गायकवाड 11 से पहले गायकवाड ने यहाँ पर ओपन किया था, उनके साथ अरावली अवनीश पटेल ने ओपन किया था। दोनों ने ताबड़तोड़ शुरुआत करी जहाँ पर गायकवाड ने 30 गेंदों में 59 रन की बेहतरीन पारी खेली थी, इसके साथ ही यहाँ पर अरावली पटेल ने यहाँ पर 39 गेंदों में 90 रन की विस्फोटक पारी खेली थी। संजू सैमसन नंबर तीन पर आये थे, 18 गेंदों में 46 रन इन्होने बनाए थे, इसके साथ ही यहाँ पर घोष ने, रामकेश घोष ने यहाँ पर 18 रन 10 गेंदों में बनाए थे, इसके साथ ही 28 रन देकर एक विकेट भी लिया था, इसके साथ ही मुकेश चौधरी ने 32 रन देकर एक विकेट लिया था। श्रेयस गोपाल ने यहाँ पर 39 रन देकर तीन विकेट लिए थे और ऋतुराज गायकवाड 11 ने 20 ओवर में 226 रन 8 विकेट पर बनाए थे, बड़ा स्कोर बनाया था। MSD 11 जब टारगेट का यहाँ पर पीछा करने आई तो इनकी भी शुरुआत बेहतरीन रही थी जहाँ पर आयुष माथुर और सरफराज की बेहतरीन ओपनिंग जोड़ी थी। आयुष माथुर ने 45 रन 20 गेंदों में बनाए थे, सरफराज ने 40 गेंदों में 90 रन की पारी खेली थी। विस्फोटक ओपनिंग साझेदारी थी, जबकि यहाँ पर कार्तिक शर्मा नंबर तीन पर आये थे, 12 गेंदों में 30 रन इन्होने बनाए थे और एम एस धोनी ने यहाँ पर 45 रन 20 गेंदों में नाबाद पारी खेली थी, इसके साथ ही प्रशांत वीर भी 35 रन 16 गेंदों में बनाकर नाबाद रहे थे और 19.1 ओवर में 227 रन 5 विकेट पर बनाकर MSD 11 ने ये मुकाबला जीत लिया था जहाँ पर खलील अहमद ने 30 रन देकर दो विकेट लिए थे। राहुल चाहर ने 28 रन देकर चार विकेट लिए थे, इसके साथ ही इस मुकाबले की जो कम्पलीट 10 मिनट की हाईलाइट है वो हम टेलीग्राम पर डाल चुके हैं। बाकी टीमों की भी जो रोज़ इंट्रा-स्क्वाड प्रैक्टिस मुकाबले हो रहे हैं, सारी हाईलाइट्स टेलीग्राम पर आ रही हैं। टेलीग्राम पर लाइव मुकाबले भी आ रहे हैं तो आप फटाफट डिस्क्रिप्शन बॉक्स खोलकर टेलीग्राम चैनल को ज्वाइन कर लें, इसके साथ ही आप कमेंट करके बताइए आप कौन सी टीमों के आख़िर और इंट्रा-स्क्वाड प्रैक्टिस मुकाबलों की जानकारी चाहते हैं, आप कमेंट जरूर करें।

title: KKR 1st Practice Match 2026 Highlights & Analysis | Kolkata Knight Riders Practice Match 2026
transcription: KKR's first inter-squad practice match ki aap ko highlights bata dete hain kis bowler ne kis batsman ne achi performance dikhayi hai lekin us se pehle channel ko subscribe kar le. Viewers aaj first match khela gaya inter-squad between Purple Knights and Golden Knights. Purple Knights ki team ne second baari li aur jo Golden Knights ki team thi unhone pehle ballebazi ki. Yahan pe jo Golden Knights ki team thi usme sabse batting pehle karne aaye Tim Seifert aur Tim Seifert ke sath yahan pe jo they Rachin Ravindra vo batting ke taur pe opener aaye, unhone char runs score kiye lekin Seifert ne 30 runs score kiye in just 13 balls. Unki baari mein do chakke bhi shamil the. 200 above ka strike rate tha, to unki baari achi rahi. Aur unke baad aaye Sarthak Ranjan jinhone 37 runs score kiye. Quickfire, unki baari mein chakke chauke bhi shamil the. Hum aapko sath ke sath summary bhi dikha rahe hain aur uske baad Sarthak Ranjan ke baad batting karne ke liye aaye Tripathi jinhone 17 runs score kiye, teen chakke lagaye aur uske baad Tim Seifert dobara ballebazi karne aaye kyunki ye scenario-based matches hote hain lekin unhone dobara 17 runs ki baari hi li. And in the end phir Rinku Singh aaye jinhone 40 runs score kiye in just 25 balls aur unki baari mein do chakke bhi shamil the. So, ye Golden Knights ki baari thi jo ke simat gayi in 199, 20 runs mein. Aur yahan pe jo bowling department tha Purple Knights ka usme Vaibhav Arora ne just two wickets li aur uske ilawa Varun Chakaravarthy ne bhi do wickets li, jabke jo Tyagi hain unhone teen wickets li aur iske sath-sath Blessing Muzarabani ne one wicket li. Yahan pe aapko batate chalein to Varun ne 37 runs diye aur Blessing Muzarabani ne 30 runs diye in just three overs. Overall, ye ek achi bowling performance thi. Jab baari lene aayi second chasing side, yaani ke Purple Knights, to unme opening karne aaye Rahane aur Finn Allen. Finn Allen ne 23 runs of 11 runs score kiye, unki baari mein chakke chauke bhi shamil the lekin Rahane zyada kuch kar nahi sake, out ho gaye. Aur uske baad kahani likhne aa gaye Raghuvanshi jo ke ek up-coming young talent hain India ka, unhone 55 balls ka ek 100 jad diya, bahut hi achi baari kheli aur team ko chase karte hue jitwa diya, 19.4 over mein ye run chase kar diye. Raghuvanshi ke sath Manish Pandey bhi aaye jinhone kuch khatir khwah performance nahi di, unhone bhi 17 odd runs score kiye aur unke sath yahan pe jab batting karne aaye Anukul Roy to unhone bahut achi baari li aur unhone quick fire runs score kiye aur in the end jab Raghuvanshi ne team ko over the line kiya to vo vahan pe maujood the. To yahan pe overall inter-squad match ki kahani ye hai, 199 runs Golden Knights aur usko chase kar diya Purple Knights ne in 19.2. Umran Malik the samne aur Navdeep Saini jo ke officially announce ho jayenge maybe lagta hai humein as replacement for Harshit Rana, unke samne is Raghuvanshi young up-coming talent ne bahut acha perform kiya. title: Marco Rubio Rails Against 'Globalist Bureaucrats' At ICC And 'So-Called International Law'
transcription: For 250 years, Americans have governed ourselves as a free and sovereign people. We choose our own leaders, we determine our own laws, and when we're accused of a crime, we stand for judgment before a jury of our own peers. This is the essential and indispensable feature of our form of government. It is the foundation of our shared way of life. But today, powerful people in faraway places want to take that away from us. They believe that they should be in charge of your laws, of your country, your life, and they don't care whether or not you agree. Halfway across the world, there's an institution that calls itself the International Criminal Court. Maybe you've heard of it, maybe you haven't. But chances are you don't know the names of its judges, of its prosecutors, or its president, and you shouldn't have to. But as we speak, the ICC and its friends are waging a war against our country, not with bullets or missiles, but with statutes and compacts and the force of so-called international law. When the ICC was born 24 years ago, they told us that it was merely a narrow backstop, a global court that would step in to prosecute only the gravest offenses, things like genocide and war crimes, and only when a nation's courts were unable to prosecute them on their own. But the truth is, it was something far more radical and extreme. It was a global tribunal staffed by unelected globalist bureaucrats who claim their power is almost unlimited. The danger of this global court has only continued to grow. Today, it threatens every aspect of our political and legal system. Border patrol agents removing violent criminals from our country, American Marines risking their lives to defend our homeland, prosecutors working to dismantle terrorist plots to attack and kill Americans. If we stand idle, all of them would be at the mercy of foreign judges thousands of miles away, facing the constant risk of prosecution and even imprisonment for the so-called crime of defending their own country. The American people never agreed to any of this, and they never will. Read the words of our Declaration of Independence. We fought a revolution against a foreign power transporting us beyond seas to be tried for pretended offenses. Independence is our birthright. We will never let foreign bureaucrats take that away from us. This administration will not sit by as the ICC and its allies seek to threaten our people. If they believe they can deprive us of our sovereignty, we will teach them the full meaning of American resolve.

title: Highlights | Quantum USA
transcription: Quantum technologies are vitally important to economic prosperity and to national security. Over the next few years, the demand for quantum-literate professionals is going to outpace the supply, and that's something that, you know, we need an answer for. Post-quantum cryptography and the exercise of migrating towards that is far more complex than anyone really understood. It's far more than just switching algorithms. We need to iterate quickly, fail fast, get back up, build the muscle memory to continue to develop what we can with what we have. There are tremendous assets in the field of quantum technology, and what we need to do is better coordinate those by developing an operational strategy and then executing together. It's important to bring people together to discuss things forthrightly and transparently. We have differing opinions perhaps, but it's important to hear those differing opinions. We're thinking about these technologies in terms of a system, how they interconnect, how they relate to one another. We are also thinking about dual-use capabilities in order to accelerate market adoption. We need to bring in different teams with diverse perspectives because we need experts in quantum, we need experts in industry to build the use cases and create those bridges, and then we need people that know how to create that interconnection layer. Now we're dealing in a multi-domain environment, not only just across networking, security, and compute or cloud, but also across land, air, sea, and space. And so all the stakeholders that will ensure a right business or mission outcome need to be involved because it's not just about quantum as a compute, it's really about how we connect and protect that compute to deliver that mission or business outcome. There is a whole lot to be discovered, and now is the time. Collaboration across domain experts, quantum scientists, software developers, business leaders, research centers, I can keep going on and on. Now is the time to start thinking about that. I really think the biggest points for a quantum strategy right now is taking care of the organizational and human layers of this transition. We have so much untapped workforce full of potential who can help us accelerate the adoption of post-quantum cryptography and the quantum strategy overall. The United States is gaining increasing awareness that we need to do better and be thinking ahead about the dependencies we have in our supply chains, advanced R&D investments that are needed to continue advancing enabling technologies that are providing key components for quantum technologies, also growing our workforce to ensure that we can continue innovating at pace as these technologies come to fruition in the next 3 to 5 years. It's critical to get together the public and private sector: policymakers, standards developers, innovators, scientists, and the folks from the commercial world together to talk about the implications of these technologies, how we roll them out, and how we secure them. There's a lot of work, but it's going to be fun, and I'm excited to be a part of it. So thank you for having me.

Earlier, the general session celebrated the innovation already happening in counties across America, recognizing more than 1,800 achievement award-winning programs from over 140 counties and state associations. Proof that some of the country's most creative solutions are being developed at the local level. That spirit of innovation carried into the exhibit hall, where main stage presentations and common ground conversations connected county leaders with new technologies, fresh ideas, and peers tackling many of the same challenges back home. From celebrating what's working to exploring what's possible, day three was a reminder that the best ideas don't stay in one county, they spread. As the conference nears its end, the momentum continues, but the conversations and connections made here will last long after everyone heads home.

title: Highlights | 21st European Spectrum Management Conference
transcription:
It's so convenient to be at the Spectrum Conference this year because we just issued our MSS regulation proposal and that's of course also in the context of our digital networks act proposal and they have in common that they really have a different kind of approach on spectrum and satellites.

It's been a very interesting conference because people are preparing for the WRC-27 that is happening next year. So, the various positions on the key agenda items are being discussed. The fact that we have a variety of stakeholders enriches the discussion and makes us see the perspectives from the different sectors of the industry, which is very useful.

Reconnecting with people, the discussion face-to-face, talking to brilliant minds, and exchanging ideas. That is the real value.

Lots of discussions about the Digital Networks Act with visions from the Commission, from the Member States, from the stakeholders. Satellite, of course, is a key area. And for the broadcast community, I think we had a lot of presentations and discussions about 5G broadcast.

I think this year has been quite special for the 21st EU Spectrum Management Conference here in Brussels. Satellite has become one of the trendy topics, one of the most valuable topics also to discuss. And I think the key takeaway that I get is that we all agree on the objectives and the goals that we have. We want to connect everyone, we want to connect Europe and make Europe relevant again in the digital conversation. And for that, satellite is a key component of the ecosystem.

We need to be prepared for the improvements in EU regulation to foster competitiveness and to promote innovation in Europe. We need to be prepared for the WRC-27 and 31 in order to address the best positions for EU interests and we need to be prepared as well with our open mind to converge on the best approach for Europe.

Two things that these conferences are very good at: one is that they try to put together a neutral panel that encompass all the players, so that we can see the discussion from the various points of view, and the other one is the convening power of Forum Global that they can bring together everybody to discuss openly and not to push any agenda forward, so I'm very happy to participate in this kind of events.

title: RSAC 2026 Conference Quick Look: The Impact of Security Usability Challenges in Cloud Environments
transcription: Hi everyone, my name is Alex Sierra and on behalf of myself and Alex Pinto, my co-presenter, I want to talk to you about a session CLS W09: The Impact of Security Usability Challenges in Cloud Environments. The point of this talk is we're going to be looking at a dataset that involves security posture checks on a variety of cloud providers, especially the hyperscalers: AWS, Azure, GCP, and OCI (Oracle Cloud Infrastructure). And we're going to correlate the UX decisions that they have made in the way that users can set up infrastructure, can set up credentials, can set up storage, with security outcomes. We're going to see how much, and if and how much, the way that the cloud providers decided to design their UI and their architecture are leading users to make more or less security mistakes. We feel like this is important for cloud providers and for people designing systems in general to understand the impact of their user experience design in security. Plus, we provide a series of practical recommendations for organizations, for companies, in the way that they use those cloud providers to minimize the impacts that those UX decisions have on their security posture. Hope to see you all there.

I love how Alana Winnick invited her students on stage to share their experience. I've seen students present before, but they've never been such a big part of the conference. The next big takeaway is about immersive technologies. We're talking about AR, VR, MR, XR. You know, virtual reality was very big at one point, and then we start seeing augmented reality really take over in education, but it was really interesting to see how it's being used in practical ways. title: Kevin Baum - Next Generation in AI Research IJCAI-ECAI 2026
transcription: Hi, I'm Dr. Kevin Baum and I lead the research group for Responsible AI and Machine Ethics at the German Research Center for Artificial Intelligence. Being a philosopher and computer scientist, I work on a problem that sounds simple, but that might be one of the most important ones in our lifetimes. The alignment problem. Put simply, it is about getting AI to do what we want in ways we find acceptable. But that framing actually hides the hard part. We live in a pluralist society and we do not agree on what we want or on what counts as acceptable. So aligning AI with human values is more than a technical challenge, it's a sociotechnical one under deep normative uncertainty. At bottom of it, it's a political problem. Whose values, decided by whom, and why? My group works on that challenge from a philosophical and a computer science point of view. We build architectures that make AI reason explicitly about norms and values, resulting in normatively competent systems that can act for the right reasons, state those reasons, and let human challenge and refine them, and we ground all that in philosophical theory. Here's why it matters. AI systems are becoming agents, making decisions in hospitals, courtrooms, and classrooms. The answer is not smarter machines, it is normatively more competent ones. Doing the right things for the right reasons, guided by real humans and keeping responsibility where it belongs.

He introduces himself as Dr. Kevin Baum, a philosopher and computer scientist leading a research group in responsible AI and machine ethics. The speaker articulates the complexity of aligning AI with human values in a pluralistic society, framing it as a political and socio-technical challenge rather than just a technical one. He explains his group's work in building normatively competent systems that can reason about values and states that the goal is not just "smarter machines," but systems that act for the right reasons under human guidance. transcription: ...and then get the PET scan, get the MRI to rule out other causes. But most importantly, there is a specific test for Lewy body dementia where we actually do a synuclein, um, skin biopsy. So, we take a punch of skin from the back of the neck, and we stain it, and we look at it under a microscope, and we can actually see these alpha-synuclein proteins deposited within the skin. And if we see an elevation of these and a negative DaTscan—which the DaTscan is the diagnostic test for Parkinson's disease—we can now know that we're leaning much more to a, to a Lewy body dementia diagnosis, as opposed to the Parkinsonian features. Um, so again, cholinesterase, the, the memantine, they do help. We have to be careful though because treating Parkinson's when you don't have Parkinson's causes trouble in itself. We try to unfreeze muscles, so putting you on medication that you don't need is, is actually problematic. And again, you've got to avoid the atypical antipsychotics in Lewy body disease. The agitation, the hallucinations we see commonly in Alzheimer's and use medications such as Rexulti or, um, quetiapine, which is Seroquel, is actually contraindicated in Lewy body disease because it will actually make you worse. And then, the non-pharmacological, um, components: support sleep—people who don't sleep are more confused—um, physical, occupational therapy—if you're shuffling, if you're falling, we don't want to add to a problem. So, in summary, um, Alzheimer's disease: hippocampal-predominant neurodegeneration, we can see it on an MRI scan, we have treatments for this. Um, vascular dementia: cerebrovascular, um, injury, strokes—prevent the strokes, prevent dementia. Um, frontotemporal dementia is atrophy within the behavioral and language areas, so instead of looking for memory problems, look for behaviors, look for problems with speech. And then alpha-synuclein pathology within the Lewy body dementia: cognitive fluctuations and very early onset, um, hallucinations—that is, that is sort of the key factor. Um, dementia is not a normal part of aging. We don't have to get more forgetful as we get older. We get slower, it takes longer to recall a fact, it takes longer to, you know, come up with a solution, but dementia is not normal. And then early diagnosis is the cornerstone of treatment. At the moment, we cannot undo the damage that dementia has done. We can't undo the loss of memory. title: Beyond Physiology: Dr. Fearon Discusses CathWorks FFRangio's Robust Clinical Evidence
transcription: As you've also heard, uh, coronary physiology continues to be underutilized, and there's probably a number of reasons. It can take extra time, there are issues with the wire-handling characteristics, pressure drift, and other, uh, factors associated with the measurement can be frustrating. If you're measuring FFR, the side effects of adenosine, uh, it's expensive, and there is a small risk anytime you put a wire in a vessel. And as you can see, all of these issues are related to the need for a coronary pressure wire, as well as the use of hyperemic agent like adenosine. And so that raises the question, well, what if we could get all of this information just with the angiogram alone and no need of a pressure wire or adenosine? And that's where angiography-derived, uh, physiology comes into play. Now, six years ago, we published, uh, these data comparing, uh, FFR Angio to wire-based, uh, FFR in a blinded fashion, 10 centers, over 300 patients. And you see that there was a very high, uh, sensitivity, specificity, and accuracy, all above 90% with FFR Angio. And, well, what we found even more impressive was if you look at the gray zone or around the cut point of the FFR cutoff of 0.80, this is where most tests have a, uh, accuracy of 50%, kind of like a coin flip. You see that FFR Angio continued to have excellent diagnostic characteristics in that gray-zone area. We also looked at how FFR Angio compares with the non-hyperemic pressure ratios with regard to its correlation with, uh, wire-based FFR. And you see that the accuracy of FFR Angio was actually higher, uh, than the resting indices, uh, when compared with pressure-wire-based FFR. So, what data do we have with FFR Angio? Well, we have a real-world registry looking at the safety of deferring lesions in almost 900 patients, and showing a very low event rate, uh, at one year in those patients where PCI was deferred based on FFR Angio, so reassuring that you can safely defer if you get a negative FFR Angio. And we also now have randomized clinical trial data from Japan. 400 patients in the provisional trial across 13 Japanese sites looking at intermediate lesions. The primary endpoint of this study was non-inferiority of revascularization rate of FFR Angio compared with wire-based FFR. And the investigators met the primary endpoint. Uh, FFR Angio, uh, was non-inferior and had a similar, uh, revascularization rate. They also saw a significantly lower, uh, radiation exposure, 20% reduction with FFR Angio compared with wire-based. And they followed the patients now out to one year, and have shown that major adverse cardiac events, both with and without procedural MI, were, uh, equivalent, if not numerically lower, uh, with the FFR Angio group, so very reassuring data.

title: PulseCast: Highlights in Leukemias From the 2025 ASH Annual Meeting
transcription: Amir Fathi, a leukemia specialist at Massachusetts General Hospital in Boston, Massachusetts. I was fortunate to attend the American Society of Hematology meeting this last December in Orlando, Florida, where multiple presentations covering a series of topics in myeloid malignancies were provided. It was an exciting meeting. There were multiple exciting presentations. Among them, we presented the results of PARADIGM, a phase 2 randomized study that compared intensive induction chemotherapy to less intensive azacitidine and venetoclax in fit, traditionally induction-eligible patients. The study met its primary endpoint: event-free survival was better for patients who received azacitidine and venetoclax. There were also multiple secondary endpoints that were important. The rate of overall response, composite remission, was significantly higher in patients who received azacitidine and venetoclax. Patients who received azacitidine and venetoclax also tolerated treatment better, with less incidence, with lower incidence of grade 3 or higher bleeding or infectious complications, decreased time in the hospital, as well as decreased admission during their initial course to the intensive care unit. There was also better quality of life and better patient-reported outcomes. This opens the field to potentially introducing less intensive therapies for patients that are traditionally thought to receive intensive chemotherapy, the long-term standard of care in AML, which allows tolerability, safety, but also allows them to move on to curative modalities such as stem cell transplant. There was also a series of presentations on the combination of azacitidine and venetoclax and targeted therapies, such as gilteritinib, the FLT3 inhibitor, as well as multiple menin inhibitors, such as ziftomenib. These data, although early, show significant promise also in patients with acute myeloid leukemia. I look forward to future meetings and ongoing progress in myeloid malignancies. Thank you.

title: Terence Tao on How AI Is Changing Mathematics
transcription: I'm Terence Tao, I'm director of special projects here at IPAM, the Institute for Pure and Applied Mathematics. AI has really been, um, improving very rapidly. It allows me to experiment. I will try crazier things. We can vibe on the blackboard and then if there's a computation that neither of us wants to do, we can just get our AI tool to finish that. I can search literature much more accurately and effectively than I could before, so I'm doing way more AI-assisted mathematics and collaborative projects. And now, I think it's ready for prime time. Fundamentally, at OpenAI, we care about being at the frontier in terms of automating science, the economy, and ourselves. We care less about winning a Nobel Prize or a Fields Medal and more about enabling a hundred mathematicians out there to do that for themselves. We lived in a world of cognitive friction until very recently, where every task required us to use our brain. And so we didn't really think about it, we just thought this was the cost of doing something intellectual. But now we have AI and the other technologies that can bring these frictions down to zero. I hope when AI usage becomes more commonplace, people will also post not just their final product but all the different paths they used to get there, because that's also very useful information. transcription: My name is Prajval Moza, I'm a senior researcher at the DFKI in Kaiserslautern, Germany, and I finished my PhD last year in AI-driven image restoration as well as meta learning. And my research interest lies in teaching AI to reconstruct fine details that were never part of the image, and to do this as faithfully and efficiently as possible, and these might be blurry photos, medical scans, or even satellite images. And when AI fills in fine details that were never part of the image, then it can either stay true to reality or it can make stuff up that looks real but isn't. And in medical scans, this can mean a shape that was never part of a patient, or in natural science, it could mean a spot in a microscopic image that was never there. And my job is to keep those models honest and to tie what they add to the image so close to reality that we can actually trust what we see and not only hope it is right. Why does it matter? Well, more and more images we take nowadays is changed by AI, for instance, at the doctor, in climate sciences, in the news, or on your mobile phone even. And if we use those images to make decisions, truth has to come first, not only pretty. Um, that's what I'm working on, and thanks for stopping by, and thanks for listening.

title: Theo Vincent - Next Generation in AI Research IJCAI-ECAI 2026
transcription: Have you ever wondered if it is possible to reproduce human intelligence inside a computer? Hi everyone, I'm Théo Vincent, a PhD student at the German Research Center for AI, called the DFKI. Recent breakthroughs in generative AI are impressive, but they remain far from human intelligence, mainly because they are limited to imitating human data, and they rely on vast computational resources. My research tackles these challenges by developing algorithms that learn from experience. Learning from experience is the field of reinforcement learning, where a sequence of optimization problems needs to be solved. I proposed algorithms that solve those problems in parallel, thereby speeding up the learning process. This framework is called Iterated Temporal Difference Learning. Regarding resources, a lot of energy is spent tuning hyperparameters of learning agents. I proposed methods that adjust the agent's hyperparameters to its learning pace, thereby eliminating the need to tune hyperparameters and therefore saving resources. I'm excited about future learning algorithms that will learn from experience just as humans do. If you're interested, feel free to check my website.

title: How to Create a Journal System in Joplin | Quick Guide 2026
category: Mental Health Vlogs & Personal Video Diaries
transcription: In today's video, I'm going to teach you how to create a journal system in Joplin. Joplin is a fantastic open source note-taking app that offers a lot of flexibility and customization for keeping track of your thoughts, goals, and reflections. Whether you're an avid journaler or looking to start this beneficial habit, Joplin can help you organize your entries in a way that makes them easy to manage and review. Let's start by setting up your journal notebook. To begin, you'll need to open Joplin desktop. Once you have the application up and running, take a look at the left sidebar. You'll find a button labeled "New notebook." Go ahead and click on that. A prompt will appear asking you to enter a name for your new notebook. In this case, you should name it simply "Journal." Naming your notebook distinctly helps maintain clarity and keeps everything organized as your digital journal grows. Now that you have your journal notebook created, you can start thinking about how to organize your entries effectively. A well-structured journal system can provide insights and make reference easier over time. One effective way to structure your journal notebook is to create subnotebooks for different aspects of your journaling practice. To do this, look at the file above your journal notebook. There, you will see an option to create a "new subnotebook." For starters, you might want to create a subnotebook titled "Daily entries." This section will be where you jot down your thoughts and reflections every day. It's a space for freeform writing, capturing everything from daily events to personal reflections. Next, consider adding a subnotebook for "Weekly reviews." This section is great for reflecting on the week that just passed. It offers a valuable opportunity to see how your thoughts and experiences have evolved over the past seven days, and help set intentions for the following week. Finally, there's the "Monthly reviews" subnotebook. Monthly reviews are vital for looking at the bigger picture. They allow you to track longer-term goals and assess progress over time. Reflecting monthly provides a macro perspective of your life, habits, and achievements. When you envision this structure in Joplin, it might look like a tree, with "Journal" as the trunk, "Daily entries," "Weekly reviews," and "Monthly reviews" act as the branches extending from it, providing a clear pathway for your thoughts to spread. By organizing your journal in this manner, you create a harmonious and systematic approach that enhances your journaling practice. This customized structure caters to different aspects of life reflection, and makes it simpler for you to navigate through your thoughts and feelings. Once everything is set up, you can start using Joplin to capture your life's details, review your growth, and make journaling an enriching experience.
