title: History Buffs: The Odyssey Impressions
transcription: Hey, history buffs, it's Nick Hodges here. Now, I know my niche is reviewing historical movies and TV shows, but today, I'm going to make an exception. I just got back from Christopher Nolan's The Odyssey, arguably the most talked about movie of 2026. People were already divided on it before they'd even seen it. Well, now I have, and I'm going to answer the question everyone's asking: Is this a movie you're going to like? Well, that depends. How much do you care about Greek mythology, or more specifically, how much do you care about Homer's Odyssey? Do you expect this movie to follow that story beat for beat, and if it doesn't, how much is that going to bother you? Because if all you care about are the monsters, I can tell you right now you're getting the Cyclops, the Laestrygonians, the witch Circe, the Sirens, Scylla, and Charybdis. They're all there. Strangely, though, there are almost no gods. Okay, we're probably entering spoiler territory here, but if you don't mind minor spoilers, Odysseus never speaks to Hermes, Aeolus, or Poseidon. The only god he ever interacts with is Athena, and even she is presented more like a hallucination than an actual goddess. Which doesn't really make much sense to me because there's definitely magic in this movie. Circe genuinely turns Odysseus's men into pigs. Calypso's in the movie too, but she isn't a goddess. She's just a mortal woman who rescues Odysseus and feeds him lotus leaves. There's no temptation of immortality like there is in the original story. If you're wondering how Christopher Nolan handles the gods, the answer is he mostly doesn't. Poseidon never appears. The closest the film gets is, after the Cyclops is blinded, he cries out to Poseidon, and Odysseus's crew conclude that the Cyclops must be his son. That's about as explicit as it gets. And yet, a little later, Odysseus literally travels to Hades and speaks to the dead. Tiresias is there, his fallen comrades from Troy are there, so the afterlife is definitely real. But the Olympian gods? Apparently, that's where Christopher Nolan draws the line. Now, what are the monsters like in the movie? Well, to be honest, the Cyclops is really disappointing. He never talks to Odysseus and his men, he just walks into the cave, seals the entrance, eats a few of Odysseus's men, and then goes straight to sleep, not considering these tiny humans a threat at all. In the original story, it's much more interesting. Odysseus actually talks to the Cyclops, he gets him drunk on wine, and then blinds him while he's asleep. By cutting all of that out, Nolan's Cyclops just comes across as an idiot. I
caption: In this audio clip, a male speaker with a clear, expressive British accent, identifying himself as Nick Hodges from the channel "History Buffs," delivers an enthusiastic and critical review of Christopher Nolan's film "The Odyssey." The speaker discusses how the movie adapts Homer's classic epic, specifically highlighting the differences in the portrayal of mythological elements. He notes that while various monsters like the Cyclops, Circe, and Scylla are included, the film largely excludes the active participation of the Olympian gods, presenting Athena more as a hallucination. He contrasts the film's portrayal of Calypso as a mortal and points out the simplified, less interactive depiction of the Cyclops, which he finds disappointing compared to the original text. The review is set against an upbeat electronic background music track with occasional sound effects that complement his narration.

questions.answer: Nick Hodges, whose niche is reviewing historical movies and TV shows.

questions.answer: After the Cyclops is blinded, he cries out to Poseidon, leading Odysseus's crew to conclude that the Cyclops must be Poseidon's son.

questions.question: Which characters does Odysseus encounter and speak to when he travels to Hades (the afterlife) in the movie?
questions.answer: Tiresias and his fallen comrades from Troy.

title: PRESSURE | STAND-UP COMEDY BY SHARON VERMA
transcription: एक तो ये बाली की जो डिस्कनेक्टिंग फ्लाइट थी यार, SpiceJet... किया है अपनी सुरक्षा में ट्रैवल? आपको पता है आजकल, आजकल पायलट इसको चालू कैसे कर रहा है? मैं चढ़ी हूँ उस फ्लाइट में पहली बार मेरे साथ ऐसा हुआ है कि मेरे अराउंड पांच बुड्ढे बैठे हैं, ठीक है, फार्टिंग नॉनस्टॉप। बिना पासपोर्ट के जर्मनी गई हूँ मैं क्योंकि जो गैस चैम्बर बना दिया था, पायलट अनाउंसमेंट कर रहा है, "Currently we are facing some turbulence from the inside of the aircraft. अरे, राजेश जी, रुक जाइए।" एयर होस्टेस इन बुड्ढों को इंस्ट्रक्शंस दे रही है कि "ये इमरजेंसी एग्जिट है, इसको खुला ही रखेंगे।" वो सेफ्टी के लिए सीट बेल्ट लगा रहे हैं... कह रही है, "आप हमारी सेफ्टी के लिए मत लगाइए। सर, उसपे और प्रेशर मत डालिए।" पता है, इन बुड्ढों ने एकदम फार्टिंग का रिले रेस बना लिया था। एक का ख़तम हो रहा था, दूसरा बोलता है, "I'll take it from here." मैं आपको कैसे समझाऊँ, गाइज़, इस फ्लाइट में अगर अल-कायदा भी होता, वो भी अपने हाथ खड़े कर लेता यार और फिर नाक पे डालता। वो भी अपने सुपरवाइजर को कॉल कर रहा है, "हाईजैक करने आये थे, हॉस्टेज बनके रह गए हैं। सौ-दो सौ ज़्यादा ले ले, लैंड करा दे भाई, जान..." पता है, आप देखोगे, आपके अराउंड जब भी बुड्ढे बैठे हैं ना, तो आपको कभी कोई ज़रुरत ही नहीं पड़ेगी उनसे कुछ पूछने की। वो खुद ही अपना चिट्ठा आपको बताने लगते हैं। ऐसे कह रहे हैं, "बेटा, हम तो एयर फोर्स में काम किया करते थे।" अंकल, आप एयर फोर्स हैं। काम तो आप ज़बरदस्त कर रहे हो यार। अचानक से एक अंकल की तबियत बहुत ख़राब हो गई पीछे। ऐसा लग रहा है उनको हार्ट अटैक जैसा कुछ आ रहा है। तो पायलट कह रही है, "Any doctors? Any doctors, please come help." Next thing we heard, guys, was the absolutely worst thing we could have heard.

title: Trump v3.0 | The Most Viral Content Creator | StandUp Comedy by Rahul Dua | 2026
transcription: उसका थोड़ा विटामिन कम है। या उसका पोटैशियम ज़्यादा आया है, क्या चक्कर क्या है उसका? रोज़ सुबह कोई अजीब बात कर दे। है ना? ऐसे ही लगता है ना? है ना? यही तो आप रह गए। आप उसका विज़न ही शेयर कर पा रहे। आप लोगों को पर्सपेक्टिव बदलने की बहुत... देखो, I know the general sentiment is कि बहुत इरैटिक आदमी है, रोज़ सुबह उठ के नई फुद्दू बात करता है। मैं कह रहा हूँ कंसिस्टेंट देखो कितना है। रोज़ सुबह उठ के एक नए सिरे से एक नॉवेल, स्टेट ऑफ़ द आर्ट, फुद्दू बात सोचना। और फिर उसको करने का जिगरा रखना। आर्ट है, कला है ये। पूरी दुनिया का फ़न लगा के रखा है, उसके चक्कर में बिग बॉस की रेटिंग नहीं आ रही है। हाँ, हाँ! सही? आंटियां इंडिया में टाइम पे सो जा रही हैं। कि नींद पूरी कर लेते हैं, कल सुबह मज़ा आएगा। It is not easy being the President of United States, it becomes very lonely at the top. Poor guy is lonely. He is out there to make friends, दोस्त बनाने निकला है वो। अब... अगर रास्ते में कहीं थोड़ा बहुत तेल मिल रहा है... उसमें प्रॉब्लम क्या है? पर दोस्ती में कोई कॉम्प्रोमाइज नहीं देखो, बिल्कुल कोई, कोई फॉर्मेलिटी नहीं करता दोस्ती में। वेनेजुएला का प्रेसिडेंट बताओ निकर-ट्रैकसूट में उठा लाया है। ये रहे यार यहाँ आके। दिल का कितना साफ़ है। कितना जो दिल में है, ज़ुबां पे है। बीच में माइंड का कोई रोल ही नहीं है। आप देखो, अरे! यार नहीं, हेलो, एक सेकंड। माइंड का क्यूँ हो रोल भी, दिल... माइंड तो बाहर है। उसकी पीआर टीम... मर गई कह-कह के। कि नहीं-नहीं, वेनेजुएला वॉज़ इन अ स्टेट ऑफ़ अनरेस्ट, उनकी गवर्नमेंट उनके लिए काम नहीं कर रही थी, डिस्टर्ब स्टेट थी, इसलिए हमको इंटरवीन करना पड़ा। कह रहा है चुप हो जाओ बिल्कुल, झूठ नहीं बोलो अब तुम। भैया, मैं बताता हूँ, इनको नहीं पता। हम उनको वेनेजुएला तेल के लिए जाना था। हमारे हेयर फ़ॉल हो रहा है, रिसीड हो रही। सीधी बात करना है, बिल्कुल कुछ छल-कपट, छलावा कुछ है ही नहीं उस आदमी के पास। आधी बात बताता है। पूरी नहीं बताता। कि, "You have to figure the fuck out."

title: Science Marathons are BACK !!!!🔥| Prashant Kirad
transcription: इस साल वेक्टर क्वांटिटी पे क्वेश्चन आने के चांसेस 90% हैं और स्केलर पे आने के चांसेस? कौन है ये छोरा? सर, ये प्रशांत भैया हैं, छात्रों के मसीहा। इस मसीहा का क्वेश्चन पेपर तो मैं सेट करता हूं। बुलाओ इसको। ठीक है, सर। वरिष्ठ अधिकारी सौरभ कुमार ने पेपर लीक मामले में मशहूर एजुकेटर प्रशांत किरार को पूछताछ के लिए बुलाया है। सर, आप तो हाथ धोकर मेरे पीछे ही पड़ गए हो। पीछे नहीं पड़ता हूं मैं। एक्यूरेट ग्रेविटी से खींच लेता हूं, ऐसे। एक्यूरेट ग्रेविटी समझता है, इन्फ्लुएंसर? सर, आप नॉर्थ पोल पे टंगे रहते हो क्या? क्योंकि एक्यूरेट ग्रेविटी तो वहीं लगती है। तेरे ना नॉर्थ-साउथ का दक्षिण कर दूंगा मैं। दक्षिण समझता है, पेपर लीकर? लीक तो सर पानी होता है, पेपर तो बटते हैं। एग्जैक्टली। बंद कर ये पेपर बांटना, समझ गया? वरना ये sin cos theta की जगह धारा और अनुच्छेद पढ़ेगा तू, समझ गया? पढ़ लूंगा, सर। पढ़ना-पढ़ाना तो मेरे लिए सेवा है। हम्म, जिसकी आड़ में मेवा खा रहा है तू, पता है मुझे। सर, प्रशांत भैया ना करोड़ों की नौकरी छोड़कर... ए, रफ-रफ, कर। कैसे मायावती बाल रखे हैं तूने? हम्म? क्या, करता क्या है तू? पढ़ाता हूं, सर। मेहनत से, मोहब्बत से, शिद्दत से। मैं करता हूं स्टूडेंट्स का बैकलाग क्लियर। हम्म, बैकलाग क्लियर। ताकि ना रहे उनके एग्जाम में कोई भी फियर। ऑफ़ कोर्स। ये पेपर बांट के?
caption: This audio recording features four distinct male speakers and one female speaker conversing in Hindi, accompanied by dramatic instrumental music in the background. Initially, we hear a young man delivering a lecture on physics concepts. Shortly after, another man enquires about his identity, to which a third person replies that he is Prashant, a revered figure among students. The second speaker, identified as Officer Saurabh Kumar, then expresses his desire to meet him. This is followed by a female voice-over, resembling a news report, stating that the officer has summoned Prashant, an educator, for questioning in connection with a paper leak. The conversation then transitions to a tense exchange between Officer Saurabh and Prashant, where the officer accuses Prashant of leaking papers, while Prashant defends himself, stating that teaching is his service to students to help them clear their exams without fear. The audio ends with the sound of a vehicle engine revving up in the background.

questions.question: What physics topic is Prashant teaching at the very beginning of the audio, and what probability does he assign to it appearing in the exam?
questions.answer: He is teaching vector quantities ('vector quantity') and states there is a 90% chance of a question on it appearing in the exam.

questions.question: What title or status do the students use to introduce Prashant to the officer at the beginning of the clip?
questions.answer: They refer to him as 'chhatron ke masiha' (the messiah/savior of students).

questions.question: What scientific concept does Saurabh Kumar claim he uses to pull suspects in, and which geographical location does Prashant link to it?
questions.answer: Saurabh claims he pulls people in using 'accurate gravity,' and Prashant wittily responds by asking if Saurabh hangs around the 'North Pole' because that is where gravity is strongest/accurate.

questions.question: How does Prashant grammatically correct the officer regarding the accusation of 'leaking' exam papers?
questions.answer: Prashant states that water is what leaks ('leak toh paani hota hai'), whereas papers are distributed ('paper toh bat'te hain').

questions.question: Saurabh warns Prashant that he will have to study legal terms instead of trigonometry if he doesn't stop. What are the specific terms he contrasts?
questions.answer: He contrasts 'sin, cos, theta' (trigonometry) with 'dhara aur anuched' (sections and articles/clauses of the law).

questions.question: When Prashant claims that teaching is a form of service ('seva'), how does Saurabh mockingly counter his claim?
questions.answer: Saurabh counters by saying, 'Jiski aadh mein mewa kha raha hai tu, pata hai mujhe' (meaning Prashant is enjoying the rewards/benefits under the guise of service).

questions.question: What rhyming phrase does Prashant use to describe his educational goal for his students' exams?
questions.answer: He says he clears their 'backlog' so that there is no 'fear' in their exams ('backlog clear' rhyming with 'exam mein koi bhi fear').

questions.question: Describe the overall tone and delivery of the two main characters during their confrontation.
questions.answer: The tone is dramatic, tense, and highly sarcastic. Saurabh speaks with authoritative, mocking anger, trying to intimidate the suspect, while Prashant maintains a calm, confident, and witty attitude, effortlessly counter-arguing the officer's points.

title: HOW OUR INDIAN EDUCATION SYSTEM FAILED US | StandUp Comedy by Rahul Dua | 2026
transcription: मैं तो CBSE में पढ़ा हूँ right तो CBSE में 6th class में algebra हमारा introduce हुआ है तो हमारी class teacher maths पढाती थी वह अपना लगी हुई है। बच्चों से लेकर teacher तक किसी को X नहीं मिल रहा है। अपना लगी हुई है। तो मुझे समझ नहीं आ रहा है मेरे को ऐसा लग रहा है कि जब X मिल जाएगा बता देगी यह। तो मैं अपना अपने दोस्त से बात करनी शुरू, मैंने अब मैं बात करनी शुरू करी ही है, मैंने तो hello का 'है' बोला, 'है'। मेरे यहाँ आकर चौक बजा चौक। रविंद्र जडेजा ने मुझे खड़ा किया। मुझे मुझे मुझे मैडम ने खड़ा किया। मुझे खड़ा करके कहती, कहती, 'बात क्यों कर रहे हो?' मैने कहा 'बात क्यों कर रहे हो' का क्या मतलब है? बात इसलिए कर रहे हैं क्योंकि man is a social animal. बिना बात किए उससे रहा नहीं जाता, societal construct है यह। यह अभी तो पढ़ाया मैडम moral science में। मैम however obviously in absolutely no mood for any sort of explanation, मैडम ने मुझे 5 मिनट पूरी class के सामने अच्छे से झाड़ा है जो है। और 5 मिनट डांटने के बाद मुझसे कह रही, 'You have wasted 5 minutes. There are 60 students in the class. You have in total wasted 300 minutes.' मैने कहा 'मैम, मैम, time has been wasted in parallel. Not in series. मैम, you have disturbed 60 students. I was at max going to disturb one. That too for 5 seconds only. ओए टिफिन बचा है? नहीं बचा, ओहो that's it.' तो मैम, maths भी ख़राब है, logic भी ख़राब है आपका। और moral science के तो हाल हम देख ही लिए हैं। Zero civic sense. I believe that the Indian schooling system is horrible. या तो गलत पढ़ा रहे हैं या unnecessary पढ़ा रहे हैं। English हमें गलत पढ़ाई हुई। अंग्रेजी मुहावरे आधे अधूरे पढ़ा के छोड़ रखे हैं। I recently got to know that 'Jack of all master of none' is an incomplete proverb.

title: EVERYTHING You Need To Know About The New WEGOVY PILL
transcription: It's 6:20 in the morning. You're half awake. Your brain is chanting one word: coffee. Now, plot twist: your new weight loss pill looks you in the soul and says, "Not yet. We need 30 minutes alone with water." Welcome to 2026 where Wegovy is now a tablet, needle-free, but it's not rule-free. Today, we're doing the great trade: the weekly shot versus the daily pill. Not which one is better online, which one fits real humans with real mornings and real habits. Quick note: this is education, not personal medical advice. Talk with your clinician before starting or switching any GLP-1 medication. And one more thing, as an obesity medicine doctor, most of my patients have been successful with weight loss by simply going low-carb, keto, or carnivore, but the reality is there are some people who need help, and that's why I made this video. All right, five rounds, scoreboard style, and I'll drop lesser-known facts that most influencers won't mention. Fast, clear, and practical for you. Round one, let's talk about convenience. Weekly shot: once a week, any time of day, with or without meals. Daily pill: once a day, but it comes with terms and conditions. title: How Jumping Rope Changes the Human Body.
transcription: The 5-minute jump rope will help you burn fat, create strong and powerful legs, and have you feeling younger than you actually are. This jump rope right here cost me about $5 on Amazon. Cheap, simple tools can have the greatest effect on your body. There's a study that shows jump rope is just as good at improving cardiovascular fitness as running. I am not here to argue that jump rope is any better than running, but there are some unique benefits to jump rope. Number one, you can plainly see on the screen right now. I can't go jogging down the street leaving my boys here to fend for themselves, but I can get 5 to 10 minutes of jump rope in while they play on their scooters around me. It can be the non-runner or parents' weapon to getting into incredible shape in the comfort of your backyard. Now, I assume that jumping rope originated with boxing, but that was only when it was popularized in America. Jump rope started as a fun game for kids way back in ancient Egypt, China, and Greece and Rome. It was brought to America by the Dutch, and eventually turned into an exercise that athletes, especially boxers, still utilize today. Why? Well, it comes down to one quality: rhythm. Boxers have found that the rhythmic, quick feet required to jump rope translates great to their sport. This is a lost quality in modern-day fitness. Many people sit on machines, lay on benches, losing that rhythmic quality that most of us had when we were younger. Here's a few things you probably didn't know about rhythm. Number one is that our brains crave it. It's why we love music. It's why dancers are the most embodied athletes. Rhythmic movement increases coordination, triggers the parasympathetic nervous system, and even increases heart rate variability. Rhythm, combined with bouncing on your feet, strengthens the vestibular system. This improves balance, coordination, and spatial awareness, all things that we slowly lose as we age. And a benefit that you won't find listed on Google is that all these qualities combined result in somewhat of a natural high. And the more competent you become with the rope, the more you experience these elevated feelings. But we also lose muscle and bone density as we age, and the less that we physically train, the easier it is to deteriorate. Most people know to do some resistance training and some cardio, but 90-something percent of the population are missing out on the benefits of plyometrics. Plyometrics are quick, explosive movements that involve lengthening the muscle and then quickly shortening it. And every time you land and rebound, it's three times your body weight in that moment. This has incredible effects on strengthening muscles, connective tissue, and bones. It's a quality that can literally keep you younger, and I think jump rope is the easiest way to safely maintain it. These small doses of impact result in a very strong frame. Skipping rope strengthens your whole lower body structure, and specifically your quads, glutes, and calves. You develop legs that are good at being active, translating well to activities like hiking, cycling, and running. And ask any orthopedic doctor. transcription: नमस्कार, मैं हूँ डॉ श्वेता आड़ात्या लिमिटलेस ब्रेन लैब से। तो आज हम बहुत ही एक सीक्रेट पे बात करते हैं। अगर आप दो या तीन मिनट में सोना चाहते हैं जो कि एक बहुत बहुत बहुत इंपॉर्टेंट सी प्रॉब्लम चल रही है। इतनी बड़ी मुश्किल हो चुकी है इंसोम्निया, यानी की नहीं सोने का प्रॉब्लम। सो बहुत सारे लोग ये प्रॉब्लम में है और अगर आप मॉनिटर करते हैं, चाहे वूप से मॉनिटर करते हो, ओरा रिंग से मॉनिटर करते हो, यूम से करते हो, कोई भी ऐसी मोडालिटी से मेजर करते हो और आप देखते हैं कि आपको डीप स्लीप जो है वो अच्छे से नहीं आ रही है, देन दिस इज़ द ट्रिक व्हिच विल वर्क फॉर यू। ये एक ऐसी ट्रिक है जिसमें ये केवल दो चीजें करने से मात्र से, मेरे पर्सनल पेशेंट्स में बहुत बहुत बहुत चेंजेस आए हैं। मेरे पर्सनली पेशेंट्स ने भी ये अनुभव किया है, मेरे रिलेटिव्स ने अनुभव किया है, मेरे फ्रेंड्स ने अनुभव किया है, तो ये एक एक्सपीरिएंशियल चीज है, जरूर करके देखिएगा। इसमें सोने से पहले आपको दो चीजें करनी होगी। सो सोने से पहले की बात आई एम श्योर स्लीप की बहुत सारी टॉक्स आपने सुनी होंगी कि अंधेरा होना चाहिए, कोल्ड थोड़ा सा टेंपरेचर होना चाहिए, वेटेड ब्लैंकेट, जो आप चादर ओढ़ते हो वो पतली नहीं, मोटी सी होनी चाहिए, कामिंग के लिए 15 से 20 मिनट तक कम से कम लाइट का एक्सपोजर, ब्लू लाइट वगैरह नहीं होना चाहिए, या तो आप फोन में फिल्टर्स फिट कर सकते हो, रीडिंग कर सकते हो, कोई भी ऐसी चीज करें जहां पर आपको एक्स्ट्रा लाइट का एक्सपोजर ना हो, अंधेरा बिल्कुल डार्क रखें, कोई भी एक्सरसाइज, एक्टिविटी, कैफ़ीन, स्टिमुलेंट्स ऐसी कोई भी चीज ना करें कम से कम दो घंटे तक। तीन या चार घंटे की दूरी रखे आपके लास्ट मील और सोने पे। ये सारा कुछ तो 100% आपने सुना होगा और कई सारे ऐसे लोग होंगे आप में से जिन्होंने ये सब कुछ कर भी लिया होगा लेकिन नींद जो है अभी नहीं आती है। सो पहले तो ये समझते हैं कि नींद नहीं आना 40 टू 45% में, यस, बहुत ही बड़ा नंबर है, 40 टू 45% में ये जेनेटिक हो सकता है। तो आपके पूर्वज, आपके जो मां बाप हैं, आपके वालिद हैं, वो नहीं सो पाते हैं इसकी वजह से भी आपको नींद नहीं आती है। सेकंड थिंग इस देयर इस एंग्जायटी, फीयर, वरी कुछ ना कुछ चलते रहता है दिमाग में उसकी वजह से नींद का प्रॉब्लम हो सकता है। अब आपको करना क्या है? आपको बेसिकली दो ही चीजों पर ध्यान देनी है और लास्ट तक सुनिएगा बिकॉज़ दिस इस वैरी इंपोर्टेंट, ये जो टेक्निक है ये कहीं पे भी टेक्स्ट बुक में नहीं मिलेगी, ये एक प्रैक्टिकल टेक्निक है जो कई साल पहले मेरे प्रोफेसर ने मुझे सुनाई थी और आज भी मैं कई पेशेंट्स को ये देती हूँ और उनको काफी बेनिफिट हुआ है इस चीज से। तो ये एक बहुत पुरानी यौगिक टेक्निक है, यौगिक पद्धति है। सबसे पहली चीज इसको जानने के लिए आपको भ्रामरी यानी की हमिंग बी की टेक्निक आना बहुत जरूरी है।

title: Claude AI Tutorial for Beginners (Step-by-Step)
transcription: In this video, I will show you exactly how to use Claude AI step-by-step. Claude is an AI assistant that helps you write, analyze information, and create things you can actually use. I'm Kevin, and we'll start with the basics, like writing, summarizing information, and working with files. Then, we'll move on to more powerful features like artifacts, projects, connectors, and skills. By the end, you'll know how to use Claude to actually get work done, not just chat with it. Let's get started. First, head to the Claude website. You'll find a link right here at the bottom of the screen, and then sign in. It's completely free to get started. Once you're in, this is the main screen where all your conversations happen. Here, in the middle, you'll see the prompt box. This is where you type what you want Claude to do. Over on the left-hand side, you have what's called the sidebar. From here, you can start a new chat, you can also access more advanced features, and down here at the bottom, you can also view your recent chats so you can always come back to your work. Let's start with something simple. I'll ask Claude to write a professional email. Then, right over here, let's run that. Here, you can see Claude created a full, professional email with structure. We even have some bullet points and all the details we would need to send this to a supplier. Now, in most cases, this is already pretty good. But I didn't actually specify the type of cookie. Here, it looks like it assumes it's chocolate chips since that is the most popular type of cookie, although I had oatmeal raisin in mind. I don't have to start over if it's not perfect. Instead, I can refine it. Down below, I'll type in a prompt to modify this email so it's for oatmeal raisin cookies instead, and then let's run that. Right up on top, we can now see the updated email message, and down below, we can see a summary of all the different changes that it made. And, of course, I could keep going from here. I could ask it to make the email shorter, maybe make it more friendly, or just give it more context like let's say who the email is for or maybe what tone I want. This back and forth is really how you get the best results.

His voice is clear, friendly, and enthusiastic, with a well-paced delivery suitable for instructional content. There is no background noise, resulting in a crisp and clean audio experience. Kevin begins by explaining Claude's capabilities and outlining the tutorial's progression from basic to advanced features. He then walks the listener through signing in and navigating the main interface, describing the prompt box and sidebar. Finally, he demonstrates a practical example: generating a professional email, and then refining the prompt to specify "oatmeal raisin" cookies instead of the default "chocolate chip," illustrating how to interactively improve the AI's output.

title: Give me 5 minutes. I'll Fix your Hips. (5 simple steps)
transcription: The ground will rewild your body back to its natural form. It's simple, free, and a better teacher than any mobility coach or influencer's flexibility plan. People have been using it for thousands of years. Here's how you can free your body for no cost and just a little effort. Katie Bowman is a renowned biomechanist who's literally wrote the book on natural movement. She's a proponent of using the connection to our natural environment to bring back our mobility. She uses this cool analogy of orca whales in captivity. Their dorsal fin starts to collapse because it lacks the natural forces of the ocean. Wild orcas do not collapse. Aren't humans the same? We need the natural forces of gravity and the ground. Soft chairs and couches give us less feedback and we become stiff. Ironically, the hard ground keeps our body softer and more pliable. Sitting cross-legged on the ground, just like when we were kids, can start to restore natural levels of hip and spine mobility. I mean, look no further than yogis, the most flexible people in the world, who spend hours sitting cross-legged in meditation. Back in 2015, I was stiff as a board. I read Katie's Move Your DNA and I started to do some computer work sitting on the ground. It didn't happen overnight, but my hips were gradually restored from all of the heavy lifting and hours of chair sitting I put them through. You can do the same. Start with using a pillow under your hips to make it more comfortable, especially if you're stiff. Just a few minutes at first, and then gradually up the time and work it into your life like I did. Kneeling on the ground with the feet flat against the floor is an ancient Japanese position used by samurai warriors. It's been used for meditation, tea ceremonies, and simply having a meal. This position starts to loosen the ankles, knees, and hips, and fully bending the knees becomes lost to many older folks. This position ensures you keep it. The feet and ankles become rigid as we age because of soft shoes and repetitive movements. This position keeps them soft and pliable, but to heels was too much for my 2015 body. I started with a prop to raise my hips slightly. Start with 30 seconds here, then reach 1 minute. Then turn it into a habit throughout your day. Changing the foot position takes this position even further. When the toes extend, we strengthen the first ray and this is our connection to the ground. This influences the way that we walk and move and working on this often restores the plantar fascia on the bottom of the foot. It also improves dorsiflexion, the ankle's ability to bend forward. Toes extended is way more intense. Start with a few sets of 10 seconds and you can also explore reps like I'm doing here. You'll be surprised at how restoring the hips, feet, and ankles with those first three positions naturally leads you to a more relaxed deep squat. We've talked so much about deep resting squats here. I'll just hit the main benefits. Restore hip and ankle mobility, improve diaphragmatic breathing and digestion, decompress spine after sitting or standing for a while. The squat is much more than an exercise, it's a natural human position used for rest, play, and function. Spending time here daily is almost a non-negotiable. title: Dhurandhar Film Joke | Stand-up Comedy Clip| Ft. Amit Maharana Saini
transcription: धुरंधर देखी है आप लोगों ने? हाँ लगभग सभी ने, हाँ ठीक करा देख ली। मैंने भी देखी थी, इतना झूठ दिखा रखा ना उस पिक्चर में भाई। सही में शुरू में तो मुझे पता ही नहीं चला था। मैंने देख ली थी ऐसी ही, कि चार-पांच एक्टर हैं तो बढ़िया ही होगी पिक्चर और बढ़िया लगी मुझे। पर फिर एक दिन ऐसा हुआ, मेरा एक दोस्त है, नदीम उसने मुझे ध्रुव राठी की वीडियो भेजी और मुझे फ़ोन करके कह रहा, अबे वीडियो देख जो मैंने भेजी तुझे है। वो तो एक प्रोपेगैंडा फिल्म है, कुछ भी सच नहीं दिखा रखा उसमें। मैंने कहा सच नहीं दिखा रखा? तो भाई मैंने देखी वो जर्मन सिटीजन की वीडियो। वो खुद झूठ बोल रहा है उसमें। कह रहा बर्फ में कत्लेआम दिखा रखा बर्फ में, भाई पूरी पिक्चर में एक भी सीन बर्फ में लड़ाई का नहीं है। बर्फ वो सिर्फ गिलास में डाल रहे, और कहीं बर्फ नहीं और ये मुझे फ़ोन करके कह रहा तुम्हारा तो कोई भी काट देता है अंधभक्तों। मैंने कहा भाई इसमें काटने वाली क्या बात है, हमें तो बढ़िया लगी पिक्चर और रही बात काटने की तो सुन भाई नदीम। देख हमारा तो बचपन में नहीं कटा अब तो क्या ही कटेगा। नहीं कुछ बच्चों के साथ होता है स्कैम ये। देख वो रही चिड़िया, वो रही, वो रही, वो रही, ए उड़ गई, उड़ गई, नीचे साँप। अरे! भाई तुम समझ नहीं रहे। देखो दो साल का बच्चा है छोटा सा, उसके हाथ में डेढ़ लाख का मोबाइल है महंगा मोबाइल है ३०-३५ हज़ार की सिर्फ डिस्प्ले है। अब उसके हाथ से लेना हो गिरा ना दे तो क्या करना पड़ेगा? तब चिड़िया ही काम आती है। हाँ, तुम कहीं और पहुँच गए थे। पर फिर भी मुझे बुरा लगा यार कि मैं कैसे नहीं पकड़ पाया वो झूठ। तो मैंने दुबारा पिक्चर देखी वो। कितना झूठ दिखा रखा भाई आदित्य धर ने उसमें। पाकिस्तान में गलत दिखा दिया बताओ डांस। पाकिस्तान में! हैं? और वहाँ पे वो गार्ड रणवीर सिंह को रोक के बोलता है अन्दर सिर्फ कपल की एंट्री है।

title: UNESCO Video Message | Youth Summit & Conference 2026 | Colombo, Sri Lanka
transcription: Good morning to all distinguished guests, experts, policymakers, and especially the young leaders gathered in Colombo. It is a privilege to join you for the Grace Island Environmental and Marine Conservation Summit 2026. I would like to extend my sincere congratulations to Grace Island and the Kolkata Society for Cultural Heritage for creating a platform that brings together stakeholders from across South Asia to confront our shared environmental challenges in a spirit of cooperation and urgency. Sri Lanka has a coastline of approximately 1,340 kilometers, a striking natural asset for a small island nation. This extensive coastline supports rich biodiversity, fisheries, and coastal livelihoods, but it also places the country at the forefront of climate change impact, such as sea-level rise, erosion, and marine pollution. These coastlines and marine and coastal ecosystems are not only of immense value for heritage conservation, but also play a vital role in fisheries, tourism, and a wide range of socioeconomic activities that sustain communities and contribute significantly to national development. Sri Lanka also holds at least 88 square kilometers of mangrove ecosystems, which are among the most important blue carbon habitats in the region. These mangroves play a vital role in storing carbon, protecting shorelines from erosion, and serving as nurseries for marine biodiversity. Sri Lanka's marine and coastal ecosystems are among its most valuable natural assets. They sustain livelihoods, protect biodiversity, and support national resilience. Yet, these ecosystems, like in most other places in the world, are undergoing pressure from climate change, pollution, and the ongoing degradation of critical habitats. Meeting these challenges demands more than awareness, and it requires coordinated, science-based action at every level.

title: Ryan Short | Keynote Speaker on Place Branding | CivicBrand
transcription: There's this Latin phrase, probably won't say it right, but I think it's "esse quam videri." It means "to be rather than to seem." Said by Cicero a long time ago. In 1893, North Carolina made it part of their seal and their motto. And I think the spirit of it is hopefully pretty obvious, but it's like, it's not something you say. It's something that you do, right? If you say you're about something, it should show up in your, your policies and your budgets and your actions, not just your marketing campaigns and the words that you say. I was talking to director of Arts and Culture Department for a city, and they, he, they had done a council workshop. It's kind of day-long thing where they're going to, you know, like councils do. The whole first half of the day, budget cuts. What are we cutting? Public art, zero. His department just got gutted, ripped apart, everything. "Where can we cut? Where can we cut? Where can we cut?" to where he's like, "I don't even have anything left to cut." Because there's, there's important stuff: fire, safety, public safety, like real things that like, we can't cut those things, so we're going to cut the art and the culture and some of these things first, right? These are the nice-to-have things, and times are tough, nobody wants to do it, but we got to be adults. We got to, you know, make the hard choices. And people get that. I think smart people get that. But then at the close of the council workshop, "Let's end on a positive note. Budget talk wasn't fun. Let's have a new mission statement, vision statement for the city." They kind of brainstormed ideas. What are we all about? Art and culture was front and center. "This is what we're about: art and culture." And he stood up, he's like, "Are you kidding me? We just spent the whole day gutting arts and culture, our reality, to then just go put it on a little poster and say, 'We're about arts and culture.' That is the opposite of "to be rather than to seem." That is, we want to seem like we're about arts and culture, but we're not really about arts and culture.

title: Minimizing Tech Turnover in Conferences & Festivals | Cut E-Waste, Reuse Gear & Recycle Responsibly
transcription: Welcome. Today we're exploring how conferences and festivals can minimize technology turnover, reducing costs, extending equipment life, and supporting sustainability across every stage of event design and production. Today's events rely heavily on technology, from digital signage to mobile apps to interactive displays, all designed to elevate audience engagement. But rapid upgrading cycles push many devices out of service long before the end of their usable life. This constant replacement adds financial pressure, creating higher purchasing, storage, and transport costs. With smarter planning, events can maintain quality while utilizing existing equipment more efficiently and sustainably. Tech turnover often stems from a desire to impress with the newest gear, even when older equipment is still functional. This perception-driven cycle leads to high volumes of discarded tablets, displays, LED panels, and networking devices. Replacing equipment too frequently strains event budgets and contributes to growing e-waste streams. Each discarded device contains materials that require proper disposal through licensed recyclers to avoid environmental harm. Strong inventory management helps reduce unnecessary replacements. By keeping accurate records of equipment age, usage, and condition, event teams can clearly determine when upgrades are truly needed. Asset management systems allow devices to be rotated across multiple events, extending their lifespan. These tools also reveal when a piece of equipment can be repaired or refurbished instead of being replaced outright. With better visibility, purchasing decisions become smarter, more cost-effective, and more sustainable. Modular equipment is one of the most valuable strategies for reducing turnover. Interchangeable components allow lighting, audio boards, and AV systems to be repaired easily without replacing entire devices. Firmware upgrades can also extend the useful life of older equipment. Interoperability ensures older and newer devices function together, preventing unnecessary full system upgrades. Planning for modularity reduces both long-term costs and the environmental footprint of constant tech replacement. Not every event requires brand-new technology. Many attendees care far more about meaningful content and clear audiovisual output than the generation of the device being used.

title: International Women’s Day 2026 Theme | Rights. Justice. Action. | Give To Gain | UN Women
transcription: As we stand in the second quarter of the 21st century, women are still not equal before the law. Not in 1926, not in 1976, and still not in 2026. Today is not a celebration. Today is not about flowers, slogans, or hashtags. Today is about power and who has it and who still does not. As we stand in the second quarter of the 21st century, with advanced technology, global institutions, and centuries of progress behind us, one truth remains deeply uncomfortable. Women are still not equal before the law. Not in 1926, not in 1976, and still not in 2026. Right now, in 2026, women hold only 64% of the legal rights that men hold worldwide. 64%. This is not a statistic from the past. This is not history. This is now. If progress continues at the current pace, it will take 286 years to close the legal protection gaps between women and men. 286 years. That is not a timeline, that is surrender. In no country on earth have women and men achieved full legal equality, not one. Across fundamental areas of life: work, money, safety, family, property, mobility, business, healthcare, and retirement, the law continues to systematically disadvantage women. And where the law fails women, justice fails women. Every year, 12 million girls are pushed into early or child marriage. Not because they lack potential, but because the law allows it, because systems look away, because justice is denied before life even begins. Each number is a stolen future, each statistic is a silenced voice, each delay is a decision. The Universal Declaration of Human Rights states

title: Shettima Urges Governors on Economic Growth | Senate Approves E-Transmission | 2026
transcription: This is Megastar Magazine TV. Hello and welcome to Megastar Magazine TV. My name is Monique Agbey. In the news, Vice President Kashim Shettima urged governors of the 36 states, ministers, and other public officials to pursue an inclusive economic growth model that filters down to the everyday lives of Nigerians. Shettima spoke in Abuja while delivering the keynote address at the opening of the National Economic Council, NEC, conference, a two-day retreat of governors and key stakeholders aimed at strengthening national economic coordination and accelerating inclusive growth. The Vice President warned that the government's mission would remain incomplete if progress does not translate into dignity, opportunity, and hope for citizens across the country. The Senate has approved the electronic transmission of election results to the Independent National Electoral Commission's results viewing portal, while permitting manual collation to serve as a backup where technology fails. The decision followed a reconsideration of a disputed clause in the Electoral Act Amendment Bill during an emergency plenary on Tuesday. The upper chamber stopped short of making electronic transmission compulsory and also rejected the provision for real-time upload of results. Under the reviewed section, presiding officers at polling units are to electronically transmit results to the IReV portal after voting and documentations are completed. The amendment, however, provides that where electronic transmission cannot be carried out due to communication or network challenges, the manual results sheet, form EC8A, will become the primary basis for collation and declaration. The Court of Appeal sitting in Abuja held that the Senate acted within its powers when it suspended the lawmaker representing Kogi Central, Senator Natasha Akpoti-Uduaghan, for misconduct. The court held that the suspension did not violate the senator's parliamentary privileges or her constitutional rights. The court set aside the contempt proceedings and the 5 million Naira fine earlier imposed on the lawmaker over an unprofessional apology she directed at Senate President, Godswill Akpabio.

title: Archaea are Highly Prevalent in the Small Intestine
transcription:
My name is Maria Jesus Villanueva Millan and I am project scientist at MAST program, and I am presenting a poster at DDW 2022, which is entitled "Archaea are highly prevalent in the human small intestine and the absolute abundance of Methanobrevibacter is associated with older age and greater microbial diversity."

Archaea are part of the microbiomes, but once they were underestimated. But now we know that they have beneficial and detrimental properties. For example, Methanobrevibacter smithii is associated with constipation and obesity, but also appears in more abundance in centenarians. Most of the studies are focus on stool, but we want to do this study to know what happens in the small intestine. And also, we wanted to use absolute abundance to have a real idea of the potential biological impact of these microorganisms.

To achieve this, we collected duodenal aspirates from human subjects that were in the REIMAGINE study. And these subjects underwent EGD without colon prep. Once we got these duodenal aspirates, we extract the DNA and do shotgun sequencing, and then we calculated the absolute abundance of these microorganisms, the archaea, in the human small intestine.

343 subjects were analyzed in this study, and one of the main results were that the most prevalent and abundant archaeal phyla were the phyla Methanobacteriota and Thermoproteota. And about the genera, what we saw is that the the genus Halorubrum and Methanobrevibacter were the most prevalent and abundant. And when we wanted to see the abundance

title: Why We Will Never "Cure" Cancer
transcription: In 1971, Richard Nixon signed the National Cancer Act and declared war on cancer. The language was deliberate: a war with a target date, the way you'd talk about landing on the moon. 55 years later, cancer still kills about 10 million people a year worldwide. We didn't lose that war through lack of funding. The United States alone has poured well over $100 billion into cancer research since that signature. We lost it because the enemy was never a single enemy. That's the part the fundraising campaigns skip. Cancer isn't a disease. It's a category closer to infection than flu. Breast cancer alone splits into at least four molecularly distinct diseases that happen to grow in the same organ. Lung cancer, pancreatic cancer, leukemia: different biology, different mutations, different behavior, filed under one word because they share a symptom: cells that won't stop dividing. Asking for a cure for cancer is a little like asking for a cure for infection. Which infection? Which mechanism? Which host? Point one: The enemy evolves faster than you can aim. Here's the detail oncologists live with and rarely get to explain on camera: a tumor isn't one clone of identical cells. Peter Nowell described this back in 1976 in a paper called "The Clonal Evolution of Tumor Cell Populations," and the idea has only gotten scarier with better sequencing. A single tumor is a population: genetically diverse, competing internally, mutating with every division. Give it a drug, and you're not killing the tumor. You're running a selection experiment. The cells sensitive to the drug die. The handful that happened to carry a resistance mutation before treatment even started now have the whole tumor to themselves, no competition left. Six months later, the cancer comes back, and it comes back immune to the exact drug that shrank it. This is why remission and cure are different words. Oncologists know the difference intimately.

title: Multi-Objective Evolutionary Design of Molecules with Enhanced Nonlinear Optical Properties
transcription: Hi, my name is Gamrich, and I'm here to talk about our GECCO project called the Multi-objective Evolutionary Design of Molecules with Enhanced Non-linear Optical Properties. So, NLO materials are essential for mainly telecommunications infrastructure, and we look at specifically the device called an electro-optic modulator, which modulates a beam of light. So, we're looking at NSGA-II, MAP-Elites, MoAM, mu-lambda, and then simulated annealing. So, a mix of QD and multi-objective optimization algorithms, and then some single-objective ones. How we encode molecules is using SMILES. We limit our molecular search space to organic atoms, and we employ these seven mutation operators, and we do not use crossover in our evolution. And you can see how symbols are used to encode molecules. We evaluate the properties which we're optimizing using quantum chemistry, and specifically the Hartree-Fock level of theory with the PySCF library. So, our multi-objective algorithms maximize the beta over gamma ratio, which is important for frequency conversion. We target a range of 100 to 500 atomic units for linear polarizability. Our HOMO-LUMO gap, we target a range of 2 to 4 electron volts. And then our energy per atom, we try to minimize, and this promotes stability in the molecule. And then our single-objective algorithms simply optimize the beta-gamma ratio. So, each algorithm evaluates approximately 2,000 molecules across 20 independent seeds. Our main metric for performance here is the global hypervolume. As you can see, we have two variations of each of the QD algorithms. We have an F and a C. That simply means fine and coarse-grained binning. So, the F is fine, C is coarse. And that's because we have a 10-by-10 and a 20-by-20 archive based on the atom count and the bond count, which the atoms range from 5 to 30 and the bonds from 4 to 32. So, the MoAM with the fine-grain binning, so MoAM F, does the best in our global hypervolume, and you can also see in the final Pareto fronts here.

title: What Brings Matter to Life? — A Physics of Life Film
transcription: For over a century, physicists have pushed the boundaries of our understanding, revealing the hidden structures of the world around us. Through these discoveries, we've unlocked the secrets of the tiniest particles and mapped the far reaches of the cosmos. And yet, physics holds a mystery that remains unsolved: the phenomenon of life itself. At Physics of Life, we explore what brings matter to life. Our goal is to reveal the physical principles that govern the complex organization of living organisms. We are bridging scales from molecules to cells and tissues, and combining experiments, theory, and simulations. We learn by dissecting living systems, and also by rebuilding them. What physical mechanisms enable cells to perform functions? Why do embryos develop so robustly? And what are the equations for life?

title: Levels Of Serum Antibodies to CdtB Predict SIBO and an Altered Small Intestinal Microbiome
transcription: Hi, I'm Gabriela Leite from Cedars-Sinai Medical Center at MAST Program, and I'm here to present my poster, which is Levels of serum antibodies to cytolethal distending toxin B, or CDTB, in human subjects predicts SIBO by small bowel culture and an altered small intestinal microbiome by shotgun sequencing. Sorry, acute gastroenteritis is associated with IBS, and is often caused by species such as Campylobacter jejuni and Escherichia coli strains that encode a toxin called CDTB. SIBO is also linked to IBS, and small bowel microbial whole genome sequencing indicates that Escherichia coli and Klebsiella species, such as Klebsiella pneumoniae, are the species dominant in SIBO. Interestingly, immunizing rats with Campylobacter jejuni CDTB caused SIBO and IBS-like traits. Antibodies anti-CDTB is a validated IBS marker, but the link between antibodies anti-CDTB and SIBO in humans is unclear. title: Beyond Silos: Transformative Change for the Caribbean
transcription: Across the Caribbean, environmental pressures are no longer unfolding separately. Climate instability, biodiversity decline, rising food dependence and economic vulnerability increasingly collide, amplifying risks across ecosystems, livelihoods and communities. For small island developing states, the consequences are deeply interconnected. So, from food security right through to spiritual well-being, ability to heal and restore, biodiversity plays a critical role. So, this sector needs to go beyond the symptom, the symptoms of the crisis. We have to go deeper. And these are things that I think the environmental sector has avoided for too long. At the second Caribbean regional trialogue, participants repeatedly returned to one central idea, interconnected crises cannot be solved through isolated action. The discussions challenged traditional approaches that treat biodiversity, climate, food systems and development as separate policy areas. What the nexus assessment did is very different from a lot of the previous assessments. It sought to move away from the piecemeal approaches and the siloed sectoral thinking to looking across different sectors: health, food, climate, biodiversity, to find response options that will deliver multiple co-benefits at scale. The conversations also reinforced that these systems extend beyond national borders. As a region, as a Caribbean, it forces us to contemplate how we treat with our neighbors.

title: Scientists Want This Banned | STEM Loft
transcription: Mirror, mirror on the wall. What's the scariest biology concept of them all? Well, there is some scary science out there. One that's getting the attention of biologists right now is called mirror life. Although even the possibility of creating it is still a long way off, scientists are talking about setting guardrails on exploring this area of research now because of the major impact it could have for life on Earth. Just because we can research something doesn't mean we should. Hey, I'm Miranda Cosgrove and welcome to my STEM Loft, where one of the elevator buttons is a skull and crossbones and I really want to press it. You likely prefer writing notes, scrolling social media, and hitting a baseball either with your right or left hand. 99% of us are either right or left-handed, making it a lot easier to do things with one side of our bodies. And the other side, well, let's just say it doesn't work quite as well. But humans aren't the only ones with a preference like this. Many other things in our universe like DNA and proteins also have a handedness. Now, what if we could change that handedness? This concept is called mirror life. The handedness of the building blocks of life is known as chirality. When a chiral object is laid on top of its mirror image, no matter how it's rotated, it won't perfectly line up. Think again of your hands. They're mirror images of each other. However, no matter how I rotate them, they can't be perfectly superimposed on top of each other. You may have experienced this when trying to put your left hand's glove on your right hand or your right hand's on your left. I wouldn't say this is my most stylish look. DNA is naturally right-handed, meaning its classic DNA double-helix shape twists to the right. On the other hand, proteins are left-handed. Some molecules like tartrate, which can be found in wine or is sometimes added to food, have left or right-handed forms. Each molecule's chirality makes a big impact on how it functions. Louis Pasteur is most famous for his creation of pasteurization, a process that kills harmful pathogens in things like milk, but he's also considered the father of molecular chirality. He discovered chirality when he separated left and right-handed tartrate crystal shapes from each other back in 1847. But what would happen if we could change the chirality of left or right-handed microbes and flip them around into something else?

title: Plaud Note Pro - before you buy
transcription: Let's talk about the PLAUD NOTE and the PLAUD NOTE Pro which I actually have right here. This is an AI note-taking device and I'm going to be honest right off the bat and tell you that you probably don't need this. This is not a device that I'd recommend to everybody. But for the right type of person, this could be pretty useful. And I did drop an affiliate link in the description below. So at first, I wasn't going to make this video. PLAUD actually reached out to me and offered me a review unit and I said, "No, I don't think that I would use this." And then I started seeing their ads everywhere and curiosity got the better of me and I thought, "You know, what the heck. I'll try it out. I'll give it a shot." So I forked over $189 to buy the top-of-the-line PLAUD NOTE Pro. So after 3 months of using this, I love it. And I've even upgraded to a minutes subscription which I'll talk about later in the video. The PLAUD NOTE has become a big part of my professional workflow. So let's talk about what this thing is. At its core, the PLAUD NOTE is a tape recorder. It has four microphones and a button. The Pro version has a tiny screen showing you battery life and has better recording capabilities. It can record up to 16 ft away. It also has a magnetic adapter for MagSafe and other phones that you can stick to your phone and it will even record phone calls in the phone mode. But the true magic happens in the app transcription. PLAUD uses a combination of AI models like ChatGPT, Claude, and Gemini to transcribe your recordings, and the transcriptions are excellent. Of all the AI transcription tools and apps that I've used, this consistently ranks among the best. When you're done recording, it syncs to the app over Bluetooth with the option of using Wi-Fi for a faster connection. You then have the option to generate a transcription and summary. You can either use the auto-generation which I think works best for most recordings or use a custom template like meeting minutes or a special analysis template, and then after a few minutes, it will deliver the full transcript and summary. You also have the ability to label individual speakers which I find super helpful. And the summary has an AI chat feature so you can ask it questions about the recording and even do things like ask it to provide infographics, which is pretty cool. Personally, I don't use the app and chat features a whole lot. I mainly use this just for transcriptions. I press a button, it starts recording, it syncs to my app and transcribes,

title: Towards Calibrating Prompt Tuning of Vision- Language Models - CVPR 2026
transcription: I am presenting our work, towards calibrating prompt tuning of vision-language models. This work focuses on improving the reliability of prompt-tuned CLIP models. Our main goal is not only to improve accuracy, but also to make the model's confidence more trustworthy. Prompt tuning is widely used because it adapts CLIP efficiently without updating the full model. However, most existing methods mainly focus on classification accuracy. In real-world applications, accuracy alone is not enough. A model must also know how confident it should be. If a model gives high confidence to wrong predictions, it becomes risky in areas such as medical imaging, autonomous systems, and safety-critical AI. Therefore, models' predicted confidence should equal to the true likelihood or model predicted accuracy. This will ensure that the model's predicted confidence is calibrated. Post-hoc calibration can adjust confidence after training, but it cannot prevent embedding drift caused during prompt tuning. Our key observation is that prompt tuning creates a dual miscalibration problem. For base classes, the model often becomes underconfident because the logit margins are reduced. For novel classes, the model becomes overconfident because the margins become inflated or unstable. The reliability diagrams and margin analysis show that margin behavior affects base and novel classes differently. Therefore, we need a train-time method that controls both logit margins and text embedding geometry, which preserves CLIP geometry by preventing prompt-induced semantic drift and stabilizes class relations, reducing overconfident wrong predictions, thereby lowering calibration error. To solve this, we propose two complementary losses. First, the mean variance margin loss stabilizes the logit gap between the ground-truth class and the strongest incorrect class. This helps improve confidence separation. Second, the text moment matching loss preserves CLIP's original text embedding geometry by matching the distribution of tuned text embeddings with frozen CLIP embeddings. The total loss combines cross-entropy, margin regularization, and moment matching. Together, they reduce base class underconfidence and novel class overconfidence. Margin loss alone is useful, but it can still create high-confidence wrong predictions, especially on novel classes. This happens because if the model predicts the wrong class, increasing the margin can make that wrong prediction even more confident. Moment matching solves this by preserving semantic geometry. So, margin improves discriminability, while moment matching prevents semantic drift. Their combination gives better calibration, especially for novel classes. We evaluate the method on 11 datasets: ImageNet, Caltech-101, Pets, Cars, Flowers...

He introduces a research paper titled "Towards Calibrating Prompt Tuning of Vision-Language Models," which aims to improve the reliability and confidence calibration of prompt-tuned CLIP models, rather than just focusing on accuracy. The speaker explains the risks of miscalibrated models in safety-critical applications like autonomous systems and medical imaging. He highlights a "dual miscalibration problem," where base classes become underconfident and novel classes become overconfident. To address this, he proposes two complementary losses: the "mean variance margin loss" and the "text moment matching loss," explaining how they work together to stabilize logit margins and preserve text embedding geometry. Finally, he mentions evaluating the method across 11 datasets, including ImageNet, Caltech 101, Pets, Cars, and Flowers. The audio is high quality, with no noticeable background noise.

title: Investigative Journalist Tom O'Neill on CIA's MKUltra Mind-Control Program
transcription: Almost 50 years ago, the last congressional hearings into MK-Ultra took place just a short walk from here in the Dirksen Senate Office Building. At those hearings convened in August and September of 1977, representatives of the CIA told Congress and the American people that its 25-year effort to control human behavior had been a colossal failure. Because I believe Congress was never told the truth about what this program actually achieved. In fact, I believe the agency misled Congress in 1977 when it characterized MK-Ultra as a failure. My name is Tom O'Neill and in 1999, I was accepted, I accepted a magazine assignment to write a story about murders committed by a group of hippies called the Manson family. For those unfamiliar with this horrific episode of American history, in the summer of 1969, four young people acting on the orders of a cult leader named Charles Manson went to the home of movie director Roman Polanski and murdered everyone they found there, including his eight-and-a-half-month pregnant wife, the actress Sharon Tate. The victims were complete strangers to the, to their killers. The following night, Manson's followers murdered another couple in the same grisly fashion. At the time I accepted the assignment, I had never heard of MK-Ultra, and I wouldn't for another two years, after I'd missed countless deadlines, lost the assignment, and fallen down a nightmarish rabbit hole trying to answer the question I couldn't quite shake. How had Manson, a barely literate ex-con, acquired the ability to persuade ordinary young people to murder complete strangers simply because he had told them to? The pursuit of that answer, the pursuit of the answer to that question led me to Dr. Louis Jolyon West, known to his friends as Jolly. West was one of the most influential psychiatrists in America. During his career, he crossed paths with some of the most controversial events of the 20th century, including the Patty Hearst kidnapping case and the aftermath of the John F. Kennedy assassination investigation.

title: Reclaiming the lost art of listening to music
transcription: To Connor Knighton now and an invitation to just listen. And we're going to ask that when we drop the needle we refrain from any conversation. This is a listening environment. Seattle Shibuya Hi-Fi is a listening bar. Our guests can chat and sip cocktails in the lounge. They then leave their drinks and their shoes behind as they settle into the back room to enjoy full-length albums in a communal setting. An evening might feature anything from Björk to David Bowie. I love David Bowie cuz I've got, oh my gosh, my Bowie tattoo. I had to be here. It's the closest thing I could get to a David Bowie concert. These curated sessions, around 80 a month, regularly sell out. People are buying $20 tickets to listen to albums they could hear at home for free. That seems to me to be something that people are really rediscovering, that pleasure and the beauty of focus and intentional listening. Quentin Ertel is the co-owner of Shibuya Hi-Fi, which takes its name from a neighborhood in Tokyo. In Japan, listening bars, often called jazz kissas, started gaining popularity back in the 1930s. But similar venues have exploded in the US in recent years, popping up everywhere from Minnesota to Missouri to Colorado. There is a new wave of like these kind of listening bars especially in the West. Oh, cool. Artist and engineer Devon Turnbull designs high-end, handmade audio equipment for his company Ojas. While his speakers often end up in private living rooms, he's also created larger public listening rooms. The Smithsonian's Cooper Hewitt Museum in New York is currently showcasing what Turnbull has deemed his Hi-Fi Pursuit Listening Room Dream No. 3, installed in what was once Andrew Carnegie's private library. Pursuit is a really important part of the title. I am not here to say that I have made the ultimate sound system. This is about my pursuit as a builder, as someone who's passionate about building audio equipment and listening to music through it. Turnbull works out of a warehouse in Brooklyn's Navy Yard. His interest in all things audio traces back to an early age.

title: Report: U.S. Attorney Jeanine Pirro applied pressure to indict Democratic lawmakers over video
transcription: There's brand new reporting in the New York Times this afternoon about the turmoil inside the Department of Justice when it came to that failed attempt to indict six Democratic lawmakers who released a video reminding the men and women of the military that they do not have to obey any illegal orders. According to that reporting in the New York Times, in mid-January, the inquiry into the lawmakers had no sense of urgency, and that when lawyers for the lawmakers were contacted by federal prosecutors, they were told that they were not told of any law that had been broken, according to six people familiar with the matter. Times goes on to report that everything changed two weeks later when, quote, "Janine Pirro abruptly instructed her team to seek an indictment of the lawmakers." Her prosecutors then faced a decision that many in the Department under Trump have confronted: comply or resist. They chose the first. That attempt to indict, of course, failed last week, but as the New York Times notes, it stood, quote, "as an example of the chaos that has roiled the Department as it has grappled with the President's increasingly erratic demands, even in the face of little evidence." Want to bring in New York Times investigative reporter Mike Schmidt, whose byline is on that reporting we read from. Also joining us, former acting assistant Attorney General for national security at the Justice Department, Mary McCord. Um, Mike, first take us through what you and your colleagues are reporting today. Well, basically, what we're trying to show is that when this investigation started, these prosecutors reached out to the defense lawyers for the six lawmakers and said, "Look, uh, we're in the early stages, we're not even sure if we're in the first inning yet, we're not even sure what law we're investigating this under, not even sure if it's an investigation. Uh, you know, could could one of the lawmakers come in and talk? You know, would one of the lawyers want to come in and talk to sort of get this thing going?" That is as informal a way of starting an investigation as possible, especially after the President of the United States has called for them, you know, essentially called for them to be investigated for this and raised the possibility that they could be punished, you know, up you know, up to um you know, Seditious conspiracy. Seditious conspiracy and execution. So, it had a very, very informal feeling to it. And within two weeks, they there was a prosecutors before grand jury trying to indict them.

title: Nolan Wells' death: FBI probes threats
transcription: Welcome back. The FBI is investigating threats against the people who were with Nolan Wells in the hours before the Mississippi teen vanished and was found dead. Wells, 18, disappeared July 4th after joining friends on a boat trip to Horn Island, a barrier island off Mississippi's Gulf Coast. Search crews scoured the area for two days before a National Park Service Ranger found his remains on the island's northwestern tip on July 6th. Wells' friends returned to the mainland that July afternoon without him, but Jackson County Sheriff John Ledbetter previously said investigators believed Wells chose to stay on the island. It wasn't until later that night that his mother learned that he was missing from one of Wells' friends and reported it to authorities. Mississippi's Department of Public Safety Commissioner Sean Tindell said Wednesday that the FBI is investigating threats made against public officials, the people who were with Wells before he vanished, and their families. Michelle Thomas is now joining us here on LiveNOW from FOX. Michelle, thank you so much for taking the time to talk with us. Thanks so much for having me. So, we talk about this case. The FBI is now investigating threats connected to the case. So, what kind of threats can become federal crimes, and why would the FBI get involved here? Well, anytime there's a threat regarding anyone's person, placing them in immediate harm, there's going to be an investigation. But here, they may also be looking for racially charged threats, given sort of the backdrop of what we've heard about in the public scrutiny, in the public eye, and with the backdrop in history of Mississippi. People are concerned about this case because of sort of the racial makeup and so forth. So, if there are any kind of threats along those lines, there's going to be an investigation, and possibly a federal one. And when we talk about authorities, you know, saying that witnesses, public officials, even family members have received some type of threat here or there, how can that affect an active criminal investigation that can be happening? Well, any kind of law enforcement is going to follow any leads and they're going to try to track any any type of threat because they don't want there to be either witness intimidation or witness coercion. They want to make sure that they're able to preserve the evidence and witness testimony, and that persons with knowledge are able to come forward without feeling fearful. So, it can taint an investigation, and possibly a forthcoming trial, if there are constant threats and people are afraid to come forward with the information needed to solve what happened to Nolan Wells.

title: 'GOBSMACKED': Nicolle reacts to BOMBSHELL new report about Trump family's brazen self-dealing
transcription: Each deeply reported account of self-dealing from the Trump White House seems to get more brazen than the one that came before it. The New York Times has now reviewed a number of federal filings and is out with an extraordinary piece of investigative reporting that details the latest way that Donald Trump's family and allies appear to be profiting off Donald Trump's policy decisions as president. It involves a billion-dollar mining deal with Kazakhstan and one that both Trump and Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick's sons stand to profit from. In a meeting last September, Donald Trump and Howard Lutnick secured a deal with the leader of Kazakhstan to give a little-known American company now called Kaz Resources access to one of the world's largest untapped reserves of tungsten. It's a crucial rare earth mineral. Here's where the apparent self-dealing comes in, according to the New York Times. Weeks after that meeting, quote, "investors with a firm called Dominari Securities, which is housed at Trump Tower in New York and partly owned by the president's two eldest sons, Donald Trump Jr. and Eric Trump, joined with other partners to take a 20% stake in the corporate entity related to the Kazakhstan project." Around the same time, Cantor Fitzgerald, an investment company controlled by Howard Lutnick's family and overseen by his sons Brandon and Kyle Lutnick, helped one of the lead investors working with Dominari on the Kazakh deal raise $210 million in new capital for a related entity. Such rounds of fundraising typically net Cantor millions of dollars in fees. The deal was, quote, "ultimately signed on November 6th, six days after the investment involving the Trump sons and their partners, which was not publicly disclosed at the time." As the New York Times reports, this continues a pattern of self-enrichment in the Trump administration that has few precedents in American history. When asked for statements, both the White House and the Commerce Department rejected any suggestion that the Trump administration was improperly mixing government actions with family business. Trump's sons both denied being involved in the specifics of the deal. Eric Trump claimed they were passive investors. A Cantor Fitzgerald spokesperson said that company's executives were not involved in discussions related to government funding.

title: Investigation reveals DOJ withheld Epstein files mentioning Trump
transcription: A new NPR investigation reveals the Justice Department withheld portions of the Jeffrey Epstein files that contain allegations involving President Trump, including material tied to claims that Mr. Trump sexually abused a minor, and that some pages mentioning him were removed from the public record. Democrats on the House Oversight Committee called that out today, saying the DOJ's withholding of information could amount to a crime. For more on that and the surrounding fallout, we're joined now by Julie K. Brown, investigative reporter for the Miami Herald, whose reporting helped expose much of the Epstein network. Julie, welcome back to the program. It's great to have you. Thank you. I want to start with this NPR reporting that the Justice Department withheld some Epstein files related to allegations that President Trump sexually abused a minor, which we should say the White House denies. What stands out to you about this? Well, I think what stands out is that we don't have the reports, even though we know they exist. This stems from an interview that they conducted that came out of a tip to the FBI about this woman who has said that she, when she was 13, that she was sexually assaulted by Donald Trump. Now, her one of her interviews is contained in the Epstein files, although it is heavily redacted so it's hard to know exactly what she told the FBI. But as a result of that, we were able to see some of the the report numbers and the Bates stamps on it. And an independent journalist, actually named Roger Sollenberger, was the person that real that found out that compared that number to the documents that the Southern District of New York prosecutors gave to Ghislaine Maxwell's lawyers as part of her criminal case. You broke this story 8 years ago with your investigative reporting. title: US military eyes MAJOR SURGE if Iran deal fails
transcription: All right, on to the Middle East, President Trump calling off a wave of strikes in Iran, citing new progress on a potential deal with the regime. But the Commander in Chief says US forces remain locked, loaded, and ready to go if needed. Our Chief Foreign Correspondent, Trey Yingst, is live in Tel Aviv with the latest. Good morning, Trey. Yeah, hey guys, good morning. For now, the strikes against Iran have been called off. President Trump posted to Truth Social overnight, talking about the requests that he received from Iran and other Middle Eastern countries to hold off any attack in that the perimeters of a deal has been agreed to. This would include the immediate, complete, and total opening of the Hormuz Strait and an end to Iran's nuclear threat. Reports do indicate that assurances were made by Iran's foreign minister, one of the country's top negotiators. Secretary Rubio told Fox News that while these negotiations unfold, the regime must change their behavior. I think what does the, the regime has to change. You may not have regime change, but the regime has to change. The, the Iranian regime traditionally has been a, expeditionary. In essence, their view is they don't want to just govern Iran, they want to govern the region. They view them, they want to export their revolution. That does have to change. And the only way you're going to change that is if you, if you make the price of it too high for them to be able to pay. Before the latest diplomatic breakthrough, Iran attacked additional vessels in the Strait of Hormuz late last week, causing damage to at least one tanker. The Iranians also launched fresh drone attacks at Kuwait. At a cabinet meeting at Camp David on Friday, the President described his displeasure with the way the Iranians have negotiated while continuing destabilizing activity. I'm losing faith in them because they do lie and do, they do misrepresent. Well, the other day, the five missiles were shot. We knocked them down, but we were in the midst of a negotiation. I mean, I'm waiting for Steve to call me. How's the negotiation going? And instead, I got a call from Pete that they just shot five missiles at one of our bases in Jordan. President Trump giving the Iranians an olive branch here to reach an agreement. We'll see if they take it. Guys. Well, that's the question, Trey. And the President has shown incredible patience in an effort to hold out for diplomacy to get a deal, but are you getting any sense that it's going to be different now? The MOU ended up not working, another negotiation, Iran just keeps going back to doing exactly what they've been doing and these negotiations aren't going anywhere. What should we expect this week?

title: Nifty Report For Tomorrow and Banknifty News For 28 July Tuesday Market Analysis
transcription: यह वीडियो स्टार्ट करने से पहले आप सभी को डिस्क्लेमर दे देते हैं। यह जो वीडियो है ना प्योरली एजुकेशनल परपज के लिए है यानी कि कोई भी फाइनेंशियल एडवाइज या रिकमेंडेशन आपको नहीं दी जा रही ऐस सेड इन द डिस्क्लेमर। हेलो ट्रेडर्स, अभी मार्केट क्लोज होने में लगभग 10 से 12 मिनट बाकी हैं। करेंटली अगर हम मार्केट की बात करें ना चाहे बैंक निफ्टी हो, निफ्टी हो या सेंसेक्स हो। तीनों के तीनों इंडिसेस पे आज एक काफी ज्यादा शानदार तेजी हमें देखने को मिली। देखिए पूरे वीकेंड पे जितने भी वीडियोस मैंने बनाए और इवन फ्राइडे मार्केट क्लोज होने से पहले जो वीडियो मैंने डाला था, उन सभी वीडियोस के अंदर मैंने बस एक ही स्टेटमेंट दिया था कि चांसेस काफी ज्यादा है कि पूरे-पूरे चांसेस हैं कि मंडे जो है एक पॉजिटिव ओपनिंग, एक गैप अप ओपनिंग देखने को मिल सकती है। एक्जेक्टली वही हुआ काफी ज्यादा शानदार गैप अप आज मार्केट ने दिखाया। पूरा दिन मार्केट ने पॉजिटिव ट्रेंड को सस्टेन करा जो कि एक्चुअल में काफी अच्छी बात है। ऑल ओवर दिन आज का बहुत ज्यादा अच्छा गया। अभी देखिए आज है मंडे का दिन एंड इस वीडियो के अंदर हम लोग बात करने जा रहे हैं कल यानी कि ट्यूसडे के दिन के लिए बैंक निफ्टी, निफ्टी और सेंसेक्स के क्या इंपॉर्टेंट लेवल्स रहेंगे। इस बारे में डिस्कशन करेंगे। साथ ही साथ मैं आपको यह भी बताऊंगा क्या कल ट्यूसडे के दिन दोबारा से कोई पॉजिटिव ओपनिंग, कोई गैप अप ओपनिंग के चांसेस हैं या फिर अब बाजार एक करेक्शन, एक नेगेटिव ओपनिंग हमें दिखा सकता है। आते हैं फटाफट बात करते हैं गिफ्ट निफ्टी की बिकॉज़ इससे ना एक क्लियर पिक्चर हमें मिल जाएगी कल मार्केट ओपनिंग से रिलेटेड और हम सही तरीके से एक जजमेंट अपनी ले पाएंगे कल बाजार के लिए। अभी देखिए गिफ्ट निफ्टी को अगर आप देखते हैं ना ट्रेंड सबसे पहले आप चेक करिए बहुत ज्यादा अच्छा है। एक टेंपरेरी रेजिस्टेंस बन रहा था मॉर्निंग से जिसका फाइनली यहां पे ब्रेकआउट हो चुका है और इस लेवल के ऊपर अभी गिफ्ट निफ्टी ट्रेड हो रही है। एक सपोर्ट है 23,900 का जिसके ऊपर डेफिनेटली काफी अच्छे तरीके से गिफ्ट निफ्टी ने खुद को सस्टेन करा। ऑल ओवर प्राइस एक्शन के हिसाब से अगर आप ट्रेंड को देखते हैं बहुत ज्यादा पॉजिटिव है। व्हाट आई एम एक्सपेक्टिंग इस दैट कि इवनिंग तक आते-आते ना यूएस title: How to Tell What's Real and What's AI-Generated on Social Media
transcription: Midnight souls again? Come on, Gus, people are sleeping. Has your social media feed started to look a little off? Tell me I'm not hallucinating right now. Fake celebrity endorsements, news reports, doorbell camera footage and more that all look real at first swipe, but have a certain eeriness. Or maybe you've seen videos that are a bit more overtly fake. Yep, it's really me, Bigfoot. Like the many clips of animals doing seemingly impossible things, these videos generated by AI tools from Meta, Google, OpenAI and more are spreading on Instagram, Facebook, TikTok, and X at a rapid pace. Every other scroll, it is some AI-generated like influencer. Dubbed AI slop, some of these clips are meant to make us laugh, like Marilyn Monroe here. While others are out to spread misinformation in a world already struggling with claims of fake news. You will be fooled by an AI photo this week, and you probably already have been and you didn't know it. We have not come to terms with what this means for society. Celebrities like Keanu Reeves having to grapple with AI deepfakes. How disconcerting is that for you? Um well, I mean, it's not a lot of fun. Even Al has been the target of AI videos trying to dupe shoppers. Reversing my hypertension in just 3 months. I don't have hypertension. It can be easy to spot the more outlandish AI clips, but what about something more believable? Like a dog cuddling up to a baby, a grandma dancing at a barbecue, or a harrowing bodycam video. I got you. Pull your leg, pull your leg. Even AI fakes designed to make you feel good, to tug on your heartstrings. These videos are turning feeds into a mix of real life content and computer made footage, and some users are tired of it. I don't know what the solution is, but this technology should never have existed in the first place. So how can the average social media user separate fact from fiction? So, we're going to show you what is out there, what is fake. The team at Corridor Digital, a production studio with more than 7 million subscribers on YouTube, put some special people to the test.
