title: BREAKING NEWS: LeBron James signs with the Philadelphia 76ers! | First Take
transcription: We have breaking news here on First Take. According to Shams, LeBron James is signing with the Philadelphia 76ers on a two-year, $80 million deal with a player option. This comes after more than 20 days since he announced that he will be leaving the Los Angeles Lakers to play the next chapter of his career somewhere else. Stephen A., we knew it was coming soon, we did not know it was coming today. Your initial reaction to LeBron joining forces with Jaylen Brown and company in Philly? Shock, because I thought that if he was going back East, he would go home. That he wouldn't dangle his pres- his- his availability in the face of the Cleveland Cavaliers, and then go somewhere else. For him to choose the Philadelphia 76ers, this is a shock amongst shockers. And I think that this speaks to Bob Myers, the for- the architect, the former four-time champion executive for the Golden State Warriors, being in Philly now and having him there, who went out and pulled off a heist as far as most of us are concerned in getting Jaylen Brown. So now you got Jaylen Brown, okay, who's big-time, obviously, with Tyrese Maxey, who's big-time, you got him with VJ Edgecombe, who is uh who shined as a rookie and got tremendous potential. And now you're looking at it, if Joel Embiid is 50%, I mean, if he can give you anything during the playoffs, the Philadelphia 76ers could win the championship. I think this right here puts the Philadelphia 76ers right there with the New York Knicks as the favorites in the Eastern Conference to come out of the East and represent the Eastern Conference in the NBA Finals. That's how big this move is because LeBron is a savant, his basketball IQ is off the charts, and you combine that with the greatness of a Jaylen Brown and a Tyrese Maxey, with the leadership that Bob Myers has emanating from above as the executive for this team. I don't think there's any question, Philadelphia 76ers, I'm shocked by this. The Philadelphia 76ers are now in play to be a championship favorite. You know, one of the top four teams in, San Antonio, okay, Oklahoma City, New York Knicks, Philadelphia 76ers. And not necessarily in that order. They're the top four teams.

title: President Donald Trump speaks with Jenny Taft ahead of the 2026 FIFA World Cup™ Final
transcription: Mr. President, thank you so much for your time. Thank you. Hard to believe that the FIFA World Cup is coming to an end. You played such a role in bringing it here. What have been the highlights for you? Well, I think my first meeting with Gianni. He's fantastic, the job he's done. And he had this idea and I said, "That's crazy, we're not a soccer country." And it turns out we are a soccer country. We're a football country, but we don't want to get it confused. But, uh, I don't think there's ever been anything like what's happened with, uh, the whole World Cup. It's been beautiful. It's a beautiful thing to watch, and I really give Gianni the credit. It has been so special to see fans from around the world fall in love with our country, with America. How proud does that make you? Well, I watched it started with Scotland, and all of a sudden, they're doing things that nobody's ever seen with the bagpipes, and it was beautiful, and it just went to every country. And they're realizing what a great country this is. Uh, we're the hottest country in the world right now for, this helped, but for a lot of other reasons. We have trillions of dollars being spent in the United States. They're coming from all over the world, and they're spending their money here. And we've never had a period of, I call it the golden age of America. It's amazing. Uh, but I'll tell you, the World Cup, uh, you know, this is your deal, right? The World Cup. But the World Cup has really helped. It's been, uh, it's been tremendous. It's gotten the world, the word out, Mm. and nobody thought it was possible. I heard numbers that it's, uh, many times what's ever been done before, so that's great. Uh, you're such a sports fan. We just had UFC at the White House, we have the Olympics coming, and a big one on FOX, the Freedom 250 Indy car race. How much are you looking forward to it? Well, Roger Penske is a friend of mine, and he's been trying to get this race for 25 years, and he's had no luck in Congress. Congress is a tough place. And he said, "I've come here 212 times," or some, some massive number like that, uh, over many, many years, and he always went home empty-handed. He's not used to that. He came to see me. He said, "I saw Trump for 15 minutes, and we had a deal done." And not only done, it's going to be the best track you can imagine, down Pennsylvania Avenue, around the Capitol. That race is going to be something, and I think they have 400,000 people already signed up. And we had UFC, which was their record. They've never done, I think it was the all-time fight record, in front of the White House, at the front door of the White House. And some fights that were incredible. When you look at, uh, those last couple of fights, they were incredible, actually. Back to this FIFA World Cup, I got to ask: Argentina-Spain, Yeah. give me a prediction. Well, I knew you were going to ask, so I thought about it very, very, I thought about it a lot. I knew that was a question. I hate to get involved, even though, politically, it doesn't matter so much. Uh, the head of Argentina's a friend of mine, he's done a terrific job. But, I would say that it's hard to bet against Messi. I watched that pass, I guess you'd call it a pass, it was exactly perfect. Although, it takes some talent to hit the ball off the head coming at that speed, but that was perfect. If you had a strike zone, it was exactly where it had to be, and

title: BREAKING: Trump calls off MASSIVE Iran attack
transcription: Here's President Trump calling off a massive attack against Iran last night. The commander-in-chief says the change comes amid progress with the regime. Rebecca Castor is live in Washington with the details. Good morning, Rebecca. Good morning, Charlie. This was set to be one of the largest bombing campaigns against Iran to date, but now the President is signaling a peace deal could be close. He wrote on Truth Social, the USA is locked and loaded and ready to go against Iran. Despite this, we have just been asked by Iran and other Middle Eastern countries to hold off any attack, and that the perimeters of a deal has been agreed to. This would include the immediate complete and total opening of the Hormuz Strait, and an end to Iran's nuclear threat. I have agreed to cancel the attack subject to being able to rapidly make a deal. According to Axios, one of those Middle Eastern allies who asked President Trump to hold off on further strikes was the Saudi Crown Prince. The White House confirmed they spoke on the phone yesterday. And this comes after the US and Saudi Arabia launched joint strikes against Iranian militias in Iraq last week. But now the Saudis and other partners in the region are pushing the US and Iran to de-escalate. In an interview with Laura last night, Secretary of State Marco Rubio says it's because of President Trump that Tehran can no longer avoid consequences and may be ready to fold. I don't think the Iranian regime has ever faced a president like President Trump, which is someone that actually takes action. You know, they got used to for 20 or 30 years, not just the US, but the broader world allowing them to get away with things like lying, breaking deals, tricking people into agreements and so forth. The regime has to change. Their view is they don't want to just govern Iran, they want to govern the region. They view them- they want to export their revolution. That does have to change. And the only way you're going to change that is if you if you make the price of it too high for them to be able to pay. Qatari mediators held separate talks with US, Iranian, and Omani officials yesterday on reopening the strait. Axios reports those talks made progress. Charlie, Laura, and Griff, back to you. All right, Rebecca. Thank you, Rebecca. Overnight, President Trump pausing the strikes on Iran, revealing a rough outline for a deal. The President writing, "The immediate complete and total opening of the Strait of Hormuz and an end to Iran's nuclear threat. I have agreed, for the future benefit of the world and likewise, the survival of a successful and prosperous Iran, to cancel the attack, subject to being able to rapidly make a deal." Joining us now is former National Security Council member, retired Vice Admiral Robert Harward. Uh thank you for joining us this morning. So, um, w- w- where do you think uh things stand right now? Obviously, we have heard, uh we've seen President Trump both uh bombing Iran and then uh holding out hope that we might get a deal. Where are you on that?

transcription:
Now let's bring in Rebecca Heinrichs, Hudson Institute Senior Fellow, and Jake Sotiriadis, National Security Strategist, former Air Force Intelligence Officer, and author of The Revenge of Ideology. Welcome to both of you.
Thank you.
Thanks, Mike.
So, Rebecca, is the Iranian regime going to disappoint President Trump once again?
I suspect it will. I mean, there is no evidence that the Iran regime, which is essentially being controlled by the IRGC, um, that this is the radical element of the military. They have been given no indication, they've been tapping the president along. We've seen that every time the president is hopeful that because of his threats, that there will be some breakthrough in negotiations, that the Iranians just continue to fire on again in the strait. I think that we're at a point, Mike, where we really need to get Admiral Cooper, the head of of the operations, in front of President Trump to say, "Look, Mr. President, there are risks in in escalating this military conflict, but I can mitigate those risks and give the president those options," because I do think expanding the number of targets, including energy infrastructure, you got to hit the things that the IRGC does not want us to hit, and that's exactly what it is.
I want to play a clip from retired Brigadier General Mark Kimmitt, and then I'll get you to weigh in.
Patience is what the Iranians are using against us. They hear about we need to, we don't like forever wars, we want to get out of this quickly, we want to get this done quickly. But that's not how you defeat the Iranians. You defeat the Iranians by going patience against patience. If you say we want to get this done quickly, they'll just strap in their seat belts and say, we win by not losing. We can take the bombing, you'll leave, and we'll have what we want.
Jake, what's your assessment of where we are in this conflict?
Mike, for the United States, this conflict is a strategic distraction. For the Iranians, it's an existential conflict. So, you have an asymmetry between what's really important for both sides. And that means that Washington is concerned with bigger issues like China, Russia, the Ukraine war, the economy, the Indo-Pacific. Uh, Iran, the regime, is just trying to stay alive. It's trying to survive. So, the problem that we have here is the United States right now is trying to accomplish three strategic objectives that don't necessarily reinforce each other. It's trying to keep the Strait of Hormuz open, it's trying to eliminate Iran's nuclear program, and it's also trying to prevent escalation of a broader war in the Middle East. All of those objectives don't necessarily fit nicely together. And in fact, sometimes they actually work against each other. That's why strategic messaging is so important, and this back and forth about imminent attacks coming and then pulling it back for a potential deal are not helpful. Military pressure is important, but you have to have the messaging that sustains it as well.
What about the threats to commercial shipping in the Strait of Hormuz? How big of a concern

title: BREAKING: Israel UNDER FIRE amid Trump ultimatum to Iran
transcription:
The clock is ticking on President Trump's 48-hour ultimatum he issued to Iran, warning last night that the US will strike its power plants if the Strait of Hormuz is not reopened. Let's check back in with Fox News senior correspondent Mike Tobin live in Tel Aviv. Mike, we're hearing that missiles are approaching Israel right now. What do you got for us?

And we should start hearing the sirens, uh, in about 2 minutes now. Uh, the way the, uh, alerts are going right now, everything from the north to the south of Tel Aviv, uh, is under, uh, watch right now, and the eastern, uh, section of Tel Aviv in particular. So, when we hear the sirens start coming, usually what we get, uh, out of Iran these days are the cluster bombs. And the reason you get the cluster bombs is they're just they're effective in terms of getting through, uh, the Israeli air defenses. And when I say cluster bomb, uh, what I'm talking about is a warhead that's made up of dozens of little bombs, and when that's intercepted by the air defenses, it'll break up, uh, into dozens of bomblets, and the bomblets still get through. And we've seen them be very effective in terms of hurting people on the ground or destroying property because those bomblets get through. Uh, what we saw yesterday was an exception because those were ballistic missiles with big 1,000-pound warheads. For the most part, those big warheads aren't getting through; they get intercepted. Last night, two of them got through into Dimona and Arad. Uh, the IDF did their investigation, and they simply determined that there wasn't, uh, a new type of weapon that was effective in terms of getting through, uh, and there wasn't a failure of the system. It's just a fact that you're shooting missiles out of sky, which is a very difficult thing to do. So, we're keeping an eye on the skies to the east of us right now because that's where we, uh, expect the missiles to appear. That's the direction, uh, par- pardon me, where the, uh, uh, where the missiles come through, uh, and then, hopefully, we'll see the interceptors launch and get after them. So, that's the situation right now, and this is a drill that the people here in Israel, uh, are repeating every day, multiple times a day. Uh, you get the alerts over your phone, that's the period we're in right now. Once you start hearing the sirens wail in the background, that's an indication that the missiles are getting close.

title: DETAILS: US deploys laser tech against Iranian drones
transcription: Iranian Shahed drones pose a real threat to US forces and our Gulf allies, so the Pentagon is now deploying new laser technology to help take them down. Brian Llenas joins us live from our London bureau. Good morning, Brian. Good morning, Lawrence, Ainsley, and Brian. You know, the US Navy is equipped with two laser systems that are capable of taking down these Iranian drones, the ODIN and the HELIOS. Now, the ODIN was spotted in a CENTCOM video that was released at the beginning of Operation Epic Fury on board the Arleigh Burke-class guided-missile destroyer. You can see it there in that box. Now, the ODIN blinds drones, firing an infrared beam that overwhelms drone sensors, causing it to crash or fail. There are at least two destroyers in Epic Fury that are equipped with the ODIN. Now, the HELIOS is a high-energy laser beam with a high-powered sensor that tracks, blows up drones and missiles in the air by igniting the fuel. Now, the HELIOS is not confirmed to be deployed in Epic Fury. It's only known to be on a US ship that was last seen in the Indo-Pacific in Japan. Now, these technologies are vital in defending against Iran's drone attacks. Iran has fired off four times as many Shahed drones as ballistic missiles attacking our Gulf Arab allies. Now, Iran's biggest advantage is that these drones cost $35,000 to make, but one Patriot missile fired to shoot down these drones costs $4 million per missile. Now, these laser technologies cost pennies per shot and perhaps they're part of the reason why the US says it is not concerned about running out of munitions in this war. We've had a number of new capabilities being fielded. Obviously, I'm not going to talk about it from an operational perspective of what those are. But, I think you have seen over a period of time, us kind of get on the other side of this cost curve on drones in general. Now meantime, Ukraine's president Volodymyr Zelenskyy says he has accepted a request by the US and our Gulf allies to help in countering Iran's drones. Ukraine has become an expert of taking down Shahed drones fired by Russia. This is an ad from a Ukrainian company, Wild Hornets, and it shows the Sting, a low-cost quadcopter interceptor that successfully takes down these drones. Ukraine has also used the Octopus. It's an AI-powered drone interceptor developed by Ukraine, US, and the UK. It can track drones at night using AI and even go past electronic jamming. The Gulf states are reportedly, guys, discussing using the Octopus to defend themselves with these drone interceptors. They cost about $5,000 to make, much cheaper than the $4 million Patriot missile, which will ensure that our Gulf allies and the US can stay in this fight for as long as they need.

title: Why Christopher Nolan shot "The Odyssey" on IMAX film
transcription: 60 minutes overtime. 3, 2, 1, action. Director Christopher Nolan has made some of the most spectacular films of the 21st century. The Dark Knight, Inception, Interstellar, Dunkirk, and Oppenheimer. With each new film, the scale and ambition of Nolan's storytelling seems to reach new heights. So, it's only fitting that his latest coming to theaters this July takes on a nearly 3,000-year-old Greek epic, The Odyssey. Let's go! Matt Damon plays King Odysseus in The Odyssey. This is his third film with Nolan. I think what separates him from other directors is the stories he wants to tell are incredibly ambitious and the way he wants to tell them is incredibly ambitious because he wants to do it all in-camera. In this case, he wanted to do it 100% in IMAX, which had never been done. And that wasn't even announced because we didn't know if we could do it. The Odyssey is the first feature film shot entirely with IMAX film. Each frame has resolution or image quality up to three times higher than digital. Action! title: The WNBA has 'no integrity': Dan Dakich
transcription: WNBA star Sophie Cunningham is not backing down from her opposition to biological men in women's sports. And her supporters are not staying quiet either. Another rally took place outside today's Fever/Lynx game. Her coach called the attention frustrating and a reporter tried to get Cunningham's teammate to weigh in. There's a frustration, of course, because we want to we want to talk about basketball. But I also understand, like, this is this is part of our growth edge as a league. We speaking of the outside noise, Sophie your teammate. Sophie came out with... Oh, thank you. Have a good day. Outkick host, Dan Dakich, joins me now. Uh Dan, why why do so many uh members of the league seem not to want to talk about this? Well, because you get excluded, you get bullied, you get harassed, you have marches. Today, Cheryl Reeve, the coach of the Minnesota Lynx playing against Sophie Cunningham, wore a shirt that said, "Trans kids belong" in reference to Sophie Cunningham saying boys should stay out of women's basketball. And I would argue, okay, what's the end of that shirt? Nobody's arguing trans kids don't belong. Sophie Cunningham simply is saying that boys should stay out of girls' locker rooms and compete against boys. And others, including, unbelievably, Stephanie White, the coach of the Fever, doesn't understand that nobody would have ever heard of Stephanie White. I live in Indiana. She's an Indiana legend. If boys were allowed to play against Stephanie White at her little high school in rural Indiana or at Purdue, we would've never heard of her. She would've never had these opportunities if boys were allowed. But the bullying, the harassment goes on in that league. The league has no integrity. The commissioners are a joke. And so, people are afraid. Yeah, it's it's not like uh LeBron James just signed on to join the Fever. Uh, you know, there is a reason they call it women's NBA, right?

तो मैच जो होगा वो रनगिरी दाम्बुला स्टेडियम में खेला जाएगा। रनगिरी दाम्बुला स्टेडियम, जहां पर फिलहाल के लिए पिछला मैच खेला गया था दोनों टीमों का और आपने देखा कि वो मैच काफी अच्छा और बेहतर तरीके से पिछला वाला रहा था दोनों टीम के बीच में। पाकिस्तान पहले इनिंग में बहुत अच्छा 170 के ऊपर का स्कोर करी थी और 170 स्कोर करने के साथ ही साथ इस टीम ने बहुत बढ़िया परफॉर्मेंस बल्लेबाजी में करके दिखाया। यह अलग बात है कि बॉलिंग में टीम का परफॉर्मेंस उतना अच्छा नहीं हो सका था और टीम का थोड़ा परफॉर्मेंस बॉलिंग में खराब गया, लेकिन ओवरऑल टीम ने बहुत बढ़िया तरीके से दोनों ने खेला था। दोनों ही टीमों का परफॉर्मेंस काफी हद तक अच्छा, जबरदस्त तरीके से देखने को मिला। उम्मीद है आज के मैच में भी दोनों टीमें बढ़िया तरीके से ही खेलेगी और जबरदस्त परफॉर्मेंस दोस्तों देखने को मिलते नजर आएंगे। जो पॉसिबल प्लेइंग इलेवन दोनों टीमों की है और टॉस हो चुका है। टॉस का अपडेट ये देख सकते हैं आप पाकिस्तान टॉस जीत के बल्लेबाजी करने के लिए गई है जबकि पिछले मैच में फर्स्ट बैटिंग करके और पाकिस्तान की टीम हारती नजर आई थी पिछले मैच में परफॉर्मेंस जो देखने को मिलता नजर आया था टीम का। तो जितना बेहतर होना चाहिए था वैसा नहीं देखने को मिला था, समझ रहे हैं ना? इस तरीके से गया था, लेकिन अब आज के मुकाबले में देखेंगे कि टीम का क्या परफॉर्मेंस रहता है। तो टॉस जीत करके फर्स्ट बैटिंग करने का फैसला इसके तरफ से फिलहाल के लिए आज के मुकाबले में नजर आया है। अब ओवरऑल देखते हैं आज क्या कर पाएगी। लेकिन जो पॉसिबल प्लेइंग इलेवन दोनों टीमों की नजर आ रही है, उसमें जो-जो प्लेयर्स होने वाली हैं उनके नाम जरा से एक बार देख लेते हैं और जानने की कोशिश करेंगे कि कौन-कौन सी खिलाड़ी को आज के मैच में मौका दिया जा सकता है। टॉस अभी जस्ट आया ही है। श्रीलंका टीम के तरफ से इमेषा दुलानी, विश्मी गुणरत्ने, नॉटी, उसके अलावा हंसनी परेरा और काव्या कविंदी होगी, साथ ही साथ चमारी अटापट्टू, हर्षिता समरविक्रमा, कविशा दिलहारी होने वाली है, नीलाक्षी डी सिल्वा और साथ में एक प्लेयर रशमिका होगी, रशमिका के साथ-साथ सुगंदिका कुमारी, काव्या कविंदी, मालकी मदारा जैसी प्लेयर आपको नजर आने वाली है। तो ये तो हो गई दरअसल श्रीलंका की टीम। दूसरी तरफ चलते हैं और जानने की कोशिश करते हैं कि पाकिस्तान की जो पॉसिबल प्लेइंग इलेवन क्या है और क्या हो सकता है आज के मैच में। तो इनकी टीम के तरफ से शवाल जुल्फिकार होगी, ऐमा नसीर, आयशा जफर और सायरा जबीन, आयमा फातिमा, उसके अलावा इनकी टीम में महान एनी करके एक खिलाड़ी होगी और नाजिया अल्वी, मुनीबा अली जो टीम की कप्तान विकेटकीपर है, उम्मे हानी होगी, नशरा संधू होने वाली है, तूबा हसन होने वाली है और साथ ही साथ हुमना बिलाल करके खिलाड़ी आपको देखने को मिलती नजर आएगी। ये तो

title: EA SPORTS FC 27 | Official Gameplay Deep Dive
transcription: More player control, more fluidity, and more changes led by you. There's so much that's new to gameplay this year. We addressed AI defending, reinvented corners, reworked attacking runs, dribbling under pressure, and fluid one-twos. And of course, retuned fundamentals to reduce intercept-backs, rebalance play styles, and deliver on more of the improvements you care about most. Let's dive in, starting with something you've called out over and over: AI defending. Your feedback is clear: manual defending should be the best way to stop your opponent. So we've tackled that from a number of angles this year, taking power away from the AI and giving it to you when you are defending. You'll feel the difference as soon as you take control. Your player will jockey more responsively. You'll also have a larger tackling range, a larger interception range, and a larger blocking range when defending manually. For example, the AI isn't quick enough to cut off the angle and can't quite reach to make the interception. But when you take control, that quicker jockey can get you into position and you're able to reach farther to win the ball. We've also minimized AI auto-tackles in competitive gameplay. The AI will still be able to win the ball if your opponent dribbles right into them, but they'll almost never lunge for the ball or reach into a challenge. And, we've loosened teammate contain and team press in the defensive third. The AI will still get into solid defensive positions, but taking manual control will give you more tools to stop your opponent. We've also reinvented corners to reduce luck and continue to reward skill. In FC 25, corners are split into two phases. One to prepare your pass and one that gives you creative control over your run. Pick your spot and power up your cross. Then, you'll have a few seconds to lose your marker so you can time your run to arrive at the perfect moment. This unlocks so much set-piece creativity, and equal amounts of set-piece chaos we see in leagues around the world. In attack, you'll have more control over how your

title: FAJARDO vs YABUKI 2026 IBF CHAMPIONSHIP | FAJARD 4X BAGSAK ANG CHAMPION SA ROUND 1!
transcription: Here we go! Yan ang pwersa na taglay! Grabe ito mga idol. Apat na beses pinabagsak ni Fajardo ang isang knockout artist sa loob lang ng isang minuto. Out of Agusan del Sur, Philippines. It's Miel Fajardo. Yabuki Masamichi! Laging sundan, huwag magpapahuli, pag-usapan ni Pakbakan. mga idol, tapos na ang paghihintay dahil may isa na namang Pinoy boxer na lalaban para sa World Championship. At hindi ito ordinaryong challenger, tahimik siya sa labas ng ring, hindi mahilig magsalita pero kapag nagsimula na siyang umatake, sunod-sunod ang bumabagsak. Siya ang mandirigma mula Mindanao, Miel "Silent Assassin" Fajardo. Mayroon siyang 14 na panalo at 12 rito ay tinapos niya sa knockout kaya huwag kayong mapalinlang sa kanyang tahimik na kilos dahil sa sandaling tumama ang kanyang malakas na kaliwa, maaaring matapos agad ang laban. Nice! Oh! What a huge knockout! Ngayon nakatakda siyang lumaban para sa IBF World Championship pero para maging kampeon, kailangan niyang harapin ang isang tunay na knockout monster. Ang kampeon mula Japan, Masamichi Yabuki, dala ang 20 na panalo, 18 rito ay knockout, galing siya sa matagumpay na depensa kontra kay Felix Alvarado at dala rin niya ang anim na sunod-sunod na knockout victories kaya sa papel, malinaw na si Yabuki ang paborito, mas beterano, mas subok at siya ang may hawak ng championship belt. Dahil dito maraming nagsasabing dehado si Fajardo pero hindi ito ang unang pagkakataon na minaliit ang Pinoy at kapag underdog ang "Silent Assassin", mas lalo siyang nagiging mapanganib. Yan ang pwersa na taglay! Tingnan na lamang ang ginawa niya kay Tobias Jeremias Reyes, isang Argentinian knockout artist na may 18 na panalo at 16 na knockout. Nagtapat sila sa isang IBF title eliminator.

transcription: Hey y'all, it's Thursday. Um I have a couple things I'm looking forward to. Um I've got school. Um I'm gonna start back up in the middle of March and going on the clinical mental health counseling track. And then work um is kind of up in the air. I've got the summer camp thing happening this summer. But for right now, um today, I woke up at nine and um went back to bed for another four hours after that, because I was like I could wake up and do the day. But I don't have work today. Um But yeah, just like dreaming and being in that dream space is so nice. title: My name is Ryan, and I am in recovery. Continuing my work story and path to addiction. #recover
category: Mental Health Vlogs & Personal Video Diaries
transcription: My name is Ryan, and I'm in recovery. Um, yeah, this is now part three of the work cocaine. Sorry, I didn't realize it would go on for so long. But yeah, I stayed in that job as kind of head of music overseeing the nine venues and the 25 staff for right up until COVID. Um. Just before COVID, things were definitely kind of ramping up in terms of my using. I was more and more so kind of going to work with no sleep and kind of just about functioning. The job itself, it's kind of interesting. Once now that I was kind of head of the department, I could almost kind of like not work as hard and hide it. Like, you know, you've when you're kind of doing the bookings, like booking the DJs or you're promoting the show, your work is visible, because, you know, if you don't book the DJ, there's no show. If you don't promote the show, there's not enough ticket sales. So, you can't really hide in that regard. But, my my kind of role now as kind of the head of the team was to more just oversee. Like, I would sign off programming ideas, I would sign off artwork, I would sign off marketing campaigns. I wouldn't actually be doing them myself, I'd just kind of be overseeing everything and kind of keeping the the wheels oiled. Um. And, I don't know if that necessarily suits me, like, kind of job. I feel like that I need that kind of creative input directly from myself to kind of give me that feeling of purpose. And, yeah, during this period, I was just not really enjoying my job, I was using a lot. I was using a lot at home. I had a flatmate, but I'd often just kind of come home and go into my bedroom and just use all night and go to work. It was pretty bleak. Um, COVID then came and all the venues closed. There was obviously lockdown, I got put on furlough. Um, not long after that, I had to furlough... Sorry, I had to make all of the staff redundant. Me and one other guy had to do all the redundancies over Zoom calls, which was brutal. You know, a lot of these people I'd worked with for many years and I considered a friend. So, to have to do that was really challenging mentally. Um. At the time, I was actually engaged to my ex and we were planning our wedding and we were also kind of saving for the future to like buy a house and stuff like that. And I remember asking my boss, "Do, you know, is there any chance that I'm going to be made redundant? You know, because I'm that's going to really put me in a difficult situation." And, and the words he said to me, I can still remember now. He said, "If the ship..."
caption: In this reflective and deeply personal audio clip, a man named Ryan continues his story about his recovery from cocaine addiction, focusing on the period leading up to and during the COVID-19 pandemic. Speaking with a sincere and somber tone, Ryan's British accent is clear as he recounts his experience working as a head of music overseeing several venues and staff. He explains how his promotion to a managerial role made it easier to conceal his escalating drug use, as his daily tasks became less visible, though it also left him feeling disconnected and lacking a sense of purpose. He describes a bleak routine of sleepless nights and isolated drug use before the pandemic shut down his industry. The narrative grows heavier as he describes the mental toll of having to lay off his colleagues over Zoom while being furloughed himself, all while planning a wedding and a future with his partner. title: Diary Entry Writing | Minor Discourse 2.1 | Class 10 SSC English | LMR
category: Mental Health Vlogs & Personal Video Diaries
transcription: Hey everyone, and welcome. Today, we're going to crack one of the easiest questions in your English exam, a question that can absolutely guarantee you full marks if you just know the secret. I know how stressful exams can be, but what if I told you there's one question that's not a trap, but actually your secret weapon for getting those marks in the bag? That's right, we are talking about the diary entry. Seriously, this can be the easiest question on the entire paper, but only if you know the simple formula that combines a little bit of format with a whole lot of feelings. So, what exactly is the diary entry? Well, think of it like you're just talking to yourself on paper. It's all about pouring out your personal feelings and what you've experienced. And because it's personal, it's always written in the first person, you know, using words like I, me and my. Okay, you ready for this? Let's dive into what I call the golden formula. It's like a simple, unbreakable code for success that's going to get you easy marks right from the start. All you have to do is memorize these five letters: D, D, T, S, B. That's it. It stands for Date, Day, Time, Salutation, and Body. This structure is your key. I mean, you'll literally be scoring points before you've even written a proper sentence. Okay, so let's break down that first part, the format. And honestly, this is where you're going to get the easiest marks in your entire exam. It is just this simple. At the top left of your page, you write the date, the day and the time, just like you see here. That's it. Boom. Instant marks in your pocket. The salutation is just as easy. You always, and I mean always, start with Dear Diary, followed by a comma. Don't try to get creative here. This is the way. All right, with the format locked in, let's move on to the most important part, the body. This is where you actually tell your story, and it's where your feelings are going to earn you the big marks. Now, you don't need to write a whole novel here. Just keep it short and focused. Two or three paragraphs is perfect. And in those paragraphs, you just need to do three things: describe what happened, express how you felt about it, and explain your reaction. And here it is, the most crucial point of all: you have to use emotional words, words like happy, sad, excited, nervous, proud. This is what separates a pretty good answer from a perfect, full-marks answer. So remember this: feelings equal full marks. Okay, enough talk. Let's actually put this all together. We're going to build a perfect, full-marks entry step-by-step, and you'll see just how simple this is.

title: Dear Leese | Loneliness [Visual Diary Entry #1]

transcription: I think that there is a loneliness epidemic. Loneliness is definitely something that's universal but not really talked about. And, it's interesting because a lot of people describe themselves as outcasts. But if everyone's an outcast, doesn't that mean that everyone is technically left out? So, it kind of made me think about my past, and it was really hard for me not to equate loneliness with being alone. I actually had a pretty tough time with making friends. Um, as social as I am and extroverted as I am, I felt like I was wasn't liked for who I was. And, that made me feel like no one wanted to be my friend, like no one enjoyed me genuinely, like me being myself. So, it made me shameful and embarrassed to be alone. So, in order to protect myself, I decided to reject them. I didn't want them to reject me. title: QUIET ORBIT | A Depression Anthem | Official Lyric Video
category: Mental Health Vlogs & Personal Video Diaries
transcription: I stop picking up the phone, stop explaining where I go. Every crowded room gets smaller till there's no more left to breathe. Too many voices hit at once, every sound becomes too much. I can feel my patience burning before I know what set it off. So I leave before I say something angry I didn't mean. I go quiet, close the distance, keep the damage far from reach. They call it cold from where they stand, but no one ever asks me why. Did you ever think I just disappear to stay in control? Did you ever ask what the noise was doing to my soul? I need a room where the world goes still, where nobody pulls at what I can't give. I need the space to come back down whenever every voice becomes too loud. Don't mistake my distance for goodbye, I still care from the other side. And if you've ever had to disappear just to feel your lungs again, I know why you choose the distance.

title: Diary Entry Writing for Class 7 | Full Explanation
category: Mental Health Vlogs & Personal Video Diaries
transcription: Hello my dear students, aaj hamari English ki class mein rehne wali hai diary entry. Diary entry kya hoti hai? Diary entry hoti hai jo bhi aapke sath poore din mein vyateet ho chuka hai, usey aap ek diary mein likhein pratidin, aur ek format ke sath. Usey kehte hain diary entry. Toh aajiye aaj hum iska format samjhenge jo ki diary entry ko sahi tarike se likhne ka dhang hota hai aur isse aap exam mein full marks paa sakte hain. Aajiye format padhne ke liye. Date, Date jis din aap apni diary entry ko likh rahe hain, usi din ki yahan pe date daal denge. Uske baad day, aap isse milaan karke rakhiye, check karke rakhiye ki is din jo bhi date hai usi ka day hona chahiye. Time, jis samay aap likh rahe hain, woh time likhenge is par, jaise ki 9:00 baje abhi aur is par p.m. aur a.m. lagana mat bhoolna, jaise shaam ko likh rahe ho toh p.m. laga dena, subah likh rahe ho, subah ke samay mein toh a.m. laga dena. Uske baad aayega apna line space, line space aap exam sheet jo aapki rehne wali hai usme line space mat likhna L.S. karke, kyunki ispe aapke number cut sakte hain, teacher samjhega pata nahi kya bawal cheez likh di isne. Aap is jagah ek line chorr doge, maine aapko samjhane ke liye yahan pe L.S. likh diya hai aur line space, isliye aap ek line chorr dena single. Uske baad aap daaloge, Dear Diary, pyaari diary, aapki diary hai toh pyaari hi rehne wali hai. Uske baad aayegi hamari heading, heading jaisa aapka question rahega us hisab se aap apni heading daal denge isme. Phir aa jata hai hamara content, content bhi question ke hi... question se hi nikala jata hai content, jaisa ki aapko question diya gaya hai usi hisab se aap apna content likhenge. Content mein hamesha I ka use hota hai, woh ki aati hai first person mein, first person I ka use karoge aap hamesha content, kyunki aapki diary hai, aap khud likh rahe ho, kisi aur se toh likhvaoge nahi, khud likh rahe ho toh I ka use karoge diary mein toh I ka use karna hota hai. Uske baad aa jata hai, isme tense ka kaunsa use karna hai? Isme tense use hota hai past indefinite, aap poochoge ab ki past indefinite kyun hota hai? Past indefinite isliye hota hai kyunki aap jo diary mein likh rahe ho, woh pehle beet chuka hai, aapke sath woh ho chuka hai woh likhoge aap.

title: Unexpected Clarity  A Prison Memoir of Mental Liberation #journeeman #prisonlife #mindfulness
category: Mental Health Vlogs & Personal Video Diaries
transcription:
I've got something to say,
something that sticks in my throat like iron.
I miss my prison cell.
Not the wires, not the count, not the smell of bleach and sweat and locked metal.
I don't miss West Wing tier,
I don't miss Seg unit,
I don't miss cell 68.
I love my wife, my kids, my desk, the open sky when I step outside.
If you handed me the keys tomorrow and said 'Go back,' I'd burn them.
But listen,
there's a part of me that still walks those three meters by two and a half,
that still feels the quiet drop when the unit locks down.

Picture it.
Green door, heavy bolt,
grey vinyl-covered cabin wood,
tiny desk, bench that bites your spine, bed thinner than regret, toilet right there, no hiding.
Sink, small curtain with its ten-centimeter rule so they can always see you breathing.
Church guitar leaning against the wall like it's waiting for permission to sing, that's it.
That's the whole kingdom. And yet, when the day died and the televisions faded to mumbles, some footsteps echoed and then stopped, that box became still.
No notifications,
no opinions screaming from screens, 
no endless choices pretending to be freedom,
just me
and my mind.
They controlled everything else.

Time,
light,
movement,
who I spoke to,
when I ate,
when I pissed. Razor wire outside, laughing at the sky. But the mind, they couldn't touch it.
In that cage, my thoughts got room to stretch, to roam, to question everything I ever preached from a pulpit, to sit with doubt instead of burying it under sermons. Meditation wasn't an effort, it just happened like breathing,
like the fan humming, low light when the heat creeping through the pipe, a summer sweat turning the air to soup. I'd joke with the boys heading back to my chalet, make them laugh, 'it's a bloody cell, Malcolm.' Yeah, I'd say.
But tonight, it's my university.

title: David Wilcock’s Last Words REVEALED: UFO Expert’s 911 Call EXPOSES Hidden Struggle Before Death
category: Mental Health Vlogs & Personal Video Diaries
transcription: The final moments of David Wilcock are now coming into focus, and they paint a deeply troubling picture. According to reports from TMZ, Wilcock made a 911 call on Monday morning, just hours before his death. During that call, he spoke about serious financial problems and ongoing health issues. At one point, he told dispatch, quote, "I need to leave, I will be to the left of the house." Authorities say he refused to clarify whether he was armed or planning to harm himself. Dispatchers, meanwhile, treated the situation as urgent. In audio obtained by TMZ, officers can be heard describing the situation in real time, labeling it a potential suicide. Moments later, the situation escalated. As deputies arrived at his Colorado home, they approached with caution. The threat level was unclear, and backup was called in. Just before officers reached him, Wilcock said something else, quote, "I'm sorry to put you through this." And then, he hung up. Seconds later, deputies saw him outside the residence with a gun to his head. They took cover immediately, issuing commands to drop the weapon. But then, a single gunshot rang out. Authorities say Wilcock shot himself in front of responding deputies. No one else was found on the property after a search. He was pronounced dead at the scene. He was 53. Now, with details from that final call emerging, the tragedy surrounding David Wilcock is being seen in a new light, one shaped by personal struggles that remained largely hidden until the very end.

title: Assam Floods 2026 Explained: Why Is the State Drowning? | Current Affairs |  Drishti IAS
category: Mental Health Vlogs & Personal Video Diaries
transcription: दोस्तों, परिस्थितियां सबके लिए एक जैसी नहीं होती और दूसरी बात यह कि प्रकृति से ज्यादा ताकतवर कुछ नहीं होता। यह बात असम के मामले में बिल्कुल सही साबित होती हुई दिखाई दे रही है। 12 से ज्यादा जिले प्रभावित हैं, 70 के आसपास मौतें हो चुकी हैं और 7 लाख से ज्यादा लोग उस असम में बाढ़ से परेशान हैं और अभी भी कई जानों की जाने का डर बना हुआ है और वहां के मुख्यमंत्री तक ने यह कह दिया है कि यह बड़ी चिंता की बात है। इतनी तेजी से बाढ़ पहले असम में नहीं आई थी। तो आखिर असम में इस तरह से बाढ़ अचानक से क्यों आ गई? तेजी से पानी कैसे भर गया? क्या मानसून जो कि बारिश का मौसम चल रहा है, इस वजह से हुआ है? तो क्या सिर्फ बाढ़ आने की जिम्मेदारी पूरी मानसून के ऊपर है या हमारा, आपका या हम जैसे कुछ लोगों का दोष है? चलिए सारी बातों को समझते हैं इस वीडियो में लेकिन सबसे पहले एक जरूरी जानकारी कि आपके लिए एक स्पेशल कोर्स आ चुका है IAS GS फाउंडेशन कोर्स। इस कोर्स की खास बात यह है कि अगर आप दिल्ली से या नोएडा से दृष्टि आईएएस की क्लास नहीं कर सकते और आप यही वाली क्लास ऑनलाइन करना चाहते हैं तो IAS GS फाउंडेशन लाइव ऑनलाइन कोर्स है। अब इस कोर्स की खास बात यह है कि 3 साल तक इस कोर्स की वैलिडिटी रहेगी। आप जितनी बार चाहें क्लास को उतनी बार देखिए। स्टडी मटेरियल हार्ड कॉपी में आपके घर पहुंचाया जाएगा तो आपको पढ़ने में भी मजा आएगा और इसके साथ ही आपको टेस्ट सीरीज प्रिलिम्स और मेंस की मिलेंगे और उसके साथ ही आंसर राइटिंग की प्रैक्टिस भी कराई जाएगी। इस वजह से यह आपके लिए बड़ा ही फायदेमंद है क्योंकि बेसिक से एडवांस तक सरल भाषा में आपको पूरा GS पढ़ाया जाएगा। आपको इसके बारे में अतिरिक्त जानकारी चाहिए तो वीडियो के डिस्क्रिप्शन में लिंक है, उसे क्लिक कर लीजिए या सीधे हमें कॉल कीजिए 87501 87501 पर। अब आते हैं हमारे टॉपिक पर। यहां पर सबसे पहली बात हम खबर को समझते हैं कि क्या है। देखिए, 66 से ज्यादा मौतें हो चुकी हैं, आंकड़े बढ़ते जा रहे हैं, 7 लाख लोग प्रभावित हैं, 856 गांव जो कि 12 जिलों के हैं वो प्रभावित हैं और 50,000 से ज्यादा लोग अभी राहत से वंचित हैं यानी कि वहां तक अभी भारत की सरकार या हम कहें असम की सरकार, सेना नहीं पहुंच पा रही है तो वह अभी इंतजार में हैं, ऐसे लोग भी हैं और इसके साथ ही असम राज्य आपदा प्रबंधन प्राधिकरण के अनुसार अभी और ज्यादा मुश्किल आने की इस डर बना हुआ है। अब अगली बात आती है कि ये सारी चीजें कैसे शुरू हुई? तो 19 जून को बाढ़ का पानी तेजी से खतरनाक स्तर पर पहुंचता है और जब वो खतरनाक स्तर पर पहुंचता है तो वो आसपास के इलाकों में बहना शुरू होता है और जिससे तीन सबसे ज्यादा शिवसागर, चराईदेव और जोरहाट, ये असम के ऐसे ऊपरी जिले हैं जहां पे सबसे पहले पानी बढ़ता है। क्यों? क्योंकि पानी ऊपर से ही नीचे आ रहा था तो जो ऊपर के जिले हैं वो प्रभावित होंगे और शिवसागर एक बहुत ही महत्वपूर्ण शहर है जो पानी के चपेट में यानी कि बाढ़ के चपेट में आया। कई लोग राहत शिविर में हैं, बहुत सारे काम चल रहे हैं लेकिन मैंने क्या कहा, इंसान प्रकृति के आगे एक छोटा सा खिलौना मात्र है, उससे ज्यादा कुछ नहीं।

transcription: गुड मॉर्निंग भाई लोगों! हाहाहा। तो किन-किन को लगता है कि मैं आप लोगों के कमेंट्स नहीं पढ़ता हूँ? अरे, कैसे नहीं पढ़ता हूँ भाई? रुको। अरे भाई मैं सबके कमेंट्स पढ़ता हूँ। हाँ, तुम पहले बोल लो। अरे मैं क्यों नहीं पढूंगा आप लोगों के कमेंट्स? अरे मैं सबके कमेंट्स पढ़ता हूँ गाइस। और अभी जो है, बहुत सारे कमेंट्स आ रहे हैं अलग-अलग वीडियोस के अंदर, अलग-अलग चीजों को लेकर। लेकिन एक कमेंट जो कि आप लोग सबसे ज्यादा कर रहे हैं, वो यह है कि सोनू भाई कहाँ हैं? सोनू भाई का क्या हुआ? तो भाई लोगों, एक बात बताऊं सच्ची-सच्ची? सोनू भाई है ना, उन ग्रेटेस्ट बंदों में से एक हैं जिन्हें मैं जानता हूँ या जिनसे मैं मिला हूँ। सोनू भाई सच में एक बहुत बहुत बहुत अच्छे इंसान हैं। और कमाल की बात पता है क्या? अब तो सोनू भाई ने भी अपना एक नया यूट्यूब चैनल बना लिया है गाइस! हाहाहा! मज़ा आ गया गाइस! तो सबसे पहले तो सोनू भाई को उनके नए चैनल के लिए हार्दिक शुभकामनाएं, बहुत बहुत बहुत सारी बधाइयां। और साथ ही साथ गाइस मैं तो आपसे भी यही कहूँगा कि जितना सपोर्ट और जितना प्यार आप लोगों ने आज तक हमारे लिए किया है ना, जितना प्यार हमें दिखाया है, गाइस उतना ही प्यार आप सोनू भाई के लिए भी दिखाइएगा, उतना ही सपोर्ट आप सोनू भाई को भी कीजिएगा। और साथ ही साथ गाइस मज़े की बात क्या है? सोनू भाई भी साइंस के बैकग्राउंड से आते हैं। तो आई होप कि सोनू भाई भी साइंस से रिलेटेड अच्छी-अच्छी वीडियोस आगे फ्यूचर के अंदर लेकर आएं, अच्छे-अच्छे एक्सपेरिमेंट्स करें। तो एक बार फिर से सोनू भाई को बहुत सारी बधाइयां। और गाइस आप लोग भी सोनू भाई को नीचे कमेंट्स के अंदर बहुत सारी बधाइयां जरूर देना, उनके चैनल पे जाकर भी, और ढेर सारा प्यार दिखाना। और गाइस एक बात बोलूं, एक और? देखो, अह मेरा मानना यह है कि हर इंसान को अपनी लाइफ के अंदर अपनी जर्नी, अपना रास्ता, अपनी मंज़िल चूज़ करने का पूरा-पूरा हक होता है। और ऐसा करना भी चाहिए। और जब आदमी है ना गाइस, अपने डिसीजन खुद से लेता है...

title: Noah Kahan - Willing and Able (Official Lyric Video)
category: Mental Health Vlogs & Personal Video Diaries
transcription: Oh, and when I left the room, did you take a deep breath? I stole the beer, drove home, there was only one left. And are you still feeling you're still thinking about that? Wide awake in your room, just seething about that? When I make my fight, I'm the devil. But would I stay the night for a drink? And we stay up and fight about the childhood lie that we both had the courage to leave. I'm within and able. If you want to kick this rock around, if you've got a bone to pick with me. If you've got a flag, plant it in the ground, I'll stay here till morning. Or we can fight like we used to fight, bony limbs, red-faced and teary-eyed. Under the glow of the TV light, I'd be willing and able. Look at you leaving again, it's all you know how to do. Go ahead, take the last of the drinks, the world belongs to you. They all say you're light, all I see is the shadow. And...

title: Steelers select Navy’s Eli Heidenreich in emotional 7th-round moment | 2026 NFL Draft
category: Mental Health Vlogs & Personal Video Diaries
transcription: And Eli Heidenreich is here. You see the emotion hitting him. He is Navy's all-time receiver, all-time leading receiver. He was a zero star recruit coming out of high school. Valparaiso, Davidson, Slippery Rock offered him finally, his dream school. Grandfather was a naval officer, his uncle was a Navy corpsman and in the Marines. And Eli, now eligible with the new rules to defer his military service to pursue a career with the Steelers. I got goosebumps right now, Reese. I do. This, going into the draft, this timing is insane. This is my favorite player in the draft. Reese mentioned some of it, a running back, but only by position. The stats and positions right now compare nothing to what we're looking at here. Tears, the Naval uniform, the hat, the theater here in Pittsburgh going absolutely nuts. Hey, he had nearly, nearly 1,000 yards receiving in this Navy offense with stats. Well, Kyle mentioned it, that he had some Navy receiving records. This is my favorite stat of any prospect that we had in the draft. He had six receiving touchdowns in 2024. No player in the Naval Academy's history has ever had more than that. Just six, it's all it takes to make history. Six touchdowns in Navy is like 30 at LSU. Correct. God bless them. He's basically the Jamar Chase of Naval Academy wide receivers. But, what I love is his versatility. He's a runner, he obviously has great speed as well, the versatility here. He was good against good competition when they had those opportunities as well. One of the best players, no hyperbole, to come out of Navy in the last quarter century. What about against Air Force? The 8 catches 243 yards, those are records. Unbelievable, three touchdowns, but he was utilized in different ways they would line him up. Kyle, you watched him. I did. Dynamic. I grew up on the Severn River. The banks of the Severn River, Naval Academy, love the Naval Academy. Beautiful, right? That's right. Nice place, American life, Severn River. It's true. You see him back there, they go out to the slot, he catches it down field. And of all the places, Steelers, the hometown story. God bless these people in the Steelers draft. We're not only clapping, we're saluting. This is really cool, really cool. Really couldn't have scripted it any better too. We still had some picks to go, we still had things to do. But, you want to put an exclamation point on this draft in this city? Yeah. Yeah. Yeah, I mean, look, this is one of the most iconic cities in, in, in the National Football League. It's just tradition rich. And you saw all the, you saw the, I mean, there was just genuine respect within the Pittsburgh Steelers draft room right there. It does give, gives me goosebumps. This is a great game, this is a great profession that we're involved in.

title: Virgo August 2026 Horoscope: Stop Overthinking and Focus on What Truly Matters
category: Mental Health Vlogs & Personal Video Diaries
transcription: कन्या राशि की बात कर लेते हैं। आप लोग अजीब ही तरह के धर्म संकट में फंस गए हैं, क्योंकि जिन लोगों से आप मिल रहे हैं, आप उनके लिए अच्छा करना चाहते हैं, इनफैक्ट कोई आपका अगर दुश्मन भी है, आप उसके लिए भी अच्छा करना चाहते हो, आप सोचते हो कि चल तुझे भी नुकसान ना हो, लेकिन वो व्यक्ति इतना एडमेंट है अपना नुकसान कराने के लिए कि आप भी सोचते हैं कि यार क्या करूं? समझ नहीं आ रहा। है ना? तो बहुत कुछ सिखाने-समझाने की कोशिश करेंगे बट नथिंग इस गोइंग टू वर्क आउट। अगर आप लोग शादीशुदा हैं तो प्लीज जरा सावधान रहिएगा इस समय पे, क्योंकि ऐसा बहुत फ्रीक्वेंटली हो सकता है कि आप कोशिश तो बहुत करें कि चीजें सुधर जाएं, चीजें सही हो जाएं पर वो इवेंचुअली ना सुधरें और ना ही सही हों। नाउ बिकॉज़ ऑफ़ दिस, लाइफ कैन बी अ लिटिल टफ फॉर यू। आप लोग यू नो, हो सकता है कि आप सोचें कि चलो भाई, सामने वाले के लिए कुछ कर दिया जाए, सामने वाले को कुछ रास्ता दिखा दिया जाए, पर उसका व्यवहार आपके प्रति ऐसा हो कि, यू नो, नाउ यू थिंक लाइक ये तो किसी चीज के लायक ही नहीं है, इसके लिए कुछ करने की जरूरत नहीं है। तो, दिस कैन बी अ ह्यूज इश्यू फॉर यू। आपकी कुंडली के पहले घर में शुक्र यानी कि वीनस डेबिटिलेटेड रहेंगे, यानी नीच के रहेंगे, तो इसकी वजह से आप लोग इस महीने खुद पर ज्यादा ध्यान ना दें, अपने प्लेजर्स पर ज्यादा ध्यान ना दें, दूसरों के ऊपर बहुत ध्यान दें, ऐसा हो सकता है। नाउ, अगर आप ऐसी इंडस्ट्री में काम करते हैं जहां दूसरों के लिए आपको बहुत कुछ, यू नो, यू हैव टू डू फॉर देम, फिर तो समझ में आता है, जैसे अगर आप डॉक्टर हैं, आप फार्मासिस्ट हैं, आप लॉयर हैं, जहां पर आपको दूसरों के लिए ही कम्पलीटली अपना जीवन लगा देना है, देन इन दैट पोजीशन थिंग्स डोंट सीम बैड, आपको बहुत ज्यादा काम करने को मिलेगा, आपको बहुत हार्ड तोड़ मेहनत करनी पड़ेगी, दैट विल बी, यू नो, अ वेरी डिफिकल्ट थिंग टू डू। तो, आपको अपने लिए बहुत ज्यादा टाइम नहीं मिलेगा, इनफैक्ट अगर आप सोने की भी सोच रहे होंगे तो नींद में भी आपका काम आपके दिमाग में चल रहा होगा। सो, दैट कैन डेफिनेटली बी एन इश्यू हियर, जिसकी वजह से आप लोग ढंग से सोए नहीं, ढंग से अपने ऊपर ध्यान ना दें। सेहत को लेकर एंजायटी आप लोगों के मन में ज्यादा हो सकती है, एक तो सोओगे नहीं, ऊपर से ऑब्वियसली जब सोते नहीं हैं तो ग्रॉगी सा फील होता है, खराब सा फील होता है, तो आपको लगेगा कि अरे यार, कुछ मुझे हो तो नहीं गया? कोई प्रॉब्लम तो नहीं है? तो ऐसी सेहत को लेकर एंजायटी आप लोगों के अंदर जरूर देखने को मिल सकती है, उसका आप लोग ध्यान दीजिएगा। डोंट अलाउ इट टू रन योर लाइफ। हालांकि, अगर हम ओवरऑल देखें, तो आप लोग कार्यक्षेत्र में अच्छा कर सकते हैं, ऐसी कोई बहुत बड़ी प्रॉब्लम नहीं है। आप लोग अपना बेस्ट देने की कोशिश करेंगे और जिन भी लोगों के साथ आप काम करते हैं, उनको ये डिफरेंस जरूर महसूस हो जाएगा, दैट यू आर पुटिंग इन मोर देन योर 100% और उसके लिए आपको सर्टेनली अवार्ड्स, रिवार्ड्स जो भी हैं, वो भी जरूर मिल जाएंगे, तो परेशान होने की जरूरत नहीं है। कई बार आपका जो इंट्यूशन है, वो बिल्कुल टॉप क्लास रहेगा, आपको एग्जैक्टली पता रहेगा कि कहां पर क्या करना है और आपके जो सीनियर्स हैं, जूनियर्स हैं, जिनके साथ भी आप काम करते हो, वो इसको जरूर एप्रिशिएट करेंगे।

title: Alysa Liu reacts to winning gold after free skate
category: Mental Health Vlogs & Personal Video Diaries
transcription: A script that would have been rejected as far-fetched and a comeback that has brought her all the way perhaps to the Olympic podium. It is like she's just playing on the ice, not even performing anymore. The joy, the passion, and she's figured out how to compete without carrying the weight of it. She stays so loose and completely herself out there. That's the secret every athlete wants to solve. That's what I'm talking about. I can't believe it. Thank you so much. Amazing. Amazing. Those are her right? I can't even believe this. The toe was amazing, the Lutz was amazing. Guys, I don't know if you believe what you've been watching since she made her comeback. But, but through it all, she's just kind of been like, "Oh, this is fun." I've never seen a comeback like it, and I've never seen someone withstand pressure like Alyssa Liu. And she did tell us that it's a whole new world this time around because she doesn't feel like her life is on the line. She has like this nonchalance both to the way she jumps and performs. Triple Lutz, triple toe, very nice second element in the program, and it just got better from there. She is just all sunshine on the ice. If you don't watch her skate and want to get on the ice and just feel what it might feel like to race around the rink, it is childlike, beautiful joy and innocence out there. Quad God loved it. So did everybody else in this arena, including her dad, her siblings, and Alyssa as well. She really couldn't have done better. This has been incredible to watch, 2 and a half years away from competition, Lori.

title: Michael Jackson’s son Prince reveals his takeaway watching ‘Michael’ film
transcription: A new movie about Michael Jackson is giving audiences a front-row seat to the King of Pop as never seen before. The biopic "Michael" chronicles MJ's rise to global fame, starting from the discovery of the Jackson 5 to his transition into a solo artist, and fun fact: Jaafar Jackson, who plays Michael in the film, is the late singer's nephew. Let's take a look. I just have all these songs in my head. Gotta get them out. And joining us now is one of the film's executive producers, the eldest son of Michael Jackson, Prince Michael Jackson. Prince, so great to have you on the show. Thank you. Thank you so much for having me. Happy to be here. So your dad having been such a public figure and icon, really, a lot is out there about him already. What can people expect to learn about the King of Pop in this film that they don't already know? I think one of the most magical things about this film is, for those of us that were lucky enough to grow up with the Jackson 5 and the Jacksons, hopefully, it will re-instigate that feeling of nostalgia and fun and family. And for those of us like myself and younger that never got to experience that, I hope that it contextualizes the growth and the rise to stardom and the hard work and effort that my father put into it, my father and my family, and overall just be a really fun, entertaining time for children of all ages from 9 to 90, you know? And I imagine that the making of this film was very personal and tough at times. It was also Jaafar's first acting gig. What was the process like in telling your dad's story? Um, I mean, first and foremost, authenticity is the biggest challenge in any story, and especially my father having such an incredible life that spans five decades of him being at the top of his career, we wanted to approach it from a way that audiences, again, of all ages could understand who he was as a person. We all know the story of the King of Pop, but I think this was our goal, was to tell the story of Michael, how he started from the small home they grew up in in Gary, Indiana, to arrive at the biggest stages and the biggest platforms all around the world. And the research that we started off, when I met Graham King in 2019 and beginning of 2020, sitting down and speaking with various family members or people who worked with him and knew him, and I had heard a lot of these stories growing up. But when you approach these conversations with a perspective from a research point, I feel like

title: “I Was Genuinely Freaked Out” Curry Barker, Inde Navarrette & Michael Johnston on ‘Obsession’
category: Mental Health Vlogs & Personal Video Diaries
transcription: Hi, I'm Indiana Massara. And I'm Michael Johnston. And I'm writer-director Kirby Barker. Today we're interviewing each other for our new film, Obsession. I love you so, so, so, so, so, so much. A love only the branch of a willow tree could conjure. What was your reaction when you first read the script and how did you feel watching Obsession with a big crowd at TIFF? I got my hands on the script and I said, "What can I do to be a part of it?" Yeah, same. I mean, I loved how it wasn't all black and white. It was very gray and unclear and yeah. And then what was your reaction? How did you feel watching it in the theater at TIFF? A little terrified. Incredible. Yeah. The audience goes nuts. I mean, I could hardly hear the movie because people were screaming and laughing. I've never seen grown men jump in their seats. Because of you. Because of me? Yeah. I love you. I love you. I love you! I love you! Kirby. Yes. Drum roll, please. What was your most challenging day on set and why? Well, I don't want to give anything away, but I would say the party scene was really difficult for all of us that night. I mean, it was just late. It was an overnight shoot, a lot of pages, too. That party scene is just long. It just feels like it goes on and on. A lot of coverage to get, too. Yeah, it's just a lot. We wanted to do some slight reshoots of the party and realized that that, that house actually burnt down in the LA fire, so that exact house doesn't exist anymore. Pretty crazy. So, what we got is what we got, and it's now memorialized in the movie. Go! Indy, how did you prepare for this role and was there one unique or quirky thing that you did to tap into the creepy mode before filming? No, it's inherently inside. It just pops out. It just is there. Effortless. Don't be alarmed, we're home. Preparing the role was really, really fun. I mean, we got to watch a lot of fun movies and kind of pick and choose like a puzzle what we wanted in the film and moments that we took inspiration from and then made them our own. I think Pearl was a really big one. Bless us, oh Lord, and these thy gifts, which we are about to receive from thy bounty, through Christ our Lord. Did I ever surprise you with a specific note while filming any of your scenes? If so, what was it and why did it surprise you?

title: What Reading My Old Journal Taught Me About Growth
category: Mental Health Vlogs & Personal Video Diaries
transcription: I read my journal from a year ago and cried, in a good way. So, I did something kind of embarrassing last week. I went back and read my journal from a year ago and I cried, and I want to tell you why that was actually a good thing. The journal was from about 12 months ago. I'd completely forgotten I even had entries from that period. It was one of those stretches that just kind of blurred by. Nothing dramatic, nothing memorable, just a lot of Tuesdays. But I picked it up on a slow Sunday and started from the beginning. And here's the strange part. I didn't recognize the person writing it, not because they were sad or doing badly, but because I had completely forgotten what that version of me was worried about, what they were hoping for, what felt impossible, and what felt small. And reading it felt like getting a letter from someone I used to know. Some of it was small. I'd written about a coffee that was really good, about being annoyed at someone in a way I couldn't even reconstruct now, about a plan I had that I was nervous about, and looking back, I know it worked out fine, but the version of me writing it didn't know that yet. And that's the thing that hit me. The person writing that entry was doing something really hard without knowing it. They were living through uncertainty with no knowledge of the outcome, and they showed up and wrote it down anyway. That's not a small thing. I don't think I would have remembered any of it if I hadn't written it. Not because it wasn't worth remembering, but because our brains aren't built for this. They compress time, they flatten the details, they remember the outcome and forget the journey. Here's the one that really got me. There was an entry about something I was trying to get better at, I won't go into detail, but it was something I'd been struggling with for a while. At the time of writing, it felt like I wasn't making any progress. But reading it a year later, I knew I had, not dramatically, not in a montage moment

title: How to Start Journaling as a Beginner | Daily Journaling for Self Growth & Mental Clarity
category: Mental Health Vlogs & Personal Video Diaries
transcription: You open your journal, you pick up your pen, and then, nothing. You stare at the blank page, and you do not know where to begin. Sound familiar? Welcome to ReadUp Daily. Today, we are solving the number one problem every beginner journaler faces: not knowing what to write. And by the end of this video, you will have a simple technique, three powerful words, and a full page ready to write. Let us begin. The technique is called stream of consciousness writing. It sounds complicated, but it is actually the simplest and most freeing way to journal. Here is how it works. You write whatever comes to your mind, no rules, no grammar checks, no perfect sentences, you just write whatever you are feeling, whatever you are thinking, whatever is sitting heavy on your heart right now, you put it on the page, and you do not stop until the page is full. That is it. That is stream of consciousness writing. Now, let us learn three words that will make your journaling more powerful and more expressive. Word one: overwhelmed. Overwhelmed means feeling like you have too much on your mind or too much to handle all at once. Example sentence: Today, I feel overwhelmed, but I know that writing it down will help me breathe again. Write that in your journal. Word two: clarity. Clarity means the feeling of being clear and certain in your mind. When the confusion clears, and you finally understand what you are feeling or what you need to do. Example: Every time I journal, I find a little more clarity about who I am and what I truly want. Write that in your journal. Word three: release. Release means to let something go, to free yourself from a feeling or a thought that has been holding you back. Example sentence: Journaling gives me a safe place to release everything I have been carrying inside me. Write that in your journal, too. Now, let us use stream of consciousness writing together. Do not think, do not edit, just write what you feel as you read along. Ready? Right now, in this moment, my mind feels...

title: Why Paper Journaling Is More Powerful then Digital Journaling
category: Mental Health Vlogs & Personal Video Diaries
transcription: In a world where we do almost everything on screens, you might wonder: Does it really matter whether we journal digitally or on paper? Surprisingly, it does. Writing in a paper journal can actually be far more powerful for healing, self-awareness, and changing behavior than typing on a screen. In this video, I'm going to explain why writing by hand can create deeper emotional clarity and lasting personal change. Writing by hand engages the brain more deeply. When you write on paper, your brain works differently than when you type. Handwriting activates multiple parts of the brain related to memory, emotion, and learning. Typing tends to be fast and automatic. But writing by hand slows your thinking down. That slower pace allows you to process your thoughts more carefully, which helps you understand your emotions and experiences more clearly. In other words, handwriting helps your brain move from reacting to reflecting. Slowing down creates emotional awareness. Healing starts with awareness. When you journal on paper, the natural rhythm of writing encourages you to slow down and become more aware of what you are feeling. Instead of quickly typing and moving on, you begin to notice your emotions, your thoughts, your reactions, and the patterns in your behavior. This moment of pause is incredibly powerful because you cannot change what you are not aware of. Paper feels more private and honest. A physical journal often feels safer than digital writing. It isn't connected to the internet. There are no notifications, no audience, no distractions. Because of that, many people feel more comfortable writing honestly about things like fears, regrets, anger, sadness, or uncertainty. And that honesty is essential for healing. Your journal becomes a place where you can tell the truth without being judged. The physical act of writing releases emotion. There's also something deeply therapeutic about the physical act of writing itself. The movement of pen on paper can feel grounding and calming. When emotions feel overwhelming, writing them out physically can help release that tension. Many people notice that after writing honestly about something difficult, they feel lighter, calmer, clearer. Sometimes, the page holds emotions that were too heavy to carry alone. Your journal becomes a record of growth. One of the most powerful aspects of paper journaling is that you can see your journey over time.

The monologue concludes by highlighting how a physical journal serves as a tangible record of personal growth over time.

title: Why Your Journal Sounds Fake (and how to fix it)
category: Mental Health Vlogs & Personal Video Diaries
transcription:
Have you ever written something in your journal, re-read it, and thought, "that sounds absolutely nothing like me"?
Here's a thing that doesn't get talked about enough: most people's journal entries sound like they're being written for an audience. Not a real audience—an imaginary one. Some future version of themselves who's going to judge the quality of the writing. Or worse, some hypothetical person who might one day read it. And so, instead of writing, "I'm absolutely furious, and I don't even fully understand why," you write, "today was challenging, and I'm processing some complex emotions." And then you close the journal feeling like you just filed a report rather than said anything true. This is the invisible reader problem, and it's the actual reason most people find journaling uncomfortable. Not because they're bad at it, but because they're performing instead of writing. So why does this happen? Because we've been trained our whole lives to write for a reader: school essays, work emails, texts to people we want to impress. Everything we write has an audience in mind, and we've calibrated our language to manage how that audience sees us. A journal asks you to do the opposite: write for no one. And that turns out to be genuinely hard, especially at first, because your brain keeps switching into "how does this sound?" mode rather than "what is actually true?" mode. The result is entries that are technically accurate but emotionally hollow. The words are right, but the voice isn't yours, and you can feel it when you re-read it—that slight uncanny valley feeling where you recognize the handwriting, but not the person. Honest journaling sounds a lot like how you'd tell a story to your best friend at midnight: short sentences, incomplete thoughts, words you'd never use in formal writing, repetition, contradiction, starting a sentence and stopping halfway through because you realized something while you were writing it. It doesn't have to be coherent. It doesn't have to conclude anything. It doesn't have to read well. The only job it has to do is be true.

title: The 5-minute Journal trick that calms panic
category: Mental Health Vlogs & Personal Video Diaries
transcription: Have you ever been lying awake at 2:00 a.m. feeling a physical weight in your chest while your mind races through a tornado of unfinished tasks, looming deadlines and vague anxieties? That sensation signals a specific biological chain reaction taking place in your nervous system. When you perceive a threat, even something as small as a tense email, your brain's threat detection center, the amygdala, fires an alarm and floods your system with cortisol. If this stress stays chronic, neuroimaging shows that your amygdala actually grows larger and more reactive, while your prefrontal cortex, the area responsible for rational executive planning, shrinks and effectively goes offline. To break this cycle, you need a mechanism called cognitive diffusion. By taking those chaotic, swirling thoughts out of your head and translating them into physical words on a page, you force your rational prefrontal cortex to re-engage, which physically turns down the amygdala's alarm system. The worry dump is a structured, analog practice designed to create this distance. It requires putting pen to paper to begin the process of externalization. Grab a physical pen, a piece of paper, and a timer. We are going to walk through this exact process together right now. Moving thoughts onto paper provides a physiological intervention to stall cortisol and reclaim your cognitive control. Step one is to find a quiet, private space where you will not be interrupted. You need an environment where your analytical left brain can focus on the physical act of writing, giving your creative right brain the safety to wander and release everything it's holding onto. Set your timer for exactly five minutes. When it starts, your only job is to write down every single worry, task, and anxious thought currently occupying your mind. Here is the single most critical rule for this phase: you must write continuously. Do not pause to organize your thoughts. Do not prioritize the list. And do not stop to analyze why you are stressed about a certain item. Ignore your inner critic. If you stop to correct your spelling or fix your grammar, you will pull yourself out of the flow and stall the exercise. Keep your pen moving. If your mind suddenly goes blank and you run out of things to say, simply rewrite your last sentence over and over again until a new thought emerges, or until the timer officially sounds. Your output does not need to make sense to anyone else. A single word, a fragmented phrase, or a complete sentence are all equally valid forms of output. Just get it on the page.

She then guides the listener through a 'worry dump' exercise. title: The Journaling Practice That Will Change How You See Your Past
category: Mental Health Vlogs & Personal Video Diaries
transcription: You've probably started a journal at some point and quietly given up on it. A few pages of raw feeling, then silence. You decided writing just wasn't for you. Most people assume that putting pain into words works because it lets something out, but release was never really the point. What actually changes you on the page looks more like construction than release, and it explains why some people write for years and feel exactly the same, while others rewire their relationship to a single memory in four short sessions. In the 1980s, the psychologist James Pennebaker ran an experiment that seemed almost too simple to matter. He asked people to write about their most upsetting, unresolved experiences for 15 to 20 minutes, four days in a row. No structure, no therapist, no feedback, just a blank page and permission to be honest. Some of the people in that study wrote about things they had never told another living person. Health visits dropped in the months that followed. Immune markers improved. People slept better and reported less physical pain, and none of it involved anyone hearing their story out loud. Here is where it gets stranger. Pennebaker and later researchers went back through the writing itself, word by word, looking for what separated the people who improved from the people who didn't. It wasn't how much emotion they expressed. It wasn't how many painful details they included. It was whether their language changed. The people who benefited most were the ones whose sentences shifted across those four days from chaos toward explanation. They started using more words like because, realize, and understand. Their writing stopped being a wound repeated on the page and became something closer to a story with a cause and an effect. That shift has a name in psychology: insight. And it turns out insight, not catharsis, is what your mind is actually rewarded for.

title: Top 5 Journaling Practices That Feel Like Therapy for Your Mind (2026)

transcription: Have you ever wished you could talk to someone about your deepest thoughts, but didn't know where to start? What if you could do that without saying a word? Journaling offers you a safe space to express your emotions, organize your thoughts, and process everything you're feeling. Whether you're feeling overwhelmed, stressed, or just in need of clarity, journaling can help guide you through it. In this video, we'll dive into the top five journaling practices that can feel like therapy. These powerful methods can help you work through emotional challenges, boost your self-awareness, and even improve your mental health. Let's get started. One, stream of consciousness, brain dumping. One of the simplest, yet most effective journaling practices is stream of consciousness writing, often referred to as brain dumping. The concept is easy to grasp. Take a few minutes and write whatever comes to mind without worrying about structure, grammar, or punctuation. It's all about letting your thoughts pour out onto the page freely. Set a timer for about three to five minutes and just write without stopping. Let your mind flow naturally. The therapeutic benefits of brain dumping are vast. This practice provides a powerful outlet for releasing pent-up emotions and mental clutter. Often, our minds are filled with a whirlwind of thoughts, worries, and stresses that can weigh us down. By putting these thoughts on paper, we get the opportunity to unload all the noise and clear our mental space. The act of writing helps us create an emotional release, allowing for more calm and mental clarity. But the benefits go beyond just relieving stress. Brain dumping can also help uncover hidden thoughts and emotions that we may not have been fully aware of. Sometimes, when we sit down to write, we realize there are lingering concerns or feelings that we've been suppressing. After expressing these thoughts, we often gain new insights into our feelings and situations, helping us look at things from a fresh perspective. It's almost like having a one-on-one conversation with yourself, unraveling those tangled emotions, and leaving you with a sense of peace. Another reason stream of consciousness writing is so helpful is because it's incredibly easy to integrate into your day. You can do this practice anytime you feel over-

transcription: Have you ever worked hard, tried everything, read advice after advice, and still felt like you're stuck at the same level while other people keep pulling ahead? What if I told you that the reason you're not where you want to be has nothing to do with talent, luck or intelligence? Today, I'm breaking down the single best self-improvement book that I read in 2025, the one that quietly changed how I think, how I work, and how I win. Here's the thing: The people you admire most aren't smarter than you. They're not more gifted than you. And they didn't magically figure life out earlier. They just learned one mental rule that most people never do. And once you see it, you can't unsee it. This rule explains why some people grow faster every year while others stay frustrated, burned out, and quietly jealous of friends who seem to be passing them by. And if you've ever felt like you're doing the work but not getting the results, you're about to understand why. And if you leave this video early, you'll miss the one shift that made everything else finally start working for me. I want to be clear with you. I've been exactly where you might be right now. Motivated but inconsistent, ambitious but second-guessing myself, starting things, stopping things, and wondering why progress felt so slow. In 2025, I made a promise to myself to read at least one self-improvement book cover-to-cover per month. Not to feel productive, but to find what actually works. Most books were fine, some were repetitive, one stood above all the rest. The book is Mindset: The New Psychology of Success by Dr. Carol S. Dweck. I was so inspired by this book that I created a mindset mastery playlist for the lessons I learned. And today, I'm going to walk you through a simple three-part plan based on this book. First, I'll show you the invisible belief that's holding you back. Second, I'll show how high performers think differently when they fail. Third, I'll show you how to install this mindset into your daily life starting today. Stick with me, because the last part is where most people finally break through. Why most self-improvement fails.
