title: Inner Engineering - Book Overview | Between The Lines | Journal
category: Mental Health Vlogs & Personal Video Diaries
transcription: You know, Sadhguru's Inner Engineering has this central idea that most of us are just living life completely by accident. So in this explainer, we're going to break down his guide for how to take back the controls and really move from that inner chaos to conscious creation. Okay, so the book kicks off with this really powerful paradox, right? Think about it. We have comforts and technologies that kings and queens from just a few centuries ago couldn't even dream of. I mean, we are, without a doubt, the most comfortable generation ever. But here's the kicker, are we the most joyful? The most peaceful? Sadhguru says, not even close. So, what on earth is missing here? Well, that question gets us right to the heart of the problem that the book lays out. It's this huge massive disconnect between the amazing world we've built around us and the, well, often chaotic world that exists inside our own heads. I mean, just look at our external world. We've achieved this incredible level of mastery, right? We've engineered our environment for total control, for maximum comfort. But then, you look internally, and what's going on in there? For most of us, it feels like a total storm of thoughts and emotions. It's accidental. It's reactive. It's completely out of our control. It's like we've perfected everything outside of us, but left our inner world, our inner landscape, totally up to chance. And this points to a really fundamental mistake in how we chase happiness, doesn't it? We're kind of taught that if we just get the right job, the right house, the right partner, you know, fix our external world, then our inner world will magically fall into place. But Sadhguru says, nope. You've got it completely backwards. The quality of your life is not determined by what's happening around you. It's all about what's happening within you. I used to study like this all the time. I thought if I kept rereading my notes enough times, eventually, everything would stay in my head, but most of the information dissipated after a few days, and the frustrating part was that I genuinely worked hard. And then I came across something called the Feynman technique. It's name it is named after Richard Feynman, a Nobel Prize-winning physicist who was known not just for being intelligent, but for explaining extremely complex ideas in a way almost anyone could understand, and he had this simple core idea that if you can't explain something simply, you don't really understand it yet, and that line stayed with me for long time, because most of us studied in a very passive way. We read, we highlight, we memorize definitions, but we rarely stop and ask ourselves, "Can I actually explain this clearly?" And that's where the Feynman technique becomes powerful. The method i- the method itself is surprisingly simple. First, you choose a topic. It could be anything, a biology chapter, a math concept, a grammar rule,

title: The Power of Journaling: How Writing Brings Mental Clarity
category: Mental Health Vlogs & Personal Video Diaries
transcription: You know, in our crazy, fast-paced world, there's a really simple, almost ancient tool that can make a huge difference in finding some clarity. And that's what we're talking about today: journaling. It might sound simple, but it's one of the most powerful ways to cut through all the noise. So, let me ask you this: does your brain ever feel like a web browser with like a hundred tabs open at once? You're trying to do one thing, but you've got to-do lists, worries, random thoughts, all competing for your attention. It's, it's just exhausting, right? Well, the great news is there is a way to start closing some of those tabs. There's a way to find that clear signal in all the static. And that way? Well, it's journaling. But before we get into the solution, I think it's really important we understand the problem. Why do so many of us feel this way? It really all starts with the state of our modern, and often, very overwhelmed minds. And you know, there's actually some science to back up that feeling of being overwhelmed. Our minds are always, always on. But what's wild is that a huge chunk of that mental energy gets spent on thoughts that are repetitive, unproductive, and sometimes even negative. They just kind of spiral around, causing stress, but never really solving anything. So, how do we get that energy back? How do we point it in a better direction? Well, that brings us to a really simple path forward. And the best part, it doesn't cost anything, and you don't need any special gear. At its heart, this is all journaling really is. It's just this simple act of taking all that chaos swirling around in your head, and giving it some shape on a page. Think of it like having a conversation with the one person who knows you best: yourself. So, what makes it such an amazing tool? Well, for starters, there's literally no barrier to entry. It's free. Plus, it's completely, 100% private. It's a space just for you, where you can be totally honest without ever worrying about being judged. It's just a simple, powerful way to clear out that mental clutter and grow as a person. And hey, this isn't just some feel-good, fluffy idea. There's actually some really solid science that shows just how effective it can be. So, let's take a look at the proof behind the practice. And get this: you don't have to write for hours on end, not at all. Studies have shown that just 15 minutes, seriously, just 15 minutes of writing a day is enough to have a significant, measurable impact on your mental well-being. So, what kind of impact are we talking about? Well, a major analysis of a bunch of studies found that journaling can lead to a real, tangible 9% drop in anxiety symptoms. And the reason it works is pretty cool. When you write your thoughts down, you're literally taking them out of your head. You're externalizing them, which frees up so much mental space. And the benefits go even deeper. That same body of research also showed a 6% decrease in symptoms of post-traumatic stress

title: Level Up Your Life: Tracking Personal Growth with the Apprentice-Master Model 📈🛡️
category: Mental Health Vlogs & Personal Video Diaries
transcription: Tracking personal growth through apprentice, journeyman, master stages. Introduction. We are constantly exploring different paths in our personal development and chasing new quests. Each new search forces us to open the door to fresh knowledge. As this continues, we unknowingly find ourselves buried under piles of information, and when we get stuck, we often don't know what to do next. In this article, I want to draw attention to a method that dates back to the Roman and Hittite states and has helped shape the formation of states that still exist today. Although these organizations were created by states that owed their existence to the labor and effort of their individuals, they actually presented a structure that encompasses the individual's own life cycle. Individuals who found themselves within a ready and continuously developing order integrated into the system very easily, and growth continued uninterrupted. In short, if we want to capture the stability of the ancients while searching for direct sources for our own personal development today, we must learn how they lived and integrate ourselves within an organization suited to that lifestyle. Come, let's look at an example and see how we can adapt our personal growth as apprenticeship, journeyman, and mastery. Our goal is to maintain stability in our lives by making decisions with professional foresight and tracking them through mastery. Historical foundation. Apprenticeship as a liminal stage in medieval English guilds. This structure is most clearly seen in the guild system of medieval England. As Rhiannon Sandy states in her 2022 PhD thesis, Apprenticeship indentures and apprentices in medieval England, 1250 to 1500, apprenticeship was an important liminal stage between childhood and adulthood, during which young men and women were molded into respectable adults. Guild contracts, indentures, clarified everything. The master was obligated to teach the apprentice the secrets of the craft. In return, the apprentice promised to serve bene et fideliter, honestly and faithfully, committing to rules of honesty, confidentiality, avoiding taverns, gambling, and sexual misconduct. The master acted in loco parentis, in place of a parent, and was responsible for the apprentice's moral well-being. This system transformed the individual from a passive learner into a responsible, respected adult, exactly the model of stable growth we seek today. Martin Prak and Patrick Wallis emphasize in Apprenticeship in Early Modern Europe, Cambridge, 2019, that this framework organized both technical and ethical development across Europe. So, how can we, as adults, adapt this

title: The Smile Nobody Questioned (New Spoken Words 2026)
category: Mental Health Vlogs & Personal Video Diaries
transcription: I got really good at smiling. So good, that nobody noticed the war happening behind my eyes. I laughed loud, showed up, answered messages with "I'm good". Even cracked jokes while my chest felt like it was carrying a thousand pounds of silence. And the scary part is, after a while, even I started believing the performance. See, depression doesn't always look like darkness. Sometimes it looks like being tired all the time for reasons sleep can't fix. Sometimes it looks like staring at the ceiling at 3:00 a.m. replaying every mistake like your mind signed a contract with regret. Sometimes it sounds like, "You're not enough! You're falling behind! Everybody else figured life out except you!" And you begin to drown in thoughts nobody else can hear. That's the thing about invisible pain. People only notice broken bones, not broken spirits. So you learn survival tricks. You become the therapist friend who secretly needs saving. You become the strong one because strong people aren't allowed to collapse. You disappear into music, into work, into scrolling endlessly at night, hoping distraction feels something like peace. But silence, silence is dangerous. Because when you sit alone long enough, you meet every version of yourself you tried to outrun. The insecure child, the abandoned heart, the exhausted soul. And one day, I realized I wasn't just fighting depression. I was fighting the version of me that believed I had to earn love by suffering quietly. I thought healing meant never hurting again. But healing is actually waking up and choosing to stay, even when your mind tells you to disappear. Healing is messy. It's crying in parked cars, it's canceling plans to breathe, it's admitting, "I'm not okay." before your breaking point introduces you to the ground.
caption: In this emotionally charged audio clip, a man with a deep, resonant, and expressive voice delivers a powerful spoken-word monologue about his personal battle with depression and the true meaning of healing. His delivery is slow and deliberate, filled with raw emotion, shifting from whispered, somber tones to intense, passionate outbursts. The speech is set against a dramatic, cinematic background score featuring melancholic piano chords and swelling orchestral strings that rise and fall in harmony with the speaker's emotional state. He speaks of the facade of smiling to hide a 'war happening behind my eyes,' the exhaustion of invisible pain, and the dangerous nature of silence. The climax of the piece is both intense and hopeful, as the music swells and the speaker passionately declares that healing is not about never hurting again, but rather a messy, daily choice to stay and admit to not being okay.

title: THIS IS ADDICTION
category: Mental Health Vlogs & Personal Video Diaries
transcription: This is addiction. It's a 3:00 a.m. phone call, the one you knew was coming but prayed never would. It's a doctor standing in a hallway saying there's nothing left to do. It's a mother falling to her knees like her heart just got ripped in two. It's a waiting room full of people blaming themselves for the pain, replaying every moment wondering what they could have changed. Questions you can't outrun, answers you'll never find. This is addiction. It don't just take one life. It leaves empty chairs at the table, every single night. It don't care who you are or how hard you fight. This is addiction. It steals in plain sight. It's a son and a daughter growing up trying to understand why. It's waking up to a world that don't make sense anymore inside.

title: SEMPER FI THROUGH THE STORM
category: Mental Health Vlogs & Personal Video Diaries
transcription: They teach you two words the day you earn the title: Semper Fi. Always faithful. Faithful to your brothers, faithful to your country. But nobody tells you sometimes the hardest battle is the one that follows you home. Yellow footprints in Carolina sand, drill instructor shaping a man, sweating grit in the rising sun, turning boys into the chosen ones. Brothers forged through fire and rain, learning courage through the pain. Every Marine knows what that means, standing tall with the Marines. You can leave the battlefield, but the battlefield won't leave you. Semper Fi through the storm, when the night feels long, God held the line when my strength was gone. War in my mind, but my heart held on. Semper Fi, Semper Fi through the storm. The world sees a Marine and they see strength, they see discipline, they see courage. But what the world doesn't see are the battles that happen in the quiet, memories that don't fade, storms that don't stop just because the war is over. title: Why You've Become Hard to Read
category: Mental Health Vlogs & Personal Video Diaries
transcription: People used to know what you were thinking. You were a open book. Easy to read. Easy to reach. Somewhere along the way, you changed. Now, people say you're hard to read, quiet, contained, difficult to get to. And part of you wonders if something closed off, if the openness you used to have was better than what you are now. It wasn't. You didn't close, you you learned, and there's a difference. If that feels familiar, stay with me. Becoming hard to read is usually the result of being misread too many times, not one big betrayal, just a a slow accumulation. Moments where you said the real thing and it landed wrong, you were opened up and the other person wasn't careful with it. I did this for years, said whatever I was thinking, assumed everyone operated the same way I did. They didn't. And somewhere in that pattern, I got quieter, not colder, just careful. That's not damage, that's data. Quiet isn't the same thing as as closed. They see someone who doesn't broadcast everything and read it as withholding, as coldness, as something being off. But there's a version of quiet that isn't absence, it's presence that's become more deliberate. You're still there, you're still thinking, feeling, noticing. You've just stopped narrating all of it out loud for people who weren't really listening anyway. There's a kind of openness that isn't actually brave, it's just untested. Early openness is easy, you haven't been burned yet. You don't know what happens when you hand someone something real and they don't handle it well. I overshared constantly in my 20s, thought that that was authenticity.

title: If I Fade First - After Everything [Official Lyric Video]
category: Mental Health Vlogs & Personal Video Diaries
transcription:
Some things don't leave
when the door closes.
They just find quieter places
to sit.
I surveyed the room before I spoke a word.
Measure every step like the floor could give way.
The kitchen lights stayed on until morning came.
Nobody slept but nobody said a thing.
Like I could keep the peace that I didn't break.
Good at carrying blame that wasn't mine to take.
My name got tangled up in every argument
like I was born knowing something I never spent.
I spent years
trying to become smaller,
thinking less of me
would make more room for everyone else.
So why do I still flinch when somebody raises their voice?
Why does my chest lock up every time I have a choice?
I built my life around surviving,
forgot that there was another way.
I've been living like a storm was coming,
even on the calmest days.

title: What I Survived [Official Lyric Video]
category: Mental Health Vlogs & Personal Video Diaries
transcription: You call it confusion. I call it what I survived. You call it confusion, 'cause you can't stand what's alive. You hate pain and try to rename it, like that makes you right. You call it confusion, but the wound and the name don't match. You never came to hear me. You came ready to speak. You don't need someone to talk to, you need someone to talk at. That's the difference, that's the bruise. Every wound turns into your sermon. Every silence into proof. You call me lost when I don't fit the neat version in your head. You call it help, but it lands like blame, with that same old voice instead. You hear fracture, you say confused, like saying it twice makes it true. You see something you can't control, so you drag it down till you... You call it confusion, I call it what I survived. You call it confusion, 'cause you can't stand what's alive. You hear pain, then try to rename it, like that makes you right. You call it confusion, but the wound and the name don't match. You use your hurt to talk down, like nobody else has bled, like pain belongs to the loudest mouth, or the one who talks best. That's the poison, that's the trick. You make other people smaller, just to make your version stick. You don't want another opinion.

title: The Space Between My Lines | Official Lyric Video (Full Song)Written by © Kush_Lar 2026 ART-101

transcription: Hum... I don't intend to hide the truth, I only draw what I can see. The pencil seems to know much more than the frightened parts of me. Sometimes I stop before the end, not because I've run out of time. The picture simply asks for things I haven't found inside. If every page could whisper, if every pencil mark could speak, the space between my lines holds the pieces I can't find. Sometimes the picture isn't finished, it's only waiting for its time. Read the words I've never spoken, follow every pencil sign. Sometimes all that's left of me is the space between my lines. Hum... Some people see a simple sketch, a tree, a bird, a little sun. They never see the hidden roads the pencil's walking on. A broken branch, an empty chair, a window open just a crack, tiny clues left quietly for anyone looking back. Every color tells a story, even when it's left behind. The space between my lines holds the pieces I can't find, sometimes...

transcription: We start things off tonight with breaking news. A vacant warehouse in Northwest Portland has been destroyed in a huge four-alarm fire this afternoon. This is at the Centennial Mills site on Northwest Naito, that's near the Fremont Bridge. Thanks so much for joining us, I'm John Adams. Crews were called out around 4:00 this afternoon. They say the fire was burning on the first floor and pushing onto the second. But as you can see, it didn't take long for the flames to take over that entire building. Firefighters had to shut down Northwest Naito to fight the flames. Firefighters say it wasn't safe for them to go inside and they had to fight the fire from the outside. And there was a lot of concern about the building and the water tower on top of it collapsing. And at one point, there was even a grass fire next to the building. Spot fires in this dry vegetation throughout our community, as well as in the trees, that just to the south, upon my arrival there was two- two hoses extinguishing a tree adjacent to an occupied condo complex. Graves says he expects firefighters to be on scene all night long. The Centennial Mills building was a former flour mill, but it's been abandoned for decades now. That's made it a magnet for squatters, homeless camps, and previous fires. In June, Portland police cleared squatters out of the building and arrested one person. City records show the building is currently owned by Stuart Lindquist, the same man who owns the Ice Building along the South Waterfront. A design review was approved for the building, and it had plans for nearly 300 homes and some retail space. We heard gunshot, a lot of rapid fire, it sounded like it was within a block of our house. It was dozens of rounds over multiple blocks. Chaos unfolded early this morning in one Northeast Portland neighborhood. An 18-year-old is now dead, and five other people, including a 15-year-old, are hurt after a shooting that police say started at a house party in the Cully neighborhood. Blair Best spoke with police and people who woke up to that gunfire. The shooting happened early Sunday morning. Police say it appears to be a house party gone tragically wrong. The neighborhood woken up to multiple rounds of gunfire followed by screaming. Some even tell me they saw teens running up and down the streets carrying guns. Dozens of gunshots rang out in this Northeast Portland neighborhood just after 3:30 Sunday morning. It was multiple rapid fire. Bang, bang, bang, bang, bang, bang, bang, bang, bang, bang, bang.

title: Conor McGregor Blows Out Knee in Seconds at UFC Return - Doctor Explains
transcription: Conor McGregor's long-awaited return ended just horrifically after suffering an injury to his right knee on the very first moment of the fight when he tried to throw this aggressive kick. In this video, we'll take a closer look, what I think this injury is, plus the footage of before the fight that showed he may have had an injury coming into this fight to begin with. Welcome back, everybody. I'm Dr. Brian Sutterer, and the goal on the channel is to teach you more about the medical side of the sports world. This was literally the very first thing that McGregor did. He came out, right, the announcers are talking about, he's he's full of energy, right? It's his first fight out. And he goes and throws this crazy ridiculous kick and he lands really awkwardly on that right leg. Now, a lot of people are going to see this. The commentators were talking about, it looked like he blew out his knee. I will admit, yes, this position looks like the classic position that you will see with an ACL tear, in terms of the rotation of how the foot is externally rotated, the idea that we see a little bit of the knee going inward, the trunk is leaning over his injured side. But what you don't see on this injury is the classic pivot shift that you will sometimes see with an ACL tear. Now, that doesn't mean that this is not an ACL tear, but you at least don't see that stereotyped kind of pathognomonic shift forward of the tibia and then pop backwards like we would if you could confirm 100% that this was an ACL. I think looking at it from this view is a little bit better because we can see kind of straight on. So, here, he goes and jumps off of that right side, twists as he lands down. This is a really awkward position for the knee, right? We can see a couple of different things. Number one, we can see how his trunk is leaning over that injured side. That's a strike against you when it comes to an ACL tear. We can see that he's landing on a relatively flat foot, that's going to be strike number two. That foot's a little bit externally rotated, strike number three. This is not a three strikes and you're out situation though, so bad comparison to use there. But as he comes forward here, we don't really see that classic like internal rotation of the lower leg, this knee abduction, the ankle kind of swinging out as the leg rotates inward. You really don't see that very clearly whenever he's coming through

title: What Does a Business Broker Actually Do? (In Under 5 Minutes)
transcription: And tell, tell us what a business broker does? You know, that's a great question, it's a good starting point because I think a lot of business owners don't realize understand what a business broker does, or even that there are business brokers out there who can help represent them through all phases of the sell of their business. So, that's exactly what we do. We are hired by the seller to represent them through every phase of selling the business. And that includes roughly four areas. So, the first area is the valuation of the business and that's really the jumping-off point. That helps business owners understand whether there's a gap between what the business is worth and what the owner needs or expects for their next phase of life. And that's really kind of the first step, that's the first informative piece for business owners to really better understand is what their business would sell for on the open market. We also help business owners assemble their advisory team, and that may include wealth advisors like Jared, transaction attorneys, accountants. And often, your broker has relationships with other people who are competent and expedient when it comes to business transactions. So, your broker will also handle all areas of your confidential marketing strategy, and that includes listing the business on all industry-leading websites, creating the marketing material, and getting that listing confidentially out there for potential buyers to see. We also have a database of thousands of potential buyers that we do send listings out to. Once those buyer leads start coming in, we start screening those buyers. And we're only going to present a seller with buyers who we feel match the criteria that they've told us that it's important to them. We're also only going to present buyers who we feel are ready, willing, and able to purchase the business. Because we really want to

title: Macbook Neo Impressions: Reincarnated!
transcription: Alright, so Apple is doing a week of new release stuff and it's all headlined by what I saw today, which is the newest, cheapest entry to the MacBook lineup: the MacBook Neo. First of all, interesting name. We've never heard that word from Apple before. I thought when it was leaked it was maybe just a code name. I would have bet it's just called "the MacBook" but no, it's actually MacBook Neo. And the basics are this: it is a 13-inch laptop, powered by the A18 Pro chip, 8GB of RAM, 256GB of starting storage, and it is a super thin and decently light all-aluminum laptop. Two USB Type-C ports on the left-hand side, not Thunderbolt. There's a headphone jack on the left as well, and then there's some side-firing stereo speakers. And it comes in four colors: Indigo, Blush, Citrus, and Silver. They all have this sort of a whitish keyboard that is kind of tinted to match the color of the laptop. In person, maybe the lighting is terrible in here, but it was kind of hard to tell when looking at a single laptop. But you can, when they're some next to each other, see that the keyboards are tinted. And there's a 1080p webcam up at the top hidden in that bezel, no notch. And most importantly, the starting price: $599. And this is really interesting. They actually hit the price. This is now, you know, the cheapest entry-level Mac laptop. It's the same price as a Mac Mini, which has actually been one of the best deals in tech for a little bit now, and I think this one's also shaping up to be pretty good value. Now, the X factor is how will the A18 Pro chip perform inside a computer? Now, in case you don't remember, the A18 Pro is the same chip that was in the iPhone 16 Pros last year, but actually, this is a binned version. This is a 5-core GPU version instead of 6-core. But I think in general, there's a lot of tasks that regular people do on regular computers that clearly don't require a ton of power. Web browsing, emailing, shopping, spreadsheet-type of stuff, right? And before I've done any testing, just messing around on this thing for a few minutes, it seems like it would be totally fine for that. I would not expect to edit videos or do anything really intensive on this thing, that would be kind of crazy. But I also wouldn't be surprised if it could handle some light photo editing, some multitasking, and just, you know, generally be a solid computer. Think of it like a Chromebook, but

ప్రొవైడ్ చేస్తాం అనేది చెప్తున్నారన్నమాట. ఈ ఎలక్ట్రిక్ బైక్ ని గుజరాత్ సిఎం గారి చేతుల మీదగా అయితే రివీల్ చేశారన్నమాట. ఇక ఈ ఎలక్ట్రిక్ బైక్ లో మల్టిపుల్ వేరియంట్స్ కూడా అందుబాటులోకి తీసుకొస్తా అంటున్నారు. ఈరోజు మన వీడియోలో ఎవోర్ ఎలక్ట్రిక్ బైక్ కి సంబంధించిన వేరియంట్స్ ఏమున్నాయో? ఇందులో ఉన్న టెక్నికల్ స్పెక్ట్స్ ఏంటి? ఫీచర్స్ ఏంటి? కంప్లీట్ డీటెయిల్స్ ని ఈరోజు మన MVS ఆటో తెలుగు ఛానల్ లో తెలుసుకుందాం. నమస్తే, నేను మీ కృష్ణ చైతన్య మండేలా. మీరు చూస్తున్నారు MVS ఆటో తెలుగు. ఎలక్ట్రిక్ వెహికల్ రంగంలో అడుగుపెట్టాలనుకుంటున్నారా? కానీ ఎక్కడి నుంచి ప్రారంభించాలో అర్థం కావడం లేదా? సరైన ఈవి డీలర్షిప్ ఎంపిక నుంచి, లాభదాయకమైన ఛార్జింగ్ స్టేషన్ ప్లానింగ్ వరకు, మీ అవసరానికి సరిపోయే ఈవి వెహికల్ సెలెక్షన్ నుంచి, కాలేజీ ప్రాజెక్టులకు టెక్నికల్ గైడెన్స్ వరకు, ప్రతి దశలో మీకు తోడుగా ఉంటుంది, ఈవి కుర్రాడు. అనుభవంతో కూడిన నిపుణుల సలహా, స్పష్టమైన మార్గదర్శకం, సరైన నిర్ణయానికి నమ్మకమైన సహాయం. ఈరోజే స్క్రీన్ పై కనిపిస్తున్న వాట్సాప్ నెంబర్ కు మెసేజ్ చేయండి, మీ ఈవి ప్రయాణాన్ని ఆత్మవిశ్వాసంతో ప్రారంభించండి. సో ఎవోర్ కి సంబంధించిన ఎలక్ట్రిక్ బైక్ డిజైన్ అయితే ఇలా కనిపిస్తుందన్నమాట. ఇది వచ్చి EX 2S అనే ఒక పేరుతో అయితే ఈ బైక్ ని అయితే మార్కెట్ లోకి అయితే రిలీజ్ చేశారన్నమాట. సో మీకు సైడ్ ప్రొఫైల్ అయితే ఇలా కనిపిస్తుంది. సో కలర్ ఆప్షన్స్ కూడా ఉన్నాయి. రెడ్ కలర్, అలానే బ్లూ కలర్, బ్లాక్ కలర్, గ్రే కలర్ ఇలా మొత్తం ఫోర్ కలర్ ఆప్షన్స్ లో అయితే అందిస్తున్నారన్నమాట. సో ఇందులో వీళ్ల టాప్ ఎండ్ వేరియంట్ వచ్చి 5 కిలోవాట్ల బ్యాటరీ ప్యాక్ కెపాసిటీతో 260 కిలోమీటర్ల వరకు IDC రేంజ్ అనేది కంపెనీ వాళ్ళైతే క్లెయిమ్ చేస్తున్నారు. అలాగే ఈ ఎలక్ట్రిక్ బైక్ లో 114 కిలోమీటర్ల టాప్ స్పీడ్ కూడా లభిస్తుంది అనేది చెప్తున్నారు అన్నమాట. ఇక బైక్ పరంగా చూసుకున్నట్లయితే కాస్త పెట్రోల్ బైక్ లుక్ లాగానే కనిపిస్తుంది అన్నమాట. ఒక్కొక్క యాంగిల్ లో మనకి బైక్ అయితే ఇలా కనిపిస్తుంది అన్నమాట. సో ముందు వెనక కూడా మీకు డిస్క్ బ్రేక్స్ తోనే ఈ ఎలక్ట్రిక్ బైక్ అయితే లభిస్తుంది. ఇక చార్జర్ చూసుకున్నట్లయితే ఫ్రంట్ సైడ్ మీకు బూట్ స్పేస్ లాగా ఉంటుంది. దాన్ని ఓపెన్ చేస్తే మీకు చార్జర్ కేబుల్ అయితే తీసుకుని మీరైతే చార్జింగ్ అయితే పెట్టుకోవచ్చు అని చెప్తున్నారు అన్నమాట. అలానే వీళ్ళు చెప్తున్న విషయం ఏమిటంటే ఫాస్ట్ చార్జింగ్ అవుతుంది. ఎవ్రీ మినిట్ కి 1.2 కిలోమీటర్లు చార్జింగ్ అయితే చేసుకోవచ్చు అనేది చెప్తున్నారు అన్నమాట. అనేది చెప్తున్నారు అన్నమాట. ఇందులో మీకు ఎకో, సిటీ, ప్యామ్ ప్లస్, స్పోర్ట్స్, అపెక్స్ మొత్తం ఐదు మోడ్స్ లో అయితే మీకు ఎలక్ట్రిక్ బైక్ అయితే లభిస్తుంది అని చెప్తున్నారు. దీంట్లో మీకు 10.5 కిలోవాట్ల పీక్ title: Surplus of Cash in the Business
transcription: Investing surplus cash within the business then. So, when when you invest in surplus cash, and again, you're looking at your cash flow needs within the business, we understand that, business savings accounts, business current accounts, generally speaking, don't pay very much in in terms of interest. Now, I'm mindful of what we were saying before about business relief because having too much cash or investments within the business can impact that. But there might be a reason why you why you need that cash or why you need those investments within the business. Similarly, it might be a holding company or a family investment company where we're looking at the underlying investments and it and it's genuinely for investing. So, you know, the first thing we're always looking at, obviously, is the pensions and and if there's surplus cash can we get it out of the business in a tax-efficient way. Um now, what I will say about holding too much cash, whether that's on a personal basis or or whether it's within a business, a great analogy with that I always think about is that when you're holding on to too much cash, it's like holding on to a snowball. It's melting before your eyes, and that's inflation, because if you're not at least matching the cost of everything going up, then, effectively, you're losing money. The value of that money is falling. And that is difficult with with cash accounts within, you know, within businesses, but we do have um an online cash management platform that we use. There's a few of these around that you can utilize where there's varying cash accounts available anywhere between, currently, 3.5 and 4.5, which are uh business savings accounts. It can be charities, it can be trusts, and it can be businesses. All UK banks and building societies um that have better rates than what you've got, potentially, with a high street bank. Um what we've had clients do is even put the money that they've been saving for corporation tax into something with a 6-month fixed rate, which is higher than what they're getting in the bank, just to park that money, they know it's there, and it'll come out in time to pay the corporation tax bill 9 months after the end of their corporation tax year.

title: Leading Change Webinar Clip
transcription: Hi, and welcome. This is Leading Change from Where You Are, Empowered Strategies for Navigating Transitions. My name is Cassie Blossey. I'm the co-founder of Sageburg Consulting, I'm a nonprofit executive leader, education policy is the core of my background and experience and I love working in the community, specifically around change management in nonprofits and small businesses. One of the things that is really important about nonprofits is that they're so core to our community and, whether they like it or not, they also experience change pretty regularly, and in fact change is the only constant, right? So what I have seen in my experience is that nonprofits that set up systems to help them go through change, uh, experience much more um, long-term success and they see fewer disruptions in their actual services, and so they can meet their impact and mission. So today, we're going to talk about a couple of key areas of change. These three are the top types of change that I see in nonprofits and small businesses every day. Uh, the first one is one that we have a little bit more control over and we'll talk about the next two because they tend to give us a little bit more anxiety, so let's start with planned. Planned change has to do with change that you can anticipate, something that you know for sure is coming up. That can be a retirement, the end of a temporary role, maybe it's the end of a grant, maybe it's something that you knew you were going to start and then had a very clear end date. So when you're talking about planned, uh, change, one of the things that's really important is making sure you have really good communication systems and thinking about, "Okay, we know that this transition's going to happen in March, so we should start setting us, ourselves up for success by thinking about that transition, maybe in January, how are we making sure that everything will be successful once that change happens?" So, you have a lot more control in this area of change. The next two, as I mentioned, not our favorite, but you can still be successful. Emergent change is the unfortunate change that happens when there's something sudden, it's unexpected, sometimes it comes with additional risk, for example, sudden illness or a natural disaster.

A female speaker, Cassie Blazi, co-founder of Sagebrook Consulting, delivers a presentation titled "Leading Change From Where You Are: Empower Strategies for Navigating Transitions." Speaking with a warm, encouraging, and professional tone, she draws on her experience in education policy and nonprofit leadership to discuss the inevitability of change within the nonprofit sector.

She categorizes change into three main types, focusing on "planned" and "emergent" change. Planned change is described as anticipated events, like retirements or ending grants, where structured communication and early preparation (such as planning in January for a March transition) are key to success. In contrast, she defines emergent change as sudden, unexpected disruptions like illness or natural disasters that carry higher risks. Her delivery is well-paced and articulate, with occasional natural pauses and filler words, creating an engaging and informative atmosphere.

title: top marketing strategies to grow your business fast in 2026
transcription: If you're still pasting a single headline and one block of primary text into Facebook and calling it a day, we seriously need to have a conversation. You can and absolutely should be serving up multiple diverse variations for every single ad you run. Facebook actually allows you to upload up to five different headlines and five primary text options for every single ad set. Sticking with just one option is honestly the biggest mistake you can make right now. The entire reason we run ads is to learn things fast about what actually resonates with people. You want to know which creative hooks land, which copy flavors make people stop scrolling, and which lines actually drive the clicks. Setting yourself up for variation means you learn more quality information in a fraction of the time. Here is a super practical workflow that I personally rely on to scale my ad copy effortlessly. Start by writing just one solid headline and one primary text option that you feel good about. Then immediately take that original content and plug it directly into your favorite AI tool for variations. Ask the AI for five alternate headlines, specifically requesting different tones like punchy or benefit-focused. title: Getting started with Claude Cowork
transcription: Claude Cowork meets you where your work happens and allows you to delegate complete tasks to Claude. If it's on your computer, Claude can find and edit it. Describe what you need done, and Claude does it. You can watch it work, steer when it matters, or step away and come back to the results. Claude Cowork is generally available in the Claude Desktop app on macOS and Windows for Pro, Max, Team, and Enterprise users. To get started, open Claude Desktop and click the Cowork tab. In a regular Claude chat, you work with Claude step-by-step. In Cowork, you hand off tasks, and Claude handles the rest while you focus on other work. First, give Claude access to a folder on your computer. Select the folder directory or project you want Claude to operate in. It asks permission before making changes to your file system. Claude can now read, create, and edit files in that folder directly. You can favorite the folders you go to most or select multiple folders to connect disparate data sources. Second, connect your tools. Cowork supports connectors that link Claude to services. These let Claude pull context from where your work already lives. Third, if you've set up Claude in Chrome, Cowork can use it for browser-based tasks, reading web pages, extracting data from sites, and navigating across tabs. Under settings, you can also click the Cowork tab and set global instructions that apply to every session, like context about your role or directions to create files as Word docs instead of markdowns. One thing to keep in mind, your Cowork sessions are stored locally on your device, and the Desktop app needs to stay open while Claude is working on a task. Let's start with something really simple.

title: How to think like a lawyer | Zero-L from Harvard Law School
transcription: Imagine I asked you, what do you learn in law school? Well, you've decided to take this course, so maybe you're more informed than the average person. So instead imagine I asked your college roommate or your parents, assuming they're not lawyers. The image that may come to mind of law school is sun-deprived, bespectacled law students surrounded by large numbers of dusty books, reading intently so they can memorize a bunch of law cases. And don't get me wrong, we do make students read a lot from books, and there's some memorization involved. But that image of someone learning the law by just memorizing things that are already out there is not at all what law school is really about. If it were, law school would be much less fun, and also much less useful. The law is always changing. So if you just learned a number of dry rules, much of what you learned might be outdated by your fifth year in practice. The chief value of legal education is not to know stuff, but to know what stuff to look for, where to find it, how to interpret what you find, what to think when some stuff says one thing, and other stuff says another. And how to use what you find to give legal advice. Let me put this very tangibly for you. If you call up a lawyer on anything other than a very simple question, and without pausing, she quickly gives you a straightforward answer, you should fire her. She's not doing a very good job for you. She's just not thinking like a lawyer. That's a phrase you'll hear a lot in law school, and while we might over-use it a bit, it does capture something important. Law is mostly about questions, choices, and analysis, about thinking and not so much about simple answers. That is the main thing we try to teach you in law school. Yes, we want to teach you a good amount of content about the law. To use an example from a course I teach, civil procedure, we want you to know what claims without subject matter jurisdiction can get jurisdiction by way of being joined to other claims through 28 U.S.C. 1367. If that sounds a bit intimidating at first, that's very normal, it is. But by the end of 1L fall, that knowledge will be at the tip of your brain, or at least somewhere in there.

title: The wild rise of OpenClaw...
transcription: One of the most exciting AI apps for developers in 2026 is Claude. No, not that Claude, but Claude Bot. A free and open-source project that's not just another lame chatbot, but a tool that takes action in the real world 24 hours a day, 7 days per week, without smoke breaks. And it does this while remembering everything, and will hit you up on Telegram or WhatsApp as it automates your entire life. Over the last few weeks, everybody's been going crazy over it. It's racked up over 65,000 GitHub stars in record time, and caused Mac Mini sales to go through the roof, selling out everywhere. In today's video, we'll take a hands-on look at everything it can do, but its popularity has already created some problems. Earlier this week, Anthropic, a company that believes open-source AI is too dangerous for the common man, woke up and chose violence. Claude Bot sounded too similar to their beloved Claude, so they threatened to break the developer's knees with a lead pipe if they don't change the name. So now, Claude Bot is officially called Molt Bot. Actually, no, wait a minute, Molt Bot, that name sucks. Today, they changed the name once again to its final form, Open Clod. A same dangerous AI assistant with a new lobster identity. It is January 30th, 2026, and you're watching the Code Report. Open Clod was created by Peter Steinberger, the founder of the developer tools company PSPDFKit, AKA Nutrient. But just look at this dude's unhinged GitHub profile. It's less of a resume and more of a heat map of pure uninterrupted software obsession. What's crazy is that this guy retired and then came back for an encore by giving us Molt Bot for free, a tool written in TypeScript that wraps Claude and GPT-5 to stay alive 24/7. It can manage your calendar, clean up your email, run scripts, find out how much money you're losing in the stock market, and deploy broken code with absolute confidence. And best of all, it can do all of this from your own tiny, self-hosted VPS, a Raspberry Pi, or even a Mac Mini if you really want to overdo it. There's no reason to pay another random startup $29 per month for the privilege. But to understand its full power, let's put it to work right now. The first step is to install it, which can be done with a single command on any system, although Linux would be the preferred route. Once installed, you'll have access to the Claude Bot or Molt Bot command, or the Open Clod command if you live in the present. And the first thing you'll want to do is go through onboarding. It is going to request that you read the security doc about all the risks involved, but I like to live dangerously. So, let's move right on to the next step by hooking up an AI model provider. You can use anything you want here, but I'm going to go ahead and drop in my Anthropic API key. The Anthropic API does cost money, but you could easily use a free open-source model here as well. Now that that's done, the second major component is hooking up some kind of messenger app like Telegram, Slack, WhatsApp, Discord, etc. I'm going to go with Telegram, which is really easy to set up. Just open up your Telegram

title: Admiral McRaven: The Letter His Mother Wrote Him Before He Left for SEAL Training
transcription: [Applause] I'm going to say three words which you're all going to know immediately and associate with the Admiral. Make your bed. [Laughter] Nine years ago, you made the commencement address here at the University of Texas, and that commencement address went viral. It's become iconic. Everybody can summon those words as an admonition, almost. How did that speech come to you, Bill? Yeah. So Bill Powers, when he was the president here, had invited me to be the commencement speaker, I don't know, three or four months before May. And obviously, you know, anytime you're invited to be a commencement speaker, it's quite an honor. Uh but I had a day job. So I was still I was running the university, I'm sorry, I was running the Special Operations Command. So I started writing the speech about, uh, yeah, maybe two weeks before uh I was supposed to give it, and I'd kind of been mulling some ideas over in my head. So I started writing it on the weekends, a little bit here, a little bit there. And I had this great theme and I thought I was going to pull it all together, and then the Wednesday before the Saturday that I was supposed to give the speech, I realized the speech didn't work. I mean, it wasn't wasn't a good speech. And I I went downstairs. I'd been writing upstairs. I went downstairs, I see Georgeann and I go, "Oh, my God. It, it doesn't work." [Laughter] "It's, it's not a good speech." I said, "I don't know what I'm going to do. I mean, I'm giving the speech in a couple of days." And she says to me, she said, "Well, why don't you write about something you know?" And I thought, "Well, there's an interesting concept." Um. And I told her, I said, "Yeah, but the only thing I know is how to be a Navy SEAL." And she said, "Well, write about that." But at the time, you know, you may recall there had been a number of kind of administration officials that had been, you know, scheduled to give commencement addresses and then the student population kind of voted them down and they didn't end up doing it. And I thought, "You know, if I talk about being a Navy SEAL to uh university students here and, you know, 8,000 students were graduating, I think, that year and 25,000 uh family members," I thought, "I I I'm going to be in uniform. I don't know how this is going to go."

title: Panel Discussion: Putting YOU into your Business Brand (life after "Corporate")
transcription:
Now, Susie, you mentioned that you've, you know, you've come from a different background. You worked in the corporate space, you worked in technology. Um, and you've had to shift from kind of that corporate mindset to a small business owner, someone who is now looking at corporate marketing to marketing your own brand, marketing yourself, marketing your small business. I'd love to know, like, what is one shift that you personally had to navigate making that transition? And what can you offer to other women in this room that are making that shift as well?

It was so hard. I don't know how many other folks left corporate and suddenly had to come out and start talking about themselves. So, I spent a lot of time on that messaging at my at my company. And it was the company's voice, it was the company's style, and it was the company's message. And it was great. I was good at it, right? It was awesome.

And then suddenly, the company wasn't there anymore. Social media was new when I was working in corporate. I never posted my own thoughts and feelings about the world because everything I said was going to reflect back on my company. How was how were they going to look at this, right? I was working for somebody else, it was their brand. I came out and suddenly said, "I am my brand. I can talk about anything I want to talk about because I am my brand." It was scarier than heck, I hated it, I didn't want to talk about myself, I didn't want to sell myself, I didn't want to market myself. It was really intimidating. And so, that was my biggest kind of hurdle as I came into this, right? I had to worry about my skills, I had those. I had to worry about my pricing, I figured that out. But talking about me and putting myself out there was a huge mental shift for me. And I wrote a blog post for the Sunnyvale Chamber of Commerce all about going my own experience going to get photos taken of myself and how terrifying it was and how important it was to get those photos to tell my story. And I was talking about it, I was using my voice, and it was great, and it felt good. And then I got to my about me, and I switched into, "Susie McFaddin is an internationally published award-winning photographer who blah blah blah." And the folks who reviewed it for me said, "That's great, but it didn't sound like you as soon as you started talking about yourself."

title: Clorox (CLX) Stock Analysis 2026 – Graphs, Risks, Opportunities & Valuation ✅
transcription: Clorox is a good example of a defensive consumer staples business that the market once priced for certainty, then sharply repriced when that certainty broke down. In the pandemic era, investors were willing to pay a premium for bleach, disinfecting and household staples because demand looked unusually strong and durable. In hindsight, that was one of the market's big mistakes. It capitalized peak demand as if it were normal demand. Then the opposite happened. The August 2023 cyberattack followed by ERP-related shipment disruption in fiscal 2024 reminded investors that even a boring staples company can suffer real operational volatility. But Clorox also had real successes. Fiscal 2024 gross margin rose to 43.8%, adjusted EPS reached $6.10, and operating cash flow climbed to $1.04 billion as cost savings and recovery actions took hold. Today the stock looks much less loved. Clorox is trading around $132.85 with a trailing PE of about 21.8x. Against management's fiscal 2025 adjusted EPS outlook of $6.55 to $6.80, the stock is trading at roughly 19 to 20x forward earnings. The quarterly dividend is $1.22 or $4.88 annualized, which puts the yield near 3.7% at the current price. For a company that historically often attracted a much richer multiple because of brand strength, resilience and dividend dependability, that is a meaningful derating. The market is no longer paying up for Clorox as a premium safe haven. It is pricing it more like a mature business that has to prove earnings quality again. The reason the multiple is compressed is not that the brands stopped mattering. It is that fiscal 2025 is messy. In Q1 FY25, net sales fell 15% to $1.39 billion, organic sales were down 15%, and gross margin slipped to 38.8% from 42.1%. Management kept full-year guidance, but said results were likely to land toward the lower end because earlier order fulfillment problems caused consumption and market share losses.

title: Navitas Semiconductor (NVTS) Q2 2026 Earnings Explained | Why the Market Misread the $0.95 EPS Loss
transcription: Navitas Semiconductor's second quarter 2026 earnings triggered a sharp market reaction, but the headline tells only part of the story. Investors focused on a reported GAAP loss of 95 cents per share, a result that appeared to miss expectations by roughly 22 times. At first glance, that looked alarming. However, a closer examination of the financial statements reveals a very different picture. The reported loss was driven almost entirely by a one-time non-cash accounting adjustment rather than a deterioration in the underlying business. Once that accounting impact is removed, the operational performance appears considerably stronger. The key comparison begins with two earnings figures. While GAAP earnings showed a loss of 95 cents per share, the non-GAAP loss was only 4 cents per share. At the same time, revenue exceeded expectations by approximately 7%. The difference between those two earnings figures was a $203 million, one-time, non-cash SPACC earn-out accounting charge tied to the company's 2021 SPACC transaction. This adjustment had no impact on cash flow or ongoing operations, and has now been fully recognized, meaning it will no longer affect future financial statements. Operationally, the quarter showed meaningful progress. Revenue reached $10.53 million, representing 22% sequential growth and finishing at the high end of management's guidance. Looking ahead, management projected another 28% increase in revenue during the third quarter. The operational loss also improved modestly, declining from $11.7 million in the previous quarter to $11.4 million. Viewed through that lens, the underlying business improved rather than weakened. Much of the market reaction reflected a comparison between a GAAP result and non-GAAP expectations, effectively comparing two different accounting measures. Once those figures are separated, the operating trend becomes much clearer. Understanding Navitas also requires understanding its position within AI infrastructure. While AI discussions often focus on GPUs and computing power, every AI data center ultimately depends on efficient power conversion.

title: This Week in Review | Fed Meeting, US GDP, Eurozone GDP (July 31, 2026)
transcription: Hello and welcome to This Week in Review. This is our weekly segment that's designed to highlight a few important developments that you might have missed this week, and we'll talk about what they mean for markets, and, most importantly, the potential impact for investors. To stay up to date with our latest market insights, subscribe to our YouTube channel or visit fisherinvestments.com. Now, let's review what happened this week. First, the Fed meeting. On Wednesday, the Federal Open Market Committee, or FOMC, voted to hold the interest rate steady at 3.5 to 3.75%. This was the fifth straight meeting without an interest rate change. It was also a split decision, and three members voted to hike rates by 25 basis points. Headlines quickly seized on the story of a divided Fed, but we wouldn't really read too much into that. Differing opinions among Fed officials tells us very little about what the committee will do next, and dissenting votes don't make a rate hike more or less likely in the meetings ahead. Some investors may also worry that Chairman Kevin Warsh's decision to step back from so-called forward guidance may make monetary policy harder to predict or less transparent. We see that differently. Central banks can, and often do, change their minds without notice based on changing economic data or fundamentals. So rather than trying to guess their next move, we think investors are better served by keeping their focus on the broader fundamentals driving markets. Central bank decisions are just one of many forces shaping the global economy and capital markets, and while we believe a rate hike would be a mistake, the talk today is of small hikes. And, really importantly, even a hike or two from here would leave policy rates within a range that this bull market has already successfully navigated. Additionally, when we look around the developed world, yield curves remain steep and healthy. For long-term investors, that's perspective worth holding on to.

Okay, Katie, I think it's, uh, it's compounded in that they beat the top line revenue by close to $3 billion. So, you have a massive top-line beat, and then you have this bottom-line, uh, huge miss. And in the car business, that's pretty straightforward math. Uh, they are falling to the temptation of feeding the top line, uh, which is a beast to continue to keep growing, with discounts. And when you discount, uh, in the form of price and in the form of the APR that people are paying, and they've done both, you see what happens to margins. They can, they can have a huge top-line beat because of course, people are going to buy a, uh, less expensive product or a below market price product, but then the profitability falls dramatically. And in this case, they missed EPS by more than a third. And I think that's the story here. This is not an AI investment story, this is a story in the base business. And the base business, I think, is giving hints that the, the product lineup is older, it's dated, and in order to move that product, you've got to discount it. And that hits, that hits the bottom line, and that's exactly, I think, what we're seeing here in these earnings.

Yeah, absolutely, a big tension there. And you think about, uh, the issues that they are having when it comes to their base business, the car business. How much of a setback is that for some of the ambitions that we know that the stock has been valued on when you think about, uh, AI, autonomous vehicles, robotics? The list goes on.

Well, I think they, the original plan was you've got a cash-flowing auto business that's going to fund you to the, then, future of autonomous cars, robotaxis, and robots. But you've got to have that cash flow, uh, and that cash flow has to be healthy, uh, and to the extent that your base business isn't funding the future, now you've got to go out and either fund it through equity or debt, uh, on top of this. And so, I think that's the question for investors, is to look forward and, and to really try to determine how much capital it's going to take to get to that future and then, uh, where that capital is going to come from. I think we see this across industries, it's one of the reasons we formed Vistashares is because the, the market tends to focus on end producers like Tesla. And the, the money's actually made in the supply chain. The supply chain has double the profit margins that Tesla has in the end. Uh, and so, although Tesla's getting squeezed by the end market, their supply chain is likely much healthier, and that's probably where investors want exposure versus betting on Tesla as an end producer here.

This guy's every game, it's undeniable that he's going to have some sort of an impact. But I don't think Argentina around him are playing well. I don't. Julián Álvarez? Not good enough. Lautaro Martínez? Not good enough. In midfield, Enzo stepped up and scored a massive goal, but overall would you say his performance has been great? No. And then the other guy, Rodrigo de Paul... Man, he's been awful! So, there are so many players who are not performing well for Argentina, they're getting an escape because the genius at work is stepping up and scoring goals. He scored in six consecutive knockout games, which is... Well, they've they've escaped twice now, haven't they? He's scored eight goals at this tournament, which is ridiculous in itself. How long can that keep going? At some point you're going to come up against a well-oiled team like Switzerland, or even in the semi-final against England, that they're going to beat you because they've got just as good a defense that can stop you. I'll be intrigued to see how Switzerland play out this game, though. Cuz, because they know if, if you're watching Egypt, their counter-attacks were so good. So, Switzerland do choose to sit in that sort of mid-low block, where they won't be as deep as Egypt, they won't sit, you know, six at the back. But they know they are so controlled. Second clean sheet on the bounce for Switzerland, obviously started off, you know, with a tie against Qatar, but they've grown and grown into this tournament. Of course, it's the biggest test both for each, each team. That's the beauty of knockout, the further you get the harder, harder it's going to be.

title: The Highest-Paid Podcasters Of 2026
transcription:
Today on Forbes, the highest paid podcasters of 2026.

When Jay Shetty started his podcast, On Purpose, in 2019, he remembers people telling him he was too late. The medium was already saturated, they said, with little room for growth. And wasn't he really just a content creator?

Seven years later, the 38-year-old self-help guru hosts one of the most popular podcasts in the world, competing not only with the biggest TV, radio, and internet-native talk shows, but blurring the lines between them entirely. Just as many people watch his lengthy interviews with celebrities, including Michelle Obama and Matt Damon, on YouTube, as listen on the iHeartMedia Network. Distribution deals that Forbes estimates paid Shetty $21 million over the past 12 months.

And when those deals expired this year, Shetty landed a new kind of contract, in which the audio and video of his show will not only be distributed by Spotify, it will also stream on Netflix, with the two companies combining to pay him an estimated $100 million over the next 3 years. Shetty tells Forbes, quote, "When I started, video wasn't normal for a podcast. Now we have the four largest streamers bidding for the show. To see that kind of interest and enthusiasm was pretty amazing, for me and for the industry overall."

The impressive thing about mega-deals like Shetty's is that, unlike the makers of movies, TV, or other forms of entertainment, podcasters retain ownership of their shows' underlying IP, meaning networks and platforms are paying millions just to license it as a distributor and ad sales partner for a set number of years. That's one reason why premium streaming giants like Netflix, Hulu, and Tubi had largely ignored the industry's rise over the past decade, allowing YouTube to grow into the largest podcasting platform in the world.

But beginning in 2025, hoping to cut into YouTube's dominance over engagement time, the streamers have made a splashy entrance. Industry dealmakers say that after Netflix's initial $1 million to $2 million bids for top podcasts were roundly rejected, the streamer adopted a strategy similar to the one it used previously to capture market share in scripted television: overpaying to lure talent away from incumbent platforms. Offers of $10 million or more per year, on a one- or two-year trial term, eventually convinced marquee shows from Spotify, iHeart, and Barstool Sports to sign on. Goalhanger, a UK-based podcast network, reportedly landed $19 million from Netflix to stream just 40 episodes of its daily talk show, The Rest Is Football, during the World Cup. The thing is, this whole confrontation just escalated over the course of one single chaotic weekend. Let's walk through the timeline. Okay, just look at how this played out. On Friday, the Supreme Court comes out and rules the president's tariffs are unconstitutional. Now, these were tariffs he levied under a specific law for national emergencies. But then, just hours later, he openly defies them, announcing a new 10% tariff anyway. By Saturday, he's on social media, hiking it up to 15%. And then, by Monday morning, we get that post where he claims the court's decision actually expanded his authority. We're talking 72 hours where a Supreme Court ruling was not just ignored, but completely flipped on its head. And this, right here, really gets to the core of the whole thing. On one side, you have the court's official judgment, a clear check on executive power. And on the other, the president's direct rebuttal, basically saying he doesn't need Congress. It's that classic constitutional friction point, right? The judiciary's check on power being met with a declaration of unchecked authority. And look, this whole showdown wasn't just some abstract debate about the constitution. It had immediate, very real world consequences for the economy and for America's standing on the world stage. The international reaction was swift and, frankly, pretty bewildered. The head of the European Parliament's Trade Committee, Bernd Lange, he just called it pure tariff chaos. Now, what's really fascinating here is how the American public already felt about all this. title: Heather Cox Richardson Video Summary: Supreme Court Expands Presidential Power (June 29, 2026)
transcription: For over a century, unassuming buildings like this have served as the quiet engine rooms of the American government. Inside, thousands of civil servants do the unglamorous work of regulating markets and keeping the country running. Starting in the late 19th century, Congress began building a specific feature into these independent agencies. They were intentionally designed as bipartisan bodies, deliberately insulated from the direct control of the President. The logic was simple. Keeping the air clean, ensuring consumer products are safe, and stopping monopolies requires technical expertise that doesn't change with every election. By keeping the executive branch at arm's length, Congress created a buffer. It guaranteed that decisions affecting public safety and financial security were driven by scientists and economists rather than political favors. In a single morning, with a landmark 6-to-3 decision, the Supreme Court erased over 90 years of established legal doctrine. President Trump immediately hailed the decision as a monumental victory, calling it the largest expansion of presidential power in over a century. He is correct about the scale of the change. The ruling legally grants the President the power to fire the head of any independent agency at any time for any reason. To understand how a foundational power of the United States government was dismantled overnight, we have to look at the legal theory that made it possible. The test case began in March 2025. The President abruptly fired Rebecca Slaughter, the last remaining Democratic member of the Federal Trade Commission. Since 1935, the standard for removing someone from these commissions was strict. You had to prove neglect of duty or malfeasance. But Trump argued he could fire her because her presence was inconsistent with his administration's priorities. This defense relies on the unitary executive theory, a framework conservative strategists have built since the 1980s. The core argument: as head of the executive branch, the President holds absolute authority over everything within it. No other branch can limit his control. By neutralizing Congress's ability to shield these agencies, this theory bypasses the legislative process. It takes national regulatory power and concentrates it into the hands of one person.

title: Dow Chemical International Private Limited Vs Commissioner of State Tax
transcription: Good morning friends. Today, let us understand a very important case law: Dow Chemicals Internationals Private Limited versus the Commissioner of the State Tax. A very important judgment, which will help you to understand. This judgment has come by the Appellate Tribunal, Delhi. The the subject matter is foreign entity procurement service for the group companies taxable as imports, not intermediary services. Let us understand in detail. The appeals were dismissed and the first appellate authority order confirming the rejection of refund claim were upheld. The tribunal ruled that the procurement services received by the Indian entity from its foreign group companies are taxable as import of service under the reverse charge mechanism, rather than qualifying as an intermediary service, which would place the supply outside India. The key reason was the foreign entity provides core procurement services on its own account as an independent contractor, not merely ancillary facilitation services between the two principles. The impugned action: the Joint Commissioner of the State Tax Appeals confirmed the rejection of refund claim for the IGST paid under the reverse charge mechanism on the procurement services received from the Dow Europe GmbH for the period January 22 to June 22, totalling approximately Rupees 13 lakh, crores. title: FP1 Highlights | 2026 Barcelona-Catalunya Grand Prix
transcription: A brand new race at a very familiar circuit. First practice ahead of the inaugural Barcelona-Catalunya Grand Prix. George Russell has been disappointed by recent results. A combination of bad luck, poor planning, and a teammate in white-hot form have left him 68 points back in the driver standings, now in third place behind Lewis Hamilton. But he found something in FP1 in Barcelona, topping the tables with a lap time of 1 minute 16.363. Ferrari have brought a slew of upgrades to Spain, including a new front wing and endplate, a redesigned floor, reshaped sidepods, and amendments to the diffuser. Added to the changes already brought in Miami, the Scuderia will be hoping these new bits will bring them much closer to Mercedes. Charles Leclerc got a little sideways at turn 10, trying out unfamiliar aerodynamics. Incidentally, the last Ferrari winner at the circuit was Fernando Alonso in 2013. The two-time champ is one of the two Spaniards contesting the weekend, the other being Carlos Sainz, who failed to finish in Monaco last time out after being tagged twice during the late restart. His first session at one of his two home races this season didn't start too well either. The Williams driver, unable to get going in the pitlane. His FW46 pushed back into the garage for a fix. Once out on track, Sainz caused some consternation for Liam Lawson. "Why, what are these guys doing? Just middle of the track?" "Classic, mate." There was a new look, too, to the VCARBs, Racing Bulls opting for a football-inspired livery and teamwear this weekend as the Copa América gets underway across the pond. title: Day 1 Highlights | 2026 Bahrain Pre-Season Test 1
transcription: F1 is back for the first official test session of the season. All 11 teams and 22 drivers are present for 6 days of running across 2 weeks at the Bahrain International Circuit. McLaren entered the 2026 season as reigning back-to-back Constructors' Champions, and it was Oscar Piastri in the car for the morning of Day 1. The Aussie, who had battled for last season's Drivers' Championship until the very final round, was on the pace from the off in Bahrain. Despite McLaren running just over half the number of laps of Mercedes in Barcelona, the Woking-based outfit were raring to go in Bahrain. Piastri, second fastest in the morning session, just 2/10 of a second behind Max Verstappen. The Australian gave Turn 10 a wide berth following Aston Martin's Lance Stroll, but completed 54 laps before the lunch break. 2025 World Champion Lando Norris took over for the afternoon session, topping the Day 1 times with a 1:34.669. The Brit added a further 58 laps to McLaren's total, ensuring they ended the day with well over 100 tours of the circuit. George Russell was the only driver other than the title protagonists to win a Grand Prix in 2025, the Brit victorious on two occasions at Canada and Singapore. And the Silver Arrows were in fine form throughout shakedown, logging 500 laps in Barcelona, more than any other team. On to Bahrain, and Mercedes were again getting the laps in. Russell ran the morning session, completing 56 laps, before teammate Kimi Antonelli took over for the afternoon. The Brit did have a little trouble at the off-camber Turn 10, running wide on three separate occasions. Antonelli's running was delayed after Mercedes found an issue while changing setups, but the Italian was able to hit the track, completing 30 laps despite a wild snap at Turn 4. Team Principal Toto Wolff, offering his thoughts on Mercedes' progress so far: "I think everything goes according to the plan we have. You know, it isn't smooth sailing. We have complication on car balance, which are a little bit more articulated here than they were in Barcelona, obviously due to the hot conditions. And we've seen a very, very strong Verstappen this morning. So, you know, we have to get our act together, all of us, and then maybe by the end of the test we will understand more whether what we've done is good, and good enough." Max Verstappen described 2025 as his greatest-ever season, just 2 points away from a fifth world title, despite driving a car which, quote, "he hated at times". The Dutchman excelled to lead the most laps, claim the most pole positions, and win

title: FP2 Highlights | 2026 Monaco Grand Prix
transcription: Second practice in Monte Carlo. F1's finest with another hour of track time ahead to really get to grips with the Circuit de Monaco. Many have touted Ferrari as the team to beat on this narrow, twisty course, where downforce rather than extreme speed rules. And so it proved in FP1 when Charles Leclerc had been fastest from teammate Lewis Hamilton. The seven-time world champion, playing catch up in this session, he flirted with disaster on an early quick lap. Oh, you just feel it's a place that you can split a Formula One car in two if you get it wrong. It's that difficult and that high speed with no barrier margin. Three times a winner on these streets, he continued to push throughout the session, locking up approaching the Nouvelle Chicane, and then taking a whole bunch of curb at the same spot the next time around. My word, that's more curb than I've seen so far down at that chicane, I think. Hamilton on the, on the edge of rear grip, pings it over the curb, bounces through. And it was the Briton with the bragging rights in this session. His lap of 1 minute 13.026, more than a tenth quicker than Leclerc's best effort for P2. The teammates even had a little race after the flag. Great foretaste perhaps for Sunday's main event. Max Verstappen had not been entirely happy with his ride in FP1, despite a decent P3 performance. This time out, he seemed much more hooked up, especially on the soft tires, and managed the same placing again. Only this time, he was a bit closer to the Scuderia drivers. Red Bull teammate Isack Hadjar, who crashed out of FP1, was P6 this time around, his mechanics working wonders in the interim. There was a hairy moment for George Russell early doors. Oh my word, the car getting loose through the first part of the swimming pool. He will need an underwear change. He was later blocked on a fast lap by a slow-moving Gabriel Bortoleto. The Briton believes he's had more than his fair share of bad luck so far this season, but was upbeat coming into the weekend, feeling the odds would even out across the year. He's currently P2 in the drivers' championship, some 43 points behind Mercedes teammate Kimi Antonelli, but he was one place ahead of the Italian in second practice, P4 after the hour. It was a short session for reigning world champion and defending Monaco master, Lando Norris, who encountered a technical problem...

transcription: All right. Order. Order in the court. This is New Jersey versus Donovan. Is the prosecution ready to present his case? It is, Your Honor. And let me just say, it's my honor to be here. No. No, none of that. Don't be cute. This is a courtroom. Now, over to the defendant. Mr. Donovan, since you do not have an attorney, the court has appointed you a public defender. Thank you, Your Honor. But before he gets here, I should probably warn you. He's Sebastian Maniscalco. Like the world-famous comedian? Yes, but I promise he's nothing like what you've seen on TV. Bailiff, please let him in. You're not going to believe this. I'm a lawyer now! I went to night school, and I passed the test. I cancelled the gig to be here, and my agent was like, "Why would you do that?" Sebastian, you are a character. Now, on to the much less delightful prosecutor. Um, all right. I'm a little thrown. I didn't expect the public defender to be Sebastian Maniscalco. But Your Honor, the case is simple. On February 19th, Mr. Donovan walked into a department store and allegedly walked out wearing $5,000 worth of stolen merchandise, including a designer suit, shoes, and a belt. Let me tell you something about a belt, okay? When I was a kid, the belt wasn't to keep the pants up. It was to keep the volume down. Okay? I never saw my dad put the belt on. I only saw him take it off. And my dad, and my dad, I don't know if your dad did this, but my dad, I don't know if your dad did this, but my dad, I don't know if your dad did this, but my dad, he used to pop it twice, he used to go pop, pop, and then it was belt to ass! Objection, Your Honor. None of that was relevant, and I know the jury couldn't possibly follow what he was saying. Uh, very well. Would the court stenographer read it back, please? I never saw my dad put the belt on, I only saw him take it off. And my dad, I don't know if your dad did this, but my dad, I don't know if your dad did this, but my dad, I don't know if your dad did this, but my dad, he would snap it twice, pop, pop, and then belt to ass. Is the baby happy now?
