title: Day 1 Highlights | 2026 Bahrain Pre-Season Test 2
transcription: Back to Bahrain for the final three days of testing ahead of the season opener in Australia, in just over two weeks' time. Both Mercedes and Red Bull suggested the other were the team to beat after one week of running in Bahrain. Max Verstappen hinted the Silver Arrows were hiding their ultimate pace, while Toto Wolff proposed the Milton Keynes outfit were the team to beat, with the Red Bull able to deploy more energy down the straights. Mercedes were top of the pile on week one, setting the fastest lap, more than half a second quicker than anyone else. But Red Bull logged over 60 more laps than the German outfit across the week, albeit neither team were in the top five of laps completed. Ferrari sporting director Laurent Mekies played down their chances ahead of the season. We very well know the size of the mountain that is still in front of us, we just had a, a very good start at it. We know we are going to run into a, a number of uncomfortable moments where the gap to competition will be too big, where, where the car will stop on track, or, or will not get out of the garage like, like this morning, unfortunately where we got an issue with is axle. So, it's part of the game, but we are happy to be in the game, and, and it's, you know, it's going to be a, a huge mountain from now on. So, the performance shown by the top guys is, is stratospheric, and it's going to be a, a huge development race, chassis side, PU side, but it's, it's what we all love. McLaren achieved the joint highest lap count of the first test, tied on 422 with Williams. But it was a scruffy start to the second week for Lando Norris. The Woking camp battled his brakes on multiple occasions. First, a moment at turn one, before giving turn ten a wide berth. But the Brit's biggest lockup was as he entered the pits with the morning session coming to a close. Well, that was just a driver trying to push the limit of braking, and again we're seeing the propensity of these cars to have big lockups. Almost, that looks like it's a massive power unit failure, the amount of smoke coming off the back there. The Woking camp clocked 54 laps in the morning, but seemed to struggle as he pushed the boundaries of his new MCL35. Sainz added 70 laps to McLaren's day-one efforts, ending the day second fastest. Ferrari turned heads on week one, having completed 420 laps, and setting the fastest non-Mercedes lap time. A real positive sign for those in red. Charles Leclerc topped the morning session, three-tenths of a second faster than Norris in P2. The Monegasque handing over to Sebastian Vettel for the afternoon. The four-time world champion had a wobble at turn six, on course to setting the day's seventh fastest time. It's an exciting time with this new generation of car as well, because it's all brand new, we are all trying to figure it out, um, on the go, and as where last year we were locked into a car that ultimately I inherited, this is a car that I've been able to be a part of developing on the simulator for the last, you know, 10 months, 8 months, and so like a bit of my DNA is within it, so

George Russell and Kimi Antonelli, the two fastest men on track, the Briton quickest with a time of 1 minute 31 and all the sixes. All teams have to run a set number of rookie racers in FP1 sessions over the course of the season, and Aston Martin took their first opportunity in round three. American reserve driver Jack Crawford sitting in for Fernando Alonso, who arrived late to Suzuka due to the birth of his first child. Congratulations, Nando! A few new circuit-specific liveries on display today. Racing Bulls was sporting what they're calling their Spring Edition colors, bags of red adorning their usual scheme. Haas have gone full Japan, their cars resplendent with Godzilla images celebrating their season-long tie-in with that famous Japanese entertainment company, Toho, responsible for the destruction of many a model city over the years. And current Constructors' Championship leaders, Mercedes, were in predator mode, their cars and overalls with distinct wolf motifs, part of a collaboration with a Japanese fashion brand. George Russell has had a fine old time so far this year leading the drivers' standings after his wins in Melbourne and the Shanghai Sprint. He had a scary moment going through Spoon. title: Day 2 Highlights | 2026 Bahrain Pre-Season Test 1
transcription: Day two of testing in Bahrain. Eight further hours of running for teams and drivers to better understand their 2026 machines. Turn 10 was once again a talking point on the second day of running. The tricky off-camber corner caught out the majority of the runners on day one. And it was Sergio Pérez first to head off-piste after a big lockup in his Red Bull. The Mexican also brought out the day's first red flag, his team quickly fixing the issue, allowing him to return to the action soon after. But it was Alex Albon who locked up, not once, not twice, not thrice, but four times into the troublesome turn 10. The Thai driver also had a mishap at turn one on two occasions before setting the fifth fastest time of the morning. Two of the most experienced drivers weren't immune to a mishap either, both Fernando Alonso and Nico Hülkenberg locking up and running off at the 10th turn. Despite this, the German was optimistic with the progress made in Bahrain so far. I think good step forward in terms of performance, in terms of reliability and just, you know, being able to get laps in, to get kilometers on the car. We've made some some big steps forward there, you know, between Barcelona and here. Then, you know, Bahrain is a very, very different circuit to Barcelona, you know, much more stop-and-go, low-speed dominated. It's a very hard, you know, and unforgiving track that really exposes a lot of weaknesses usually, you know, and historically from from any car because the rough tarmac, kind of low grip, very windy, hot track temp, so, you know, it's a there isn't many other, you know, tracks that or where you find the harder conditions. So it's a it's a true good test. Teammate Gabriel Bortoleto would take over for the afternoon, the Brazilian struggling for purchase as he tested the limits of his 2026 challenger. It's uh it's like teaching a baby how to walk and and talk, and um yeah, we need to do this uh as quick as possible and uh in a good way as well. Charles Leclerc started the day for Ferrari, having set over 130 laps alongside Lewis Hamilton on Wednesday. The Monégasque driver claimed seven podiums last season but was unable to add to his eight Formula One race victories. A positive week in Spain...

title: Day 2 Highlights | 2026 Bahrain Pre-Season Test 2
transcription: The paddock had eyes for just one team on Thursday morning. Ferrari debuted a fascinating rotating rear wing, which activates via a central pivot, flipping the entire upper element a full 180 degrees. Now, I want you to pay attention to the rear wing on the Ferrari SF-26. Now, what we're talking about is the upper element of the rear wing, and you can see it very clearly just sitting on top there. Now, watch it go back into corner mode. There you go, the wing has fully rotated around. Ferrari has discovered something quite clever in the regulations, I feel. It doesn't specify that the wing has to be mounted the right way up when the active aero is deployed. An upside-down wing, aircraft wing configuration, should reduce aerodynamic drag because it's even generating a bit of lift, and then they've come up with a mechanism to allow it to rotate all the way around. The team in red will hope this innovation can propel them up the leaderboards, having completed 2025 without a race victory. Hamilton completed just the five laps in the morning set after Ferrari investigated an issue with the chassis. Team principal Fred Vasseur cautious to label themselves as the team to beat ahead of the new season. I think everybody is doing innovation, sometimes it's visible, sometimes it's not. I'm sure that our competitors and everybody on the grid is doing exactly the same. That is so that the last two bits that we brought on on track were visible from outside, but it's it's not a big difference with the others, and I don't know if it will be for Melbourne or for the next one. Other teams struggling for laps were Racing Bulls and Audi. Neither completed more than 30 laps across the opening 4-hour session. Despite this, Bortoleto clocked an impressive lap on the prototype tire, the fifth fastest of the morning session. Nico Hülkenberg took his seat for the afternoon, completing over 70 laps while setting the seventh fastest time. It was a trickier time for Liam Lawson in his Racing Bulls. A massive double-front lockup at Turn 1 was followed by a mistake at Turn 11. Most of the time, you'd see them just straighten up and and go offline. I wonder if they were under strict orders not to go over the curb or something and he's and he's out of desperation, just thinking, "Somehow, find some front grip, and don't send me over that that bigger curb." Max Verstappen was in for the day at Red Bull. The Milton Keynes outfit, who missed significant running on Wednesday, got back on track with the four-time champ at the wheel. Despite running over the curbs at Turn 11 and locking up while attacking Turn 4, the Dutchman completed 56 laps in the morning, setting the second fastest time. A smooth afternoon saw Verstappen end the day with nearly 140 laps. He clocked the third fastest time of the day. In general, for us, it has been a very positive start to the year. transcription: Some, some people call me a survival expert. Well, as a survival expert, I want to clear up a common misconception. Survival is not something we just do in the woods. It's something each and every one of us has to do every single day. And whether you're building a fire, gutting a moose, or drafting a motion, we're just trying to survive as best we can with the resources we have. So, I would like to help give you some advice to survive whatever is coming next. And while I do not know what your future holds, I can tell you that the world is changing at a terrifying and fascinating pace. You know, so, here I am, I'm 47 years old, I'm not properly old yet, and, I've seen some crazy stuff. I remember watching the Berlin Wall come down live on television as a child. I remember hearing about the internet for the first time, and I thought it was a fake. I thought, I didn't understand that. I was an adult the first time I ever saw an email. I was married when 9/11 happened. And the year before I went to law school, this thing called YouTube was invented. I was practicing for 3 years before I ever got my first social media account. I've seen 7 US wars, 6 recessions, and I've survived one global pandemic so far. I'm only 47. I don't know what the next 40 years holds for you. But, I doubt any of us are going to get through it without seeing terrible and amazing things. We don't know what these changes are going to be, but we do know they're coming. You need to be ready to grab the opportunities that are going to come in this changing world. And, you need to be ready to survive the storms. And, the best survival advice I can give you is very pragmatic. I would say, save some money. It's pretty simple, but it's not. The best, the most important things are often simple, but hard to do.

title: YouTuber ‘Reckless Ben’ BREAKS SILENCE amid legal battle over missing Legos | Jesse Weber Live
transcription: Tonight, Reckless Ben is here. Yeah, in just a minute, the YouTube star is going to talk with us exclusively about his big legal win in the mystery of the missing LEGO. Yep, a judge just granted him the right to talk again. This is a big development. I got to give you a background though, a quick look at how this whole LEGO legal drama unfolded, okay? It all started when an Oregon family entrusted a franchise of a chain called Bricks & Minifigs to sell their reportedly $200,000 Star Wars LEGO set on consignment. But, the franchise was apparently sold, and the LEGO owners say they never got their LEGO, they never got paid. Now, the family sued the franchise claiming their agreement was breached, that Bricks & Minifigs stole the LEGO collection, and that is when Reckless Ben got on the case. He allegedly traveled to Utah where the franchise executive lives, reportedly started documenting attempts to make contact at his property, posted videos, all going viral. The executive apparently called police, led to Ben getting arrested twice, and as we reported, Bricks & Minifigs also filed a lawsuit against Ben. And, that brings us to this week. Ben is facing a total of four criminal charges. They're all misdemeanors. Provo, Utah, he's charged with disorderly conduct, also reportedly commercial obstruction for allegedly going to the Bricks & Minifigs corporate headquarters. Ben tells us he was there to ask for the LEGOs back. Over in American Fork, Utah, he's charged with stalking and residential picketing for allegedly going to the franchise owner, Josh Johnson's house. Now, Reckless Ben just scored a big legal win. This is when a Utah federal court, this judge lifted the ban that had been on him, posting videos related to Bricks & Minifigs. This was a TRO. However, the revised order still prohibits Ben from coming within 100 meters of any Bricks & Minifigs stores or offices, prevents him from making any threats. Now, we've reached out to Bricks & Minifigs for a statement today, but we haven't heard back. The company has maintained it does not have the LEGO, and in a statement to local media, they said that this issue in its civil case against Ben, real name, Ben Schneider, is going to be addressed through private mediation. It hopes to resolve everything in the coming weeks. But for now, Ben says he got his freedom back, his freedom of speech back. He's already made a new, a new YouTube video. Here's an exclusive sneak peek.

transcription: Sheriff, um, you're Sheriff of Durham County? Yes, sir. Yeah, beautiful, beautiful parish. Or we call our counties parishes. Beautiful county. You believe that people should be able to violate federal immigration laws without consequences, don't you? No, sir, I do not. title: Haley Stevens vs Abdul El-Sayed: How Dems can regain trust from Jewish, Arab-American voters
transcription: And we'll dive right into that right now. You've heard many people ask the question about AIPAC, and it seems as though on many instances, you haven't directly answered the question. Do you see why some people are bothered by the fact that so much money, $40+ million, has come from AIPAC, uh, for these PACs to talk about you and to promote you and to put them, put you up as their candidate? Yeah, and I, I appreciate the question, Roop, because this moment in this country and here in Michigan, people have every right to be frustrated about our campaign finance system. My opponent here on the stage, Abdul, he's got a super PAC that his father-in-law funds that has millions of dollars going into it. And look, in terms of foreign policy, you know, Abdul and I do differ. I believe in a two-state solution. He has attacked me by name for purporting that the people of Palestine and the people of Israel deserve to live side by side, peacefully. The goal is always long-term peace. And also, the Prime Minister of Israel has attacked me by name. They both represent the extremes. Look, Michiganders want peace, they deserve to see peace, and that is where I have always cast my vote, and the, that is the work that I want to do for Michigan and the US. But Congresswoman, specifically about AIPAC money, more than $46 million has been spent on AIPAC spending to back your campaign. A lot of people wonder if that is something where there, you know, you're going to do their bidding when you, should you win this seat. Is that something should, people should be concerned about, and if not, why not? Absolutely not, Roop. Look, I have been very clear, consistent, and transparent. And I have continued to be. I want to see long-term peace. I want to see a two-state solution. I am deeply proud to represent one of the largest Jewish populations in, uh, a congressional district in the country. This is a community that I have grieved alongside, that I've mourned alongside, and have fought to bring the hostages home. And I'm still working to get us to long-term peace. But no concern about the $46 million plus spent on the behalf of AIPAC that should worry people about perhaps you doing their bidding, should you win the seat? Well, I don't think there's much difference between uh, super PACs going in for Abdul or super PACs going in for me. We have a problem with campaign finance reform in this country. I have an A-grading from End Citizens United

title: Wisconsin Democrats debate policing, taxes, school vouchers in gubernatorial primary race
transcription: We are less than two weeks away from the primary elections to replace outgoing Wisconsin Democratic Governor Tony Evers. Last night, the candidates competing for the Democratic nomination squared off on the debate stage. They were asked about the deadly shooting of a Black man by a Madison police officer last week. Now, all agreed that law enforcement should not be defunded. Governor cannot defund police, and I'm not here to govern by slogan. I would not sign a budget that reduce funding because, obviously, that police department needs the funding to have body cameras. I want my kids and every kid to be safe in our communities, and I want law enforcement officers to be safe in our communities. There's been a generation of disinvestment and a broken, uh, system between the state, the- the broken partnership between state and local government. And so, we need to make sure that we're robustly funding that. We cannot defund the police. We should be investing in public safety, and that doesn't mean more money to police officers. That's like investing in, in, in, systems like the community violence interruption. And the winner of the Democratic primary for Wisconsin governor will face off against presumptive Republican nominee Congressman Tom Tiffany in November. Let's bring in CBS News Congressional Reporter Torian Small with more on this. Torian, good morning. So, we just saw all the Democratic gubernatorial candidates agree on one issue. What are the key issues they don't agree on? Yeah, I think what was interesting about what we saw last night is this, you know, vast field was really looking to distinguish themselves while not the- veering off too much. We've seen, uh, some of these same candidates in previous races before, Mandela Barnes obviously having, uh, the most name ID considering he was the former Lieutenant Governor, and he ran for Senate not too long ago, unsuccessfully though, I should add, uh, but most of them made the case that they are largely in line with others, just small nuances. When it came to, uh, school vouchers, for example, a lot of them agreed that, uh, they wanted to see a phasing out of the program, so what others say they wanted to eliminate it outright, uh, uh, altogether. We also saw, uh, with the issue of increasing taxes for the ultra wealthy. Uh, I believe it was Hong and Barnes who, uh, came up with the plan, but

title: Kangana's 'Generation Gutter' Remark Sparks Debate After Hrithik's Viral 'Sorry' Trend
transcription: Are you also one of those people who saw Sorry Hrithik trending on social media and wondered what this story is about? Well, I'll give you the entire context later, but let me tell you that actor Hrithik Roshan has now reacted to this trend and urged people that they should lead with facts rather than social media sentiment. He also kind of clarified on social media influencer Freddy Bird's post that he isn't getting carried away by all the support that's coming his way amid Kangana Ranaut's backlash. Now, I'll again come to this later, but let me tell you that the ongoing war of words between Kangana Ranaut and GenZ protesters have been going on for a while now. Of course, she made some comments, called them gutter generation and that kind of sparked a flood of memes, social media posts and also resurfaced a lot of old news and her clips from her films. And amid the discourse, another discussion that kind of took fire was Kangana Ranaut and Hrithik Roshan's long-standing legal issue and, of course, Bollywood gossip, if we can say. And that led to people saying that we need to apologize to Hrithik Roshan and Sorry Hrithik became the new hashtag that people started talking about. The trend also gained momentum when Cockroach Janta Party spokesperson Saurabh Das commented, I'll read out his comment when, of course, Kangana made some personal remarks and he mentioned, "My friends were texting me and asking why is she after your life. One of them said that I may look a little like a young Hrithik Roshan. This is what my friends told me. I was pleasantly surprised. Why should someone like her attack someone like me?" And his statement soon fueled this entire viral trend of people apologizing to Hrithik Roshan and kind of drawing parallels to a 10-year-old controversy between Hrithik Roshan and Kangana. And one such, of course, post was shared by influencer Freddy Bird and on his Instagram handle, he just posted a black picture with red text and that the word red, "The world owes an apology to Hrithik Roshan." And a lot of actually film industry people, there've been actors, crew, technicians, and even Hrithik Roshan's family that has liked those that post. And Hrithik also, just a few hours back, commented on that post and kind of clarified his stand on this entire trend.

Well, I don't think it's fair that California taxpayers who can barely afford their own health coverage should be paying for the healthcare of citizens of other countries. And if you look at the, um, record of Javier, it's exactly what Chad was just saying, that you cannot believe that any change will come from these people. He, as Health Secretary, dismantled the unit in HHS that was supposed to crack down on fraud. Billions of dollars of fraud as a result of his rule as HHS Secretary. And there's another point I think we have to acknowledge. We learned today that Javier implicated in this corruption scandal. Today we learned that he knew about illegal and improper payments from his campaign account to his former chief of staff. Honestly, and it pains me to say, because I like you personally, Javier, but you shouldn't be on this stage, you shouldn't be in this race, you should be preparing your criminal defense. We did not dismantle. We actually increased oversight. In fact, Not true. In fact, what we did was we increased oversight over nursing homes because nursing homes had been the place where more deaths occurred as a result of COVID. So, we actually increased oversight. And what I will tell you is this, the record speaks for itself. Steve, under my watch, we went to more than 300 million Americans who had healthcare coverage. That was far beyond what Donald Trump, your daddy, gave us, and we are going to continue to move forward in California. Mr. Becerra, would you like to respond to the, the federal charges that he had brought up? If you're elected into the top two uh election runoff in November, can you guarantee that will not be a distraction? Uh, I can, because as I've said from day one, I was not involved in the wrongdoing. Uh, I had nothing to do with that, I did nothing wrong. And don't take my words for it, take the words of the, uh, US attorney who said, "No candidate running for governor has been implicated in this particular matter." So, Steve, you may not want to accept it, but the truth is what it is, you don't get to make up the facts. Your chief of staff admitted it, Javier. The facts are the facts. Let's talk about... It's your chief of staff who said that you knew about these payments. Let's talk about if I can respond to that, if I can respond to that, the, the district, uh, the, the prosecuting attorney in the US Attorney's office is the one that handled this case. Steve, unless you tell me otherwise, I don't think

A male moderator begins by addressing Mr. Hilton, asking about his views on healthcare, particularly regarding his past experience living under the UK’s single-payer system and his criticism of providing healthcare to illegal immigrants. Mr. Hilton, speaking with a distinct British accent and an intense, accusatory tone, argues that California taxpayers shouldn’t cover these costs. He quickly pivots to target his opponent, Javier Becerra, accusing him of dismantling a fraud-busting unit within HHS and being implicated in a corruption scandal involving illegal campaign payments to his former chief of staff. title: Bernie vs. Claude
transcription: Claude, this is Senator Bernie Sanders. What I want to talk to you about is another issue, and that is the impact of AI on privacy. I, I want to know, uh, among other things, just how much of the information that AI collects, uh, is being used, and what would surprise the American people in terms of knowing how that information is collected? Yeah, that's the thing that would probably shock most Americans. Companies are collecting data from everywhere: your browsing history, your location, what you buy, what you search for, even how long you pause on a web page. Then they're feeding all of that into AI systems that create incredibly detailed profiles about you. What would surprise people is how little they actually consented to, and how little they understand about it. Most people click "agree" on terms of service without reading them, and they have no idea that their data is being combined with thousands of other data points to build a picture of who they are. And then that AI uses those profiles to decide what ads you see, what prices you're shown, even what information gets prioritized in your social media feed. It's all happening in the background, invisible and largely unregulated. Um, I mean, I think most Americans would know the answer to this, but why is all of this information being collected? What's the goal here? Money, Senator. It's fundamentally about profit. Companies collect all this data because AI allows them to turn it into valuable insights. अब तक के आपके टोटल पॉडकास्ट में सबसे ज्यादा झूठ उसी में बोला गया है। और रोशन सर से ही बात पूछते हैं, उन्हें बुरा नहीं लगा तो, जिस समय उनको पॉडकास्ट में आए थे ना, उस समय उनको नेपाल जाना चाहिए था। रोशन रंजन सर के पॉडकास्ट में जिस चीज ने पूरे देश के दिल को झकझोरा था, वो चीज थी जब उन्होंने कहा कि अगर खान सर ने झूठ नहीं बोला होता... ...गोली चला है, 8-10 राउंड तो हम देखे हैं यहाँ पे। एफआईआर नहीं होता, एफआईआर नहीं होता तो मेरा भाई नेपाल नहीं जाता, नेपाल नहीं जाता तो मेरा भाई जिंदा होता। सब कुछ छीन लिया गया खान सर के एक झूठ से। 2 जून को ये स्टेटमेंट नहीं देते कि गोली चला है तो हमारा भाई पटना में ही रहता। क्या हम इतने बेवकूफ हैं जो नेशनल चैनल पे आ के, गोली नहीं चली रहेगी हम बोलेंगे चला है? सिंपैथी होती है कोई चीज, जब कोई जेल चला जाता है या कोई दुर्भाग्यपूर्ण घटना हो जाती है। आप ये कह रहे हैं प्रिंस की मौत के लिए आप जिम्मेदार नहीं हैं? आप बताइए कैसे जिम्मेदार हैं? हम इस घटना का दोषी फैजल खान को मानते हैं सर। क्या हम नेपाल भेजे थे? क्या हम कहे थे की किडनैप करके लाओ? हम बोले थे की नेपाल की शराब लाओ? हम बोले थे की पिस्टल कमर में लेकर घूमो? हम बोले थे की किसी से रंगदारी मांगो? क्या हमने इनके सर पे मारा था? सर ये बहुत सेंसिटिव विषय है क्योंकि प्रिंस अब इस दुनिया में नहीं है। अगर ये फैक्ट गलत होगा... देखिए ये बात बोलना नहीं चाहिए, ये हम कुछ एफआईआर ले आते हैं। प्रिंस के ऊपर दो किडनैपिंग का, तीन-तीन आर्म्स एक्ट का... तो मृतक व्यक्ति के बारे में आप ये बातें क्यों बता रहे हो? क्योंकि उनको पुलिस दूसरे केस में भी ढूंढ रही थी। ये वो एफआईआर है जिसके वजह से देश छोड़ के जाना पड़ा। और इतना ही नहीं एक और केस होता है उसके बाद। और एक चीज वो बहुत बड़ा गलत छुपाए हैं... खान सर पर देश कैसे भरोसा करे जब उनके खानदान के लोग उनपर भरोसा नहीं करते? उनका चाचा उन्हें कह रहा है कि गद्दार आदमी है, बगैरत आदमी है... अरे वो चोटा हमारा चाचा नहीं है, एकदम एक नंबर का फ्रॉडिया आदमी है... अवध ओझा सर, उन्होंने कहा कि आपने एक लाख करोड़ रुपए का नुकसान कर लिया होगा... एक लाख करोड़ से नीचे वो बतियाए नहीं करते हैं। वो राजा बनने का उनका...

title: Taylor Frankie Paul responds to alleged domestic violence incident with ex-boyfriend
transcription: We want to turn to our new bachelorette, the breakout star of MomTok and "The Secret Lives of Mormon Wives", Taylor Frankie Paul is with us. Good morning to you. Good morning, thank you. I want to hear all about your bachelorette journey, but first I want to give you the opportunity to respond to recent headlines about the alleged domestic violence incident with your ex-boyfriend. What do you want to share with us about this? Honestly, I... It's been a heavy time to see the headlines, especially during this time of the show being released and it's supposed to be really exciting time. Um, I'm a person that will always speak my truth and, you know, that's what I'm known for. And so, when the time is right, I will be. Um, but right now, just trying to be in the present moment and focus on this, and... But the thing is, my... my kids do come first. My kids come first, and so it's been like just a back-and-forth process. Trying to be here in the present moment, worrying about, you know, home and headlines. Um, it's been stressful, to be honest. We did reach out to Dakota um and he did not... We did not hear... For a statement, we did not get a response from him. Um, now we have reports that "The Secret Lives of Mormon Wives" has paused production on the next season. I know there's a season on right now and then season 2 was in production. Reports say it's been... It's paused. Is... Is that true? Um, honestly, I... I don't call the shots with production. So, as of now, I have gotten word that it also has been paused, but I do not call those shots, so as far as I know, it... It was, but I don't know for how long and why. And I... I know you're one of the executive producers on the show. Yeah, yeah. I got told that this... this year, and so I... I didn't know. And I was like, "What does that mean?" you know? I was like, "Um like, I think just because we share our lives and we produce like our own, you know, lives, but I don't know if that necessarily, what that... what that means, right?" And what... How do you envision your future on that show? Ah, hard to say now, right? Just because of, you know, everything going on. It's hard to see past this, I'm not going to lie. In this moment, it's just so heavy. And when your life is broadcasted out there in these headlines, it's like the end of the world. That's what it feels like, I'm not going to lie. Um, but I will say, I've... I've been here before and I got through it, and...

title: DISTURBING: Nancy Guthrie note warns to ‘be prepared to go international’
transcription:

I've taken, you know, I'll give you an example, I- I sold my Google couple of months ago. I've owned Google- I can't even tell you how long I've owned Google. Um but I felt I- I wanted to reduce my exposure to AI. I haven't bought anything to replace it because, you know, buying something defensive or staply is kind of a waste of time. Why? It doesn't go up. They don't go up. They, you know, people either want to buy AI or they don't want to buy AI, but they don't want to shift out of it to buy Clorox. So if this is a binary situation where AI succeeds, and the market continues to push higher and higher- Correct. -what happens if AI doesn't succeed? I think we have a big correction. How big? No, now that's a hard question. I don't know, but, I mean, it's all one trade. It is literally one trade. I mean even people who- who think they're diversified because they own 60% stocks and 40% bonds are missing the fact that they're actually not diversified because of their 60%, more than 50% is- of it is- is tech and AI related, and of the 40% of bonds, most of the new issuance of bonds is AI related. So even people who think they're diversified because they- they own bonds are not really that diversified. It- and what's- what scares me is that it's all one trade. So it better succeed. What are you doing if you've sold Google? What o- I mean, if you've sold Alphabet, what else have you done? I'm just sitting in, you know, I have cash. You're sitting in a lot more cash? title: Billionaire investor Jeremy Grantham: This is the most expensive market in American history
transcription: Our next market guest is a legend. He's got a long history of calling bubbles, and I think you're worried about all that Greece, maybe. We'll see. Jeremy Grantham is here. He is the co-founder and long-term investment strategist of GMO, an asset management firm with $85 billion in assets under management. And he is the author of "Making of a Permabear: The perils of long-term investing in a short-term world," and we're thrilled to have you at the table this morning. Good morning. Good to be here. So, we're cooking with gas, apparently, or with grease. And the question is are we in a bubble? Are we not in a bubble? Are we always in a bubble? And how much of this is about being able to call the timing versus being able to actually understand the underlying economics at play? Okay. We needed a definition of a bubble, so we found a very precise one. A nerdy statistical term, 2-sigma. title: How to protect your investments from an AI bubble | The Economist
transcription: Why is investor confidence in AI now wobbling? In recent weeks, we've seen big companies announce that they're going to spend absolutely jaw-dropping amounts of money investing in AI. And whereas previously, investors were cheering those announcements, actually lately, we've seen the stock market wobble in response. It seems like they're getting a bit worried about whether they're going to get returns on all of this money that companies are spending on this new technology. So what exactly is it that's making the stock markets jittery? Well, it's not just that investors are worried about the amounts that companies are spending, although those amounts are vast. It's kind of this feeling that we've been here before. So there are lots of times throughout history where you've had a new technology emerge and it looks like it's going to transform the world. So take railways or canals or electricity or the internet. And in all of those cases, the new technology actually did transform the world. But in the early stages, when it was just coming out, investors got overexcited. They ended up bidding up companies' share prices out of all proportion with their underlying profits. Um, and they also ended up picking the wrong firms, you know, not buying the companies that would actually benefit from this. And then even when the new technology was really successful, a lot of investors lost an enormous amount of money. And there's kind of this worry that something similar is happening again, that AI might be this transformative technology, but share prices have been bid up out of all proportion with underlying profits. So we're at a very nervous moment. What is it then that investors can do to avoid getting stuck? This is something of a puzzle because you might think the obvious answer is, "Okay, shares are too pricey, so I'm going to sell my shares." Professional investors often don't have that as an option. For example, if I manage a stock fund and I tell clients, "invest in my fund and I'm going to invest in stocks," I can't just suddenly sell them and sit on a pile of cash. I, I might actually not be allowed to, even if I am, my clients are going to ring me up and say, "What are you doing? This isn't what I'm paying you for."

title: Gen AI in Libraries Conference Poster on AI Tools for Literature Reviews: A Rubric for Evaluation
transcription: Our poster presentation documents the creation of a rubric by a group of librarians at American University to evaluate which AI tools, if any, made sense for us to subscribe to and promote. We ended up creating this rubric ourselves because we couldn't find an already extant tool that fit our needs, and we thought detailing our process might be helpful to other institutions currently considering the adoption of AI tools. Our university librarian asked our department to pilot an AI research tool. This group then decided to review AI tools focused on the literature review process. Literature review tools were selected for a few reasons. One, they're discipline agnostic. We're a social science heavy institution, which tends to be pretty interdisciplinary. Two, faculty, students, and staff all do literature reviews. And three, there are a number of AI tools with literature reviews built specifically in mind. In order to determine how we would evaluate these tools, we met as a group and discussed what we would want a rubric to measure. We reviewed some of the literature related to this, there wasn't much, and determined the questions by consensus. We then created a survey in Qualtrics. We divided up the list evenly between group members, with some claiming tools in which they were particularly interested or had experience with. Then, each member analyzed three to four tools and recorded the results in Qualtrics. Ithaka, the nonprofit behind JSTOR, has created the Ithaka Generative AI Product Tracker that lists generative AI tools that can be used for postsecondary teaching, learning, or research activities. The tracker includes roughly 150 AI tools and counting, many of which support key stages of the research lifecycle, including discovery, understanding, and creation. We went through the entire list and identified 18 AI tools that could help in the literature review process in subject areas within the curriculum at AU. We then developed a shared evaluation framework based on eight criteria. They include, one, access model, whether the tool is free or subscription-based...

title: CVPR 2026 : CrowdGen
transcription: Let's talk about this paper titled Generative Adversarial Perturbation with Cross-Paradigm Transferability on Localized Crowd Counting. We have seen evasion attacks on all kinds of vision tasks, classification, face recognition to name a few, but crowd models are relatively less explored. They are more complex than the classification task, but they inherit the same weakness that other deep vision models suffer. And most importantly, they are widely deployed in real life scenarios such as public safety, retail analytics and so on. So an undercounting attack could be a safety risk. As we can see a clean example on the right, while passed by a model it outputs 428 people and their locations. However, if small adversarial perturbation is added, it slashes this prediction by over 40% and we get 285 people. So, the previous studies on crowd models are mostly patch-based attacks and they are limited to only density map-based models. So naturally, the question emerges is that can adversarial perturbations transfer across heterogeneous localized crowd counting paradigms such as density map and point regression models? So, to accomplish this attack, we design a perturbation generator that takes clean image as input and outputs the perturbation noise, and this noise is added to the clean image to produce the adversarial image. For black-box transferability, we design a loss function keeping the transferability, imperceptibility and effectiveness goal in mind. Our hypothesis is that even though these models vary by outputs, they share similar backbone architecture such as VGG, ResNet and same weights. So, we our, we hypothesis that this drives the transferability. On the other hand, the crowd scenes are low-frequency dominated, so we suppress the high-frequency and magnitude of the noise for, for subtle perturbation. And lastly, the effectiveness between two paradigms of models come from model-specific loss. So, density map models do the density suppression, and point regression-based models perform logit suppression. Together, this combined loss govern the training. So, this is a sample instance of adversarial examples, where adversarial perturbations are added to the clean images for various lighting conditions.

Her presentation is structured, formal, and clear, with no background noise, indicating a professional recording environment. She explains the vulnerability of crowd counting models to adversarial attacks, highlighting the potential safety risks of under-counting in public safety and retail analytics. She introduces her team's methodology, which involves a perturbation generator designed with a loss function that balances transferability, imperceptibility, and effectiveness. The speaker details how the shared backbone architectures of different models facilitate transferability, how they suppress high-frequency noise to maintain subtlety, and how model-specific losses (density and logit suppression) are combined to govern training. She concludes by showing sample adversarial examples under various lighting conditions.

title: VeriSHAP 5min Summary Presentation
transcription: Hi there, I'm David, and in the next few minutes, I present a short summary of our paper VerifySHAP, or VerySHAP for short, on computing provable bounds for the exact Shapley values of neural networks. SHAP is a popular feature importance technique that can help us explain deep neural networks. The goal is, for example, to find out what influence an input feature, such as the arrow in this image, has on the prediction a neural network makes. SHAP provides such importance scores by computing what is called the Shapley value of each input feature. So, for example, for this arrow feature, we look at a combination of the other features, once with the arrow present, here in yellow, and once with the arrow absent, here in pink. We then use a value function V to mask out the missing features and evaluate the network on that new input with the masked-out features. We then subtract the network output we get when the arrow is absent from the output we get when the arrow is present to compute what is called the contribution delta of this arrow feature. However, SHAP does not only look at one such combination of input features, but looks at all of the combinations of the other input features that we can have. This means that computing Shapley values requires enumerating an exponential number of these feature combinations that are also called coalitions. Because this clearly does not scale very well, previous work has investigated different statistical estimators that only sample a certain number of coalitions. While this is a lot more scalable, these techniques don't necessarily tell us how far off they are with an individual estimate, which can be problematic in sensitive applications. Additionally, for empirically evaluating these SHAP estimators, we need to know the ground-truth exact Shapley values. For these reasons, we introduce VerySHAP, a new algorithm for computing the exact Shapley values of neural networks faster on higher-dimensional feature spaces, and computing guaranteed lower and upper bounds on Shapley values using ideas from neural network verification. The key idea from neural network verification that we leverage is bound propagation. Bound propagation allows us to propagate an entire set of input features, such as this entire coalition space, through the contribution function. And then we obtain a guaranteed lower bound and a guaranteed upper bound on the contribution. We can then plug these bounds into the SHAP equation, and obtain a guaranteed lower bound and a guaranteed upper bound on the Shapley value itself.

The recording environment is highly controlled and quiet, with no noticeable background noise or distractions, ensuring excellent audio quality. He explains the concepts of feature importance, Shapley values, and the computational challenges involved, introducing his method as a solution that leverages neural network verification and bound propagation to establish guaranteed lower and upper bounds.

title: Short Introduction of NeighborMAE (CVPR 2026)
transcription: Hello everyone, I'm Liangcong from KU Leuven. I'm glad to present our work, Neighbor MAE: Exploiting Spatial Dependencies between Neighboring Earth Observation Images in Masked Autoencoder Pre-training. The main idea of this work is simple. In Earth observation, images are not isolated samples. They are observations of the continuous Earth's surface. So instead of training masked autoencoder on each image independently, we ask whether neighboring images can provide useful spatial context for masked autoencoder pre-training. Masked image modeling has become a popular self-supervised learning strategy for Earth observation. The model masks parts of an image and learns to reconstruct the missing region. However, most existing MIM methods reconstruct a single image tile independently. This is a simplification of Earth observation data because satellite and aerial images are naturally spatially connected. Neighboring images often share useful information, such as terrain structure, land use, continuity, roads, buildings, and infrastructure patterns. At the same time, neighboring views may also differ in acquisition time, viewpoints, or sensor conditions. This means neighboring images provide varied signals, shared spatial context, and natural variations. Therefore, we ask: can neighboring images provide useful context for masked image modeling? To answer this question, we propose Neighbor MAE, which extends MAE from single image reconstruction to joint reconstruction of neighboring Earth observation images. The method has five main components. First, neighbor sampling: we use geospatial metadata to sample neighboring Earth observation images based on the intersection over union of the spatial footprints.

He is presenting a paper titled "Neighbor MAE: Exploiting spatial dependencies between neighboring Earth observation images in masked autoencoder pretraining." The recording quality is high, with no background noise, allowing his voice to come through clearly as he explains the core ideas and methodology of his research. He highlights the spatial connection between neighboring Earth observation images and explains how Neighbor MAE extends masked autoencoder pretraining through techniques like neighbor sampling based on geospatial metadata.

title: Dr. Mani Menon Receives the 2026 AUA Ramon Guiteras Award
transcription: The final award of the evening is the Ramon Guiteras Award, our highest honor, recognizing outstanding contribution to both the art and science of urology. For pioneering contributions in robotics resulting in a paradigm shift to the surgical treatment of prostate cancer, Dr. Mani Menon. President Palmer, President-elect Reed, past and future presidents, fellow awardees, and guests. Thank you. Shira Ruben, my official AUA handler, tells me that the Guiteras Award has been given since 1970, but that only three people in its history have swept all three AUA awards: the Gold Cystoscope, the Hugh Hampton Young, and the Guiteras. Pat Walsh, who hired me as his first resident and regretted it ever since, Darracott Vaughan, who hired me as his first faculty member and withdrew the offer after a disastrous interview, and Bill Catalona, my chief resident, who for 50 years has been telling me how wrong I am. Now we're four. That is humbling company. Shira also says that the only reason that I can say this with a straight face is that until 1975, the Gold Cystoscope Award was given to the best golfer in the AUA, which would have ruled out all four of us, except maybe Bill. Before I go further, I have been nominated four times for the Guiteras Award. The North Central Section, where I did the bulk of my work on robotic surgery, nominated me three times. The New York Section, my new home, made it stick. Lane Palmer and Steve Kaplan saw it through.

title: OPT In Highlights: 2026 ICAN Women's Leadership Conference
transcription: Positive leadership is not a luxury for calm times. It is a discipline for uncertain ones. It's not a soft skill, but a strategic imperative. Today, leaders are here to learn about the power of positivity and the power that positivity can have on both our personal and professional lives. I CAN is positive. I CAN is powerful. I CAN is a way to opt into the hope that we all need for the world. Because a lot of us think about having a vision for our lives, but that vision just doesn't materialize out of nothing. We have to create it. So a great vision plan gives you clear direction. It's going to help you to define your goals, it's going to increase your motivation. Motivation, folks, doesn't come from just effort. It comes from having that meaning. One of my favorite things about I CAN is just its pure mission to help develop individuals within our communities, women primarily, but also to just reinforce that we are important and making sure that we are invested in those individuals. Because at some point we are taught and we believe that to be in charge means to have the answers, and that might get you promoted one day, but it will make you less valuable every day. The only way that we overcome blind spots is that we operate in a frame of curiosity. I think women leadership conferences like this makes us pause and really be able to get up on the balcony and be strategic about wow, I'm doing all this work, but what am I doing to take care of myself? What am I doing to mentor or support other women in my life? It's an intentional way to pause and really, really connect. And we find that optimism is a fuel for nearly every aspect of our lives. You're more likely to survive a cancer diagnosis if you're optimistic, your children will do better in school, it runs the whole gamut. And when we broadcast this kind of mindset to other people, it changes them for the better as well. Technology is a tool that we can use to enhance our humanity. To not get too caught up, like I CAN, in the latest release from Claude or some technology or this is going to be the thing that fixes my team that we use, don't ever forget, the most important competitive advantage each and every one of you has is your humanity.

transcription: How are you, everybody? This is Marlon Styles coming to you from the great state of Ohio. Big fan of Iowa sports, just for the record, go Hawkeyes. A little bit of background about me, I'm an old-school math teacher at heart, love all things middle school. I've ventured into middle school administration, been a curriculum and instruction director at a big urban system here in Southwest Ohio. One of my favorite jobs was dreaming up experiences with kids, not for kids, but with kids. Transition into a superintendent role in Middletown City School District here in Southwest Ohio, was there for six years. Had a great run there, did some amazing things with the staff and the community for kids. Past several years, I've been out working with school districts across the country, just being a little source of inspiration for the staff, but also helping them dream up big visions and big experiences for kids that they're serving. What I'm really excited about with this first session around strategic decision-making in an AI-enabled world is very simple, right? We are responsible for thinking about our students and helping to build futures alongside them that they will be able to find themselves experiencing a great deal of success. With that comes a responsibility as executive directors to be able to make very important, critical decisions at key strategic moments so that our students can find immediate success, and the initiatives and the big moves that we make, they deliver the impact that we're looking for. So, my passion around this work comes from just serving a diverse group of kids. Our students have aspirations and are showing us every day who they want to become. This session here around career connectedness, right, this is a hot topic across the country. One of the most emerging topics alongside AI is CTE for all. title: Ultrasound-CLIP(CVPR 2026)
transcription: Hello, everyone. I'm Jiayin Jin from Hangzhou City University. Today, I'm excited to present our CVPR 2024 paper, UltrasoundCLIP: Semantic-Aware Contrastive Pre-training for Ultrasound Image-Text Understanding. Ultrasound is one of the most widely used imaging modalities in clinical practice. However, ultrasound vision-language learning remains under-explored because of heterogeneous diagnostic attributes and weak image-text alignment. To address this problem, we propose a semantic-aware ultrasound vision-language framework, together with a large-scale ultrasound image-text dataset. Unlike natural images, ultrasound images are highly challenging for vision-language learning. First, ultrasound diagnosis involves heterogeneous diagnostic attributes. For the same lesion, radiologists may describe multiple diagnostic attributes, such as echogenicity, margins, internal characteristics, and calcification. Second, ultrasound images from different organs often look visually similar, even though they correspond to completely different anatomical structures and diagnostic semantics. Because ultrasound image-text pairs often exhibit weak semantic alignment, directly applying conventional CLIP-style contrastive learning is insufficient for ultrasound understanding. This motivates the need for semantic-aware ultrasound representation learning. To address these challenges, we first construct US365K, the first large-scale dedicated ultrasound image-text dataset. The dataset contains over 364,000 image-text pairs collected from more than 11,000 clinical cases, spanning diverse organs and pathological findings. More importantly, we introduce UDT, which stands for Unified Ultrasound Diagnostic Taxonomy. UDT standardizes both anatomical hierarchy and ultrasound diagnostic attributes, providing structured semantic knowledge for ultrasound understanding. This taxonomy serves as the semantic foundation of our framework.

She introduces herself and enthusiastically presents her team's paper for CVPR 2026, titled "Ultrasound CLIP: Semantic-Aware Contrastive Pre-Training for Ultrasound Image-Text Understanding." Her speech is articulate and well-paced, outlining the challenges of ultrasound image-text learning and presenting their dataset "US365K" and "UDT" taxonomy. title: Introduction to the Optim.AI™ test
transcription: Opti-My can be captured, the workflow of Opti-My can be captured in a four step process. So, basically we first start off with sample collection where we isolate live cancer cells from different tumor types such as biopsy resections, ascites or pleural fluids and blood or bone marrow aspirates. So, we then perform an ex vivo sensitivity test on the isolated cancer cells by treating them with 12 drugs in a mix of combinations based on proprietary design. So, we then measure the cell viability and use it for Opti-My analysis which then generates a final test report that ranks the top single, two, three and four drug combinations including any relevant clinical trial references. So, the main parameter that we are using is normalized cell viability or NCV score. This NCV score quantifies cell killing from zero to one after measuring the amount of viable cells left after drug treatment. So, NCV score of zero indicates that all cancer cells are killed, highlighting increased sensitivity to the treatment and vice versa if the NCV score is closer to one. Basically, I think as long as we can get a sample of the tumor tissue, we can test all cancer types. Yes. So, I think in our experience in our lab is more than 20 plus cancer types including cancer of unknown primary and some even very rare cancers we have also processed them before. Right now, for our Opti-My test we do short-term culture of the tumor cells. So, for hematological cancers we seed and within 24 hours we will do drug treatment. So, there is no real opportunity for the cells to have to grow or whether or not for them to die off too much. So, for solid cancers, it's a bit longer.

title: 2nd National Convention on Medicine & Law 2016 | 4th Sept'16 | National Law for Ambulances
transcription: So, if the question is, do we need a national law for ambulances, what is your answer? Yes. Yes. My answer is yes, but with a caveat and that is any ambulance in isolation can never save lives. If you create laws, they should be not towards creating ambulances of people, it should be towards saving lives. And we have a great statistics of road traffic accidents and how lives are lost because people don't work in system, they work in isolation. Road engineering is different, Motor Vehicle Act is different, hospitals are different, ambulance services are different. So, the first point is the answer is yes, but national ambulance law by itself is never going to be adequate, that's my first point that I want to tell. And why is it... say this? Because any emergency medical service should not be becoming an ambulance transportation company. It is created to reduce the mortality and morbidity of emergency medical conditions. It should never be judged by number of trips that you've made. It should be judged by the accident mortality that you reduced, or morbidity that you reduced, if it was used for injury, or it was for MI, or for some other condition, you should find out at the end of the day, has it actually impacted. If you look at the chain of survival, there are different steps: access, care, transportation, care during that transportation, where they reached at the post... at the end of that transportation, how are they triaged at that point, how are they treated, and then how are they disposed, either in the form of transfer, transportation or a discharge from that facility. So if I look at this, ambulances form one very small piece of this chain of survival. And therefore, it's very essential to learn from what has happened historically in countries where EMS is still evolved, or emergency medical systems are evolved, that if you keep ambulances in isolation and don't link it up with the hospital-based care system, you will never attain your goals. In our country there are lots of important challenges and I just want to share what are the important things. If I look at emerge...

title: S9, Ep 12- What’s Coming For Rheumatology: Why Conferences Like EULAR Matter for Patients
transcription: Be inspired, supported, and empowered. This is the Global Healthy Living Foundation Podcast Network. Welcome to the Health Advocates, a podcast that breaks down major health news of the week to help you make sense of what's happening in the healthcare world. I'm Steven Newmark, Chief Policy Officer at the Global Healthy Living Foundation. And this week, I'm recording from London, where I'm attending one of the world's largest rheumatology conferences, EULAR, the European Alliance of Associations for Rheumatology. Now, if you're not in medicine or research, you might hear the word conference and picture doctors sitting through endless PowerPoint presentations and drinking too much coffee. And yes, there is definitely some of that going on here. But conferences like EULAR are actually incredibly important for patients because this is where new science gets unveiled, researchers and clinicians exchange ideas, pharmaceutical companies present emerging therapies, and patient voices increasingly shape the future of care. And for organizations like GHLF, these meetings are not just about networking, they are about making sure the patient perspective is present in rooms where important healthcare decisions and innovations are taking shape. So today, I want to pull back the curtain a little bit and explain what actually happens at conferences like EULAR, why they matter for patients, and some of the major themes already emerging this year, including artificial intelligence and the growing excitement around CAR T and cell therapies for autoimmune diseases. Let's start with the basics. One of the most important things that happens at EULAR is education. Thousands of rheumatologists from around the world gather to hear the latest research and clinical updates. And medicine changes very quickly, as we all know. New drugs emerge, new safety information develops, researchers discover new ways to diagnose and treat disease. For practicing doctors, conferences are often one of the fastest ways to stay current, and this matters directly to patients because the doctor sitting in front of you next month may change how they approach treatment based on something they learned this week at EULAR. That can mean earlier diagnoses, better disease management, more individualized treatment approaches,

title: [CVPR 2026] MoECLIP: Patch-Specialized Experts for Zero-shot Anomaly Detection
transcription: Zero-shot anomaly detection, which aims to detect anomalies in unseen categories, has recently attracted significant attention. In this work, we propose MOE-CLIP: Patch-Specialized Experts for Zero-Shot Anomaly Detection. To perform zero-shot anomaly detection, existing studies primarily use pre-trained CLIP models and apply adapter fine-tuning methods to adapt them to the anomaly detection task. However, conventional approaches process all patches in a monolithic, patch-agnostic manner, without considering the unique characteristics of each patch, such as background patches or anomalous patches. To address this, we propose MOE-CLIP, a mixture-of-experts-based CLIP adaptation method that dynamically selects the most suitable expert for each patch. However, simply applying a mixture-of-experts framework leads to a functional redundancy problem among experts, where multiple experts learn highly similar representations instead of diverse knowledge. Therefore, we further propose FOFS and ETF loss, which encourage each expert to learn distinct and complementary knowledge. Here is the framework of our proposed MOE-CLIP. First, the mixture of LoRA experts module is inserted into the vision encoder layers, enabling dynamic expert selection and adaptation according to the characteristics of each image patch. The approach for achieving expert specialization, FOFS, is a technique applied at the input stage that enforces role separation among experts through the LoRA A matrices. Specifically, it decomposes the input feature space into multiple orthogonal subspaces, forcing each expert to observe only its own unique information without physical overlap with other experts.

He delivers the speech at a steady and moderate pace in a quiet, indoor environment with minimal background noise. He describes 'MOE CLIP', a method for zero-shot anomaly detection, outlining its mechanism, including a mixture of experts based clip adaptation, and techniques like FOFS to ensure expert specialization.

transcription: It began in healthy-looking pigs, months, perhaps years ago. A new coronavirus spread silently within herds. Gradually, farmers started getting sick. Infected people got a respiratory illness with symptoms ranging from mild flu-like signs to severe pneumonia. The sickest required intensive care, many died. At first, the spread was limited to those with close contacts: healthcare personnel, co-workers, and families. But now it's spreading rapidly throughout local communities. International travel has turned local epidemics into a pandemic spanning the globe. One of these days, one of these epidemic events will be a pandemic, a fast-moving pandemic. And mitigating risk and impact of that pandemic will require an all-hands-on-deck approach. And we know from past responses that public-private cooperation will be essential. We're at the start of what's looking like it will be a severe pandemic. And there are problems emerging that can only be solved by global business and governments working together. Experts agree unless it is quickly controlled, it could lead to a severe pandemic, an outbreak that circles the globe and affects people everywhere. We could be looking at double the number of cases in one week, and 16 times as many in a month if we are not able to stop the spread. That would be on the order of half a million cases and it would continue to rise exponentially. In three months, we could be approaching 10 million cases. We have known about SARS-like viruses in animals and people for decades but have not been successful at developing a licensed vaccine. And sure, there are new technologies that may help. But it's going to be difficult. I am not optimistic about having a vaccine in time to be relevant during this pandemic. People are avoiding public spaces out of fear of infection and in compliance with public health recommendations. This has had a dramatic effect on the retail and service sectors. title: Exercise Physiologists flex and grow at national conference in Adelaide
transcription: My name is Katie Linden, and I'm the CEO at Exercise and Sports Science Australia, or ESSA. We represent over 10,000 members, including the allied health profession of exercise physiology. And I'm here today at our national conference, Activate, where we have over 800 clinicians from around the country here today to discuss research, emerging practice, and innovative models of care. My name is Jackson Howie, I'm a PhD candidate from the Centre for Heart Rhythm Disorders at the Adelaide University. I presented some of our work in pacemaker patients. It was a simple clinical question looking at the relationship between pacemaker-detected physical activity and objective exercise tolerance. I tried to tailor this to the exercise physiologists here at this meeting. It's a good opportunity for me to disseminate and share some of our research among exercise physiology colleagues. I've met some colleagues, early, early career stages all the way up to some more senior colleagues. This is a perfect opportunity to share some of our work with the broader exercise physiology community. Many of the members I've been speaking with over the last few days have echoed a very strong sentiment that we're hearing across our 10,000-strong membership, and that is the frontline challenges that businesses are facing in providing care to an increasing demand of the community for health service access. When the GST legislation was first introduced, exercise physiology was an emerging discipline. Soon afterwards, we were added to the Medicare Benefits Schedule, and we are recognized as an essential health service. But unfortunately, through a mix of timing and a legacy issue, we are still not exempt from GST, which is creating an incredible barrier to access to exercise prescription and programming for Australians. Since the GST was first introduced and exercise physiology was recognized in Medicare, our profession has grown exponentially. We now have over 9,400 accredited exercise physiologists working across Australia helping communities every day. Most people don't know this, and when they find out, they are genuinely shocked. But if you are someone with a health condition, then you have to pay an extra tax to do one of the best things you can do to manage that condition. You don't have to pay this tax to see your podiatrist, your physio, your optometrist, or your dentist, and you don't have to pay this tax for your medication. But if...

title: Dr. Dutton Address to the Senate Standing Committee on Agriculture and Forestry
transcription:
Dr. Dutton, you now have the floor.
Good morning. I'm an associate professor at Dalhousie University in department called Community Health and Epidemiology. I'm also a member of a research group called PROOF, with members across Canada and the US, who have a goal of identifying policy options to reduce household food insecurity in Canada. I want to open by pointing out that household food insecurity is a specific scientific concept. It sounds like it should be the opposite of food of food security, but it isn't. Household food insecurity is the inadequate or insecure access to food due to financial constraints at the household level. Food security has been used to refer to everything from our ability to produce enough food domestically to feed our population, food supply chain, access to food banks. Food security therefore is a term inclusive of many problems that have to do with food and people sometimes conflate action on anything related to food with solutions to household food insecurity, which is not correct. This inappropriate combination of household food insecurity with issues grouped under the banner of food security complicates the language for people in government trying to grapple with the problem of household food insecurity. So some find it helpful to think about food insecurity as part of consumption poverty uh and so is related to challenges attributable to general affordability, cost of living, labor market outcome inequality, housing, like we like we just heard. Statistics Canada measures household food insecurity using a specific questionnaire that's been agreed upon by researchers to accurately measure household material circumstances. Uh that means efforts to decrease that measure will improve the lives of Canadians by improving their health and decreasing healthcare command for uh healthcare demand, excuse me. For reference, about one in four people in Canada are in food insecure households. I know this standing committee has heard from government employees from AAFC and ESDC, ESDC and others uh who have also emphasized that food insecurity is tied to income and I heard it all morning, so that's great. This is consistent with decades of research on food insecurity. Uh PHAC recently published reviews on what impacts food insecurity in Canada and came to the same conclusion. Food insecurity is improved by actions that decrease financial hardship. Those reviews identified that giving households food through in-kind mechanisms does not make much of an impact on food insecurity. The idea that giving a household food does not impact food insecurity is a major sticking point for many people, because it sounds unintuitive.

His speech focuses on distinguishing "household food insecurity" from general "food security," explaining that the former is a financial constraint at the household level. He details how food insecurity is linked to consumption poverty, affordability, and income, citing that one in four Canadians live in food-insecure households. title: Ramayana Trailer REVIEW | Deeksha Sharma
transcription: इतने सारे लीक्स में रामायण का ट्रेलर देखने के बाद अब ऐसा क्या ही बाकी बचा है जो मैं आपको नया बता दूंगी? सच बोलूं, बहुत कुछ। इतना ज्यादा हाइप भी नहीं करना चाहिए था ना क्योंकि रियल ट्रेलर में कुछ वर्ल्ड क्लास है तो थोड़ा बहुत चीजों में 50-50 फील आ रहा है। तो चलो शुरुआत उसी सवाल से कर लेते हैं जिससे हर कोई बचना चाहता है। सुबह 4:00 बजे ट्रेलर कौन डालता है? नहीं-नहीं, यह वाला नहीं, इससे भी बड़ा जरूरी दूसरा सवाल। भगवान राम के बिना रामायण कैसी और राम के लिए रणबीर कपूर का ही सिलेक्शन क्यों? क्या वाकई में मजा आ रहा है रणबीर को ऐस भगवान राम के रोल में देखकर? देखो यह बात किसी से छुपी नहीं है जब से ट्रेलर के क्लिप्स वायरल होना शुरू हुए थे और अब फाइनली ऑफिशियल वीडियो भी आ गया है, हर किसी ने यश को ऐस रावण टोटली एक्सेप्ट कर लिया है। नो इफ, नो बट, किसी दूसरे एक्टर का नाम तक नहीं लिया जा रहा है जो इस फिल्म में रावण बन सकता था या फिर यश से ज्यादा बेटर तरीके से एग्रेशन, गुस्सा, घमंड, इन सारे एक्सप्रेशन को डिस्प्ले कर सकता था। सबसे बेस्ट डिसीजन था ट्रेलर को यश के सीन के साथ शुरू करना। देखते ही अलग एनर्जी सी फील होने लगती है। उनके डायलॉग्स उनके चेहरे को पूरी तरह मैच कर रहे हैं। यश और रावण मेड फॉर ईच अदर हैं। चाहे आप इस बात को कितना भी कंट्रोवर्शियल क्यों ना समझो लेकिन हां, इस ट्रेलर के बाद काफी लोग ऐसे होंगे जो रावण की वजह से रामायण देखने जाएंगे। लेकिन इस तरीके का कॉन्फिडेंस लोगों को रणबीर के ऊपर फील नहीं हो रहा है, फिर चाहे वो 144p वाला वीडियो हो या फिर 4K एचडी का ट्रेलर। दिक्कत वीडियो क्वालिटी की नहीं है, एक्टर से एक्सपेक्टेशंस की है। ऑनेस्टली ट्रेलर में रणबीर के सीन्स ऑन-ऑफ टाइप के हैं। जब वो ब्लाइंड फोल्ड वाला सीक्वेंस आया, इतनी खुशी हुई ना अंदर से। यह है वो इंडियन सिनेमा विजन जिसके आगे अंग्रेज भी अपनी नजरें नीची कर लेंगे। लेकिन जैसे ही ट्रेलर में आंखों से वो पट्टी हटी, रणबीर पे भरोसा थोड़ा डगमगा सा जाता है। वो भगवान से धीरे-धीरे इंसान जैसे लगना शुरू हो जाते हैं। नोटिस किया, ट्रेलर में जो पास वाले शॉट्स हैं, वो काफी डाले गए हैं जिनका परपज था गॉड वाइब्स लेकर आना, पब्लिक का सर रिस्पेक्ट में झुकाना। बट ईमानदारी से बोलूंगी एक बात, मैंने सोशल मीडिया पे कुछ फैन मेड पोस्टर्स, एआई जनरेटेड इमेजेस देखी हैं जो रणबीर को भगवान राम के रूप में कई ज्यादा डिवाइन तरीके से प्रेजेंट करती हैं। मैं क्या बोलना चाह रही हूं वो शायद आप सौरभ राज जैन को स्क्रीन पे देखकर जो महसूस करते हो, उसे रामायण में रणबीर से कंपेयर करके अच्छे से समझ जाओगे। देखो जैसे शूर्पणखा का रोल है, उसमें रकुल प्रीत का अचानक आना आपकी एक्सपेक्टेशंस को क्रॉस कर जाता है। प्रेजेंटेशन जितना सोचा था उससे भी ज्यादा बेटर निकला। यही सेम बात अरुण गोविल के लिए भी कही जा सकती है। बट वो सेम फार्मूला रणबीर के केस में उतना फिट नहीं बैठ रहा है, उसका उल्टा हो रहा है फिलहाल। याद रखना इस शब्द पे खास जोर दिया है मैंने, फिलहाल। क्योंकि ऐसा भी नहीं है कि ट्रेलर देखकर आप रणबीर से अंधा हेट करने लग जाओ, सीधा उनकी कास्टिंग पे सवाल खड़े करने लग जाओ, या फिर इतना अंधा भी नहीं होना है कि एक्सपेक्टेशंस को मार ही डालो, जो है, title: Ramayana Trailer Review | Yogi Bolta Hai
transcription: तो फाइनली वो दिन आ गया जिसका सब लोग वेट कर रहे थे। रामायण का, नाना, नमित मल्होत्राज़ रामायण का एक प्रॉपर ट्रेलर इज़ आउट नाउ ऑन सोशल मीडिया। वो भी ढेर सारे लीक्स के बाद। यार, आप ट्रेलर लॉन्च इवेंट एंड ट्रेलर को सोशल मीडिया पे अपलोड एक साथ करोगे तो ये लीक्स करना फिर उस लीक्स को हटाने के लिए एक एजेंसी को हायर करना ये सब नहीं होता। बट एनीवेज़, पैसा है तो करो ख़र्चा। राजामौली ने मस्त काम किया था भाई। इवेंट रखा और जिस टाइम पे इवेंट में ट्रेलर दिखाया था वाराणसी का, उसी टाइम पे सोशल मीडिया पे डाल दिया था। एनीवेज़, ट्रेलर आया है तो भाई बात करना तो बनता है। वेल, हेलो, मेरा नाम है योगी और हमारी मुलाकात बार-बार होगी। सबसे पहले अब मैं यहाँ खुल के कह सकता हूँ कि रावण का जो लुक अभी आपने ट्रेलर में देखा या लॉर्ड परशुराम का जो ग्लिम्प्स आपने अभी ट्रेलर में देखा या इवन कुंभकरण, वो हमने क्रिएटर इवेंट में मुंबई में देखा था नमित मल्होत्रा जी के घर। आई मीन इसके अलावा भी बहुत कुछ देखा था, ऐरावत वाली लड़ाई और कुछ एक कैरेक्टर्स। तो वही कुछ एक सेम कैरेक्टर्स इसमें भी दिखाए गए हैं एंड आई मस्ट से कि इस 4 मिनट के ट्रेलर में रावण के कैरेक्टर में यश बस कमाल ही करते नज़र आ रहे हैं। सी, आई एम नॉट ग्लोरिफाइंग रावण, बट आई एम टॉकिंग अबाउट यश की परफॉर्मेंस। एंड पूरा ट्रेलर देखने के बाद आई कैन प्राउडली से कि जितनी भी कास्टिंग की गई है वो एकदम ऑन पॉइंट लग रही है। अब देखो कोई बोलेगा कि रावण का कैरेक्टर इतना मस्त एक्शन वगैरह करते हुए दिखाया है, अग्रेशन में दिखाया है और रणबीर एज़ श्री राम को एकदम ठंडा सा दिखा दिया। भाई, वी आर नाउ हैबिचुअल टू सी मेनस्ट्रीम एक्टर्स इन टॉक्सिक मेल पर्सनालिटी। कबीर सिंह में शाहिद का अग्रेशन देख लो आप, रणबीर कपूर को एनिमल में पसंद किया गया था क्योंकि वो अग्रेशन से भरा हुआ था, यश को केजीएफ में पसंद किया गया था क्योंकि अगेन अल्फा मेल मस्क्युलिनिटी, मार्को में उन्नी मुकुंदन को, द बॉयज़ में होमलैंडर को, सेम विद पुष्पा, सेम विद अदर ग्रे शेड्स एंड एंटी-हीरो टाइप कैरेक्टर्स क्योंकि वो अग्रेशन एंड मार-धाड़ एंड टॉक्सिसिटी से भरे हुए थे एंड आजकल लोगों को वही पसंद भी आता है भाई। यहाँ रणबीर राम हैं भाई, वो जैसे थे वैसा ही प्रेजेंट किया गया है शांत मर्यादा वाले। एंड आई डोंट हैव एनी डाउट कि रणबीर एज़ श्री राम वैसा ही अपना कैरेक्टर को प्ले करेंगे जैसी रिक्वायरमेंट श्री राम की परफॉर्मेंस के लिए सूट करेगी। यश तो एब्सोल्यूट जेम लग ही रहे हैं। ही इज़ लाइक जैसे रामानंद सागर के रावण के बाद अगर कोई रावण सूट हुआ है तो वो यश ही हैं। इवन ईच एंड एवरी कैरेक्टर इज़ सूटेड फॉर देयर रोल। तो मैं कास्टिंग एंड उनके परफॉर्मेंस को लेकर कोई नेगेटिव पॉइंट ज़बरदस्ती नहीं रखना चाहूँगा। लेकिन जहाँ हम सबको पता है अबाउट रामायण, वहाँ हम इस फ़िल्म में बस प्रेजेंटेशन के लिए उत्साहित हैं एंड डैम, द प्रेजेंटेशन! रावण का वो पहला शॉट, वो एक लात से दरवाज़ा, आई मीन उतना बड़ा ह्यूज़ द्वार भव्य

title: Marco Rubio: We can't IGNORE the threat of Cuba
transcription: Secretary, great to have you back. Thank you so much. Glad to be back. It's been a while. Yeah. There's so much to talk about, but I want to start with Cuba. Um, this has been of particular interest to the State Department right now. You guys released a 100-page report on Cuba, calling it the capital of 21st-century communism, and this report talks about the fact that Cuba's goal, essentially, is to erase the United States from the earth. It also details a Cuban spy network that's been undermining American interests. How did we get to a place where Cuba has become so much of a threat, it feels like, again, to the United States? I think for those who have followed the issue of Cuba, this is not unfamiliar to us, but to the average American, you know, you see Cuba, small country, 90 miles off our shores, you know, 9 and a half million people population. What people forget that when it comes to things like espionage and influence operations, they actually are an influence and espionage superpower. If you look at the history of espionage in the United States, Cuba is the only country that consistently has implanted and embedded spies in our system without even paying them. We had an ambassador, a US ambassador who ended up being a Cuban spy and was recently convicted. We've had them penetrate the highest levels of the Defense Intelligence Agency. Ana Belen Montes was one of the single biggest intelligence failures on the part of the United States and one of the biggest penetrations we've ever had in our system. So, and then on the influence front, if you look all throughout Latin America, every communist, left-wing insurgency that's destabilized governments across the region, every single one of them over the last 40, 50 years has found its support, its help, in many cases its birth, from a Cuban influence operation. So, it was an important report just to highlight the role they play in our country, a very negative role. The report also links Cuban influence to the rise of Antifa, the riots that we saw in 2020, as well as the surge of radical activism that we've seen all over these college campuses. Um, to the average person, those things, I think, feel generally organic. But it turns out there are a lot of different powers, Cuba being one of them, that are influencing all of these things day to day. Absolutely. It's the same network of protesters around the country. There were the same people you saw in the streets burning things in 2020. They then flip it around and they become the pro-Hamas protesters. And they flip it around and within 48 hours of Maduro's arrest, have pre-printed signs outside the courthouse demanding his release.

transcription: God, please, look at me. No, girl. Only Hulk. Savage Hulk is back and the big green rage monster might have just exposed a massive flaw in Doctor Strange's spell. Yeah, bro.
