title: I Found My Old Journal...I Didn't Recognize Myself.
category: Mental Health Vlogs & Personal Video Diaries
transcription: I found an old journal recently. I don't date my entries, I've never been good at that, but I can tell when it was because of the entries around it. But, I can tell that this one is an older one, it's from before my mother passed away. This is hard. I don't know how to be seen. I keep thinking I will open up my mouth and something will come out that makes sense of me, but it never does. I look at other people and it seems so easy for them. They just exist and people respond to them like they matter. I feel like I'm always just on the edge of everything. I want to be heard. I want to express myself. I want to be someone who has something inside of them that's worth noticing. But I don't think there is. Sometimes I think it would just be easier if I just wasn't here. title: I Found My Grandfather's Old Journal, and What I Read Shocked Me!
category: Mental Health Vlogs & Personal Video Diaries
transcription: We live our days as if we have an endless supply of tomorrows. But every spring here in Japan, the cherry blossoms remind us of a truth we often try to ignore. A beautiful life isn't one that lasts forever. It is one that blooms fully before the wind takes it away. Every spring, the entire country stops to watch the sakura open. People gather under the trees, lay out blankets, and share food, tea, and be happy together. It's a tradition called Hanami. But if you've never experienced this exact thing in your life, you might not realize what makes the sakura so deeply connected to how we experience life. They only bloom for about 10 to 14 days, sometimes even less. A single strong wind or an early heavy rain can take them all away in one night. And that is exactly why they are so beautiful. If cherry blossoms stayed on the trees forever, nobody would stop to look at them. Since everyone sitting under those trees knows that this moment will not last, they pay attention. They just sit there and soak it in, feeling a deep stillness, aware that the petals are already falling. When I was younger, I used to live as if time was unlimited. I would waste entire days doing things I didn't care about. I would stay in situations that made me unhappy, telling myself I'd change things later. I felt this constant pressure to do everything faster and achieve more, while consistently postponing the things I truly wanted to do. This truth about time really hit me when my grandfather, Daiki, passed away. It happened so quickly that one season, he was sitting with me in his garden, pouring tea and telling me stories. And the next season, his chair was empty, like a petal falling from a branch. After he passed, I was going through his things and found an old journal entry he had written during his last spring. I carry his words with me every single day. He wrote, "Hiroto, the real tragedy of life is how many of our years we waste. The sakura never worries about tomorrow's wind."

Speaking with a slow, deliberate pace and a slight accent, he draws a parallel between human existence and the brief, beautiful blooming of cherry blossoms (sakura) in Japan, explaining how their short-lived nature is what makes them so deeply appreciated during the Hanami tradition. The speaker transition into a personal reflection, recalling how he once wasted time until the sudden passing of his grandfather, Daiki, made him realize how quickly life can change. He closes with a touching quote from his grandfather's journal, reminding the listener not to waste their years and to live fully in the present.

title: Investigation uncovers sexual abuse allegations against Cesar Chavez
transcription: There are new revelations and allegations of sexual abuse and rape of women and minors by one of America's iconic civil rights and labor leaders, the late Cesar Chavez. transcription: So hello everyone. My name is Abhil. I'm a postdoctoral scholar at the Computational Science Group at the Scientific Data Division. So, my topic for today is multimodal AI for cryo-electron microscopy and cryo-electron tomography towards biological particles. To give you a context, we are living through a revolution in structural biology, where AI-based methods like AlphaFold predicts the three-dimensional atomic structure of protein. So, which made to the head of the paper in Nature. Image on the top right shows the mechanism of how AlphaFold works. It inputs the one-dimensional amino acid sequence, and predicts a three-dimensional atomic structure from the sequence, with high accuracy. Below are some of the examples of the structure predicted by AlphaFold, where the green structure is the experimentally determined structure and the blue structure are the computationally generated structure. So, overall AlphaFold helps us to predict the static structure of the protein with very high accuracy. However, the proteins are not static in nature. They are dynamic molecules that change their shape as they are performing different functions in our bodies. For example, one of the proteins called KaiB protein, shown in the image on the left here, adopts different conformational state during different times of the day. When we run AlphaFold, default AlphaFold, it predicts only fold-switch state. However, we want to understand how this protein works and how it performs different function, we need to understand different state of this protein. One of the experimental method that helps us to identify this dynamic state of the protein is called cryo-electron microscopy. It helps us to understand how this protein changes its shape, or how these proteins opens and closes when it binds to different molecules, small molecules, ligand molecules, or different drug targets. উত্তর হবে ভয়ের। পরের প্রশ্ন, উবা চখড়ি, লতাপাতা না কাঠকুটো দিয়ে ছবি আঁকতে ওস্তাদ? উত্তর হবে কাঠকুটো। নেক্সট, প্রশ্ন নম্বর ঘ, লক্ষ্মী মেয়েটি ধলেশ্বরী, ইছামতি না দামোদর? উত্তর হবে ইছামতি। পরের প্রশ্ন, দূরের পাল্লা কবিতাটির কবির নাম সত্যেন্দ্রনাথ দত্ত, রবীন্দ্রনাথ ঠাকুর না জসীমউদ্দীন? উত্তর হবে সত্যেন্দ্রনাথ দত্ত। পরের প্রশ্ন, বুনোহাঁস ডিম তার কিসে ঢাকছে? উত্তর হবে শ্যাওলার। নেক্সট, দাগ নম্বর ২, শূন্যস্থান পূরণ করো। প্রশ্নের মান ৩। প্রথম কোশ্চেন, নৌকোয় এগিয়ে চলে ড্যাশ করে? উত্তর তরতর করে। পরের প্রশ্ন, জলময় শৈবাল পান্না ড্যাশ? transcription: Yeah. Look. You ever feel the storm coming before the first drop of rain even hits? It's a specific kind of terror. When you look around your room and you realize it's happening again. You're watching your own mind slide into the dark, and you can't find the brakes. I can feel it in my chest. Listen. I can feel the exact moment the chemistry starts to shift. The heavy gravity pulling me down, beginning to drift away from the people I love, away from the things that I enjoy. My phone rings and the sound of a simple notification just starts to annoy me. I haven't left my bed in two days, the sheets feel like a prison cell. I'm looking at the clutter in my room, it's just a physical reflection of my mind. Motivation is dead, the creative spark is a ghost. The things that used to bring me joy are the exact things I'm avoiding the most. It starts with a heavy sigh, then it moves to a blank stare, then suddenly you're sitting at the edge of the bed, completely unaware of the time passing by. An hour feels like a second or two. And you're desperately trying to remember the last time you felt like yourself. I'm pulling away from my friends, I'm making up excuses to hide. I'm just tired, I'm busy, I'm good. But the truth is, I am lying. I see the shadows stretching out, and I can hear the train coming down the track. Oh, I can feel it in my bones. I'm headed for the dark again. I'm losing all my focus, I don't know where the light has been. I see the walls closing in, I feel the weight on my chest. I'm trying to fight the shadow, but my spirit can't arrest. Is anybody out there watching themselves start to slip? Losing your footing, losing your mind, losing your grip. I'm screaming at the mirror, trying to make the monster stop. But I'm standing on the edge, and I am terrified

title: Inside Robinhood's Original Pitch Deck: Why Investors Said Yes
transcription: In 2013, two Stanford math graduates named Vladimir Tenev and Baiju Bhatt attempted to pitch a radical concept: zero commission stock trading managed entirely through a mobile phone. At this point, they had been entrepreneurs for the better part of five years. They had built several pieces of financial software for high frequency firms, but they had very little tangible success to show for that time. When they tried to raise money for Robinhood, they ran a brutal gauntlet. They were rejected 70 times, then 90 times. Eventually, 110 investors told them no. The feedback was consistent: professional investors didn't believe people would manage their finances on a smartphone. They looked at the founders' math backgrounds and dismissed them as being incapable of building a product for regular consumers. Many founders react to this kind of rejection by treating their pitch deck like a sales brochure. They try to hide their lack of traction behind flashy design elements or unrealistic multi-billion dollar projections. Robinhood took a different path. They realized that before a deck can sell a product, it has to prove the founders are worthy of trusting. Vlad and Baiju began a process of ruthless subtraction. Instead of adding slides to answer every objection, they cut the presentation down to its absolute essentials. They removed the industry jargon and the dense maps of the financial ecosystem. They focused the entire narrative on one universal problem: the high cost and unnecessary friction of the traditional brokerage model. They avoided the trap of pitching a vague, massive market. Instead, their narrative shrinks the opportunity down to a single, sharp data point. They targeted an underserved generation of millennials wanting to invest, but frustrated by $10 commission fees. This narrow focus made it difficult for investors to dismiss the idea with broad generalizations. By proving they understood one user group better than anyone else, they signaled a level of competence that forced investors to take them seriously. But the digital slides are only half the battle. Eventually, that trust has to be validated by the founders in the room. This reached a breaking point during a meeting with Tim Draper...
caption: In this high-quality audio clip, a woman delivers a clear, professional narration detailing the origin story of Robinhood. Her voice is articulate and engaging, set against a subtle, modern electronic background track. She recounts how, in 2013, Stanford math graduates Vlad Tenev and Baiju Bhatt pitched their concept for a zero-commission stock trading mobile app. Despite having years of experience building financial software, they faced immense difficulty securing funding, suffering 110 rejections from investors who doubted everyday consumers would manage finances on smartphones. Instead of inflating their pitch with complex projections, the founders simplified their presentation, eliminating jargon and focusing on a single, compelling issue: the frustration of millennials facing high commission fees. This strategic simplification ultimately established their credibility and won over investors.

title: The Funniest Episode in TV History
transcription: You know, first of all, we are doing this for her, okay? Because neither one of us wants to get divorced. And second ofly, I know you're the big marriage expert. Oh, I'm sorry, I forgot. Your wife is dead. This might be the most perfect episode of Arrested Development. Not because of any single joke, but how each joke is constructed and told. Where most sitcoms rely entirely on funny dialogue and quips between characters, this show builds comedy through editing, music, narration, and structure. Stacking jokes so each moment works on multiple levels at once. I once saw a tweet that said, "The comedy of Arrested Development folds in on itself so much, we no longer process it as funny, but as beautiful." And no episode proves that more than Season 2, Episode 3, Amigos. Here's some money, go see a Star War. An episode that reaches comedic heights I am constantly in awe of. Amigos opens with a simple exchange between Michael and his brother Gob. On the surface, it's just funny dialogue, but the script is quietly planting seeds. Legoland I'm going to go look into some Legoland tickets for the weekend. Circumvent We should circumvent union penalties. Circumvete. Circumvent. Gob has terrible printing. These are very small. Tell you what, from now on, we're going to use just the big printer. Gob having no friends. I've got friends, Michael. None of these are throwaway lines, but setups for later. In fact, the callback is probably what Arrested Development is most famous for. The number of times it can put a different spin on the same punch line is kind of ridiculous. Her? Her? Her? Her? Her? Her? Him? So all these throwaway lines won't be throwaway lines for long. So, I got a call today from Gene Parmesan, our private eye. This is similar, but it's also setting up a structure. Why is it? Because I'm a private detective? Gene Parmesan, how are you? Gene! It's a funny moment on its own, but it's establishing a recurring joke pattern to take advantage of later. So many times in this show, an episode will teach you how a joke works, so it can pull the rug from under you later. First blue Tobias reveal, second blue Tobias reveal, then there's the expectation.

title: Development and Planning Breakfast at UKREiiF 2026
transcription: It was a really great way to start the Wednesday morning in Leeds. I think the importance of events like today is making sure that you've got a diverse range of opinions. There's lots of different issues in the planning in the planning system and when we can come together collectively and discuss these issues there's more opportunities for solutions. I'm really passionate about showing the industry that there is a different way to engage and when you do, when you engage the people that are in need of housing, we can speed up delivery, we can give stakeholders more confidence to approve schemes that should be approved and essentially help get the homes that we need delivered. My role is to make sure that actually they're hearing from the people that are in need of new homes, so they got confidence to say yes and they're they're hearing from the wide range of views in their community, not just with kind of self-serving 1%. I found it a really engaging panel discussion. And I think that's demonstrates one of the things that I really like about this event and coming to UKREiiF is that you come here to listen, to learn. As a, an industry, we have to change, we have to adapt. That sometimes takes time to explore like different models of developments. Me personally, in terms of what I do, I had to look at redesigning schemes, you know, to respond to the Building Safety Act. We're seeing like a a trend towards single family housing and away from apartments, which I'm very positive about. It's amazing to be in Leeds at the center of UKREiiF um in an office that is absolutely fantastic, one of you know, one of many we have right across the country, and putting us at the center of, you know, re- of a regional network. title: Does Civic AI Mean? | Ron Ivey (Noēsis Collaborative) | Civic AI Conference 2026
transcription: With the question that we've been wrestling with today about how should AI care for communities and who gets to decide, I think one of the challenges I have is the it's kind of very fundamental uh kind of premise of that question, whether AI can care. From what I understand and from, you know, talking to and working with uh the developers of these systems, there's there's a real debate whether AI actually cares, where whether it actually has the capacity for empathy, uh whether it has the capacity for moral consideration of others, attentiveness to others, and and really understanding others' uh feelings and perceptions. We already heard this morning about how, you know, the systems themselves cannot distinguish between these issues of of parental sacrifice, which I'm a parent, I'm having to sacrifice every day in terms of my relationships, and child sacrifice. So, just that fundamental understanding of relationship of relational language uh these systems don't understand. So, can an AI care? I don't think so, but could an AI system be designed to support care, to support human relationships? Well, we had already have some great examples from today's conference uh of both in the context of democracy, the use of of AI as a tool to support uh participation uh and engagement and real understanding and legitimacy of bills that are being passed related to synthetic media. That's exciting. Uh we have the application of AI to support uh care and relationship in the healthcare context, in terms of what's happening related to to some of the patients and and getting data that their caregivers can can improve the care. That's exciting as well. And then, in terms of who gets to decide, I think it goes back to this fundamental question of how these systems are built and the power that's that's driving them. Do we have the right kind of cultural framework, uh ethical framework, and the right kind of policy framework to decentralize uh power and decentralize the way these markets are concentrated right now? Until we do that, until we fundamentally deal with the market concentration, the wealth concentration, the power concentration, we'll have challenges on a broader scale in terms of really implementing AI systems that support both those intimate, close relationships and then as the relationships expand into these larger uh contexts of solidarity and trust. Now, that being said, we do have an opportunity, even in the midst of the dominant systems, to to create an alternative ecosystem. To think about funders and investors and inventors and and researchers and policy uh uh experts and local activists and community uh groups. I, you know, seeing inspiring things at the local level where communities are taking control and building their own models, and that's exciting. So, even if we have a dominant system that's can continue to move forward in one direction, there might be a pathway, and I'm hopeful there is a pathway, for alternative systems. It's just about encouraging those and and supporting them and and finding the right kind of resources and uh connecting the dots between those that are doing incredible things in different communities around the world.
caption: A male speaker delivers an articulate and thoughtful speech, discussing the capacity of AI to "care" for communities and who gets to decide its development. He is accompanied by an upbeat, electronic instrumental track that plays in the background throughout the recording. The speaker argues that while AI may not have the capacity for empathy, it can be designed to support care and human relationships, citing examples from democracy and healthcare. He also raises questions about power concentration and the need for a decentralized, alternative ecosystem where communities have more control.

questions.answer: Market concentration, wealth concentration, and power concentration.

title: 2026 Annual Conference Highlights
transcription: This SASTA annual conference is an opportunity for science educators across the state to come together and explore different professional learning opportunities with workshops from various presenters. Been to, I've been to a few different conferences over the last couple of months and I'd say this is probably the one that I've probably enjoyed the most. It's been very informative and very engaging, as well. Yeah, it's been great. Hearing lots of interesting science ideas from professionals, but also colleagues that are sharing their ideas with everyone. Loved the keynotes. The one on light was really inspirational and um the one yesterday where we were talking about timber and I didn't realize that there was a whole illegal timber trade and that they were using DNA to find out more about it. That was really really interesting. Uh, this is my first day. I just uh saw the first um light um speech. That was really cool. I learned so much about how light is in all parts of science and how you can connect any interest that a student could have back to light or back to physics, which was very interesting. Well, I just came out of the keynote presentation and that, that guy was spectacular. I was just so impressed. He had example after example and he was just impressive, so animated, lively, and uh was engaging. I mean, just was non-stop, just one slide after another slide and the conversation was just relentless. So, you know, you want that energy in your class to get to promote the curiosity, which is what it's all about, promoting curiosity. If we can get that going up and running, you're away. Cultivating curiosity is such a huge thing in science. So many things would not be discovered if it weren't for the curious minds behind them. So, essentially, it does come down to cultivating curiosity. Ask all the questions, don't be afraid to find the answers. This is my second professional development thing I've done through SASTA and I'm really glad that I've come today. It's only been about an hour and I'm already just shocked and I've learned so much. I think the biggest takeaway for me is going to be about the ways that I can engage my students, the ways that I can bring that real world, that really fascinating, interesting areas of application into the classroom and how I can talk to them about it and get them engaged and active in it. It's always great just to refresh our ideas and um and my teaching practice, but it's also for me about connecting with other teachers and other colleagues that I don't normally have time to. The two days have been amazing. We've had lots of people reconnecting. So, this is the first big SASTA event for the year. So, since our last STEM conference, it's been about four, four months, so it's great to see everybody again, hear about what they're doing in the new year, as well as just building up our professional skills.

title: HIGHLIGHTS: Qualifying 1 | 2026 Isle of Man TT Races
transcription: Conditions were once more perfect for the first qualifying of TT 2023, with record temperatures and clear skies across the island. It would be Superbike and Superstock machines that would open the evening, with Dean Harrison leading the field onto Glencrutchery Road. The Honda Racing UK rider would complete two laps on his Fireblade Superbike with the best lap of 133.514 mph, the fastest lap ever seen on an opening day of qualifying. The adopted Manxman looking for his first Superbike win since 2018. Second fastest on the Superbike, a similar Fireblade of Michael Dunlop. The 21-time TT winner returning to Honda machinery on the big bike with a fastest time of 130.398 mph. Also in the 130 club on Tuesday evening, and sporting a similar Honda, John McGuinness. Just two seconds adrift of Dunlop, the Morecambe Missile finished with an average speed of 130.088 mph. While the returning Peter Hickman was seventh fastest, his best lap at 125.592 mph. Hickman fared much better in the Superstocks, finishing second fastest on the day, just six seconds adrift of the fastest time. With the nine-time TT winner crashing in both the previous two events, he will surely be aiming for a clean 2023 Tourist Trophy. Australia's Josh Brookes was the only other rider to break the 130 mph barrier on the Superstock, piloting his FHO Racing BMW to a 130.197 mph time. With Davey Todd fifth, Brookes could be a dark horse for podiums or more. And in third place, Jamie Coward. The Yorkshireman missed the 2022 event with injury, but it's clear he's quickly jelling with the KTS team, a best time of 128.788 mph. What's next? Following the Superbike and Superstock session, the next outing was for the Supersport and Supertwin machines. And in the Supersport class, it was all the familiar faces at the front, bar Dean Harrison. The pit limiter on his Honda got stuck on, so he had to return to the assembly area while the mechanics got to work, missing out on important track time. Of those who completed laps, it was no surprise to see Michael Dunlop at the top of the timesheets. Aiming to continue his Yamaha dominance in class, an average lap speed of 126.917 mph would be good enough for the top spot. Next best was the BPE by Russell Racing Yamaha of James Hillier, the Hampshire...

And the reason for this, largely, has been school. Each generation spends more time in school. We use school to develop our cognition. Congratulations, you see your correlation. Until Gen Z. Gen Z is the first generation in modern history to underperform us on basically every cognitive measure we have, from basic attention to memory to literacy to numeracy to executive functioning to even general IQ, even though they go to more school than we did. And if you ask people about Iraq, what was the source of many of our casualties in Iraq, you'll get estimates as high as 75 or 80% of them were due to Iranian-made roadside bombs. The film has been on the radar since 2019 and after numerous setbacks, reshoots, and a lot of tinkering, it's here and you can feel all of that interference on the screen. Much of these complications stem from the fact that the script originally focused on the sexual abuse allegations towards Jackson, so much so that the film supposedly opened with that part of his life and looped back around to focusing on the scandal for the third act. But after an attorney for the Jackson Estate discovered a clause in one of the accusers' settlements with Jackson, barring the depiction or mention of him in any movie, things changed. This and some other factors ultimately pushed the film back an entire year, leading to 22 days of reshoots that occurred as recently as last June. And the result is a movie about a flawless protagonist, a really talented guy who, after overcoming some seemingly minor hurdles, became the most famous person on the planet thanks to writing some of the best songs of all time. Michael was, like any musical biopic about a beloved artist, always going to work on me just a little bit. title: "No Country Matches India's Energy": Sam Altman's Viral Speech at AI Summit 2026 | News18
transcription:
**Shereen Bhan**: I'm Shereen Bhan and we've got probably one of the biggest headliners here at the India AI Impact Summit, OpenAI's Sam Altman. Sam, great to have you join us on CNBC-TV18. It's wonderful to see you here back in India. You were sharing the stage with the Prime Minister just a few moments ago talking about how important India is, but how significant is India for OpenAI specifically? It is your second-largest market today.

**Sam Altman**: It is our second-largest market and the energy here, that people are, what people are building with the technology is just amazing to watch. We have more than 100 million weekly active users of ChatGPT. This is the fastest-growing market for Codex. And it's, it's amazing to see the energy here. Every time I come, it feels like it's gone up another level.

**Shereen Bhan**: You know, Sam, you've also shared the stage with Pratyush Kumar of Sarvam. The last time you were here, there were questions being asked on whether India can do an LLM. Have you had a look at what Sarvam has been able to put out?

**Sam Altman**: India's, yes, but more generally, India is just building incredible AI, the entire AI stack, from, you know, like data centers to models to applications, and I think there's no country in the world quite matches India for total AI energy.

**Shereen Bhan**: Sam, can you give me a sense of what we can expect now from OpenAI for India? How much can you customize OpenAI and ChatGPT for India? What should we expect?

**Sam Altman**: The number one request we get is better support of local languages and dialects, which is something we are hard at work on, and we're open to taking any other requests if you have some.

**Shereen Bhan**: Is that something you are going to double down on?

**Sam Altman**: Yeah, we're hard at work on that already now.

**Shereen Bhan**: Okay. You've just announced a partnership with TCS, and of course, you're going to be one of the first clients as far as TCS's data center is concerned. What do you envisage as far as that relationship and that partnership is concerned, and do you believe you're likely to ink more partnerships here in India, especially on the enterprise side?

**Sam Altman**: Totally. Hard to overstate, as I mentioned earlier, how much energy there is for building AI and building with AI in India, and I think you should expect to see more partnerships and much more activity here as we try to work with the Indian people to bring AI to the rest of the world in all of these amazing ways.
caption: In this engaging video interview, Shereen Bhan, a female host with a bright, energetic, and professional Indian English accent, speaks with Sam Altman, the CEO of OpenAI, who responds in a calm, measured, and articulate American accent. Set at the India AI Impact Summit, the conversation highlights India's massive significance to OpenAI as its second-largest market, with Altman expressing amazement at the country's vibrant AI energy, high user engagement, and rapid growth in Codex usage. They discuss India's growing AI ecosystem, including efforts like Sarvam, and address customization needs, with Altman confirming that OpenAI is actively working on better support for local Indian languages and dialects. The interview wraps up with a discussion on OpenAI's partnership with TCS, with Altman hinting at more upcoming collaborations and deeper integration with Indian talent to advance AI globally.

transcription: इंसान भाई साहब, इंसान! क्या बोलूं मैं? इतनी ज्यादा बारिश हो रही है ना बाहर। अच्छा हां, मूवी के बारे में बात करनी है। तो कौन सोच सकता है कि उनका अपना फेवरेट सुपरहीरो स्पाइडरमैन इस मूवी में... ना रे, स्पॉयलर देने थोड़ी आया हूं मैं। डोंट वरी, सीधा रिव्यू चालू करते हैं। वेल हेलो, मेरा नाम है योगी और हमारी मुलाकात बार-बार होगी। भाई, सबसे पहले तो आपको सारे स्पाइडरमैन मूवीज का नॉलेज होना जरूरी है, स्पेशली टॉम हॉलैंड वाले। एंड नहीं आता है कुछ तो वीडियो बना लिया है तुम्हारे भाई ने, यह वाला देख लेना। लेकिन ऑनेस्टली बोलूं तो एक सीटी मार मूवी में जो-जो एलिमेंट होने चाहिए, इसमें है। लेकिन उतने नहीं जितना आप एक्सपेक्ट करके जा रहे हो। जो भी ट्रेलर वगैरह में देखा होगा आपने एक्शन पीसेज, वह तो यार स्टोरी लाइन समझाते वक्त दो-दो सेकंड के लिए ही है जितना ट्रेलर में दिखाया था। बट यह सिर्फ एक्शन एंड सुपरहीरोइक एलिमेंट पर डिपेंड नहीं करती। स्पाइडरमैन अपना सब कुछ खो चुका है, लेकिन सबको खोने के बाद भी उसको अपनी सुपरहीरो वाली जिम्मेदारी निभानी है। लेकिन इन सबके बीच सबसे बड़ा सवाल यह है कि क्या उसकी आइडेंटिटी अब एटलीस्ट नेड और एमजे के सामने आएगी या वह फिर से अकेला रह जाएगा? एंड क्यों उसको हल्क एंड स्कॉर्पियन के साथ लड़ना पड़ रहा है, वह तो अब मूवी देखो और खुद जान जाओ। भाई, सुबह-सुबह 6:30 बजे का शो देखने गया था मैं एंड इट वास टोटल हाउसफुल। उतना ही नहीं, इंग्लिश हो या हिंदी, सारे शोज हाउसफुल है भाई। इतना क्रेज है इस मूवी का। फिर भले ही टिकट के प्राइस स्काई हाई क्यों ना हो, 500, 700, 1400! एनीवेज, क्या मुझे इस फिल्म को नो वे होम के ग्रैंडनेस के साथ कंपेयर करना चाहिए? बिल्कुल भी नहीं। वह एपिक बनी थी भाई। उसका एपिक मास लेवल अगर यहां एक्सपेक्ट करके आए हो तो यार निराशा ही हाथ लगेगी। लेकिन, लेकिन, लेकिन, अगर तुमने टोबी मैग्वायर वाली स्पाइडरमैन देखी है, आई मीन उसका सेकंड पार्ट, तो बार-बार आपको वह फिल्म याद आएगी, मैं लिख कर देता हूं। उस फिल्म में उसका जो इमोशनल स्टेट था, वैसा का ही कुछ इमोशनल स्टेट यहां टॉम हॉलैंड के स्पाइडरमैन में भी आपको दिखेगा। जिसकी वजह से स्पाइडरमैन के अंदर का डीएनए स्ट्रक्चर चेंज हो जाता है। आई मीन इस बार वह अपने एनिमीज से लड़ने के साथ-साथ अपने आप से भी लड़ रहा है कि साला यह हो क्या रहा है। ऊपर से ट्रेलर से भले ही आइडिया ना लगा हो कि एग्जैक्ट विलन कौन है; द हैंड, द स्कॉर्पियन, हल्क या वह जो हमेशा हूडी में है। आप देखो, आपको आइडिया...

title: Squary AI Presentation at FVCC (Florida Venture Capital Conference 26)
transcription:
Presenting next will be Sanjay Chopra of Squary AI.

Hi, I'm Jai, co-founder and head of product at Squary AI. The problem that we are trying to solve is that mid-market legal teams and in-house counsels are stuck between manual document review and unreliable AI solutions. Attorneys spend 60% of their time reviewing thousands of pages per case. Generic AI tools hallucinating and lacks citations, while many enterprise platforms are expensive and overly complex. Now, that doesn't work for all the firms. So, we built Squary specially for them. Squary analyzes 10,000 plus page documents in full context and supports exclusive standardized legal workflows tailored to each firm. We are usage-based and not per seat. So, firms can start small, level up as they see value, and scale during the heavy workload months without long-term commitments. From 2024 to 2025, we grew our revenue 5x and processed 1.5 million pages for a single firm.

Sanjay, welcome.

Thank you, thank you.

Okay, um, first of all, thank you, Jai, for the awesome video, and also Florida Venture Forum for holding sort of this event, so thank you, everybody. So, you started this business a while ago, and you have gone through a couple of machinations to end on in-house legal AI optimization. So, maybe give us a little bit of the history, but then focus on why'd you pick that vertical?

Awesome. Great question. So, I've been doing AI and computer science for a really long time, 30 plus years. This is before AI was sexy the way it is right now. So, but when we started the company about 10 years ago, it was called Cognistx, and we were doing a lot of bespoke AI solutions, so our expertise is natural language

title: 6th International HKL Conference Telford, UK | 11 April 2026 | Dr Anna Stewart | HKL Board Member
transcription: Now on stage I'd like to welcome the wonderful Dr. Anna Stewart, HKL board member. Good morning, dear brothers and sisters, hermanos y hermanas. It is such a joy to be here with you today at the 6th Conference of HKL. Please let us take a moment now and close our eyes. Feel your feet on the ground. Tap your toes, wiggle your toes, tap your feet on the ground. And feel them deeply connected to this beautiful place on Earth called Telford. Take a few deep breaths in, out, in and out. And as we breathe, we connect to all the trees and the plants, the soil and mycorrhizae, rivers and oceans, birds, animals, and each other. And as we open our eyes gently and look around, we can see that we are all breathing together. We are one. And we could not exist for more than a few minutes without this precious air, made and refreshed by our beautiful Mother Earth, vibrant and of full of life, so humble, kind and loving to us, her children. And yet we continue to treat her and each other as though we were disposable. To be used and discarded, pollution in our air, water and soils, war between nations, and wars in our homes. Where is the humility, kindness and love? The deep reverence and love for all life beginning with our own? We are asleep, deeply asleep. And we should be troubled. In our slumber we are causing great suffering to our Mother Earth, to each other and to ourselves. HKL, Humility, Kindness and Love, is the antidote we so desperately need today. Each of us has the seed of HKL living within, a beautiful golden seed patiently waiting to grow and flower. The HKL movement is the fertile ground, the water, the gentle breeze that this seed has been waiting for, for a long time.
caption: In this audio recording, a female speaker introduces Dr. Anna Stewart, HKL board member, who is met with applause from the audience. Dr. Stewart begins her speech in a spacious hall with an echo, greeting the audience warmly. She then invites them to close their eyes and perform a grounding exercise, guiding them to feel their feet on the ground and take deep, audible breaths. Throughout the speech, she speaks at a slow, measured pace, emphasizing a message of connection to Mother Earth and each other. She contrasts this connection with the harsh reality of human pollution and conflict, questioning the absence of humility, kindness, and love (HKL). Finally, she describes HKL as a vital antidote and a seed waiting to grow within everyone, with the HKL movement acting as the nourishing environment it needs.

title: BREAKING NEWS: Thomas Massie Explodes On DOJ Over Epstein Handling, Names People He Wants Prosecuted
transcription: Thank you, Madam Speaker. Congress created the Department of Justice, Congress funds the Department of Justice, and Congress is responsible for the oversight of the Department of Justice. When will we see justice? I'll tell you what I've not seen. I've not seen any arrests from the revelations in the Epstein files, over 3 million documents describing horrible things, describing unspeakable things, much of it redacted. Over two dozen people have resigned, CEOs, members of government worldwide, but I haven't seen any arrests or investigations here in the United States from this Department of Justice. Prince Andrew, Duke of York, who has since been stripped of his royalty, his royal titles due to his affiliation with Jeffrey Epstein, has been arrested? Peter Mandelson, who previously served as UK's ambassador to the United States resigned in disgrace from United Kingdom's House of Lords and the Labour Party, and he's been arrested? Former Prime Minister of Norway, Torbjørn Jagland, has been charged? But we don't see any charges, arrests, or investigations in the United States. What do we see? We see our FBI Director celebrating in the locker room at the Olympics overseas. It's fine to be proud of this country, but we should be proud of this country because we have a system of justice that works, and yet we do not. Who are the men that should be investigated? I'll name them right here. Leon Black, you don't even have to see past the redactions to see that this man needs to be investigated. Jess Staley, accused of terrible things, it's right there in the files. Why is he not being investigated? And Leslie Wexner, why did the FBI list him as a co-conspirator in their own documents in a child sex trafficking case and then tell him, according to him, that they had no questions for him? Why is that? Well, the Epstein Files Transparency Act requires the DOJ and the FBI to disclose to us their internal memos and emails about how they made those decisions whether to prosecute or not prosecute, yet they have not delivered those memos. And we still don't have the memos and documents and emails from 2008 to explain why Jeffrey Epstein was given such a light sentence in what would have been an open and shut case

title: 'What are we doing here?': Fmr. fed judge slams Trump admin naming 'worst of the worst' judges
transcription:
Worst of the worst. That is what James Percival, a senior Trump administration official in the Department of Homeland Security, is calling sitting federal district judges whose rulings he doesn't like. He's name-checking them on social media over their immigration-related rulings the Trump administration disagrees with at a time when threats against judges are escalating. And that phrase, "the worst of the worst," you've probably heard it before because Percival is borrowing that from the department's description of undocumented immigrants who have committed serious crimes. Joining us, former Chief Judge for the US Middle District of Pennsylvania, appointed by President George W. Bush, John Jones, III. He's currently the president of Dickinson College. Judge, uh, Jones, thank you so much for joining us. Just your reaction, first off, to this DHS, this, this administration official posting judges' names.

Well, he's not only, uh, Laura, name-checking them, but he's also showing their pictures on the website. And, uh, he's also showing, uh, the, the, a picture of, uh, my, my good friend, uh, Esther Salas, uh, who's a judge, as you know, in New Jersey who lost her only child, her son, uh, shot by an assailant a couple of years ago. This is really, my view, uh, beyond the pale. And I guess Mr. Percival missed the hearing a couple weeks ago, uh, with, uh, Justices Kagan and Coney Barrett, uh, who, as you just said, indicated that the threat level is higher than it has ever been, uh, for judges and for justices. Uh, so we're not operating in a vacuum here. Uh, I think it's just absolutely beyond the pale what Mr. Percival is doing. This isn't about the First Amendment. This is about, uh, endangering, uh, judges and their families.

And James Percival, I should say, is the General Counsel of the Department of Homeland Security, and it's stunning that someone who is in that position is doing this. And, and you mentioned, uh, Judge Salas, Judge Esther Salas, uh, a federal judge who did talk to the Huffington Post recently about this, and she...

title: Broken By Abuse but Not Destroyed (Female Version | Healing from Trauma | Renee Solace
category: Mental Health Vlogs & Personal Video Diaries
transcription:
I learned to be quiet before I learned my name.

Walking on eggshells just to dodge the pain.

Love felt like fear, I couldn't tell the difference.

Every "I'm sorry" came with more resistance.

I carried your anger like it was mine.

Tried to make sense of it a thousand times.

I shrunk myself just to survive your storms.

Called it love, but it was never warm.

You took my voice but you couldn't take my soul.

Buried me deep, but I'm still whole.

I was broken by abuse,
but I'm not destroyed.

You tried to silence me,
but I found my voice.

Every scar tells a story of how I survived.

I bent, I bruised, but I'm still alive.

You don't get to write the ending of me.

I'm reclaiming my power, I'm finally free.

I was broken by abuse,
but I'm not destroyed.

I used to blame myself for your hands and your words.

Thought if I was better, it wouldn't hurt.

But healing showed me what I couldn't see.

The pain you gave had nothing to do with me, no.

I'm unlearning all the lies you told.

Rebuilding a heart that was left in the cold.

Piece by piece, I'm choosing me.

Learning what safe love is supposed to be.

You tried to break me down to feel in control.

title: AI x Society | I/O 2026 Keynote
transcription: Today we showed you our next-generation models, Gemini 3.5 and Omni, new coding capabilities in Anti-gravity 2.0, agents in search and Gemini Spark, and so much more. It's great to see Gemini transforming so many Google products used by billions of people every day. All of these advances show the staggering pace of AI progress. It's incredible, even for those of us who have spent our entire lives working on this. AGI is now on the horizon, and it will be the most profound and impactful technology ever invented. If built right, it could propel human progress and flourishing beyond our imaginations. We're in a moment of immense promise, but also enormous responsibility. It's important that we are clear-eyed about the potential challenges, and use all the tools at our disposal to ensure the safety of our agentic systems and ultimately, AGI itself. One area of risk that has gained a lot of attention recently is cybersecurity. Google has invested in this area for decades, and we're bringing our frontier capabilities and deep expertise to help secure the world's codebases. We have tools like our code security agent, CodeMender, which automatically finds and fixes critical software vulnerabilities. Today, we're inviting a select group of experts to test the new CodeMender API, and we'll be launching it more broadly soon. Stepping back, the whole reason I've worked on AI my entire career was because I saw it as the ultimate tool to advance science and our understanding of the world. It's awesome to see those dreams become a reality, with AI beginning to help scientists in almost every field. Building on this momentum, I'm excited to announce Gemini for Science.

category: Mental Health Vlogs & Personal Video Diaries
transcription: The loudest cry ever made, was the one nobody heard. Stopped asking for help, and everybody thought I was healing. And everybody thought I was healing. I became the friend everybody leaned upon. The one who stayed steady when everything went wrong. Always saying, "I'm good" with a practiced smile. Even though I've been breaking for a long, long while. I mastered the art of hiding in plain sight. Laughing in daylight, unraveling at night. Every "I'm okay" felt heavier to say. Because the truth kept begging me, not to look away. I answered every message, returned every call, but nobody noticed I was disappearing through it all. Not because they didn't care, maybe because I became too good at pretending I wasn't hurting. How do you explain a wound nobody can see? How do you ask for rescue, when you've convinced everyone you're free? My silence was crying for help. Every quiet moment said my name. I smiled so nobody would worry, while carrying invisible pain. My silence was crying for help, but nobody knew what to hear. Sometimes the strongest disguise is looking like you're doing fine. The hardest conversations that ever left my chest, I rehearsed them a thousand times, then buried every sense. I wasn't afraid of being judged, I was afraid of becoming a burden, so I carried everything myself until my own heart began to feel too heavy to lift. People celebrated the version of me they could see, nobody met the exhausted soul trying to survive behind closed doors. There were nights I stared at the ceiling not asking for answers, just hoping.

title: Report: Donald Trump told Florida police chief ‘everyone’ knew about Jeffrey Epstein
transcription: There is brand new reporting from Julie K. Brown of the Miami Herald. She's been a trailblazer on the Epstein story. Once again, calls into question every single statement Trump puts forward when it comes to the central issue. What did Donald Trump know, and when did he know it, about Jeffrey Epstein's child sex trafficking? From that reporting, quote, "In July 2006, just as Jeffrey Epstein's criminal sex charge became public, Donald Trump called then Palm Beach Police Chief Michael Reiter to tell him that Epstein's activities with teenage girls were well-known in both New York and Palm Beach." Reiter recalled his conversation with Trump in a 2019 interview with the FBI. More from the reporting, quote, "Thank goodness you're stopping him, everyone has known he's been doing this," Trump told Reiter. Reiter told FBI agents that Donald Trump revealed that Epstein's associate Ghislaine Maxwell was Epstein's, quote, "operative," and that Donald Trump said, quote, "She is evil," and to focus on her, according to the reporting. Trump told Reiter that, quote, "He was around Epstein once when teenagers were present, and Trump got the hell out of there," the report said. Donald Trump also told Reiter that he threw Epstein out of his Mar-a-Lago club. A Justice Department official tells us that, quote, "We are not aware of any corroborating evidence that the president contacted law enforcement 20 years ago." Well, this squares with something the White House has said in the past, it does not square with what Trump has said himself about the past. This is from 2019, the days after Jeffrey Epstein's arrest. Did you have any suspicions that he was molesting young women? Underaged women. No, I had no idea. I had no idea. I haven't spoken to him in many, many years. If, quote, "everyone has known he's been doing this," as Trump reportedly put it, and Trump himself was with Epstein when there were teenagers present and, quote, "got the hell out of there," as he said, why didn't he contact authorities? Why didn't he contact authorities when Epstein, quote, "stole," Trump's words, not ours, survivor Virginia Roberts Giuffre from her job at the spa at Mar-a-Lago in the year 2000? Trump did say this, though, about all that back in July of this year, last year. Yeah, he took people, and because he took people, I said, "Don't do it anymore." You know, they work for me, and he took, uh, beyond that, he took some others. And once he did that, that was the end of him. I didn't like— when they steal people, I don't like it.

transcription: Welcome. I hope that you had a wonderful Easter or Passover. It was an eventful first quarter of the year. Let's reflect on a few of the major themes. Gas prices were up nearly a dollar a gallon in the first quarter, and when multiplied across millions of households filling up week after week, the cumulative impact on consumer spending and savings rates is significant. However, it's the indirect costs that are possibly more meaningful. Gasoline and diesel fuel are basic inputs to nearly everything the economy produces. Transportation, manufacturing, agriculture, and distribution all depend on energy, which means that higher fuel costs raise the price of goods and services across the board. The stock market saw its share of volatility as well. In Q1, the S&P 500, in blue, we see here was down about 4.3% for the quarter, with the sectors on the left in green being the out-performers, and on the right in red, being the under-performers. The standout on the left is energy, having a terrific start to the year, for perhaps not so terrific reasons. And then many of the sectors that outperformed in the past, on the right, financials, consumer discretionary, technology, not performing especially well, with this highlighting the potential benefits of diversification. So, how does this negative 4.3% return compared to past quarters? Well, this chart shows quarterly S&P 500 returns, ranked from worst on the left to best on the right, going back to 1988. And interestingly, what we see is that the Q1 return from '16 is exactly the same as the Q1 return from '15, -4.3%. Now, interestingly, the other three quarters of '15 happened to be very strong, with Q2 returning 10.9%, Q3, 5.9%, and Q4, 2.7%. This, of course, isn't to suggest that the rest of '16 will be just as the rest of '15 was, but it's a good reminder that often when market participants are most concerned is when the market performs best. Thanks for watching. Enjoy today.

title: Staying | The Cost of Choosing Loyalty Over Safety
category: Mental Health Vlogs & Personal Video Diaries
transcription: The hardest battles are often fought in silence. Behind polite smiles, behind tired eyes, behind voices that still say, "I'm fine." Some people carry storms so quietly that even the people closest to them never fully see the rain. And sometimes, the mind becomes heavy for so long that exhaustion starts feeling normal. Thoughts repeat themselves, doubts grow louder. The world slowly loses color and people begin believing they are far less important than they truly are. Pain has a way of shrinking perspective. It whispers things that sound permanent during temporary seasons. It tells tired hearts that nothing will change, that peace belongs to other people, that healing was never meant for them. And slowly, the weight of those thoughts begins to feel real. But thoughts are not always truth. Some people are not trying to leave life behind, they are simply trying to escape the heaviness of carrying everything alone. The pressure, the expectations, the loneliness hidden beneath functioning lives. And sometimes, the people who seem strongest are simply the ones who learned how to suffer quietly. Not because they are weak, but because they became used to surviving silently. One day at a time, sometimes one hour at a time, and occasionally, one breath at a time, there is no shame in surviving slowly. None of us truly know how deeply we are woven into the lives of others. Sometimes, we minimize our importance because pain has made us forget how much of our presence...

Her speech is slow, gentle, and whispered, conveying a sense of warmth, sadness, and profound understanding. Accompanied by a soothing and melancholic ambient background track with gentle piano chords, she speaks about the battles people fight in secret, hiding behind polite smiles and tired eyes. The message is one of validation and comfort for those carrying heavy burdens alone, emphasizing that there is no shame in surviving slowly, one day, one hour, or even one breath at a time.

title: Broken Bone Healing Process | How Plaster Helps in Fracture? | Bone Fractures | Dr. Binocs Show
category: Mental Health Vlogs & Personal Video Diaries
transcription: What are you timing, little kitty? Figuring out how quickly this plaster cast helps my broken bone heal. Ah, then let's find out how does plaster help heal fractured bones? Zoom in! You might think that a plaster cast heals a broken bone. Surprisingly, that's not the case. Plaster doesn't repair the bone itself. Instead, it provides the support and stability your body needs to heal the fracture naturally. In fact, the healing process begins the moment the bone breaks. Firstly, a blood clot forms around the fracture, helping stabilize the fracture site and causing swelling. Meanwhile, specialized white blood cells, including macrophages, remove damaged tissue and prepare the area for repair. Before applying a plaster cast, doctors examine the injury and use x-rays to assess the position of the fractured bone. If the broken pieces are out of alignment, the patient may first be given pain medication or sedation to improve comfort. The doctor then carefully moves the bone fragments back into their proper position in a procedure called a reduction. Once the bone is correctly aligned, the injured limb is wrapped in a protective layer and covered with wet plaster bandages. These bandages can be molded to fit the body shape and gradually harden
caption: This audio clip features an engaging educational narration tailored for children, explaining how a plaster cast helps heal fractured bones. It begins with a brief dialogue between a child and the main narrator, an enthusiastic adult male with a lively, dramatic, and friendly voice. The background is filled with upbeat, playful instrumental music and a variety of cartoon-like sound effects, such as ticking clocks, whooshes, and squishing sounds, which complement the narrative. The narrator explains that the plaster cast itself does not heal the bone but provides stability for natural healing. He details the physiological process starting from blood clot formation and the role of white blood cells, followed by the medical procedure involving X-rays, bone reduction, and the application of wet plaster bandages.

title: Trump Iran War Address Cold Open - SNL
transcription: Last evening, at the very normal time of 2:00 in the morning, President Trump informed the nation that we were at war with Iran. And now with some further thoughts, President Trump. Hello. Hi. Good evening and happy World War III to all who celebrate. It's me, Donald Trump, FIFA Peace Prize winner and Nobel Peace Prize taker, yoink. Remember when I did that? I launched this attack after me and my Board of Peace decided that we were bored of peace. Little wordplay there. Did you catch it? As we all know, Iran has been 2 weeks away from developing a nuclear weapon for like the last 15 years or something. So we had to act now and we're doing war. War! What is it good for? Distracting from the Epstein files. And I know on the campaign trail I promised no new foreign wars, but listen, wars is plural, right? I'm allowed to do one. title: ITR Filing Online 2026-27 | ITR 1 Filing Online For Salaried Employees FY 2025-26 (AY 2026-27)
transcription: जी हाँ दोस्तों, अगर आप भी कहीं नौकरी करते हैं और आपकी इनकम का सोर्स सैलरी है, तो आप केवल 5 मिनट के अंदर अपनी ITR को खुद से ऑनलाइन फ़ाइल कर सकते हैं। उसके लिए आपको किसी CA या फिर प्रोफ़ेशनल को कोई भी चार्जेज़ पे करने की ज़रूरत नहीं है। आज की इस वीडियो में मैं आपको लाइव दिखाऊँगा कि कैसे आप ऑनलाइन खुद से अपनी ITR को 5 मिनट के अंदर फ़ाइल कर सकते हैं। वीडियो आपके लिए बहुत ही इंपॉर्टेंट होने वाली है, वीडियो को एंड तक बिना स्किप किये ज़रूर देखना। और अगर आपने चैनल को अभी तक सब्सक्राइब नहीं किया है तो प्लीज सब्सक्राइब कर लेना। मेरा नाम है प्रमोद और आप देख रहे हैं 'My Simple Guide'। तो सबसे पहले आपको इनकम टैक्स के पोर्टल को ओपन करना है। पोर्टल का डायरेक्ट लिंक आपको नीचे वीडियो के डिस्क्रिप्शन में मिल जाएगा, जहाँ से आप क्लिक करके डायरेक्ट पोर्टल को ओपन कर सकते हैं। जैसे ही आप पोर्टल को ओपन करेंगे, कुछ इस तरह का इंटरफेस आपको दिखाई देगा। यहाँ पर ऊपर राइट हैंड साइड में आप देखेंगे आपको 'Login' ऑप्शन पर क्लिक करना है। और उसके बाद अगले पेज पर अपने पैन नंबर और अपने पासवर्ड की सहायता से यहाँ पर लॉगिन कर लेना है। जैसे ही आप लॉगिन करेंगे, अगला इंटरफेस आपको कुछ इस तरह से दिखाई देगा। सबसे पहले यहाँ पर आपको अपने असेसमेंट ईयर को चुनना है, यानी कि 2026-27 को चुनना है। उसके बाद नीचे मोड ऑफ़ फ़ाइलिंग में आपको 'Online' चुनना है और नीचे 'Continue' ऑप्शन पर क्लिक कर देना है। अगले पेज पर 'Start New Filing' ऑप्शन पर क्लिक करना है। उसके बाद अगले पेज पर स्टेटस में आपको 'Individual' चुनना है और नीचे 'Proceed' ऑप्शन पर क्लिक करना है। क्लिक करते ही अगले पेज पर आपको अपने ITR फ़ॉर्म को चुनना है। तो यहाँ पर सिंपली आपको ITR-1 को चुनना है। फ़ॉर्म को चुनते ही आपको बताया जाएगा कि कौन-कौन लोग इस फ़ॉर्म को सबमिट कर सकते हैं। कोई भी इंडिविजुअल रेज़िडेंट जिसकी इनकम ₹50 लाख तक है और इनकम का सोर्स सैलरी, टू हाउस प्रॉपर्टीज़ यानी कि कोई रेंटल इनकम है, अदर सोर्सेज यानी कि सेविंग बैंक अकाउंट या फिर FD पर कोई इंटरेस्ट मिला है, और ₹1,25,000 तक कोई लॉन्ग टर्म कैपिटल गेन हुआ है, और अगर ₹5,000 तक की कोई एग्रीकल्चर इनकम है, तो ITR-1 को आप लोग सबमिट कर सकते हैं। उसके बाद नीचे 'Proceed with ITR-1' ऑप्शन पर क्लिक करना है। एक अलर्ट मैसेज आएगा, उसको 'OK' करना है। और उसके बाद नीचे 'Let's Get Started' ऑप्शन पर क्लिक करना है। अगले पेज पर आपसे पूछा जाएगा कि आप अपनी ITR को क्यों फ़ाइल करना चाहते हैं, तो सिंपली आपको पहले ऑप्शन को चुनना है, 'Taxable income is more than basic...'

title: BREAKING: Trump makes MAJOR announcement about Iran ahead of deadline
transcription: We're just getting some breaking news here about the war. The President has just issued a Truth Social from the White House saying this: "Based on conversations with Prime Minister Sharif and Field Marshal Munir of Pakistan and wherein they requested that I hold off the destructive force being sent tonight to Iran and subject to the Islamic Republic of Iran agreeing to the complete, immediate, and safe opening of the Strait of Hormuz, I agree to suspend the bombing and attack of Iran for a period of two weeks. This will be a double-sided ceasefire. The reason for doing so is that we have already met and exceeded all military objectives and are very far along with a definitive agreement concerning long-term peace with Iran and peace in the Middle East. We received a 10-point proposal from Iran and believe it is a workable basis on which to negotiate. Almost all of the various points of past contention have been agreed to between the United States and Iran, but a two-week period will allow the agreement to be finalized and consummated. On behalf of the United States of America as President, and also representing the countries of the Middle East, it is an honor to have this long-term problem close to resolution. Thank you for your attention to this matter, President Donald J. Trump." Again, just seconds ago, um, before the deadline, uh, for attacks on Iran tonight, and it seems like a deal is in the making. Um, there had been talk, Mark, all day long about maybe this was happening. How do you see this, and how does it play politically here at home? Well, I I think the President had to do it if he could get terms that include an unconditional opening of the strait, which it sounds like he's got. Because the markets had to look at that and see. Well, he has to do it because, look, people are, in my latest poll, 51% uh, support the war, 54% said it was justified, but 57% said if he could get a good deal, he should take it. So, I think it's a risky two-week period because it enables them to regroup. But on the other hand, the President, if he thinks he has a real opportunity to come out with a negotiated victory, then I think he had to do it. A lot of people got, you know, really energized about some of the things he posted about, you know, annihilation of civilization. But now he's coming with this deal, Kellyanne, how do you see this big picture? It's the 11th straight year of them in high dudgeon about everything he writes and says. He said he doesn't care about his critics, but he does care about getting peace in a just cause here. He does care about oil flowing again. If he gets a deal, the ultimate dealmaker, part of how he wins these elections, Brett, then that will matter to people. Um, there's one group that he's not mentioning at all, and they're called Europe and NATO. It's really fascinating what's happened there in a short amount of time. You even have Volodymyr Zelenskyy running around in these Gulf State countries saying, "I'm not getting weapons, I'm giving them to you and giving you our intelligence for the last couple years in this war with Russia." It's really fascinating what's happened there in short order. NATO's coming to the White House tomorrow

title: Ransom Note Clues Revealed | Jesse Weber Live
transcription:
6 months ago tonight. This is after 84-year-old Nancy Guthrie disappeared from her Tucson-area home. The Pima, the Pima County Sheriff's Office has finally released the alleged ransom notes that were supposedly sent by these alleged kidnappers. Now, as you may know, these notes have been the source of more than a little controversy in the months since Today Show host Savannah Guthrie's mother vanished, mostly because we still don't know if they're real. And though the cops still won't verify their authenticity, because of something that I'm going to get into in just a little bit, it is important to read them in full. So here we go. The first alleged note that was apparently sent on February 2nd says this, "Hello, Savannah. We have your mother, Nancy. She is safe but scared. She will be held for ransom and once payment is received, she will be released unharmed. We will be holding her for a maximum of 7 days. You will need to send Bitcoin in the amount of $4 million USD, United States Dollars, before 5:00 p.m. on Thursday the 5th. If payment is not received, the ransom will be increased to $6 million USD, which will need to be paid by 5:00 p.m. on Monday the 9th. Once payment is received to the Bitcoin address below, she will be released within 12 hours of deposit to a safe drop-off location back in Tucson. If payment is not received by the last deadline on Monday the 9th at 5:00 p.m., she will be killed. Your mother is aware of this, and her life is in your hands. It is in the best interest of everyone to have this completed as soon as possible. You will not be able to contact me from here on out. There will be no negotiation. Do not play games. Law enforcement will not be able to help you. She had a white smartwatch on the floor of the foot of her bed, and the white floodlight in back yard was destroyed."

Then you have the second alleged note. Very different, very different tone. This was apparently sent on February 6th, so 3 days before the deadline from that first note. It says, "Guthrie family, we did not fully grasp the seriousness of her physical condition. We never intended to hurt her, that was not our intention. She perished shortly after she was taken. We believe it was heart-related. She is buried in nature now. Nothing you could have done could have changed the outcome. We want your family to know this, and hope you can find peace. We are truly sorry."

Now, despite the fact that the Sheriff's Office couldn't authenticate the notes, they are now asking for the public's help in finding whoever wrote them. Said in a press release, quote, "These communications reveal distinctive patterns of word choice, syntax, and phraseology that reflect the writer's unique linguistic style. We believe these distinctive linguistic characteristics may be recognizable to someone who knows or has interacted with the note's writer."

title: Who Is LB~Sickning? | The Story Behind SicKKo Entertainment
transcription: So, who is LB Sykning? He's more than a rapper, more than a creator, more than a personality online. LB is a storyteller, someone who uses music, visuals, and conversation to shine a light on the real emotions most people try to hide. The name Sykning carries attitude, edge, impact. It represents the side of life that isn't polished—the late nights, the struggle, the scars, the lessons learned the hard way, and the strength it takes to survive all of it. Because behind the music is a human being who's lived through real things: pain, chaos, growth, redemption, reflection, and instead of burying that, LB turned it into art. Okay, enter Syk Kaco Entertainment. Not just a name, not just a label, but a movement. Syk Kaco Entertainment became the platform where music, video content, collaborations, conversations, and creativity all come together under one vision: keep it real, keep it raw, keep it authentic. There's no big corporate machine here, no glossy PR filter, just independent grind, built brick by brick. Syk Kaco Entertainment grew as a space where outsiders felt seen, where people who've been through something could recognize the emotion in the music and say, "Yeah, I feel that." So what makes pound Sykning's music different? It's the truth inside it. The delivery is raw, emotional, and unapologetic. There's no pretending to be something else, no fake image, no plastic persona. LB talks about real-world issues: pain, struggle, love, loss, frustration, survival, street-level reality, mental battles, and the journey toward becoming stronger than the past. Every bar carries weight, every verse comes from a place of experience, not imagination, and that's why the audience connects, because the music doesn't talk at you, it talks to you. It speaks a language that resonates with anyone who's ever had to fight to find their way. But here's the thing...

title: Changing the Way DFL Politicians Speak to People Is Only the First Step
transcription: Hi, and welcome to another episode of Better Minneapolis. I'm your host, Terry White. If you're interested in what we're doing here and appreciate it, please consider becoming a paid subscriber. Today's episode is called, Changing the Way DFL Politicians Speak to People is Only the First Step. Real programs that improve residents' lives, daily lives, are needed to rebuild the DFL's brand. The Humphrey Mondale Dinner Thursday night drew a sold-out crowd to the Minneapolis Convention Center. For DFL leaders and donors, it was an opportunity to network and discuss the party's path forward. Past keynote speakers have included Hakeem Jeffries, Nancy Pelosi, Hillary and Bill Clinton, and Elizabeth Warren. This year's speaker was Andy Beshear, Governor of Kentucky, a choice that carried a message. Beshear's record speaks for itself. According to the DFL website, the Beshear administration has secured more than 35 billion in private sector investment, the most of any governor in state history, driving over 60,000 new full-time jobs and supporting over 1,100 new and expanded business projects. Under his leadership, Kentucky has achieved record budget surpluses and experienced historically low unemployment rates. That's a resume most governors envy. It's also, it also gives weight to a central message. Democrats need to stop using jargon like, quote, "justice-involved individuals," end quote, and start speaking normal language, as Paula Chesley, who attended the event, shared with us. Beshear understands the reputational damage Democrats have inflicted by importing language from sociology seminars into everyday conversation. Surveys confirm it. People dislike Trump, but they dislike Democrats even more. The polling points to two areas where the DFL could gain traction with voters if they develop a coherent plan: the economy and immigration. The economy. Ditching classroom-scrubbed language for plain speech is necessary, but it's not enough. The DFL must demonstrate that it can improve people's economic lives, that working people can earn wages to raise families and afford healthcare.

title: Disconnected Management Systems Are Undermining Strategy Execution
transcription: Here we're focusing on strategy and performance, right? And when we talk about strategy and performance, there is a series of corporate processes that are part of this big umbrella that we call strategy and performance corporate processes. So we have governance, we have succession management, we have project management, audits, balanced scorecards, ISOs, certifications, innovation management, KPIs, OKRs, budgets and so much more, right? I'm not going to go through all of these. The idea is there is a number of practices or processes or management models that have, that interact with each other and we call corporate management. And each one of these can have a software to support that practice, right? So you can have a software for OKRs, for example, another software for your BIs or your dashboards or your balanced scorecard, another software for your Scrum projects or task management and so on. So for each of these practices, we have a whole ecosystem of softwares to support that practice, right? And what we've been seeing in organizations is that as you adopt an app or a software for each of these practices, they stop interacting with themselves. This should be practices that are make sense independently, but they're also part of a management system, and they should interact with each other. But when you have apps or softwares for each of these, they stop talking to each other. They start acting as silos of information, right? And this is the reality that we see in most organizations. If we take a look at this chart, this chart is the number of app SaaS apps, on average, for each organization, right? So the average number of SaaS apps. And we see that in 2015, we had only 8 SaaS apps, on average, for an organization. And this jumped to 80 in 2020 in just 5 years, then to 130 in 2022. This is the phenomenon that we call SaaS sprawl or app sprawl, right? It was the proliferation of SaaS applications in organizations, and it just boomed, right? From, in 7 years, from 8 to 130. And all of these specialized apps came about and companies adopted them, and for each activity, each management practice, you had an app for that or you have an app for that. But this created big problems in the organizations, right? Managing SaaS is a new problem for IT. So there are so many providers, that managing it all is a huge problem. And integrating it all is a huge problem. So if you have 8 SaaS applications, and you buy the 9th, okay, you're going to integrate, you know, this new SaaS application with 8 others to connect the information. But if you have 130 apps, and you buy the 131st, how are you going to connect all this? It's- it's impossible, right? So this has become a big pain in, especially in larger corporations.

He begins by outlining various corporate processes like governance, project management, OKRs, and KPIs, noting that each typically has its own supporting software. The speaker then highlights the problem of 'information silos' that occur when these individual apps fail to communicate with each other. To illustrate the scale of this issue, he presents statistics showing the dramatic increase in the average number of SaaS applications used by organizations—growing from just eight in 2015 to 130 in 2022—a phenomenon he terms 'SaaS sprawl' or 'app sprawl.' He concludes by explaining how this proliferation creates significant management and integration hurdles for IT departments, particularly within larger corporations. The speaker's delivery is measured and educational, making the complex topic easy to follow.

title: 🏆 WINNER: Best Video Pitch & 4th Runner-Up Overall | PSC X Bicol Region
transcription: The heart of the Philippines, a broken system is hurting everyone. Farmers harvest with sweat and sacrifice, yet sell at prices too low to survive. Ang hirap po kasi kahit malakas ang ani ay mababa pa rin ang presyo na naibibigay sa amin. Yung ni-harvest ko ngayon may presyo pero hindi naman alam kung magkano ang pagbili niya. Presyo ng gulay is uh parang ang may gain doon is yung middleman. Mababa ang bili ng disposer sa farmer. Kasi mababa ang presyo pag hinarvest wala na, pupunta sa ano sa pamasahe wala nang matitira para sa amin. Buyers want local produce but face high cost and unreliable supply, and customers they pay more for less. This isn't just a gap, it's a broken chain that fails us all. Lalong lumalalim pa ang ugat ng problemang kinakaharap ng mga kababayan nating magsasaka lalo na nitong nakaraang buwan. Farmers face unfair pricing, limited market access and constant uncertainty. Buyers pay inflated cost and face inconsistent supply. Consumers struggle with affordability and freshness. This inefficiency hurts our economy, our health and our communities. But what if we could bridge this gap fairly, transparently and sustainably? Agrikita is a digital marketplace connecting farmers, buyers, consumers and organizations. We're not just an app, we're a movement to achieve the UN Sustainable Development Goals and transform Philippine agriculture. Agrikita empowers four key segments: smallholder farmers, local businesses, consumers, and support organizations. Farmers are verified through secure digital profiles, ensuring trust and authenticity. They can also create product listings with just a few taps, giving them direct access to reliable buyers.
caption: The audio features a professional and engaging male narrator who speaks with clarity and expression. It begins with a solemn tone, detailing the systemic issues within Philippine agriculture. This segment is supported by real-life testimonies of local farmers speaking in Tagalog about their struggles with unfair pricing and middlemen. The narrative then shifts dynamically to a highly positive and energetic tone as an upbeat, modern electronic track plays in the background. The narrator enthusiastically introduces 'AgriKita,' a digital solution designed to bridge the gap between farmers, buyers, and consumers, explaining its features and benefits in an inspiring manner.

title: Diksha CPD Courses for Primary and High School Teachers। Diksha Courses for Teachers।
transcription: Welcome to SD Bio. দেখুন গতকাল অর্থাৎ ২৭/০৭/২০২৬ পশ্চিমবঙ্গ সমগ্র শিক্ষা মিশন স্কুল এডুকেশন ডিপার্টমেন্ট থেকে একটা নোটিফিকেশন দিয়েছে যে নোটিফিকেশনকে ঘিরে কিন্তু বিতর্ক তৈরি হয়েছে। কি রয়েছে এই নোটিফিকেশনে? আপনারা হয়তো অনেকেই দেখে নিয়েছেন, কিন্তু বিতর্ক যেটা রয়েছে সেইটা নিয়ে আজকে আলোচনা করবো এবং তার সমাধান কী সেটাও বলবো। এই নোটিফিকেশনে দেওয়া হয়েছে যেখানে বলা হচ্ছে সমস্ত স্কুলের সমস্ত হেডমাস্টার এবং অ্যাসিস্ট্যান্ট টিচারদের সিপিডি অর্থাৎ কন্টিনিউয়াস প্রফেশনাল ডেভেলপমেন্ট কোর্সগুলো মিনিমাম ৫০ ঘণ্টা করতে হবে। এর মধ্যে আমরা তো কেউ ৫০ ঘণ্টা, ৬০ ঘণ্টা, ৭০ ঘণ্টা করে ফেলেছি। কিন্তু সেগুলো সিপিডি কোর্স কি না সেটা আমাকে দেখতে হবে। সিপিডি কোর্সগুলো কিন্তু মিনিমাম ৫০ ঘণ্টা, বাকি যত কোর্স আছে আপনি ৭০, ৮০, ৯০ ঘণ্টাও অনেকে করে নিয়েছে শুনছি, কিন্তু করে নিতেই পারেন কোনো অসুবিধা নেই, যত বেশি করবেন তত আপনার স্কিল ডেভেলপমেন্ট হবে। তার সঙ্গে আর একটা গুরুত্বপূর্ণ যে খুব সম্ভবত ৯০% আমি যা দেখছি সারা ভারতবর্ষের সিচুয়েশন, টেট আমাদের দিতে হবে। তো যেহেতু টেট আমাদের দিতে হবে, এমন কোর্সগুলো সিপিডি কোর্সগুলো বেছে নেব যেগুলো আমাদের টেট দিতে সুবিধা হবে বা টেটের কিছু নলেজও গ্যাদার হবে, সেই বিষয়টাও আজকে আলোচনা করবো। যেমন ৫০ ঘণ্টা যেটা আছে সেটা হচ্ছে ম্যান্ডেটরি করা হয়েছে সিপিডি কোর্সের এবং এটা প্রতি বছর করতে হবে। এই বছর করে নিলাম মানে না, প্রতি বছর কোর্স পালটে দেবে তারা সেই অ্যাপস এর মধ্যে এবং সেই অ্যাপস এ গিয়ে আমাদের কোর্সগুলো করতে হবে এবং প্রতি বছর কী কী কোর্সগুলো দেওয়া হবে সেগুলো জানিয়ে দেওয়া হবে। এনরোলমেন্ট হওয়ার শেষ তারিখ হচ্ছে এবছর ৩১শে আগস্ট অর্থাৎ ২০২৬-২৭ শিক্ষাবর্ষের এনরোলমেন্টের শেষ তারিখ হচ্ছে ৩১শে আগস্টের মধ্যে কিন্তু এনরোলমেন্ট করে নিতে হবে। এবং অনেকগুলো কোর্স কিন্তু শেষ হয়ে যাবে ১৫ই সেপ্টেম্বর, কিছু কিছু কোর্স কিন্তু ৩১শে আগস্ট বা জুলাই মাসেও, এই ৩১শে জুলাইয়ের মধ্যেও কিন্তু কিছু কোর্স শেষ হয়ে যাচ্ছে। তাই তড়িঘড়ি করে কিন্তু আমাদের এই কোর্সগুলো করতে হবে এবং এই কোর্সগুলো আমরা করছি কিনা সমস্ত ডিআই, সরি ডিআই নয়, স্কুল ইন্সপেক্টর এসআই এবং এআইকে দায়িত্ব দেওয়া হয়েছে, তারা স্কুল ওয়াইজ মনিটারিং করবেন যে সমস্ত শিক্ষকরা এনরোলমেন্ট করলেন কিনা বা তারা কোর্সগুলো করলেন কিনা। তাই এবার কিন্তু আমাদেরকে এই কোর্সগুলো কিন্তু করতেই হবে। তো কীভাবে করবো, কীভাবে সিপিডি কোর্সগুলো বেছে নেব, সেই পুরো ব্যাপারটা আমি স্ক্রিনে দেখাবো, তাই ভিডিওটা চলুন দেখে নিন পুরো ব্যাপারটা। তো আমি আমার মোবাইল স্ক্রিনে চলে এসেছি। মোবাইল স্ক্রিনে এই যে দীক্ষা অ্যাপ, দীক্ষা কোর্সে যাবেন না, প্রথমে দীক্ষা অ্যাপে ক্লিক করবেন। এই যে দেখতে পাচ্ছেন, এখানটায় দীক্ষা অ্যাপে ক্লিক করার পর এখান থেকে আপনাকে নিয়ে যাবে ও দীক্ষা কোর্সে আপনাকে যেতে হবে। সেটা কীভাবে সেটাও আমি দেখিয়ে দিচ্ছি চলুন। আমরা দীক্ষা অ্যাপে চলে এসেছি।
